## Classroom Scrolling Watermark

### What is the "scrolling watermark"?
The "scrolling watermark" is an anti-recording feature used in the ClassIn classroom. It scrolls a student's phone number across the screen at a set speed so that class content cannot be secretly captured by screen recording and traced back. When enabled, each student can only see their own phone number in their own classroom view, not anyone else's.

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### When to use this
Teaching staff can enable the student scrolling watermark feature in the Backend Management System. In every classroom using this configuration, every student and auditor will see a randomly moving phone number on their own screen during class, corresponding to that student's own phone number. This effectively deters students from recording class content and sharing it with others. If a student still records the video, the school can identify the person responsible from the phone number shown in the recording.

### Usage Notes
Each student can only see their own phone number on their own screen — they cannot see other students' phone numbers.

The scrolling watermark does not appear on the teacher's screen in the classroom.

To disable the scrolling watermark, contact teaching staff to turn it off in the Backend Management System.

### Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, teachers need to exit and re-enter the classroom for the new configuration to take effect.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Create or edit a custom classroom configuration.
5. Go to Toggle Settings.
6. Under "Student and Auditor Classroom Scrolling Watermark Settings," turn on or off "After a student enters the classroom, their nickname and phone number will move randomly around the classroom."
7. After finishing, click Next or Confirm.
8. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

## Classroom Anti-Recording Protection

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### When to use this
When teaching staff enable the classroom anti-recording feature in the Backend Management System, in every classroom using that configuration, students (but not the teacher or co-teacher) will be unable to use any screen-recording software to capture the classroom view. This helps prevent teaching content from being illegally captured or distributed, protecting intellectual property. Note: with this feature enabled, students attending on a phone or tablet also cannot mirror the classroom view to another device.

### Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, teachers need to exit and re-enter the classroom for the new configuration to take effect.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Create or edit a custom classroom configuration.
5. Go to Toggle Settings.
6. Under "Chat Window Settings," turn on or off "Roles other than the teacher and co-teacher cannot use screen-recording software to capture the classroom view on computer, phone, or tablet (once enabled, mobile devices also cannot mirror to other devices)."
7. After finishing, click Next or Confirm.
8. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

## Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration

### What is a "custom classroom"?
A "custom classroom" refers to a personalized configuration that teaching staff create for a classroom in the Backend Management System — including a custom classroom background, enabling or disabling certain classroom features, and adjusting classroom parameters — to give teachers a better teaching experience.

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
Teaching staff can add a "Custom Classroom Configuration" in the Backend Management System. Within it, they can change the classroom background, enable or disable certain classroom features, and adjust classroom parameters. See below for the classroom features that can be enabled or disabled.

### Notes
Up to 50 custom classroom configurations can be created.

### Related Articles
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Under "Custom Classroom Configuration," click + to add a new custom classroom.

## Preventing Recorded Lessons from Problematic Windows 7 Computers

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### When to use this
When a teacher uses a Windows 7 computer to teach, if their ClassIn recording capture range is set to "Minimized Classroom Window" or "Current Classroom Window Size," and the Aero theme is not enabled on their computer, the resulting class playback recording will include content from the desktop outside the classroom. To prevent this, teaching staff can enable "Prevent Teachers From Recording on Problematic Computers" in the Backend Management System. With this enabled, if a teacher tries to record on Windows 7 without Aero enabled, ClassIn will automatically block the recording to avoid the issue.

### Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, teachers need to exit and re-enter the classroom for the new configuration to take effect.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Create or edit a custom classroom configuration.
5. Go to Toggle Settings.
6. Under "Prevent Teachers From Recording on Problematic Computers," turn the feature on or off.
7. After finishing, click Next or Confirm.
8. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

## Hiding Student Class Notes

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### When to use this
When lesson content involves private or confidential information, teaching staff can disable the student class notes feature for privacy and intellectual-property protection. This effectively prevents students from taking screenshots of classroom content via the notes feature and sharing it with others.

### Usage Notes
To prevent students from using the class notes feature, teaching staff need to check "Hide Notes Button" under "Student-Side Notes Settings" in "Custom Classroom Configuration" in the Backend Management System. To restore access to class notes for students, simply uncheck "Hide Notes Button."

### Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, teachers need to exit and re-enter the classroom for the new configuration to take effect.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Create or edit a custom classroom configuration.
5. Go to Toggle Settings.
6. Under "Student-Side Notes Settings," turn on or off "Hide Notes Button (student side)."
7. After finishing, click Next or Confirm.
8. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

## Hiding the Chat Tool

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### When to use this
To prevent students from posting inappropriate remarks in the chat tool, teaching staff can hide the chat tool in "Custom Classroom Configuration" in the Backend Management System. Every classroom using this configuration will hide the chat tool by default — this avoids situations where a teacher or co-teacher forgets to restrict student chat once class begins.

### Usage Notes
Once the chat tool is hidden in the classroom via the Backend Management System, it takes effect in every classroom using that configuration — neither teachers nor students will be able to use the classroom chat tool.

### Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, teachers need to exit and re-enter the classroom for the new configuration to take effect.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Create or edit a custom classroom configuration.
5. Go to Toggle Settings.
6. Under "Chat Window Settings," turn on or off "Hide chat button (both teacher and student side)."
7. After finishing, click Next or Confirm.
8. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

## Advanced Mirror Mode

### What is "Advanced Mirror Mode"?
There are two places in ClassIn where mirror mode can be set: one in the classroom, and one in the Backend Management System — and they are fundamentally different. If a user only enables mirror mode within the classroom, only that user will see their own camera feed flipped left-right. If teaching staff enable mirror mode in the Backend Management System, then when a user in the classroom enables mirror mode, other users in the classroom will also see that user's camera feed flipped left-right.

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### When to use this
When a teacher wants others to see their flipped camera feed from their own point of view, teaching staff can enable Advanced Mirror Mode in the Backend Management System to make this possible.

### Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, teachers need to exit and re-enter the classroom for the new configuration to take effect.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Create or edit a custom classroom configuration.
5. Go to Toggle Settings.
6. Under "Camera Mirror Mode Settings," turn on or off "Sync the local mirrored video to other viewers."
7. After finishing, click Next or Confirm.
8. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fad66f871d8a76c8b7312b445c4e0aa7cc8801412da1a5138cb1f8ef75da61e92_739281?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=2bd3b708213c6db92b42bc8e278efab406532b0e)

```yaml
title: "Default Classroom"
source_title_zh: "默认教室"
```

## Default Classroom

### What is the "default classroom"?
Classroom settings in the "Backend Management System" differ from classroom settings within the ClassIn app itself. Classroom settings in the Backend Management System are mainly used to enable, disable, and customize certain in-class features for classrooms within the app, while classroom settings within the app configure the basic audio/video functionality of each classroom. In the Backend Management System, teaching staff can choose between two types of classroom settings: System Classroom Settings and Custom Classroom Settings. System Classroom Settings cannot be changed, while Custom Classroom Settings can be personalized based on teaching needs — for example, setting the classroom background, features, and parameters — to provide a better teaching experience. So classroom settings in the Backend Management System and classroom settings within the app are two separate, non-conflicting features. If teaching staff do not assign a specific classroom setting to a "course (class)" when configuring it, every classroom under that course (class) will automatically use the default classroom setting.

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
The "Default Classroom Setting" cannot be used in self-study rooms.

If teaching staff select a specific "Classroom Setting" for a "course (class)" when creating it, that course (class) will no longer use the "Default Classroom Setting" from the Backend Management System.

### Related Articles
"Adding a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Editing a Custom Classroom Configuration"
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings at the top.
4. Use the Default Classroom Setting.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fdb5906764b4cdab12c02d31f9c01108fdb749383b48fcf7c4b8a625b9e3e737f_369062?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=942cb2a72721d50714af61ee5abff873be89b847)

## Syncing Class Nicknames

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
Teaching staff can enable a class nickname sync feature in the Backend Management System. Once enabled, every time a student joins a class under this school, the student's name in the Backend Management System is automatically synced as their nickname in the newly joined class.

Note that this sync only happens when a student first joins a class. If the student's name is later changed in the Backend Management System, the new name will not be synced to classes they've already joined. This feature also only applies to classes at this school — if a student joins a class at a different school, their nickname will not be synced.

### Related Articles
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Class Settings at the top.
4. Under "Class Nickname Sync Settings," turn on or off "Sync a newly joined student's backend name as their ClassIn class nickname."

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3793f3d6eabd588d61ec08dd9305eee8026e0c812d11f5338285cbf25b78dcb2_410636?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b8287b4d0a5dfb9f972d64c6082c790ca8db6ce8)

- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
When this feature is enabled, in situations such as "a student was removed from the class by a teacher," "the class was dissolved," or "a student left the class voluntarily," students who have left the class can still view class/lesson playbacks, whiteboard writing, recorded lesson videos, and other activity attachments.

When this feature is disabled, in the same situations, students who have left the class will no longer be able to view class/lesson playbacks, whiteboard writing, recorded lesson videos, or other activity attachments.

### Notes
Enabling or disabling "Allow Students Who Left the Class or Whose Class Was Dissolved to View Course Content" only affects the playback videos of courses (classes) created after the change; playback videos of courses (classes) created before the change are unaffected. Even if this setting is toggled again later, access permissions for students already affected by it at the time will remain unchanged.

Access to whiteboard writing, recorded lesson videos, and other activity attachments will be adjusted according to the current state of "Allow Students Who Left the Class or Whose Class Was Dissolved to View Course Content." Both new and existing courses (classes) are affected by this setting, and the state can be changed at any time.

### Related Articles
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Class Settings at the top.
4. Under "Allow Students Who Left the Class or Whose Class Was Dissolved to View Course Content," turn on or off "Enable 'Students who left the class or whose class was dissolved may view course content' by default for classes."

## Default Course Cover

### Applies to

Teaching staff can set a default "course (class)" cover in the Backend Management System. When a teacher at the school creates a class without a custom "course (class)" cover, the system will use the default "course (class)" cover set in the Backend Management System. The teacher can still change to a custom "course (class)" cover at any time.

Images uploaded by teaching staff support fixed-ratio cropping; the recommended image ratio is 900px x 900px, and the file size should not exceed 1MB.

```yaml
title: "Task Center"
source_title_zh: "任务中心"
```

## Task Center

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
You can create multiple download tasks at once without waiting on the current page.

Previously downloaded data can be viewed, so the same data doesn't need to be downloaded again.

You can view each administrator's download activity, which helps protect data security.

1. **View download progress and results.** Completed download tasks can be downloaded as files. Each file supports exporting up to 100,000 rows of data; if this is exceeded, the export is split across multiple files. If there is only one file, it downloads directly; if there are multiple files, they download as a zip archive (named the same as the download task, following the same naming logic), with each file inside numbered "_1," "_2," and so on.

2. **Task naming convention:** task type + data date range — for example, a task named "Lesson Attendance 20240301-20240331" generates a file containing lesson attendance data for March 1–31, 2024.

3. You can look up historical download tasks by task name, task type, or operation time, so the same data doesn't need to be downloaded again.

4. The organization's primary account can see every administrator's downloads in the Task Center; organization sub-accounts can only see their own downloads. Every task records the operation time and the person who performed it, so system administrators can review each administrator's actions, quickly spot and prevent unauthorized activity, and improve system security.

### Notes
There is some delay in data downloads — for example, if you download data at 19:00, the earliest available data will be up to 18:40 that day. Workaround: wait 10–20 minutes after a lesson ends before downloading its data.

### Related Articles
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to Task Center in the left navigation.
3. Find or download a generated task.

- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
Teaching staff can enable or disable SMS and phone alerts for account balance and contract expiration in the Backend Management System. Once enabled, teaching staff can set alert thresholds — up to six thresholds. When the balance falls below a threshold, or 30 days before the contract expires, the system will notify the user via SMS and phone call.

```yaml
title: "Smart Homeroom Teacher"
source_title_zh: "智能班主任"
```

## Smart Homeroom Teacher

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
Teaching staff can enable or disable the Smart Homeroom Teacher feature through the school's Backend Management System. Once enabled, teaching staff can use it for two types of alerts: reminding students to prepare for class via SMS or phone call before class starts, and reminding students who haven't shown up within 3 minutes of class starting.

In the Backend Management System, teaching staff can configure the specific behavior of Smart Homeroom Teacher, which includes the following options:

- Remind students by phone or SMS the day before class that they have a class the next day.
- Remind students again by phone or SMS 1 hour before class starts.
- If a student still hasn't shown up 3 minutes after class starts, remind them by phone or SMS to join immediately.
- Remind teachers by phone or SMS the day before class that they have a class the next day.
- Remind teachers again by phone or SMS 1 hour before class starts.
- If a teacher still hasn't shown up 3 minutes after class starts, remind them by phone or SMS to join immediately.

These six reminder features can be enabled or disabled all together, and for each reminder type, you can choose either phone call or SMS (not both).

### Related Articles
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Value-Added Services at the top.
4. Under Smart Homeroom Teacher, turn the feature on or off and configure its settings.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8a2439f210504bbb7f92d3bad4fa46ccc1550fc505cfe84742e7f9ad6374389d_374548?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=d7323114974f51271b0a86165954036aef9b385b)

```yaml
title: "Super Customer Service"
source_title_zh: "超级客服"
```

## Super Customer Service

### Applies to
- Primary account of the Backend Management System
- Sub-accounts with the "School Settings" permission

### Usage Notes
Teaching staff can enable or disable the Super Customer Service feature in the Backend Management System. Once enabled, teaching staff can use voice callback on the Class Monitoring Management page in the Backend Management System to directly contact teachers, co-teachers, and students — quickly resolving issues in the classroom.

If there are many teaching staff members in the Backend Management System, the school can enable "Phone Number Masking" to protect teacher and student privacy. Once enabled, 4 digits of student and teacher phone numbers will be masked on the Class Monitoring Management and Account Lookup pages, preventing contact information from leaking.

Note: this feature only supports mainland China phone numbers, excluding Xinjiang, Tibet, and Inner Mongolia. The caller ID shown to both the caller and the callee is a Hangzhou, China number: 0571-57184557.

### Related Articles
"Adding Sub-accounts in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log in to the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Value-Added Services at the top.
4. Under Super Customer Service, turn "Super Customer Service" and "Phone Number Masking" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa44e826f3aba6f609cee16ae1c297fee83f69dd98d1e73d7b8269a93ad7b2854_529003?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ea76e7588eba0a8b73cade53f76aa2eae203ab69)

# Admin Console: Login & Basic Settings

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Admin Users"
source_title_zh: "后台管理员"
```

## Admin Users

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Permission Management" access

### Overview
The Admin Console is used to manage school data such as courses, teachers, and students. The primary account holder can add admins (sub-accounts) to the Admin Console, letting them log in and granting each one a different set of permissions. Each permission controls which area of the console that admin can manage:

| Section | Area | What the admin can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Course Center | Class/Session Management | Create, edit, and end classes; add students to a class; create, edit, and delete sessions. |
| | Public Classes | Create, edit, delete public classes; add students to a public class. |
| Storage Management | Teacher Management | Add, edit, activate/deactivate teachers; assign resources and tags to teachers. |
| | Student Management | Add, edit, hide, show, delete students; assign resources and tags to students. |
| | Data Overview | View storage usage in the Admin Console. |
| | Org Cloud Drive | Create folders, upload courseware, copy/move courseware. Includes delete, download, and member-management sub-permissions, each independently toggleable. |
| | Question Bank | Add, edit, delete questions and papers in the org question bank. |
| | Class Resources | View storage used by each session's recordings, monitoring screenshots, and whiteboard notes; lock these to prevent accidental deletion; manually delete them. |
| | Class Group Resources | View storage used by class files, course attachments, and co-created documents; lock these to prevent accidental deletion; manually delete them. |
| | Resource Center | Add resource products and manage resource orders; view resources acquired by the primary account. |
| Teaching Management | Live/Playback | View and edit personalized settings for web live stream and playback. |
| | Teaching Data | Edit post-class evaluations; view teaching reports, learning reports, and teaching/learning analysis in class data. |
| | Assignment Management | View/download assignment data. |
| | Quiz Management | View/download quiz data. |
| Academic Management | Class Monitoring / Account Lookup | Sit in on live classes; view teacher and student attendance; view network and device status during class. |
| Finance Center | Finance Center | View billing rules, order details, invoices, and related information. |
| My School | My School | View and edit the organization's personalized configuration. |
| | Permission Management | Add more admins to the school's console, and edit or remove existing admins. |
| Client Permissions | Create Public Class / Class | Create public classes or classes directly from the ClassIn app. |

### Notes
- When editing an admin, the account/email cannot be changed — only the display name and permissions can be updated.

### Steps

**(1) Add an admin**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Permission Management in the left navigation.
3. Click Add Sub-account on the right.
4. Enter the sub-account's basic info.
5. Set the sub-account's permissions.
6. Click Confirm.

**(2) Edit an admin's permissions**
1. Search for the admin (top-left).
2. Click Edit next to their name.

**(3) Remove an admin**
1. Search for the admin (top-right).
2. Click Delete next to their name.

## School/Org Introduction

This introduction appears on the web live/playback page, the public class registration page, and learning reports.

- "Setting the School Name and Logo"

## Logging In / Out of the Admin Console

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Admin Console sub-accounts

### When to use this
Every school using ClassIn has its own dedicated Admin Console. There, academic staff can schedule classes, adjust settings, monitor class groups and sessions, and view teaching data and billing — all of which directly affects how classes, teachers, students, and other features function in the app. To schedule classes or change settings, staff must first log into the Admin Console.

### Overview
Each school's Admin Console has one primary account with full access to all console permissions. If multiple staff members need access, the primary account can add sub-accounts and assign each one a different set of permissions, enabling multi-person collaboration.

The Admin Console supports the following display languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Japanese, Arabic. Switch languages from the top-right corner of the console homepage.

If a teacher holds a sub-account or primary account at multiple schools, they can log into the console and switch to another school's console from the top-right corner.

### Related articles
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps

**(1) Log into the Admin Console**
1. Open your browser.
2. Go to www.eeo.cn.
3. Click "Admin Console" in the top-right corner.
4. Log in with your ClassIn username/password, or via verification code.

**(2) Switch to another school's console**
1. From the Admin Console, use the top-right corner to switch to another school's console.

**(3) Log out of the Admin Console**
1. Click your profile picture in the top-right corner.
2. Click Log Out.

## Verification Documents

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account

### Overview
Academic staff use the "Verification Documents" page in the Admin Console to submit or update the school/organization's verification info. Required fields include: school/business name, logo, primary business category, region, detailed address, contact person's name/phone/email, and verification method. Common verification methods include business license, ID card, or passport. For example, business license verification requires a photo of the license, company name, legal representative, and unified social credit code. After submitting, the verification undergoes review.

To use ClassIn's cloud recording feature, the account's verification status must be "Verified."

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Verification Documents in the left navigation.
3. Click Edit to update your verification information.
4. Click Confirm to save.

## Head Teacher Management

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Course Management" access

### When to use this

**Change the head teacher**

## Excluded Students Management

### I. What is an "excluded student"?
An excluded student is a student a teacher has blocked from attending a specific session within a class. The excluded student cannot enter that particular session's classroom, but can still attend the class's other sessions normally.

### II. Setting an excluded student

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**Overview**
If a student drops out early or academic staff need to block certain students from a specific session, staff can mark them as excluded for that session. Once excluded, the student can't enter the blocked session, nor watch its recorded playback.

**Related articles**
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find and open the class.
4. Go to Schedule.
5. Find the session, then click Add next to "Excluded Students."
6. Add the excluded student(s).

### III. Removing an excluded student
Requires a sub-account with "Course Management" access.

Find the session, hover over "Excluded Students," and click the pencil icon that appears to remove excluded students — supports removing all at once or individually.

```yaml
title: "Auditing Students Management"
source_title_zh: "旁听生管理"
```

## Auditing Students Management

### I. What is an "auditing student"?
An auditing student can sit in on a class without being visible to the teacher or other students — neither the teacher nor other students can see them, and their name doesn't appear in the roster. In effect, they attend invisibly. Even so, if their cumulative attendance reaches 10 minutes, it still counts as a valid attendance record. Auditing students can't use any classroom tools — they can only listen. Once added, they appear in the class's student list but cannot watch the class playback.

### II. Adding an auditing student

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**When to use this**
Each class can have up to 20 auditing students. This feature is mainly meant to let academic staff offer trial-listening seats within a class, helping students preview the course. Auditing students can join the class group chat and interact with other students and the teacher, but no one in the classroom can see them — they're effectively invisible while listening in. This is useful for students exploring elective/interest classes, letting them audit a session before deciding whether to formally enroll.

**Related articles**
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find and open the class.
4. Go to Members.
5. Go to Auditing Students.
6. Click "Set Auditing Students."

### III. Removing an auditing student
Requires a sub-account with "Course Management" access.

Remove the auditing student from the list.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Guest Students Management"
source_title_zh: "插班生管理"
```

## Guest Students Management

### I. What is a "guest student"?
A guest student is a student who isn't formally part of a class, but has been arranged by academic staff to attend one specific session of that class.

### II. Adding a guest student

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**When to use this**
When a teacher wants to invite a student to sit in on a particular session — and wants that student to be able to interact with the teacher and other students in the classroom — but doesn't want to formally add them to the class, they can add the student as a guest student for that session.

**Overview**
A "guest student" is a non-enrolled student arranged by academic staff to attend a specific session of a class. Guest students have no class group, so they can't take part in homework, quizzes, or chats assigned in the class group chat. However, within the classroom itself, guest students have the same permissions as regular students — they can speak on stage, be granted tool access by the teacher, and participate in in-classroom chat.

**Notes**
- If a student is already formally enrolled in a class, they cannot also be added as a guest student for any session in that same class.
- Guest students share the same class headcount cap as regular enrolled students.

**Related articles**
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find and open the class.
4. Go to Schedule.
5. Find the session, then click Add next to "Guest Students."
6. You can add guest students from students/teachers within your school, or from outside your school.

### III. Removing a guest student
Find the session, hover over "Guest Students," and click the pencil icon that appears to remove — supports bulk removal or removing individually.

```yaml
title: "Class Student Management (Admin Console)"
source_title_zh: "班级学生管理（后台）"
```

## Class Student Management (Admin Console)

### I. Adding students to a class

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**Overview**
In the Admin Console, academic staff can add any student to a class, whether or not they've registered a ClassIn account. If the student already has a ClassIn account and appears in the console's student list, staff can simply search by name or phone number to find and add them. If the student isn't yet in the console's student list, or hasn't registered a ClassIn account, staff can register an account on their behalf while adding them to the class.

**Related articles**
- "Auditing Students Management"
- "Guest Students Management"
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find the class and click its name to enter.
4. Go to Members.
5. Click "Set Class Students."

### II. Copying students from another class

**Who this applies to** / **When to use this**
In the Admin Console, when a class's sessions have reached the maximum allowed, teachers who need to add more sessions must create a new class. To avoid manually re-adding every student to the new class, the system lets teachers directly copy all students from the original class into the new one — saving time and improving efficiency.

**Notes**
- If your class already has students, copying a student list from another class will replace all existing students in the current class. Use this feature carefully.

**Steps**
1. Click "Copy Class Students."

### III. Editing class students
When academic staff need to change class membership, they can edit it directly from the class student list.
- Use the top-right corner to add or remove students.

### IV. Removing class students
Remove a single student, or select multiple students and use Bulk Actions > Bulk Remove Students.

## Create/Edit/Delete Public Classes (Admin Console)

### I. Creating a public class

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Public Classes" access

**When to use this**
If a teacher wants to hold a session that isn't tied to any class — such as a class meeting, parent-teacher conference, guest lecture, or teacher workshop — consider creating a public class instead. This better supports a variety of non-standard teaching scenarios.

**Overview**
Creating a public class in the Admin Console automatically generates a matching public class in the ClassIn app, and vice versa — creating one in the app generates a matching entry in the Admin Console. The two are identical; there's no difference between them.

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Public Classes in the left navigation.
3. Click Create Public Class.
4. Set the parameters.

### II. Editing a public class
Requires a sub-account with "Class Management" access.
1. Find the public class.
2. Hover over the parameter you want to change; when a pencil icon appears on the right, click it to edit that field.

### III. Deleting a public class
1. Click "Actions" on the right, then select "Delete Public Class."

## Tag Management

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Course Management" access

### When to use this
In the Admin Console, tags help academic staff manage courses, sessions, and teacher/student members more conveniently. Using tags, staff can quickly search for and categorize courses, sessions, or members — making management more efficient.

### Overview
The Admin Console supports up to 2,000 tags total. Each course and session, and each teacher and student, can have up to 10 personal tags.

### Related articles
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps

**(1) Add/edit course tags**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Course Management in the left navigation.
3. Click "Create Course" on the right.
4. Below, click "Select Course Tags."
5. Create a new tag or choose an existing one.
6. Click Confirm to save.

**(2) Add/edit session tags**
1. Find the course, click its name to enter session details.
2. Click "Add Session."
3. Click "Select Session Tags."

**(3) Add/edit teacher tags**
1. Go to Teacher Management in the left navigation.
2. Find the teacher, click View on the right.
3. Then click Edit.
4. Select tags.

**(4) Add/edit student tags**
1. Go to Student Management in the left navigation.
2. Find the student, click View on the right.

```yaml
title: "Create/Edit/Delete Dual-Teacher Sessions"
source_title_zh: "创建修改删除双师课"
```

## Create/Edit/Delete Dual-Teacher Sessions

### I. Creating a dual-teacher session

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Course Management" access

**Overview**

**Method 1: Create a new class and add a main/satellite session**
If academic staff haven't yet created a main session for a dual-teacher setup in the Admin Console, they can: first create a new class in the Admin Console, then add a session within that class, then bulk-add satellite sessions and set the newly created session as the main session.

**Method 2: Set an existing session as the main session and add satellite sessions**
Alternatively, staff can go directly into a class in the Admin Console, click "Bulk Create Satellite Sessions," designate an existing session as the main session for a dual-teacher setup, then add satellite sessions.

**Notes**
- The dual-teacher feature must be enabled separately by contacting your account manager.
- Each dual-teacher main session supports up to 100 satellite sessions.
- Satellite sessions cannot be created within 5 minutes of the main session's start time, or after it has already started.
- Both the app and the Admin Console support editing/deleting the main session; satellite sessions automatically sync with changes made to the main session.
- Satellite session settings cannot be edited in the app — only in the Admin Console.
- Dual-teacher sessions don't require a dedicated class — an existing class can be used.
- The main session and its satellite sessions cannot belong to the same class.

**Related articles**
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**

**Create the "main session"**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find and open the class.
4. Go to Schedule.
5. Click New.
6. Select "Create Session."

**Add "satellite sessions"**
1. Select the session (the selected session will automatically become the main session).
2. Click "Bulk Add Satellite Sessions."
3. Set the satellite sessions' parameters (you'll need to pre-create an empty class to hold the satellite sessions — when creating them, assign them to that pre-created empty class).

### II. Editing a dual-teacher session
When editing a satellite session, you cannot change: start date, start time, session duration, or teacher.
- Satellite sessions can only be edited in the Admin Console.
- The main session can be edited in both the Admin Console and the app.

**Edit the "main session" or a "satellite session"**
1. Find the class containing the main or satellite session and open it.
2. Edit the session.

### III. Deleting a dual-teacher session
Academic staff can delete both main and satellite sessions from the Admin Console. First, find the relevant main session. Delete satellite sessions from the main session's dual-teacher page. Deleting the main session automatically deletes all its satellite sessions. To delete just one satellite session, deleting it alone won't affect the others.

Deleting a main session automatically deletes all associated satellite sessions.

1. Go to Course Management in the left navigation.
2. Find and open the class containing the main session.
3. Click "Actions" next to the main session, then select "Dual-Teacher Online."
4. Delete the main session or a satellite session.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Create/Edit/Delete Sessions (Admin Console)"
source_title_zh: "创建修改删除课堂（后台）"
```

## Create/Edit/Delete Sessions (Admin Console)

### I. Creating a session

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**Overview**

Parameters available when adding a session:

| Setting | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Session Name | Up to 50 characters. |
| Start Date | Can be today or any other date. |
| Start Time | Earliest allowed is 5 minutes from now. |
| Session Duration | Minimum 15 minutes, maximum 23 hours 55 minutes. |
| Teacher | Add the main teacher — only one per session. |
| Co-Teachers | Up to 6 co-teachers per session, or none at all. |
| Teaching Mode | "Online Classroom" suits pure online teaching; "Smart Classroom" suits hybrid online/offline teaching. |
| Auto Stage | When enabled, students' camera feeds automatically appear on stage upon entering the classroom (regardless of whether their camera is on). When disabled, students enter "off-stage" and their camera won't automatically appear on stage. |
| On-Stage Capacity | From 1v0 to 1v12. 1v0 means only the teacher's camera shows on stage (no student cameras). 1v12 means the teacher's camera plus up to 12 students' cameras can be shown simultaneously. |
| Session Cloud Drive Resources | Public courseware resources that can only be opened within this specific session's classroom. |
| Cloud Recording | Supports enabling "Record Classroom" and "Record On-site" simultaneously, or either individually, or neither. |
| Live/Playback | Supports enabling "Web Live Stream" and "Web Playback" simultaneously. With "Web Live Stream" enabled, viewers can watch the real-time class broadcast via a link shared by the teacher. With "Web Playback" enabled, viewers can watch the recorded playback via a shared link. |

**Notes**
- If "Session-Authorized Resources" is set when creating a session, the teacher can only use courseware authorized under "Session Cloud Drive Resources" or their own personal cloud drive during that session — not courseware authorized under "Class Cloud Drive Resources."

**Related articles**
- "Adding Students to a Class"
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"
- "Editing a Session"
- "Deleting a Session"

**Steps**

**(1) Create a single session**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find the class and click its name to enter.
4. Click Schedule.
5. Click New > Create Session.
6. Set the relevant parameters.

**(2) Bulk-create sessions**
1. Click New > Bulk Create Sessions.

### II. Editing a session

**Who this applies to** / **Overview**

When editing session info and settings, note the following time restrictions:

**(1) Session name, start date, start time, duration:**
Editable window: any time more than 20 minutes before the session's start time.
Restriction: cannot be edited within 20 minutes of the start time, during the session, or after it ends.

**(2) Teacher and co-teachers:**
Editable window: can be added or edited before or after the start time.
Restriction: cannot be edited once the session has ended.

**(3) On-stage capacity (e.g. changing 1v1 to 1v6):**
Editable window: any time more than 20 minutes before the session's start time.

**(4) Cloud recording and web live stream:**

**(5) Web playback:**
Editable window: can be changed anytime — before, during, or after the session — including viewing permission for web playback.

**(6) Deleting a session:**
Editable window: can be deleted at any time before the session officially starts.
Restriction: cannot be deleted once the session has officially started.

**Steps**

**(1) Edit a single session**
1. Find the session you want to edit, click "Actions" on the right, then select "Edit Session."

**(2) Bulk-edit sessions**
1. Select the sessions to edit, click Bulk Actions, then choose the setting to bulk-edit; or hover over a session and click the pencil icon to open Bulk Edit.

### III. Deleting a session
Sessions that have already started or already ended cannot be deleted — only sessions that haven't started yet can be deleted.

**(1) Delete a single session**
1. Find the session to delete, click "Actions" on the right, then select "Delete Session."

**(2) Bulk-delete sessions**
1. Select the sessions to delete, click Bulk Actions, then select "Bulk Delete Sessions."

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Create/Edit Class / End Class (Admin Console)"
source_title_zh: "创建修改班级结课（后台）"
```

## Create/Edit Class / End Class (Admin Console)

### I. Creating a class

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**Overview**
Classes created in the Admin Console support more advanced configuration — such as adding guest students, excluded students, and auditing students. The Admin Console also supports features like reassigning the head teacher. For this reason, we recommend creating and managing classes in the Admin Console whenever complex management is needed.

Parameters available when creating a class:

| Setting | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Class Name | Required. Give the class an easily recognizable name, up to 40 characters. |
| Head Teacher | Assign a head teacher for the class. The head teacher can manage class members and create/delete sessions from within the ClassIn app. |
| Class Teachers | Teachers who can teach or assist with management. Can also be set later via Members after the class is created. |
| Class Students | Students who participate in class activities. Can also be set later via Members after the class is created. |
| Class Cover | Upload a cover image from the system library or your local computer. |
| Class Description | Write an appealing, concise description for the class — shown within the ClassIn app and on live/playback links. |
| Class Cloud Drive Resources | Set the class-level cloud drive resources. All sessions in the class can use courseware authorized here, unless a session has its own "Session Cloud Drive Resources" set, in which case the teacher can only use resources authorized at the session level during that session. |
| Class Classroom Settings | Choose a custom classroom configuration for the class, applied to all its sessions. If not selected, the school's default custom classroom configuration is used. |
| Class Tags | Add tags for easier management and searching. |
| Class Expiration | Set an expiration date. If the class has no upcoming or ongoing sessions after this date, the system automatically ends the class.<br><br>Note: classes default to never expiring. To enable auto-ending, set the expiration to a certain number of days after the last session ends (minimum 1 day, maximum 365 days). |
| Playback View Limit | Set how many times students can watch the class recording playback, from 1 to 20 (a view counts as valid once the student has watched at least 75% of the total video duration). |
| Advanced Settings | Enable or disable: "Allow students to join the class on their own," "Allow class members to add each other as friends," "Allow teachers to add sessions," "Allow students to edit their class nickname," "Allow content to remain viewable for students who've left the class or after the class ends," "Allow class members to start temporary classrooms." The head teacher can also configure these from within the ClassIn app. |

**Notes**
- The Admin Console doesn't support sharing a QR code to join the class. To share one, go to the corresponding class's settings within the ClassIn app and use "View/Share Join QR Code."

**Related articles**
- "Adding Students to a Class"
- "Adding a Session"
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Click "Create Class."
4. Fill in the class parameters.
5. Click Confirm.

### II. Editing a class

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Management" access

**Overview**
Existing classes can be edited in the Admin Console. Editable fields include: class name, cover, description, head teacher, class cloud drive resources, classroom settings, tags, expiration, playback view limit, and advanced settings. Advanced settings include toggles for: allowing students to join independently, allowing members to add each other as friends, allowing teachers to add sessions, allowing students to edit their nickname, allowing content access after leaving/dissolution, and allowing temporary classrooms. The head teacher can also edit these options from within the ClassIn app.

See also: "Ending a Class"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management.
3. Find and open the class.
4. Go to Settings to edit the class.

### III. Ending a class

**What does "ending a class" mean?**
"Ending a class" refers to academic staff ending a class in the Admin Console, which simultaneously dissolves the corresponding class in the ClassIn app. Conversely, when a class is dissolved in the ClassIn app, the system automatically ends the corresponding class in the Admin Console. So "ending a class" and "dissolving a class" refer to the same action — one performed from the Admin Console, the other from the ClassIn app.

**When to use this**
If academic staff want to dissolve a class in the ClassIn app but aren't the head teacher of that class, they can't do so from within the app. In that case, they can log into the Admin Console, find the class, and end it there. Once a class is ended, its corresponding class in the ClassIn app is also dissolved.

"Ending" a class in the Admin Console and "dissolving" it in the app refer to the same action — doing one automatically does the other. However, a class can't be ended if it still has sessions that haven't started or haven't ended yet. Once a class is ended, students and teachers can no longer communicate via the class group chat, but this doesn't affect their ability to watch the class's recorded playback videos.

After ending a class, if you want students to keep watching historical playback videos from the class, enable the "Allow content to remain viewable for students who've left the class or after the class ends" setting.

Classes cannot be deleted — only ended.

**(1) End a single class**
1. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
2. Find the class and click "End Class" on the right.

**(2) Bulk-end classes**
1. Select multiple classes, click Bulk Actions, then select "Bulk End Class."

# Admin Console: Class Monitoring

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Receiving & Replying to Help Requests from the Classroom"
source_title_zh: "接收教室求助信息并回复"
```

## Receiving & Replying to Help Requests from the Classroom

### I. Receiving help requests

**Who this applies to**
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Monitoring" access

**When to use this**
When a teacher or student in the classroom needs help, they can use the classroom's help feature to send a request to the Admin Console. Academic staff can log into the Admin Console, find the corresponding session on the Class Monitoring page, and click the issue notice below the session to view what was reported. Staff can then reply to help resolve it.

**Related articles**
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

**Steps**
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Monitoring in the left navigation.
3. Find the session.
4. Check for help requests in the bottom-left of the session.

### II. Sending a message to the classroom
Requires the Admin Console primary account.

While monitoring a class, academic staff join as a silent observer and can't interact with anyone in the classroom. If they notice an issue with a specific user, they can send that user a text message from the Admin Console explaining how to resolve it.

**Steps**
1. Click Contact below the session.
2. Choose "Contact Teacher" or "Contact Student."
3. Select the recipient(s), enter your message under "Describe the Issue," then click Send.

```yaml
source_title_zh: "查看监课图片"
```

## Viewing Class Monitoring Screenshots

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Monitoring" access

### Overview
Academic staff can view classroom monitoring screenshots from the class monitoring detail page. These screenshots are automatically captured by ClassIn from the teacher's viewpoint, saved once per minute.

### Notes
- Class Monitoring shows a maximum of 1,000 screenshots.

### Related articles
- "Entering a Monitored Classroom"
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Monitoring in the left navigation.
3. Find the session.
4. Click on a screenshot thumbnail to view details.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Account Lookup (View a User's In-Class Device Status)"
source_title_zh: "账号速查（查看用户上课设备使用状况）"
```

## Account Lookup (View a User's In-Class Device Status)

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Account Lookup" access

### When to use this
When a teacher or student reports an unstable network or laggy class experience, academic staff can use the Admin Console to check that user's network and device status during class.

### Overview
In Admin Console > Account Lookup, staff can search by a user's phone number or email, plus the class time, to retrieve details of their network and device status during that session. Available data includes: session name, course name, start time, session duration, on-stage headcount, the user's role in the classroom, their network usage and CPU load at each point during class, when they entered and left the classroom, the reason they left, whether they had cloud recording enabled, and whether the recording ran normally. Hovering over a device icon in the device info section shows details of that camera, microphone, or speaker — including whether it was disabled, undetected, which device was selected (if multiple were available), the OS version of the device used, the server they connected to, the device's CPU model, the ClassIn version, and whether they were on wired or wireless network.

### Related articles
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Account Lookup in the left navigation.
3. Select a date and enter the ClassIn account at the top.
4. View network and device usage during that class below.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Entering a Monitored Classroom"
source_title_zh: "进入监课教室"
```

## Entering a Monitored Classroom

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Class Monitoring" access

### When to use this
- When academic staff want to sit in on a teacher's class, they can enter the corresponding classroom from the Class Monitoring page in the Admin Console.
- If a teacher's cloud recording is interrupted due to network or device issues and can't resume, and there's no co-teacher in that session, academic staff can enter that classroom from the Class Monitoring page and start a local recording.

### Overview
To monitor a class, academic staff click "Enter Classroom" on the Class Monitoring page in the Admin Console. The browser will prompt whether to launch the associated app — staff need to click "Allow" or "Open ClassIn" (or similar) to enter the classroom successfully. If the ClassIn app doesn't launch as expected, staff should close any antivirus software and use the "Repair Registry" feature in ClassIn's settings, then try again. Note: entering a classroom to monitor from the Admin Console is free and doesn't incur any charges.

When academic staff enter a classroom to monitor it, they join as an invisible observer — the teacher and students in that classroom can't detect their presence, and staff can't interact with anyone there. However, if the Admin Console account used also has a co-teacher or student role in that classroom, staff will automatically take on that role instead when entering — in that case they can interact with classroom members, and members can see them. Once a staff member enters as anything other than an "invisible observer," normal classroom fees will apply to the Admin Console account.

### Notes
- Class Monitoring shows a maximum of 1,000 classrooms.

### Related articles
- "Viewing Class Monitoring Screenshots"
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Monitoring in the left navigation.
3. Find the session.
4. Click "Enter Classroom."

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: admin_batch3_class-monitoring.md -->

## Viewing/Downloading AI Teaching Analysis Reports in the Admin Console

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Teacher Development" access

### Overview
Once AI Teaching Analysis is enabled under Value-Added Services in the Admin Console, if academic staff check "Cloud Recording" (recording the ClassIn classroom or the physical classroom) and "AI Teaching Analysis" when scheduling a session, and the teacher records normally with clear audio, an AI Teaching Analysis report will be generated for that teacher after class.

Teachers can view and download their own AI Teaching Analysis report within ClassIn.

Academic staff in the Admin Console can review a teacher's classroom performance (including overall score and flagged issues to watch) under "Teaching Management > Teacher Development," and can view or download the detailed report for each session.

The report can also be deleted from the Admin Console — this action is irreversible. Once deleted, the teacher can no longer see the AI Teaching Analysis section in their ClassIn class playback, and staff viewing that session's score and issues under "Teacher Development" will see "Report Deleted."

### Related articles
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Teacher Development in the left navigation.
3. Find the session.
4. Click "Actions" on the right, then select "View Report" or "Download Report."

Quiz data includes: quiz title, associated course, start/end time, status (not started / in progress / ended), total score, time limit, number of questions, whether answers are public, whether late submissions are allowed, total number of students assigned the quiz, number who submitted, number graded by the teacher, the teacher's name and phone number, when the quiz was assigned, and its display status (visible or hidden in the client).

## Viewing/Downloading Assignment Data in the Admin Console

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Assignment Management" access

### Overview
Academic staff can view or download assignment data for the school in "Admin Console > Assignment Management." Staff can filter by assignment title, course name, teacher/student name, phone number, email, assignment status, display status, assigned time, start time, or end time. Downloaded assignment data includes: course ID, assignment title, associated course, teacher's name/phone/email, start and end time, status (not started / in progress / ended), total score, grading display method (numeric score, percentage, letter rating, ABCD rating, etc.), how the assignment is shared, whether late submissions are allowed, total students assigned, total submissions, total graded, number of students rated "excellent," the responsible teacher, when it was assigned, display status (visible or hidden in the client), submission rate, number of late submissions, how many students' work has been graded, how many were sent back for revision, how many students revised their work, number of "excellent" ratings, and the average, highest, and lowest scores.

### Notes

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Exporting Class Data in the Admin Console"
source_title_zh: "后台导出课堂数据"
```

## Exporting Class Data in the Admin Console

### What is "class data"?
"Class data" refers to statistics generated from tool usage and interactions within the classroom, covering both teacher and student attendance and behavior analysis. It has two sections: "Teaching Analysis," which covers teacher performance data during class, and "Learning Analysis," which covers student learning behavior data.

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Course Management" access

### When to use this
When a teacher wants to download class attendance and behavior statistics to their computer, they can filter the desired data in Class Data and export it as an Excel spreadsheet.

### Overview

**Teaching Analysis**

In Class Data, the "Teaching Analysis" page lets you analyze data for a specific teacher or time period, including: attendance, average number and duration of courseware used, average number of rewards given, hand-raises, tool authorizations, and usage of other teaching tools. This data can also be shown as a line chart of usage counts and cumulative duration over time. "Count" and "Cumulative Duration" can be toggled via the chart customization controls in the top-left of the chart.

At the bottom of the Teaching Analysis page, you can view or download per-session detail data, including: total teaching time per session, teacher attendance per session, student attendance per session (excluding auditing students), student ratings/comments for the teacher, teacher ratings/comments for students, total number of students who watched the class playback in the ClassIn app, average playback viewing duration across students, total playback video duration per session, and detailed usage counts/durations for: text-based courseware (Word, PowerPoint, PDF, and other document types), audio/video courseware, mute-all actions, student removals, student rewards, student hand-raises, tool-authorized student tool usage, "Screen Share," "Timer," "Dice," "Buzzer," "Response Clicker" (including accuracy and detail breakdown), "Mini Whiteboard" (including detail breakdown), "Collaborative Text," "Multi-way Screen Share," "Browser," "Assignment" tool, "Countdown Timer," "Random Picker," "EDB Courseware" (with names, open times, and sources), "Breakout Rooms" (including detail breakdown), "Auxiliary Camera," and "Video Wall."

**Learning Analysis**

In Class Data, teachers and admins can use the "Learning Analysis" page to better understand student performance, including: total time per session, attendance records, teacher ratings/comments for the student, and the number and duration of times a student watched the class playback. It also covers statistics on student speaking, going on stage, raising hands, being removed, and being rewarded, as well as usage of buzzer and response clicker tools. Total camera-on duration per session is also tracked. This data helps teachers and admins understand student performance and take targeted steps to improve learning outcomes.

### Related articles
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Class Management in the left navigation.
3. Find the class, click "Class Data" on the right.
4. In the top-left, go to "Teaching Analysis" or "Learning Analysis."
5. Filter the data.
6. Click "Download Table" at the bottom.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: admin_batch4_data-reports.md -->

## Expanding Storage Capacity

### Who this applies to

### When to use this
When the console's remaining storage is running low, the primary account can expand storage capacity from the Admin Console — ensuring whiteboard notes, courseware, and class files auto-saved during class continue to save normally.

### Overview
Available storage plans: 100GB/year and 1000GB/year. Supported payment methods: WeChat Pay, Alipay, PayPal, Stripe.

### Steps

## Storage Data Overview

### What is "Data Overview"?
"Data Overview" refers to storage usage across various data types in the ClassIn Admin Console — including school files, class monitoring/recording data, class files, course attachments, and more.

### Who this applies to
- The Admin Console primary account
- Sub-accounts with "Data Overview" access

### Overview
The Admin Console has a "Data Overview" section that lets you see the current storage status across all data types — such as school files, class monitoring/recordings, and class files — including how much storage capacity each occupies and the percentage of total capacity used, helping you better understand your storage usage.

### Related articles
- "Expanding Storage Capacity"
- "Adding Sub-accounts in the Admin Console"

### Steps
1. Log into the Admin Console.
2. Go to Data Overview in the left navigation.
