## Class Teaching Evaluation Settings

## I. Managing Grading Schemes

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
"Manage Grading Schemes" offers four default schemes: numeric score, percentage, rating (Excellent/Good/etc.), and letter grade (ABCD). The numeric score and percentage schemes cannot be deleted or edited. You can also create a custom "grading display scheme," where you can set its name, percentage, and grade levels. This grading scheme applies to recorded courses, assignments, check-ins, quizzes, answer sheets, discussions, AI Speaking Cards, and other teaching/learning activities that involve grading, helping teachers evaluate teaching and learning activities more precisely.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Find and enter the class.
3. Click the class name.
4. Go to Course Management.
5. Go to Manage Grading Schemes.
6. Set up a grading scheme.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fcb65eed67cd170bbf86c8fb6a557040149974625765515c7100bebc9b1957c98_434914?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=d4af83fe78bf16d41428807607fae13c555756f3)

**Phone**
1. Find and enter the class.
2. Tap ">" to the right of the class name.
3. Go to Manage Grading Schemes.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa9eee79b0aeaf0a26b31119822f00ac0cbe2d79ee6df5c35fb5a48cff1235f8c_295082?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ad8c930978d7cbaa697525b1e7f3c3293ed64b31)

## II. Managing Competency Models

In "Manage Competency Models," you can customize a competency model and set rubric levels and scores, so teachers can better complete phase-based teaching goals and accurately assess competency levels. Competency models are used in recorded courses, assignments, discussions, and AI Speaking Card teaching/learning activities that have a grading scheme set.

**Computer**
1. Click Home in the left navigation.
2. Click the class name in the top-left corner.
3. In class settings, go to Course Management.
4. Go to Manage Competency Models.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F06ec0b68d34c1ea25a9b16ef3bf44ad277e7783b370efd93e51911a3667c3952_435734?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=80b0072db5433d9a5ec5138a23c558803b1ed283)

**Phone/tablet**
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Find and enter the class on the Home page.
3. Tap ">" to the right of the class name.
4. Tap Course Management.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F61dbf27efb202ef0eb866a44febc4b4be16cb63f90f5959e290ba9953e6333be_294562?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=6eb40deb943f9bb54dca10f539e1134a62eb026b)

## III. Overall Grade Calculation Method

"Overall Grade Calculation Method" offers two ways to calculate a learning activity's overall grade: total score and weighted score. You can also set the grading display scheme for the overall grade in the current course, choosing from: numeric score, percentage, rating (Excellent/Good/etc.), letter grade (ABCD), or a custom grading scheme. You can also add grade categories, which are used in recorded courses, assignments, check-ins, quizzes, answer sheets, discussions, AI Speaking Cards, and other teaching/learning activities that involve grading. If the overall grade calculation method is set to weighted, the overall grade will be calculated based on the grade categories selected for each learning activity.

Go to Overall Grade Calculation Method.

## Class Settings

## I. Setting the Class Name and Cover

### Applies to
Head teachers.

### Usage Notes
After creating a class, the head teacher can change its name and cover image.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Find and enter the class.
3. Click the class name.
4. In Class Settings, click the class name again to change the class cover and name.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fac273d4be5c6e252a7840ee573249552812dd0f8211d11655cdf1a501f386640_772985?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=51348a86f482640fcc126582018a89614698fa06)

**Phone**
1. Find and enter the class.
2. Tap ">" to the right of the class name.
3. In Class Settings, tap ">" next to the class name again to change the class cover or name.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F185d1066f4517a00f397b6e6a94b71fe5b3e13054db75e0a59a64a01768c6856_260885?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=aa6656695958ad80e1ed13320e28a39a698cc132)

## II. Class Introduction and Class Note

### Applies to
Head teachers can set the class introduction.

Head teachers and teachers can set the class note.

### When to use this
The class introduction helps teachers and students get a fuller picture of the class's composition and characteristics, helping students, parents, and other interested parties evaluate and choose a class.

The class note is used by teachers to record core class attributes and basic management info, helping them quickly tell classes apart.

The head teacher can set a class introduction on an existing class, up to 400 characters.

Head teachers and teachers can set a class note, visible only to themselves, up to 32 characters.

In Class Settings, edit the Class Introduction or Class Note.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3813fd1515d4581766c4aaf1d03bc25fc257773f76a4866b03a0c2623eee8578_364879?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=7c871184e8b350aa33828a14585391cf8fc02705)

In Class Settings, edit the Class Introduction or Class Note.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F4f348fbfbffb743ae7a7c64d89b6a7ba0bc6a9ca5b449e525c786b181af11314_1360328?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b3ebd489fafaf78b794560ea25ec07313f808ab9)

## III. Class Header Image

### What is a class header image?
The class header image is the banner image at the top of the class group in the ClassIn app. It's mainly used to highlight the class theme, strengthen the class atmosphere, and improve visual impact.

The head teacher can change the header image on an existing class.

### Notes
Setting a class header image is not yet supported on phone.

Click Replace Image to change the class header image.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fecd1f7940babbbd03fd149f5f32ca8b21bc6c08e2d9c30367d3d8eed58f6e8d2_526797?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=9fa3b535f6eba01d9e7439e5470e1e627ce4eda4)

## IV. Open Class Enrollment

When teachers and students who aren't yet in a class want to sign up and join through self-service enrollment, the head teacher can enable "Open Class Enrollment." This is set in Class Management, and provides a convenient sign-up method — it lets you quickly bring more people into the class so they can start learning.

Once the head teacher enables "Open Class Enrollment," teachers in the class can share the class sign-up entry with teachers and students who need to join.

1. Go to Class Management.
2. Turn Open Class Enrollment on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F89c7e56f16f95abf81341949c2a4f6b94e6b4e6b86d4e7a8a3b2aa9b84f94137_326347?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c3e1496eded65fa7e47a1e42f2dbfdf68dca7ca2)

Turn Open Class Enrollment on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F56712ff783597669fb9d94f092aae789e0f91cbaba58c61dcaafe3ced769afc5_302013?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5a817e17051c77f33a36cfd5d30e731c260700f1)

## V. Showing the Class Sign-Up Entry on Shared Pages

If the head teacher wants to improve the class's ability to attract new members, they can enable "Show Join Class Entry on Shared Pages" in Class Management. Once enabled, shared class assignments, quizzes, web live stream/playback pages, and so on will show a "join this class" entry, making it easy for interested users to sign up on their own.

Once the head teacher enables "Show Class Sign-Up Entry on Shared Pages" in Class Management, shared class assignments, quizzes, web live stream/playback pages, and so on from class teachers will show that class's join entry.

Turn "Show join class entry on shared pages" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F80419527a51f9917ca562be59e2afaa0cc1be58aa661110d252e2ef47c9abaec_332028?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ad19a3108399bc0d27e779a9c97ae04522c16900)

Click Class Management, then turn "Show join class entry on shared pages" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F25b668885170368980853b53ddc53028074d043f982b1ba84d39892e238bcc6d_307796?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f48822aff0c1255d79fa20d0fd5ef9c31ce1e3d7)

## VI. Students Changing Their Class Nickname

When a class has a large number of students, to make it easier and more efficient for teachers to manage everyone's class nicknames, the head teacher can enable "Allow students to change their class nickname" in Class Management. Once enabled, students can change their own class nickname in the class settings screen to suit their preference.

The class nickname set will be shown in the class's lessons and activities.

Turn "Allow students to change class nickname" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F2da9033f2850da681977cf132d4161b4c822fe6f89803ef34eed225ae1641566_331809?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=61bba7a3c08e93dc4cfa7a1ea1420d2432e1bdee)

Turn "Allow students to change class nickname" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7a27e68c9de7632cec64792d438e5a9d23189445c6acee75bb5509657f08be68_307142?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cc86326c72258943bbef910976ca0802fd50ce0a)

## VII. Class Members Can Add Each Other as Friends

Controlling whether class members can add each other as friends is a way to manage social interaction within the class. The head teacher can enable or disable "Allow class members to add each other as friends" based on actual needs, to better manage interaction between class members. When enabled, class members can normally add each other as friends through the system; when disabled, class members cannot add each other as friends — this keeps class management running efficiently and avoids unnecessary social interaction disrupting normal teaching order.

Once "Class members can add each other as friends" is enabled, teachers and students, as well as students and other students, can all add each other as friends; once disabled, they cannot. The head teacher adding class members as friends is not restricted by this setting.

Turn "Class members can add each other as friends" on or off.

## VIII. Allow Teachers to Create Lessons

If you want every teacher in the class to have permission to create lessons, the head teacher needs to enable "Allow teachers to create lessons" in Class Management. Enabling this lets every teacher member in the class create new lessons on their own, and edit lessons they teach — making it easier to teach, manage the class, and distribute tasks, and improving teacher autonomy and professionalism.

Once "Allow teachers to create lessons" is enabled, teachers in the class can create lessons and edit lessons where they are the lead teacher or co-teacher.

### Related Articles
"Creating a Lesson"

2. Turn "Allow teachers to create lessons" on or off.

## IX. Allow Students Who Left the Class or Whose Class Was Dissolved to View Course Content

When this is enabled, in situations such as "a student was removed from the class by a teacher," "the class was dissolved," or "a student left the class voluntarily," students can still view lesson playbacks, whiteboard courseware, recorded course videos, and other activity attachments.

When this is disabled, in the same situations, students will no longer be able to view lesson playbacks, whiteboard courseware, recorded course videos, or other activity attachments.

This setting — "Allow Students Who Left the Class or Whose Class Was Dissolved to View Course Content" — can be turned on or off for all classes from the "Backend Management System."

Turn "Allow students who left the class or whose class was dissolved to view course content" on or off.

# 5. Class Teaching Activities (Part 1: WeChat Notifications, Learning Materials, Unit Topics, Discussion)

```yaml
title: "WeChat Official Account Notifications"
source_title_zh: "微信服务号通知"
```

## WeChat Official Account Notifications

## I. Linking a WeChat Official Account

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
Once a user links the ClassIn WeChat official account, they can receive class notifications and notifications about LMS learning activities in their class via WeChat, even without logging into the ClassIn app or enabling ClassIn app notifications — so they never miss anything important.

### Usage Notes
Once linked, ClassIn will send reminder messages to teachers and students via the WeChat official account before class starts. Specific timing:

**(1) Paid ClassIn class notifications:**
- Teachers: notified 20 minutes before class starts.
- Students: notified 10 minutes before class starts.

**(2) LMS activity notifications:**
- When a teacher publishes an LMS learning activity, or grades, sends a reminder for, or requests a correction on a student's already-submitted LMS learning activity, the student will receive a WeChat push notification.
- When a student submits an LMS learning activity, the teacher will receive a WeChat push notification.

Through these targeted notifications, ClassIn ensures every teacher and student gets timely updates on important class and learning activity information.

### Notes
For free-tier classrooms, teachers, co-teachers, students, and auditors are all notified 5 minutes before class.

The WeChat official account can send up to 1 million pushes per day; beyond that, further pushes are blocked.

Course or lesson names longer than 24 characters will also be blocked from notifications.

### Steps
1. In WeChat, tap the magnifying glass in the top-right corner.
2. Search for "ClassIn Official Account" and tap it in the results.
3. Go into the ClassIn official account.
4. Tap Follow.
5. Tap Link Account.
6. Tap Confirm Link.
7. Enter your phone number, email, or ClassIn account and password to link.
8. When a class or LMS activity reminder is due, it will show up in the WeChat official account.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb4a3cbcf1b5b14d75dd0f3cf2b491c56c1dd4e642b7b6903c31b13b284beecfb_1507329?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=9f159abae583c5ed9f0e84d3e01da991ca112b9b)

## II. Unlinking the Official Account

#### Applies to
#### Steps
1. Go to Home.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Go to Account & Security.
4. Go to Account Linking.
5. Turn off "Official Account Linking."

## Learning Materials

## I. What Are "Learning Materials"?

In teaching practice, teachers can upload preview or review materials to the Learning Materials section so students can preview before class or review afterward. This enriches teaching content, improves teaching outcomes, and gives students a more complete, organized set of learning resources.

## II. Creating "Learning Materials"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
After entering the class page, teachers can post learning materials under the course tab. Learning materials support several types of attachments: images, voice recordings, cloud drive files, local files, and website links. File limits: up to 15 image attachments, up to 15 recording attachments, up to 15 video attachments, and the combined total of local files, cloud drive files, and links cannot exceed 50; each video or file must be under 500MB. When uploading from a computer, you can drag and drop images and files directly into the learning material.

**(1) Settings available when creating "Learning Materials":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the start and due time for the learning material. |
| Publish to | Publish the learning material to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the learning material belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the learning material belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Allow students to download attachments | Once enabled, students can download the learning material's attachments. |
| Allow newly joined students to view | Once enabled, students who join the class before the learning material activity ends can also view it. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this learning material activity. |

### Notes
If "a student was removed from the class by a teacher," "the class was dissolved," or "a student left the class voluntarily," whether the departed student can still view file attachments in learning materials depends on the class setting for allowing students who left the class or whose class was dissolved to view course content.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home in the left navigation.
2. Create a new course, or open an existing one, in the top-left corner.
3. Click New.
4. Create Learning Material.

**Phone**

3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Create Learning Material (if not your first time creating one, tap "+" in the bottom-right corner).

## III. Editing "Learning Materials"

Learning materials can be edited, but which content can be edited depends on the material's status.

For drafts and materials that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; everything else can be edited.

For materials currently in progress, content can be edited, but "Start Time" and "Course" in the settings cannot be changed.

For materials that have ended, the content can no longer be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: time, publish to, teacher, course, allow newly joined students to view, and unlock conditions.

## Unit Topics

## I. What Is a "Unit Topic"?

In course design, we often organize teaching content around a central theme, forming a connected series of teaching activities that together span several class sessions — we call this a "unit." Note: "unit" here doesn't fully correspond to a "chapter" in a traditional textbook, and "topic" is not simply a textbook unit or chapter title either.

## II. Creating a "Unit Topic"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
A unit topic can include a variety of teaching/learning activities, such as class sessions, recorded courses, assignments, quizzes (exam papers), answer sheets, check-ins, discussions, learning materials, and AI Speaking Cards. Through this range of activities, students can gain a full, coherent understanding of related knowledge within a single topic framework.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Unit Topic.
6. Add the unit topic's title and description.
7. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb55c2f77ee579a53846ac75d777a8e7f89650fea693f78376db09fc4c4ce16bf_466138?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=77e913e8be15411b207c076310d97fe2aca422b3)

**Phone**
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Find and enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Create a Unit Topic (if not your first time, tap "+" in the bottom-right corner).

## VI. Sorting "Units and Activities"

Applies to everyone.

### When to use this
When a class has many unit topics or learning activities, teachers or students can switch sort order to more easily find what they need.

Course sorting supports "ascending order" and "descending order."

Ascending order sorts topics/activities by creation time, from oldest to newest.

Descending order sorts topics/activities by creation time, from newest to oldest.

Items that can be sorted: unit topics, class sessions, recorded courses, assignments, quizzes, answer sheets, discussions, learning materials, check-ins, AI Speaking Cards, and so on.

1. Open the filter panel.
2. Sort ascending or descending, or filter by activity type, teacher, or completion status.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3790419f28f840edd44bd2eff29d8661b051db6ec61f55da5e1d12d03ef19161_337069?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ddab8264af8c7ebb1dd73b8f3dd8f1c5ff2a322a)

Go to Filter, and sort teaching activities by order, activity type, involved person, and so on.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F30cc444b889e0850ebbeacc73230b087193722d43dd478fa76e7b9fd8586560b_927717?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=0329e8370f37138ca9fe375b3272c7a85491b52d)

## VII. Filtering Activities

There are three ways to filter learning activities, to suit different needs:

**Condition filtering:** filter by a specific condition — for example, a teacher can filter all teaching activities related to them; a student can filter all teaching activities under a specific teacher, or filter by not-yet-started, in-progress, or ended activities. Students can also use this to filter learning activities they still need to complete, or filter by "unit topic" or "competency," and so on. Combining multiple filter conditions lets you pinpoint exactly the learning activities you need.

**Type filtering:** filter by activity type — for example, class sessions (lessons, live sessions), recorded courses, assignments, check-ins, quizzes (exam papers), answer sheets, discussions, learning materials, AI Speaking Cards, and so on. This helps users quickly find a specific type of teaching/learning activity.

**Keyword search:** search for teaching/learning activities by entering a keyword, to quickly find relevant activities.

## VIII. Grades

Applies to head teachers, teachers, and official class students.

Every course within a class has a grades page. On the teacher side, it includes learning activities and competency models; clicking on an official student navigates to that student's course report. On the student side, clicking on grades navigates to your own course report, and switching units shows that unit's report.

When a teacher views the grades page on a phone, only the student's overall grade and progress are shown; clicking on a grade navigates to their course report, and switching units shows that unit's report.

**Learning Activities:** teachers can view the overall grades and participation of students across graded activities in the selected course, filterable by unit and activity type; on computer, the current page's content can be exported, and the overall grading scheme can be managed and changed in Evaluation Settings; clicking on a student navigates to that student's unit report — Learning Analytics.

**Competency Models:** teachers can view student competency model results for activities that use grading rubrics within the selected course, and can search by student and by competency model; on computer, the current page's content can be exported, and competency models can be managed in Evaluation Settings; clicking on a student navigates to that student's unit report — Competency Analysis.

## IX. Unit Reports

A unit report is a summary and evaluation of a student's learning at a given stage, made up of two main pages: Learning Analytics and Competency Analysis.

The Learning Analytics page includes a summary of unit activities (activity completion, class attendance, etc.), competency analysis, the learning process (completion status of every activity in the unit, with clicking through to activity details or activity reports), and teacher comments. The Competency Analysis page visually presents a competency map and list based on the selected competency model.

Both Learning Analytics and Competency Analysis can be shared: on computer/tablet, you can share to a ClassIn class/friend, copy the link, or share via WeChat QR code; on phone, you can additionally share to Moments, Weibo, or QQ.

1. Find the unit topic, click "···," then click Unit Report.
2. View the Learning Analytics page.
3. Click Competency Analysis to switch to the Competency Analysis page.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F212e613565b7824b4adbff9dac2f4ee2494578211db8de9a64b2d93306c6057e_807130?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5c625867dddad7eccbc3ff1eb802f8f2f5899ec4)

## X. Course Reports

Selecting all unit topics on the unit report's Learning Analytics page produces the course report — a comprehensive summary and visualization of learning in the selected course, made up of two main pages: Learning Analytics and Competency Analysis.

The Learning Analytics page includes a summary of activities in the course (activity completion, class attendance, etc.), competency analysis, unit data, unit grade trends, activity analysis (completion across different learning activity types in the class), and teacher comments. The Competency Analysis page visually presents a competency map and list based on the selected competency model.

1. Select all unit topics.
2. View the Course Report page.

## Discussion

## I. What Is "Discussion"?

"Discussion" refers to creating a discussion group within a class. In this group, all students and teachers in the class can freely ask questions, share opinions and views, explain concepts, or post their thoughts. This kind of discussion group creates an open, inclusive atmosphere that encourages students to think and express themselves actively, while also giving teachers an important window into students' thinking and learning needs. In addition, by exchanging ideas with classmates, students can share knowledge and experience with each other, promoting mutual learning. This kind of interaction and collaboration helps spark students' enthusiasm and motivation to learn, and helps build their critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

## II. "Discussion" vs. "Group Discussion" — What's the Difference?

ClassIn has two discussion features. One is the discussion feature outside the classroom, within a class — once created, any class teacher or student can take part. The other is inside the classroom, called "Group Discussion," which mainly splits students into several small groups to discuss within the classroom, and also lets the teacher join in on discussions across different groups.

## III. Creating a "Discussion"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
When creating a new discussion, teachers can type text and upload various attachments to the discussion content — images, recordings, cloud drive or local files, and links. File limits: up to 15 image attachments and 15 recording attachments; the combined total of local files, cloud drive files, and links cannot exceed 15; each file must be under 500MB.

When uploading discussion attachments from a computer, you can drag and drop images and files directly into the discussion.

**Settings available when creating a "Discussion":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the discussion's start and end time. |
| Grading | Set the discussion's grading scheme and points. |
| Publish to | Publish the discussion to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the discussion belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the discussion belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Allow students to see each other's grades | Once enabled, students can see each other's grades. |
| Allow newly joined students to participate | Once enabled, students who join the class before the discussion ends can also take part in the already-published discussion. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this discussion activity. |

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Discussion.
6. Add the discussion title.
7. Add the discussion content.
8. Configure the discussion's settings.
9. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

**Phone**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Create a Discussion (if not your first time, tap "+" in the bottom-right corner).
5. Add the discussion title and content.

## IV. Editing a "Discussion"

Discussions can be edited, but what can be edited depends on the discussion's status.

For drafts and discussions that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; everything else can be edited.

For discussions currently in progress, content can be edited, but "Start Time" and "Course" in the settings cannot be changed.

For discussions that have ended, content can no longer be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: time, publish to, teacher, course, allow newly joined students to participate, and unlock conditions.

1. Go to the course.
2. Find the discussion, click "···," then select Edit.

Discussion activities can be deleted whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended.

## VI. Ending a "Discussion"

Teachers can manually end a discussion any time before its due date, once published. After the discussion ends, students can no longer post replies, like, or delete comments — but teachers can still post replies, like, delete comments, mute students, and grade.

Discussion activities can be duplicated to the same class or other classes, whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended. Except for the start and due time, the duplicated discussion's content and settings default to match the original.

## VIII. Sharing a "Discussion"

Teachers can share in-progress or ended discussion activities to WeChat or other platforms, making it easier to prompt students to join in on time.

When a teacher shares a discussion from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares a discussion from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, or by copying a link.

When viewing a shared discussion on another platform, images, recordings, and videos can be viewed and played directly; other files require launching ClassIn to view within the class.

When a teacher shares a discussion that already has comments, the top-level comment currently shown under the "Hottest" tab will also appear in the shared view.

1. Enter the discussion.
2. Click the share button.
3. Select a sharing method.

## IX. Students Taking Part in a "Discussion"

Applies to students.

Students can view and take part in discussions from their to-dos or within the class.

The comment section has "Hottest" and "Newest" tabs. Within the comment section:

Students can like, post, and reply to (their own or others') comments; comments support typed text and uploaded images, recordings, and audio/video files. File limits: up to 9 image attachments and 9 recording attachments, with the combined total of audio/video files also capped at 9; each file must be under 500MB. On computer, students can drag and drop image files directly into a comment.

Students can tap "Show only my comments" or "Show only this person's comments" after their own or someone else's comment; they can delete their own replies or comments; on phone, they can also copy a comment.

If a student is muted by a teacher, attempting to post a reply will show a message that they are (or have been) muted; while muted, they cannot like, post, or reply to comments.

In the Students area, students can see their own comments, replies, likes received, and grade; on computer or tablet, they can also share their own discussion report. If the teacher has enabled "Allow students to see each other's grades," students can also see other classmates' discussion activity.

Once a discussion ends, students can no longer post replies, like, or delete comments.

Take part in the discussion.

## X. Teachers Taking Part in a "Discussion"

After finding an in-progress or ended discussion in their to-dos or within the class, teachers can enter it to view, participate, and grade.

Teachers can like, post, and reply to (their own or others') comments; comments support typed text and uploaded images, recordings, and audio/video files. File limits: up to 9 image attachments and 9 recording attachments, with the combined total of audio/video files also capped at 9; each file must be under 500MB. On computer, teachers can also drag and drop image files directly into a comment.

Teachers can tap "Show only my comments" or "Show only this person's comments" after their own or someone else's comment. A head teacher can delete anyone's comment; a class teacher can delete their own and students' comments (but not the head teacher's); on phone, comments can also be copied.

Teachers can mute students — once muted, a student trying to post a reply will see a message that they are (or have been) muted, and cannot like, post, or reply to comments while muted.

In the Students area, teachers can see each student's comments, replies, likes received, and grade; on computer or tablet, they can also share a specific student's discussion report; on computer, they can also download the discussion content.

If grading is enabled for the discussion, teachers can grade a student both after their comment in the discussion area and in the Students area.

# 5. Class Teaching Activities (Part 2: Answer Sheet, Recorded Courses, Check-Ins)

```yaml
title: "Answer Sheet"
source_title_zh: "答题卡"
```

## Answer Sheet

## I. What Is an "Answer Sheet"?

On the ClassIn platform, an "Answer Sheet" is an answering tool commonly used for exams. Compared to the complex question-entry process of a traditional "Quiz," an Answer Sheet doesn't require entering the question content — you just upload an image of the exam paper and add the corresponding answer options, which greatly reduces the effort of entering questions. Answer Sheets support multiple question types: single choice, multiple choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer. Both head teachers and teachers can create answer sheets, giving students a convenient way to answer.

## II. Creating an "Answer Sheet"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
After entering the class page, teachers can create an answer sheet under the course tab. There are limits on the number of attachments for the exam paper file and answer file — for example, up to 15 images, up to 15 audio recordings, and up to 15 local or cloud drive PDF/Word/audio files. Uploading from a computer supports drag and drop.

You can save the answer options you've added as an answer sheet template, and you can also select from previously saved templates.

Answer sheets support these question types: single choice, multiple choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer. Up to 200 questions' worth of answer options can be added. Bulk adding of questions is supported, as is adding structural notes.

On computer or tablet, teachers can have AI generate an answer sheet by analyzing an exam paper file — supported formats for AI analysis are image, PDF, and Word.

**Settings available when creating an "Answer Sheet":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the answer sheet's start and due time. |
| Time limit | Set a time limit for students to complete the answer sheet. |
| Grading | Set the answer sheet's grading scheme. |
| Publish to | Publish the answer sheet to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the answer sheet belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the answer sheet belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Manual grading for fill-in-the-blank | Once enabled, if a student's fill-in-the-blank answer doesn't exactly match the correct answer, it's automatically routed for manual grading. |
| Allow students to see each other's content and grades | Sets whether students can view each other's content and grades — and whether this applies once the answer sheet is submitted, once it's graded, or once it has ended. |
| Publish answers and explanations | Sets whether answers and explanations are made public — and whether this applies once the answer sheet is submitted, once it's graded, or once it has ended. |
| Allow late submission after the activity ends | Once enabled, if a student didn't complete the answer sheet on time, they can submit it after the activity has ended. |
| Allow newly joined students to submit | Once enabled, students who join the class before the answer sheet activity ends can also take part in the already-published answer sheet. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this answer sheet activity. |

### Notes
Creating an answer sheet is not currently supported on phone.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Answer Sheet.
6. Add the answer sheet title.
7. Add the exam paper and answer files.
8. Configure the answer sheet.
9. Configure the answer sheet's settings.
10. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Facc35221e9d12efb854dbc6fd0f20127b18ef80227205490414d2bdfdb2a6db6_916305?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ec08293792933a7626041d89da3e1ff1d771f970)

## III. Editing an "Answer Sheet"

For drafts and answer sheets that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; everything else can be edited.

For answer sheets currently in progress, question types and options cannot be added or removed; "Start Time," "Time Limit," and "Course" in the settings also cannot be changed.

For answer sheets that have ended, question types and options cannot be added or removed; the following settings also cannot be changed: time, time limit, publish to, teacher, course, manual grading for fill-in-the-blank, allow newly joined students to submit, and unlock conditions.

For drafts, in-progress, and ended answer sheets, saving as a template and editing the answer set in the options are both still supported.

Editing an answer sheet is not currently supported on phone.

1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Go to the course.
4. Find the answer sheet, click "···," then select Edit.

Answer sheet activities can be deleted whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended.

Once deleted, an answer sheet activity cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

## VI. Duplicating an "Answer Sheet"

Answer sheet activities can be duplicated to the same class or other classes, whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended. Except for the start and due time, the duplicated answer sheet's content and settings default to match the original.

## VII. Sharing an "Answer Sheet"

### When to use this
Teachers can share an assigned answer sheet to WeChat or other platforms even when a student hasn't logged into ClassIn or hasn't enabled ClassIn notifications, making it easier for teachers to prompt students to study on time.

When a teacher shares an answer sheet from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares an answer sheet from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, or by copying a link.

Viewing a shared answer sheet outside the ClassIn app only shows things like the exam paper's structure — not the actual question content. To answer the questions, the student still needs to launch ClassIn and join the class.

1. Click the share button in the top-right corner.
2. Select a sharing method.

## VIII. Students Using an "Answer Sheet"

**Finding the answer sheet:** find the teacher-assigned answer sheet under the course tab within the class.

**Entering the answering screen:** tap the "Start Answering" button to the right of the answer sheet, and you'll enter the answering screen. On the left is the exam paper file view, which can be collapsed or expanded; it supports switching between file pages/images, zooming in/out and resetting the image, and playing recorded audio from the bottom-left corner. On the right is the answer sheet view, showing the number of questions and total points. The remaining time to answer also appears in the bottom-left corner — important information for pacing your answers.

**Answering process:** you can now begin answering. Based on the exam paper, select the correct answer or fill in your answer for each question in the interface. Once you complete a question, the system automatically marks it as answered in the question list on the right (on tablet it appears on the left; on phone, in the top-right corner), helping you track answered and unanswered questions. You can also tap questions in the list to quickly jump to them.

**Submitting the answer sheet:** once you've finished, tap the "Submit" button in the bottom-right corner. This means you've finished answering, and the exam paper will be automatically collected.

Once a student submits an answer sheet, they can no longer edit their answers — so please double-check your answers before submitting.

For a time-limited answer sheet, the timer keeps running even if you exit partway through; once time runs out, the system automatically submits it.

1. Go to To-Dos.
2. Go to Pending.
3. Find the answer sheet, then tap Go Answer.

## IX. Grading an "Answer Sheet"

"Grading an answer sheet" refers to the process of a teacher evaluating and scoring a student's submitted answers. When grading, the teacher works through the student's answers based on the exam paper and answer key, taking into account the student's understanding, problem-solving ability, accuracy and completeness, expression, and reasoning, in order to assign an appropriate score or rating.

Once a student submits an answer sheet, the teacher can find the corresponding answer sheet under the course tab within the class page, and click the "Go Grade" button on the right. This takes the teacher into the "Pending Grading" section, where they can judge each question one by one. Single choice, multiple choice, and true/false questions are graded automatically by the system based on the answer set in the answer sheet, and the automated result cannot be edited during grading (if a particular option's answer was set incorrectly, the teacher should fix the answer sheet's answer set instead). Fill-in-the-blank and short-answer questions support manual grading, and besides right/wrong, "partially correct" is also supported. In addition, the question list on the right also supports tapping to jump directly to a question.

Once grading is complete, teachers can click "Done" or "Save & Grade Next" to finish the current student's grading, or continue on to the next student. If "Save & Grade Next" is selected, the system automatically jumps to the next student's answer sheet.

Teachers can re-grade a student's submitted answer sheet multiple times; no history of intermediate grading is kept — only the final record applies.

Use search or filters to find what you need.

1. Find the answer sheet, then click Go Grade.

Go to Pending Grading, then tap Grade.

## X. Viewing/Downloading "Answer Sheet" Data

## When to use this
In ClassIn, teachers can directly view or download answer sheet data, using it to analyze and evaluate student learning, and to deliver personalized teaching and targeted feedback.

When viewing answer sheet data statistics, you can view them question by question, and filter by question type. Clicking on a specific question shows the correct answer, that question's accuracy rate and the overall accuracy rate, how many students chose each option, and the percentage for each option.

When exporting a student's detailed answer sheet data from a computer, the data is saved locally as an Excel file. The spreadsheet includes, per student: class nickname, whether the answer sheet was submitted, whether the student submitted late, submission time, time spent answering, whether the answer sheet has been graded, score, accuracy rate, number of correct answers, number of incorrect answers, number of partially correct answers, number of unanswered questions, the score for each question, and the selected answer for each question. Additional information is also included: class ID, class name, answer sheet title, number of questions, full score, and grader.

Phone and tablet can only view the data statistics, not export a student's detailed answer sheet data.

View the Data Statistics, or click Export.

## Recorded Courses

## I. What Are "Recorded Courses"?

The "Recorded Course" feature lets teachers pre-record teaching videos and upload them to the "Recorded Courses" module under "Learning Activities," for students to watch anytime. This format isn't limited by where or on what device students watch, and is typically used for pre-class preview, post-class review, and asynchronous (non-real-time) course delivery.

## II. "Recorded Course" vs. "Recorded Class Playback Video" — What's the Difference?

On the ClassIn platform, "Recorded Course" and "Recorded Class Playback Video" are two different features.

"Recorded Class Playback Video" refers to when a teacher uses ClassIn's "Cloud Recording" feature during a live lesson in the classroom, automatically saving the teacher's-eye-view recording of the class as a "playback video" that can be watched afterward in the "Schedule."

"Recorded Course," by contrast, refers to teaching videos a teacher records ahead of time and uploads to the "Recorded Courses" module under "Learning Activities." These videos can be watched by students anytime, and are suited to pre-class preview, post-class review, and non-real-time course delivery. This format is not limited by where or on what device students watch.

## III. Creating a "Recorded Course"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
Supported video formats for recorded courses: mp4, 3gp, mpg, mpeg, 3g2, avi, flv, wmv, h264, m4v, mj2, mov, ogg, ogv, rm, qt, vob, webm.

Up to 15 video files can be uploaded per recorded course, each up to 2GB.

When uploading recorded course videos from a computer, you can drag and drop videos directly into the recorded course content.

**Settings available when creating a "Recorded Course":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the recorded course's start and due time. |
| AI recorded course summary | Optionally have an AI agent produce an intelligent summary of the recorded course content, including chapter summaries and a subtitle list. |
| Grading | Set the recorded course's grading scheme and points. |
| Publish to | Publish the recorded course to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the recorded course belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the recorded course belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Allow variable playback speed | Once enabled, students can watch at a variable speed the first time they play the video. |
| Allow dragging the progress bar | Once enabled, students can drag the progress bar the first time they play the video. |
| Allowed number of views | Set the maximum number of times the recorded course video can be watched; each viewing must cover at least 75% of the video's duration to count. Once the maximum is reached, the video can no longer be watched. The maximum settable value is 20 views, or you can set it to unlimited. |
| Allow watching after the activity ends | Once enabled, students can still watch the videos in this "Recorded Course" activity after it has ended. |
| Discussion area | Once enabled, discussions can be precisely anchored to a point in the video's timeline. Once disabled, neither teachers nor students will see a discussion area. |
| Scrolling watermark and anti-recording | Once enabled, the viewer's nickname and phone number move randomly around the video area, and screen recording is blocked while watching. Mobile devices also cannot mirror to another device. This effectively protects the copyright and security of teaching resources. |
| Allow newly joined students to watch | Once enabled, students who join the class before the "Recorded Course" activity ends can also watch the videos in the already-created recorded course. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this "Recorded Course" activity. |

### Notes
How long a recorded course video can be watched depends on the due date, allowed number of views, and whether watching after the activity ends is allowed, all as set by the teacher. In addition, if "a student was removed from the class by a teacher," "the class was dissolved," or "a student left the class voluntarily," whether the departed student can still view the recorded course video depends on the class setting for allowing students who left the class or whose class was dissolved to view course content.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Recorded Course.
6. Add the recorded course title.
7. Add the recorded course content.
8. Configure the recorded course's settings.
9. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F55ded090318f59bfd3f0cf2452db7978fac18565d0a6c908219c0562f96cf5d6_691897?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=8bca4fda2654842db07cac241869f18a5134ab7f)

**Phone**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a Recorded Course (if not your first time, tap "+" in the bottom-right corner).
4. Add the recorded course title and content.
5. Publish, or save as a draft.

For recorded courses currently in progress, content can be edited, but "Start Time" and "Course" in the settings cannot be changed.

For recorded courses that have ended, content can no longer be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: time, publish to, teacher, course, allow newly joined students to watch, and unlock conditions.

## VIII. Sharing a "Recorded Course"

Teachers can share in-progress or ended recorded course activities to WeChat or other platforms, making it easier to prompt students to watch on time.

When a teacher shares a recorded course from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares a recorded course from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, and can also copy the link to share with others.

Watching the video content of a recorded course is not supported outside the ClassIn app; to watch, we recommend launching ClassIn to join the class.

## IX. Viewing "Recorded Course" Data

For a recorded course, teachers can view or export students' recorded course data to better understand how students are learning. For the recorded course as a whole, this includes: student participation rate, video completion rate, average watch duration, and average watch progress.

Per-student recorded course viewing data includes: watch duration, watch progress, number of discussions posted, number of replies posted, likes received, and grade. On computer, teachers can also export data on students' participation in the recorded course; the exported data also includes number of views and viewing status, in addition to the above.

In addition, teachers can view the discussion area's content; on computer, teachers can export detailed discussion data, which includes: number of discussions, video timestamp, poster, comment content, and comment time.

Phone and tablet can only view students' recorded course data and discussion area content, without export support.

## X. Students Using a "Recorded Course"

## Applies to
Students.

## Usage Notes
Once a teacher publishes a recorded course activity, students can see the activity's details: title, teacher, start and due time, and number of allowed views (depending on how the teacher configured the recorded course's parameters).

While watching a recorded course video, students can pause/resume, switch to another video, adjust volume, watch at variable speed (depending on the teacher's settings), drag the progress bar (depending on the teacher's settings), and go full screen. If the teacher has enabled the discussion area, students can join discussions anchored to a specific timestamp; discussions support adding text and images. Each video also has its own discussion area, where students can interact, reply to and like others' discussions, and delete their own posted discussions.

Students can see their own recorded course learning data — watch progress, cumulative watch duration, comment/reply likes received, and grade. Clicking View Details also shows detailed video-viewing breakdown, and supports sharing personal viewing data.

## Notes
With the scrolling watermark and anti-recording feature enabled, while watching the recorded course video, students will see their own nickname and phone number moving randomly around the video area, and won't be able to screen-record or mirror it while watching.

## Steps
1. Open a created course.
2. Find the recorded course, then tap Go Watch.

## Check-Ins

## I. What Are "Check-Ins"?

"Check-Ins" in ClassIn are a tool for tracking completion of recurring learning tasks. Teachers often assign tasks that need to be completed repeatedly — for example, memorizing 100 English words each day. Teachers can create a check-in task in ClassIn, describe the requirements in detail, and publish it to students. After completing the task, students can log their check-in with a photo, video, or audio recording. This check-in mechanism mainly helps teachers understand how well students are mastering the material, and decide whether more focused teaching is needed in certain areas. Teachers can adjust their teaching content and methods based on check-in results, to better support student needs. Check-ins also help boost student motivation and task completion efficiency.

## II. Creating a "Check-In"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
After entering the class page, teachers can assign check-ins under the course tab. A "Check-In" task supports several types of attachments — images, voice recordings, cloud drive files, local files, and website links — to help students better understand and complete the check-in content the teacher described. File limits: up to 15 image attachments, up to 15 recording attachments, up to 15 video attachments, and the combined total of local files, cloud drive files, and links cannot exceed 15; each video or file must be under 500MB. When uploading check-in attachments from a computer, you can drag and drop images and files directly into the check-in content.

**Settings available when creating a "Check-In":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Check-in period | Set the check-in's start and end time, frequency, and daily reminder time. |
| Grading | Set the check-in's grading scheme and points. |
| Publish to | Publish the check-in to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the check-in belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the check-in belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Allow makeup check-ins | Once enabled, you can set a time limit — up to 30 days — during which students can complete a makeup check-in after missing one. |
| Allow students to see each other's content and grades | Once enabled, students can view each other's check-in content and grades. |
| Allow newly joined students to submit | Once enabled, students who join the class before the check-in activity ends can also take part in the already-assigned check-in. |

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Check-In.

**Phone**

## III. Editing a "Check-In"

Check-ins can be edited, but what can be edited depends on the check-in's status.

For drafts and check-ins that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; everything else can be edited.

For check-ins currently in progress, content can be edited, but "Start Time" and "Course" in the settings cannot be changed.

For check-ins that have ended, content can no longer be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: check-in period, check-in reminders, publish to, teacher, course, and allow newly joined students to submit.

1. Go to the course.
2. Find the check-in, click "···," then select Edit.

Check-in activities can be deleted whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended.

### Notes
Once a check-in activity is deleted, all its file attachments are also deleted and cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

1. Find the check-in, click "···," then select Delete.

Teachers can manually end a check-in any time before its due date, once published. If "Allow makeup check-ins" was not enabled in the settings, once the check-in ends, students will no longer be able to submit a check-in.

## VI. Duplicating a "Check-In"

Check-in activities can be duplicated to the same class or other classes, whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended. Except for the start and due time, the duplicated check-in's content and settings default to match the original.

## VII. Sharing a "Check-In"

Teachers can share in-progress or ended check-in activities to WeChat or other platforms, making it easier to prompt students to take part on time.

When a teacher shares a check-in from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares a check-in from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, or by copying a link.

When viewing a shared check-in on another platform, images, recordings, and videos can be viewed and played directly; other files require launching ClassIn to join the class and view the teacher's assigned check-in content.

1. Click Share.
2. Select a sharing method.

## VIII. Reminding Students to "Check In"

After a teacher opens the check-in page, they can see under the "Not Submitted" or "Sent Back" tabs which students haven't submitted a check-in, and can remind all students who haven't submitted.

The "Notify" reminder is a ClassIn app push notification, sent at 15-minute intervals.

"Copy Roster" copies a text-and-link list for manual reminding.

## IX. Students Submitting a "Check-In"

Once a teacher publishes a check-in, students can find and view it, and submit, from the ClassIn class or their to-dos.

On the check-in page, after a student selects the check-in date, they can see the remaining time to check in that day, or the makeup check-in deadline. After tapping "Check In Now" or "Makeup Check-In," students fill in the check-in content, which supports uploaded attachments — images, recordings, videos, files from their personal cloud drive, local files, and links. File limits: up to 15 image attachments, up to 15 recording attachments, up to 15 video attachments, and the combined total of local files, cloud drive files, and links cannot exceed 15; each video or file must be under 500MB. When uploading check-in attachments from a computer, you can drag and drop images and files directly into the check-in content.

After filling in the check-in content, students can tap Submit Check-In.

Once a student submits a check-in, if the teacher hasn't yet commented on it, the student can still edit or delete the submitted content. If the teacher requests a revision when commenting, they can mark the student's check-in as "Sent Back for Revision" — the student can then revise and resubmit; a revised check-in that hasn't yet been commented on can still be edited by the student, but can no longer be deleted.

1. Open a created course.
2. Go to the check-in page.
3. Select a check-in date, then tap Check In or Makeup Check-In.
4. After filling in the check-in content, tap Submit Check-In.

## X. Teachers Commenting on "Check-Ins"

Once a student submits a check-in, teachers can find it in the class or their to-dos to review and comment.

On the check-in page, after selecting a check-in date, teachers can review and comment on a student's check-in content under "Pending"; comments support text and voice recordings. If a student's check-in content is exceptional, the teacher can mark it as an "Excellent Check-In," and can also assign a grade if grading is enabled for the check-in.

Once teachers finish commenting, they can click Submit Comment. If a student needs to revise and resubmit, teachers can check "Send Back for Revision."

Teachers can also edit their own comments on a student under the "Graded" tab.

1. Go to Pending, review a student's check-in content, then click Comment.
2. Once commenting is complete, click Submit Comment, or set Send Back for Revision.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F9d285b124138dcdaa35e0952fa54a17c7dd00b45132be2f3b468b65749d72218_628418?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=fc178106792ab80d4a9610aa089325f8e8725014)

## XI. Students Using "Check-Ins"

Applies to students.

Students can view and submit check-ins from their to-dos or within the class. Entering the check-in page shows the check-in leaderboard, a calendar, check-in details, "My Check-Ins," and check-in activity feed.

On the leaderboard, students can see their own number of check-in days and check-in rate, as well as the class's ranking by check-in rate; they can also share their ranking as an image.

On the check-in calendar, students can tap to switch between dates, viewing that day's check-in content, or completing a check-in or makeup check-in; a grey or green checkmark is shown under each date to indicate whether the check-in was completed.

Under check-in details, students can see the teacher's assigned check-in content and details like the activity's start and due time.

Under "My Check-Ins," students can see their number of check-in days, current streak, number of "Excellent Check-In" awards, and likes received; they can also see each day's check-in content, the teacher's comment, score, and likes; students can like, share (either that day's check-in or their overall check-in record), edit, or delete their own check-ins (a submitted check-in that hasn't yet been commented on can be edited or deleted; once revised, it can still be edited but not deleted before the teacher comments). Students can also check in or complete a makeup check-in directly from "My Check-Ins."

If the check-in allows students to see each other's content and grades, once a student selects a date, in addition to seeing their own check-in for that day, they can also see other classmates' check-in content, score, and likes in the activity feed, and like them.

Once the check-in ends, students can no longer edit or delete their own check-in content.

1. View the check-in Leaderboard.
2. View "My Check-Ins" — submit, complete a makeup check-in, like, share, edit, or delete your own check-ins.
3. Select a date to see classmates' check-ins with likes.

## XII. Teachers Using "Check-Ins"

After finding an in-progress or ended check-in in their to-dos or within the class, teachers can enter to review students' check-ins and comment. Entering the check-in page shows a leaderboard, calendar, check-in details, and students' check-in records.

On the leaderboard, teachers can see overall check-in progress, and each student's number of check-in days, check-in rate, and ranking; the ranking can also be shared. On computer, teachers can download students' check-in analysis data locally; on tablet, they can save it to their cloud drive or send it to a ClassIn class/friend. The data includes each student's check-in score, number of check-in days, number of makeup check-ins, longest check-in streak, likes received, and number of "Excellent Check-In" awards.

On the calendar, teachers can tap to switch between dates and see that day's check-in progress; each date shows the completion rate — if a date is fully surrounded by a green ring, all students submitted a check-in that day; a red dot under a date indicates that day's check-ins need teacher review.

Under check-in details, teachers can see the check-in content they assigned, along with the activity's start and due time.

Teachers can remind students or review and comment on check-ins under the "Not Submitted," "Pending," "Sent Back," and "Graded" tabs. For a submitted check-in, teachers can like, comment on, share (either that check-in or the student's overall check-in record), and delete the content, and can see the number of likes it has received. Clicking a student's nickname followed by their streak count takes the teacher to that student's check-in record; teachers can also access a student's check-in record by clicking their check-in rate or number of check-in days in the leaderboard. A student's check-in record shows their number of check-in days, current streak, number of "Excellent Check-In" awards, and likes received; teachers can see each submission's content, their own comment, score, and likes received, and can like, share (either that check-in or the overall record), or delete a student's check-in content.

1. Select a date to view, like, comment on, share, or delete a student's check-in.
2. View a student's check-in record.

# 5. Class Teaching Activities (Part 3: Quiz)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Quiz"
source_title_zh: "测验"
```

## Quiz

## I. What Is a "Quiz"?

The "Quiz" feature in ClassIn is essentially an "exam paper," designed to assess a student's mastery of knowledge and skills in a specific subject or field. Exams are not just an important way to check learning outcomes — they also help schools and educational institutions evaluate teaching quality and how effective their curriculum design is. In addition, quizzes help students self-check their own learning progress and weak points. By taking a quiz, students can see how well they've mastered each subject and quickly spot gaps. This helps students focus their study, improve efficiency, and close knowledge gaps quickly.

## II. Creating a "Quiz"

## 1. Creating a Quiz Activity

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
On the question-adding screen within the quiz:

Teachers can add questions or exam papers from the "ClassIn Question Bank" under "Select from Question Bank," and can filter questions and papers by keyword or condition.

If a teacher has previously entered their own questions, they can pull from previously entered questions and papers under "My Question Bank."

If the school has granted the teacher access to question/paper resources, the teacher can pull from those authorized resources under "Organization Question Bank."

Add the needed questions and papers to the question basket; questions already added to the basket can be removed there, and adding them to the current paper completes question selection.

Teachers can also manually add a single question, or add questions in bulk, via "Add/Bulk Add Questions." Because bulk-added questions must follow a specific format for ClassIn to recognize them, teachers should first download the template, add questions following the template and entry instructions, save the completed questions, and then upload them.

On computer or tablet, teachers can have an AI agent generate questions based on a teaching objective or specific knowledge point.

Added questions support setting points, moving position, deleting, editing, duplicating, and other actions. Preview is supported, letting teachers see how the paper will look to students on computer and phone. Saving the paper as a resource to "My Question Bank" is also supported, and on computer, teachers can also download the paper locally.

**Settings available when creating a "Quiz":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the quiz's start and due time. |
| Time limit | Set a time limit for students to complete the quiz. |
| Grading | Set the quiz's grading scheme. |
| Publish to | Publish the quiz to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the quiz belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the quiz belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Manual grading for fill-in-the-blank | Once enabled, if a student's fill-in-the-blank answer doesn't exactly match the correct answer, it's automatically routed for manual grading. |
| Allow late submission after the activity ends | Once enabled, if a student didn't complete the quiz on time, they can submit it after the activity has ended. |
| Allow students to see each other's content and grades | Sets whether students can view each other's content and grades — and whether this applies once the quiz is submitted, once it's graded, or once it has ended. |
| Publish answers and explanations | Sets whether answers and explanations are made public — and whether this applies once the quiz is submitted, once it's graded, or once it has ended. |
| Allow newly joined students to submit | Once enabled, students who join the class before the quiz activity ends can also take part in the already-published quiz. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this quiz activity. |

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Quiz.
6. Add the quiz title.
7. Add questions.
8. Configure the questions.
9. Configure the quiz's settings.
10. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

**Phone**
1. Create a Quiz (if not your first time, tap "+" in the bottom-right corner).
2. Preview the paper.
3. Once the paper is complete, tap Next.

## 2. Bulk Adding Questions

### When to use this
When a teacher needs to import a large number of questions into ClassIn at once, they can use the "Bulk Add Questions" feature.

Under Bulk Add Questions → Upload Questions, you can directly copy and paste questions from a local Word or Excel document that follows the entry format into the "Bulk Add Questions" window. You can also drag and drop a local Word or Excel document that matches the template directly into the window.

Under Bulk Add Questions → Edit Questions, you can edit or delete questions, and also save them to "My Question Bank."

#### (1) Single Choice Question Format

**Question number format:**
- Must be an Arabic numeral.
- Must be followed by punctuation or a space, e.g. "1." or "1、" or "1 ".

**Question stem format:**
- Can include text and images; text up to 15,000 characters.

**Options area format:**
- Option labels must be uppercase letters.
- Each option must be followed by punctuation or a space, e.g. "A." or "A、" or "A ".
- Number of options: 2–26, labeled A–Z in order.
- Option content can include text and images; text up to 200 characters.

**Answer area format:**
- Must follow the required format, e.g. "Answer: A."

**Explanation area format (optional):**
- Must follow the required format, e.g. "Explanation: Why the answer is A."
- Explanation content can include text and images; text up to 15,000 characters.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8760844d3fb88bf4085e0d2abdadfbce7cae62f9af5affadd899ac3252bad330_188752?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=293d086c89a6cb0836a662285deb1742c0b4a0f3)

#### (2) Multiple Choice Question Format

Multiple choice question number format, stem format, and options area format all follow the same rules as single choice questions.

**Answer area format:**
- Must follow the required format, e.g. "Answer: A."
- The system only auto-detects a question as multiple choice if multiple answer options are set.

**Explanation area format (optional):** same as single choice.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff406a3f60ae320d5a00bf770fafd8bcdf906708ac65747b123171c1a16b0fc1d_205667?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=7d51c26ba59887834c57f0055841e1282d82fac5)

#### (3) True/False Question Format

**Question number format:**
- Must be an Arabic numeral.
- Must be followed by punctuation or a space, e.g. "1." or "1、" or "1 ".

**True/false answer area:**
- Must follow the required format, e.g. "Answer: A."
- The answer must be one of: 正确/错误 (Correct/Incorrect) or T/F, where 正确/T means correct and 错误/F means incorrect.

**Explanation area (optional).**

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F405d87c659f66ef2a41b2b847452d766968f578a2340d8cadb4fd5dda36b02d2_172141?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=8faa6e6b7e36082c521070721a585f259e15a5e5)

#### (4) Fill-in-the-Blank Question Format

**Question number format** and **stem format:**
- Each blank must be at least three underscores long.
- With multiple blanks, the number of blanks must match the number of answers; number of blanks can be 1–40.

**Fill-in-the-blank answer area:**
- If there are multiple answers, separate them with "|".
- Answer text is up to 500 characters.

**Explanation area (optional).**

Note: press Shift and the "-" key to the right of "0" on the main keyboard row to type an underscore "_" (must be in English input mode).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fe9ae427375bee37dd665dccd953b8ff47b17aeef46aa2ba1997d9801f6402dd0_184557?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=9638f3650b0bcdca23ddde13b1b8beb12fc673d1)

#### (5) Short Answer Question Format

**Question number format:**
- Must use an Arabic numeral.

**Answer area (optional):**
- The system automatically identifies it as a short-answer question, which requires manual grading.
- The answer can include text and images; text up to 15,000 characters.

**Explanation area (optional).**

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F27e81f6343a4c16fb89e5cb700a6d648523d0891b48b5e3da435fb6bbc65794a_167524?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=895b2524c26291cd837a8fc70213d75340769dd1)

#### (6) Composite Question Format

**Question number format** and **stem format** for the composite question itself.

**Sub-question number format:**
- Must use an Arabic numeral in parentheses, e.g. "(1)", "(2)", "(3)".
- Number of sub-questions: 1–50.

**Sub-question format:**
- Follows the format requirements for the relevant question type above: single choice, multiple choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, or short answer.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fd8527ba64d4508e35bc79b72bc4a9bc578fbaa772c90493c60fa0f288c3041e9_270278?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f567defe6ba488ead9abbf81904b22db9adaeb1d)
