## III. Editing a "Quiz"

Once a quiz is published, its questions and title can no longer be edited.

For drafts and quizzes that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; everything else can be edited.

For quizzes currently in progress, the quiz content cannot be edited, and "Start Time," "Time Limit," "Course," and "Manual grading for fill-in-the-blank" in the settings also cannot be changed.

For quizzes that have ended, the quiz content cannot be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: time, time limit, publish to, teacher, course, manual grading for fill-in-the-blank, allow newly joined students to submit, and unlock conditions.

For drafts, in-progress, and ended quizzes, saving the paper as a resource to "My Question Bank" is still supported.

1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Go to the course.
4. Find the quiz, click "···," then select Edit.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F1133c454c2e73e895d375322e7f7f6f1f775f807289f41bdaf2ccc3da73004ee_360104?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ae8c85f04e57a0a69379e40cc019eda7f51a9ce2)

## VII. Sharing a "Quiz"

Teachers can share an assigned quiz to WeChat or other platforms even when a student hasn't logged into ClassIn or hasn't enabled ClassIn notifications, making it easier for teachers to prompt students to study on time.

When a teacher shares a quiz from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares a quiz from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, or by copying a link.

Viewing a shared quiz outside the ClassIn app only shows things like the exam paper's structure — not the actual question content. To answer the questions, the student still needs to launch ClassIn and join the class.

1. Enter the quiz.
2. Click the Share button, then select a sharing method.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fde7e7dabaa949ae0b1aad58e0c0736942ea066a6b58d305616cb1d6bd40a0caf_307114?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4e46f4fb7704a7c55456df6aaced058d4767723b)

## VIII. Students Taking a "Quiz"

**Finding the quiz:** find the teacher-assigned quiz under the course tab within the class.

**Entering the answering screen:** tap the "Start Answering" button to the right of the quiz, and you'll enter the answering screen. At the top, you can see the number of questions and total points. The remaining time to answer also appears in the bottom-left corner — important information for pacing your answers.

**Answering process:** you can now begin answering. Based on the question, select the correct answer or fill in your answer. Once you complete a question, the system automatically marks it as answered on the answer card to the right, helping you track answered and unanswered questions; you can also tap questions on the answer card to quickly jump to them.

**Submitting the quiz:** once you've finished, tap the "Submit Quiz" button in the bottom-right corner. This means you've finished answering, and the paper will be automatically collected.

Once a student submits a quiz, they can no longer edit their answers — so please double-check your answers before submitting.

For a time-limited quiz, the timer keeps running even if you exit partway through; once time runs out, the system automatically submits it.

1. Go to To-Dos.
2. Go to Pending.
3. Find the quiz by search or filter.
4. Tap Go Answer, then tap Start Answering.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F6db5681f2dcb304bbd6d21262e9a58d28bafc6726c80927bd837973b3106b6c7_274858?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c0396d6ec4fc39dfcbc98581d0d7cbc31be0d5f9)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fad9d68daf22d98be3131315043a72b8e5b39a131b75f0ce4fcce5cdb9e67299c_523292?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=92cbe8ca7fb68fe475b7437ac9ca17a57419261c)

## IX. Grading a "Quiz"

"Grading a quiz" refers to the process of a teacher evaluating and scoring a student's answers. If a student actually took the quiz offline, teachers can still grade it. When grading, the teacher works through the student's answers based on the quiz's question requirements and standard answers, taking into account the student's understanding, problem-solving ability, accuracy and completeness, expression, and reasoning, in order to assign an appropriate score or rating.

Once a student submits a quiz, the teacher can find the corresponding quiz under the course tab within the class page, and click the "Go Grade" button on the right. This takes the teacher into the "Pending Grading" section, where they can judge each question one by one. Besides right/wrong, multiple choice and short-answer questions also support "partially correct." Teachers can make manual judgments on top of the automatic grading, based on the student's answers and the question's answer key; even for objective question types (true/false, single/multiple choice) that were automatically graded by the system, teachers can still edit the grading result. The answer card on the right also supports tapping to jump directly to a question.

Once grading is complete, teachers can click "Done" or "Save & Grade Next" to finish the current student's grading, or continue on to the next student. If "Save & Grade Next" is selected, the system automatically jumps to the next student's answer sheet.

Teachers can re-grade a student's submitted quiz multiple times; no history of intermediate grading is kept — only the final record applies.

Use search or filters to find what you need.

1. Find the quiz, then click Go Grade.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F44f1e5cf88749e20258175bf76a0171fbde5ad9257ee2e6ebdc3f3fef98514a1_328028?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=416925c8223cb67be98c67642729dde559caaade)

## X. Viewing/Downloading "Quiz Data"

Teachers can download quiz data from the Backend Management System. In addition, teachers can directly view or download quiz data within the app itself. Teachers can use this data to analyze and evaluate student learning, and to deliver personalized teaching and targeted feedback.

When viewing quiz data, you can view it question by question, and filter by question type. Clicking on a specific question shows the correct answer, that question's accuracy rate and the overall accuracy rate, how many students chose each option, and the percentage for each option.

When exporting a student's detailed quiz data from a computer, the data is saved locally as an Excel file. The spreadsheet includes, per student: class nickname, whether the quiz was submitted, whether the student submitted late, submission time, time spent answering, whether the quiz has been graded, score, accuracy rate, number of correct answers, number of incorrect answers, number of partially correct answers, number of unanswered questions, the score for each question, and the selected answer for each question. Additional information is also included: class ID, class name, quiz title, unit ID, unit name, number of questions, full score, and grader.

Phone and tablet can only view the quiz data, not export a student's detailed quiz data.

1. View the Data Statistics, or click Export.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F83f33eb2b056c5c552bde7f35a2a978131811cd62a23d0d7f67ef4b3072983a1_465230?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=520ed342c8c43f0895a373618a7551c87c34a351)

Find and enter the class, then click Quiz Data.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8246ec0582a3d3525cf3508d7257cdb5c5fde672c9797e0bc7ac456816393e14_2127892?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5f07d4e1fab8ce799fe8086d1bcb8b88a9fdab06)

# 5. Class Teaching Activities (Assignments)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Assignments"
source_title_zh: "作业"
```

## Assignments

## I. Creating an "Assignment"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### When to use this
The "Assignment" feature refers to a teacher assigning students a certain amount of learning tasks or questions, which students are required to complete and submit within a set time. Teachers assign homework to help students reinforce what they learned in class, build self-directed learning and problem-solving skills, and use it as a way to assess and give feedback on student learning.

### Usage Notes
After entering the class page, teachers can assign homework under the course tab. An assignment supports several types of attachments — images, voice recordings, cloud drive files, local files, and website links — to help students better understand and complete the assignment. File limits: up to 15 image attachments, up to 15 recording attachments, up to 15 video attachments, and the combined total of local files, cloud drive files, and links cannot exceed 15; each video or file must be under 500MB. When uploading assignment attachments from a computer, you can drag and drop images and files directly into the assignment.

On computer or tablet, teachers can have an AI agent help generate or polish assignment content based on a teaching objective or specific knowledge point.

Teachers can select assignment resources authorized by their organization, or resources from their own cloud drive.

Teachers can also set an answer key for the assignment, which also supports uploaded attachments. The answer key's visibility can be set to: never public, public immediately, public after submission, public after grading, or public once the assignment ends.

**Settings available when creating an "Assignment":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the assignment's start and due time. |
| AI grading | Once enabled, an AI agent will grade student submissions based on the assignment content; the AI's grading is saved as a draft for the teacher to review. This feature can only be configured by teachers on computer or tablet. |
| Grading | Set the assignment's grading scheme and points. |
| Publish to | Publish the assignment to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Course | Choose which course the assignment belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which unit topic the assignment belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| Allow late submission after the activity ends | Once enabled, if a student didn't complete the assignment on time, they can submit it after the activity has ended. |
| Allow students to see each other's assignments and grades | Sets whether students can view all of each other's assignments and grades.<br><br>Once enabled, you can choose "all visible" or "only excellent content and grades visible"; and the visibility timing can be set to "visible immediately," "visible after submission," "visible after grading," or "visible after the assignment ends." |
| Allow newly joined students to submit | Once enabled, students who join the class before the assignment activity ends can also take part in the already-assigned assignment. |
| Allow students to download attachments | Once enabled, students can download the teacher-uploaded attachments in the assignment. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this assignment activity. |

### Notes
If "a student was removed from the class by a teacher," "the class was dissolved," or "a student left the class voluntarily," whether the departed student can still view assignment attachments depends on the class setting for allowing students who left the class or whose class was dissolved to view course content.

If you select "AI Grading Helper," "Assignment Review & Feedback Assistant (supports assignment answer key)," "Short-Answer Grading Assistant (supports assignment answer key)," or "RE Dictation Grading Assistant (supports assignment answer key)" as the AI grading agent, the AI will grade based on the standard answer key the teacher uploaded with the assignment, improving grading accuracy.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Assignment.
6. Add the assignment title.
7. Add the assignment content and answer key.
8. Configure the assignment's settings.
9. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

## II. Editing an "Assignment"

Assignments can be edited, but what can be edited depends on the assignment's status.

For drafts and assignments that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; everything else can be edited.

For assignments currently in progress, content can be edited, but "Start Time" and "Course" in the settings cannot be changed.

For assignments that have ended, content can no longer be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: time, publish to, teacher, course, allow newly joined students to submit, and unlock conditions.

For in-progress and ended assignments, the assignment resource can be saved to the cloud drive for future use.

1. Go to the course.
2. Find the assignment, click "···," then select Edit.

## III. Deleting an "Assignment"

Assignment activities can be deleted whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended.

Once an assignment activity is deleted, all its file attachments are also deleted and cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

## IV. Ending an "Assignment"

Teachers can manually end an assignment any time before its due date, once published. If "Allow late submission" was not enabled in the settings, once the assignment ends, students will no longer be able to submit an unfinished assignment.

## VI. Uploading Grades

If a teacher publishes an assignment on ClassIn but the student actually completed it offline, the teacher can use the "Upload Grades" feature in the assignment to upload the student's offline grade to ClassIn — making it easier to statistically analyze grades later.

Teachers using a computer can upload grades for in-progress and ended assignments that have a grading scheme.

The Upload Grades feature in ClassIn supports manually adding a grade for a single student, or downloading a template to bulk-add grades for students — once filled in and uploaded, the students' existing grades will be overwritten.

Because the assignment grade spreadsheet must follow a specific format for ClassIn to recognize it, when bulk-uploading assignment grades, teachers need to download the template from ClassIn's upload grades screen. The template's first column is the student's name for the current assignment, and the second column is their score; once the completed Excel spreadsheet is ready, upload it in the "Upload Grades" window.

**Computer**
1. Enter the Assignment.
2. Click the three-dot icon, then select Upload Grades.

## VII. Sharing Assignments

Teachers can share an in-progress or ended assignment to WeChat or other platforms. When a student opens an assignment shared this way in WeChat, they can complete it inside the WeChat mini program, or tap through to the ClassIn app to complete it inside the class.

**Sharing an assignment from computer:** share to a ClassIn class/friend, copy the link, or share to WeChat friends/groups via WeChat scan/mini program.

**Sharing an assignment from phone/tablet:** share to a ClassIn class/friend, WeChat (friends/groups/Moments), Weibo, or QQ friends; you can also share the assignment or its mini-program link, or copy the link.

**Viewing a shared assignment outside the ClassIn app:** images, recordings, and videos can be viewed and played directly. The WeChat mini program additionally supports viewing files like PPT and Word. Other content, such as EDOC files, still requires launching ClassIn to join the class and view it there.

1. Click Share.
2. Select a sharing method.

## VIII. Reminding Students to Do the "Assignment"

After a teacher opens the assignment page, they can see under the "Not Submitted" or "Sent Back" tabs which students haven't submitted the assignment, and can remind all students who haven't submitted.

The "Notify" reminder is a push notification through both the ClassIn WeChat official account and the ClassIn app, sent at 15-minute intervals.

"WeChat Reminder" generates a WeChat mini-program image that's copied for use as a WeChat reminder.

"Copy Roster" copies a text-and-link list for manual reminding.

1. Select Not Submitted.
2. Select a reminder method.

## IX. Students Doing an "Assignment"

## 1. Doing an Assignment in ClassIn

When a student opens a teacher-assigned assignment, they should first open the teacher's uploaded attachments to fully understand the assignment questions. While working on the assignment, students should use the system's support for loading the teacher's original assignment content, and build on it with their own creative thinking to produce a high-quality answer.

Students can upload various types of attachments to enrich their submission — images, recordings, videos, files from their personal cloud drive, local files, and links. File limits: up to 15 image attachments, up to 15 recording attachments, up to 15 video attachments, and the combined total of local files, cloud drive files, and links cannot exceed 15; each video or file must be under 500MB. When uploading assignment attachments from a computer, you can drag and drop images and files directly into the assignment.

Once a student submits an assignment, if the teacher hasn't yet graded it, the student can still edit their submission. If the teacher requests a revision when grading, they can mark the student's assignment as "Sent Back for Revision" — the student can then revise their submitted assignment and resubmit it.

1. Go to To-Dos.
2. Go to Pending.
3. Find the assignment, then tap Do Assignment.

## 2. Doing an Assignment in the WeChat Mini Program

When a teacher shares a ClassIn assignment to WeChat, if the student's phone or tablet doesn't have ClassIn installed, they can fill in and submit the assignment directly inside the ClassIn assignment mini program in WeChat.

**Login restrictions:** the assignment mini program supports logging in with a phone number or email.

**Student features:** students can use the assignment mini program to submit an assignment, edit an already-submitted assignment, submit late, or revise an assignment sent back by the teacher.

**Teacher features:** the assignment mini program does not support teacher grading — please grade within the ClassIn app.

**Mutual viewing permission:** once "Students can see each other's assignments and grades" is enabled for the assignment in ClassIn, students can view classmates' assignment grades and content within the mini program.

**Attachment types:** the assignment mini program supports submitting text, images, recordings, videos, and files — unlike the ClassIn app, the mini program does not support adding links.

**Attachment source:** attachments can be taken/recorded directly, selected from the photo album, or selected from WeChat chat history. Selecting from the ClassIn cloud drive is not supported.

**Attachment limits:** in the mini program, a single recording can be up to 10 minutes, and a recorded video up to 1 minute; other attachment limits match those for submitting an assignment in ClassIn. Images and videos are processed and compressed according to WeChat's rules.

1. Open a ClassIn assignment someone else shared in WeChat.
2. Tap Submit Assignment.
3. In the privacy notice, tap Agree.
4. Log in to your ClassIn account.
5. Tap Submit Assignment again to open the content entry area.
6. After completing the assignment, tap Submit Assignment.

## XI. Grading an "Assignment"

"Grading an assignment" refers to the process of a teacher reviewing and scoring a student's submitted work. If a student actually completed the assignment offline, the teacher can still grade it. Grading typically involves understanding and analyzing the submission, evaluating and scoring it, and writing comments and suggestions. By grading assignments, teachers help students understand their academic performance and progress, and guide them toward improvement in knowledge and skills.

Once a student submits an assignment, the teacher can find it in the class or their to-dos to grade it.

Teachers grading on computer can see the grading status of every student's assignment in the sidebar, and can select a pending assignment to jump directly into grading it.

While grading, teachers can view and download the attachments a student submitted, to better assess the quality of their work. Teachers can also upload attachments to a student's assignment, or delete attachments the student uploaded, and can mark up image attachments directly to grade the work.

Once done reviewing and grading, teachers can leave feedback on the student's assignment, supporting both text and voice comments.

If AI grading is enabled, the AI agent in ClassIn can identify the assignment's questions, answer key, and attachments in the student's submission (supported attachment formats include images, audio, video, PDF, and PPT), and teachers can review the AI's grading.

If a student's work is exceptional, teachers can mark it as an "Excellent Assignment" to encourage the student's effort and growth. If there are issues with a student's work, teachers can send it back for revision, helping the student identify the problem and improve.

When a teacher clicks "Done," it marks that student's assignment as fully graded; clicking "Grade Next" moves on to the next pending student. If a teacher switches to another student's submission from the sidebar while grading the current one, the current student's grading is automatically finalized.

Teachers can re-grade a student's submitted assignment multiple times, and a history of intermediate grading is kept.

Use search or filters to find what you need.

1. Click Go Grade.
2. Review and grade the student's assignment content.
3. Fill in the assignment's comments and score.
4. Click Done, or Grade Next Student.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F52afec72ac1de7f5593a74124b326e5ada01611cb3a827ff6b05da8353501ab7_516306?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=8e933ca513793118293ee82bdd981dad6341e45b)

Go to Pending, then tap Grade.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa04da820222d83f3b08fe6f3334e20792a83102a5ecf6dd3c237154811cb8f6c_1893193?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ffb3f149ca5a43ae4c02cc5669dba9440708a4ce)

## XII. Sharing an Excellent Assignment

When a student's assignment stands out, teachers can share it with the rest of the class as a model example, motivating other students to strive for excellence — giving them something concrete to learn from.

Teachers can find an outstanding student assignment on the assignment page and share it with other students. Assignments also support making a student's excellent work public, so students can view each other's work within ClassIn or the WeChat mini program — achieving the same sharing effect and helping raise the overall academic level of the class.

When a teacher shares an assignment from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code or mini-program with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares an assignment from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or the assignment/mini-program link to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, or by copying a link.

Viewing a shared assignment outside the ClassIn app: images, recordings, and video files can be viewed and played directly; other content requires launching ClassIn to join the class and view it. In the WeChat mini program specifically, files like PPT and Word can be viewed; other files, like EDOC, still require launching ClassIn to view within the class.

1. Go to Graded, then click the student whose work you want to share.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa55f40c487523850a824f16ebf949b14368464d00e334aba47d691dc903dda38_414411?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=adad8ebb06d66f47c7d5d89d85f1de6882176775)

Go to Graded, tap a student, tap the share button, then select a sharing method.

## XIII. Viewing/Downloading "Assignment Data"

## Applies to
## When to use this
Assignment data lets teachers view statistics and download data for all assignments in the class, or for the current assignment. This data includes student completion status, scores, submission time, and more. Teachers can use it to analyze and evaluate student learning, and to deliver personalized teaching and targeted feedback. Schools and educational institutions can use this data for comprehensive evaluation, identifying student strengths and areas for improvement, and comparing across classes or schools. Teachers can also use assignment data to statistically analyze overall student performance, learning trends, and teaching effectiveness, and adjust their teaching strategy and course planning accordingly. Downloading assignment data makes it easier for teachers to conduct overall analysis and reporting, providing a solid, data-driven basis for their teaching.

## Usage Notes
Assignment data downloaded on computer is saved locally as a spreadsheet; data downloaded on tablet or phone can be saved to the ClassIn cloud drive or sent to a ClassIn class/friend for use.

## Steps

### (1) Downloading Assignment Data
1. Click More.
2. Click Download.

## XIV. Downloading Assignment Content

Head teachers and class teachers using a computer can download assignment content from the details page of a published assignment. The downloaded content includes the teacher's assigned content, all submitted student content, and the content as it stands after teacher grading.

Two ways to bundle the content are available: the default method bundles everyone's assignment attachments into a single folder, with content mixed together; the other method groups content by student, generating a subfolder named for each student's class nickname, containing all of that student's content (including graded content), with the teacher's assigned content stored separately in its own subfolder.

Once you choose a local download location, a download task is created immediately in ClassIn's file transfer feature; once complete, you can view it locally.

The top-level folder is named: Assignment Name-Class Name-Organization Name-Download Time.

Once downloaded locally, assignment content is converted as follows:

**(1) Text:** displayed as an HTML web page.
- Default bundling: teacher content file name = assignment title; student content file name = student's class nickname.
- Grouped by student: both teacher and student content file names = assignment title.

**(2) Files (images/EDB whiteboard files/audio-video/regular files):** kept in their original format.
(EDOC files can only be viewed within ClassIn, and are not supported for local display or download.)
- Default bundling: teacher attachment name = assignment title + file name; student attachment name = student's class nickname + file name.
- Grouped by student: teacher attachment name = assignment title + file name; student attachment name = file name.

**(3) Links:** displayed as a .txt file.
- Default bundling: teacher's links are all saved into a single .txt file named "Web Links"; student links are all saved into a single .txt file named "Student's Class Nickname + Web Links."
- Grouped by student: links are all saved into a single .txt file named "Web Links."

1. In the top-right corner of the assignment details page, go to More, then click Download Assignment Content.
2. Choose the bundling method: Default or By Student.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fccbfb081a3658f8a7bad65e25816691e417c7a18d65a2112b2ad273104169a6e_565593?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=babf2565c30a70f2dcef68b225374e97f1f38a66)

# 5. Class Teaching Activities (AI Speaking Card)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "AI Speaking Card"
source_title_zh: "AI口语卡"
```

## AI Speaking Card

## I. What Is an "AI Speaking Card"?

Among the four core skill areas in English education — listening, reading, speaking, and writing — objectively scoring or evaluating reading and speaking has always been a challenge, since they involve multiple factors like pronunciation, vocabulary, intonation, grammar, and fluency. Manual grading is not only a heavy workload, but also demanding on a grader's stamina and focus. In addition, since a grader's state can vary, grading results can fluctuate, adding to an institution's operating costs. AI speech evaluation can comprehensively improve students' speaking ability, while giving teachers an efficient, time-saving grading solution.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fcd6da8be8f050fd314f074c7642511db3b7ec966863a4f37fac427a897bbd8e3_39962?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=87414dafaa2970ea6709c5c9d7b6b55faaa93bc2)

## II. Creating an "AI Speaking Card"

### Applies to
Head teachers and teachers.

### Usage Notes
Teachers can create an AI Speaking Card within a class using a computer or tablet.

On the new speaking card screen, teachers can click "Add Card" to add a question — each question accepts one word or one sentence (up to 150 characters). Pressing Enter automatically generates audio and a definition; if the input is a single word, phonetic notation is also generated. Up to 100 practice questions can be added. Teachers can also click "Bulk Add" to add questions, entering card content separated by line breaks for each question; on computer, teachers can also import questions from Excel. In addition, teachers can use AI to add questions intelligently — enter specific requirements in the AI interface, click Generate, and apply the generated content to the speaking card.

When a teacher enters a word or sentence for a card, the system automatically generates the corresponding audio, phonetic notation, and definition. If the teacher isn't satisfied with the generated audio, phonetic notation, or definition, they can hover over the text box to delete it. After deleting, the teacher can click to regenerate it automatically, or enter it manually; for audio specifically, teachers can also re-record, upload audio, or regenerate it automatically. Phonetic notation and definition are optional — leaving them blank won't affect normal publishing or grading.

Questions can be reordered by dragging, so teachers can arrange them as needed.

**Settings available when creating an "AI Speaking Card":**

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Time | Set the AI Speaking Card's start and due time. |
| Grading | Set the AI Speaking Card's grading scheme and points. |
| Publish to | Publish the AI Speaking Card to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class, or to multiple classes at once. |
| Teacher | Assign the activity's teacher to receive related notifications. |
| Unit Topic | Choose which course the AI Speaking Card belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Allow students to see each other's content and grades | Sets whether students can view each other's full content and grades.<br><br>Once enabled, you can choose "all visible" or "only excellent content and grades visible"; and the visibility timing can be set to "visible after submission," "visible after grading," or "visible after the activity ends." |
| Allow late submission after the activity ends | Once enabled, if a student didn't complete the AI Speaking Card on time, they can submit it after the activity has ended. |
| Allow newly joined students to submit | Once enabled, students who join the class before the AI Speaking Card activity ends can also take part in the already-published activity. |
| Unlock conditions | Add prerequisite activities that must be completed. If unlock conditions are added, students must complete them before starting this AI Speaking Card activity. |

### Notes
Non-mainland-China (+86) accounts do not support automatic definition generation.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click Create.
5. Create AI Speaking Card.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa51aa5fe891fc6a14fa01e85265fbd2209972371cae5ecf7220c12235399a6f3_532244?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5d60ba86112bb1218f11abf47aac3be4fe6c7e2d)

## III. Editing an "AI Speaking Card"

Teachers using a computer or tablet can edit an AI Speaking Card, but what can be edited depends on the card's status.

For drafts and cards that haven't started, "Course" cannot be changed; the card content and settings can both be edited.

For cards currently in progress, "Start Time" and "Course" in the settings cannot be changed. Whether the card content can be edited depends on whether any student has already recorded a practice reading for a question: if a student has recorded, the teacher cannot edit that card's content; if no student has recorded yet, the teacher can still edit it.

For cards that have ended, the card content can no longer be edited, and the following settings can no longer be changed: time, publish to, teacher, course, allow newly joined students to submit, and unlock conditions.

1. Go to the course.
2. Find the AI Speaking Card, click "···," then select Edit.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F5256926ad7f2b1f725579372c733b4828eef9391579c30e752910aec532a0d82_327715?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=546a08d7eb1a44996f860c9c6c83f71e4d47b97b)

## IV. Deleting an "AI Speaking Card"

AI Speaking Cards can be deleted whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended.

Once an AI Speaking Card activity is deleted, all its data is also cleared and cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

1. Find the AI Speaking Card, click "···," then select Delete.

**Phone**

2. Open a created course.

4. Tap the three-dot icon in the top-right corner.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Faf154762d48e6d5dcf54806365b7e8a49ac0702278ec68487ded1e272e2336bb_1007020?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=567eb7ad1aec3c92c6c8019ea137f013e834562d)

## V. Ending an "AI Speaking Card"

Teachers can manually end an AI Speaking Card any time before its due date, once published. If "Allow late submission after the activity ends" was not enabled in the settings, once the activity ends, students will no longer be able to submit an unfinished practice recording.

1. Find the AI Speaking Card, click "···," then select End Now.

## VI. Duplicating an "AI Speaking Card"

AI Speaking Card activities can be duplicated to the same class or other classes, whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended. Except for the start and due time, the duplicated card's content and settings default to match the original.

Duplicating an AI Speaking Card activity is only supported on computer and tablet.

1. Find the AI Speaking Card, click "···," then select Duplicate Activity.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fde7913e715227b34763b2dedd2e6488e35edd24859b8fc0be49df6e566c4b97b_356070?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=113333cdeb64d6eeb765ce0e9e13d2120bfbc63b)

## VII. Sharing an "AI Speaking Card"

Teachers can share an in-progress or ended AI Speaking Card to WeChat or other platforms, making it easier to prompt students to record and submit on time.

When a teacher shares an AI Speaking Card from a computer, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or copy the link, or scan a WeChat QR code with their phone to share to WeChat friends or groups.

When a teacher shares an AI Speaking Card from a phone or tablet, they can share it to a ClassIn class or friend, or to WeChat friends/groups/Moments, Weibo, or QQ friends, and can also copy the link to share with others.

When viewed outside the ClassIn app, the shared content supports playing the teacher-published speaking card audio; to record and submit, students still need to launch ClassIn and join the class.

1. Tap AI Speaking Card.
2. Click the Share button in the top-right corner.
3. Select a sharing method.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F9845ed6407b5ed5228ee1aa3e6d2633d0b508b7eb9383db14a0251d9cbe44561_466592?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=e7b1be937ae6bda8f6fae28f0c1f51f72c57b34e)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F2641c1b126c0535d775aeb075ebd743426da8c838a2b70e618b1674ac6fba393_1048825?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=29a44f20016d1edd245b5ce66af5ca667851f820)

## VIII. Reminding Students to Record the "AI Speaking Card"

After a teacher opens the AI Speaking Card page, they can see under the "Not Submitted" or "Sent Back" tabs which students still need to submit a recording, and can remind all students who need to submit.

The "Notify" reminder is a push notification through both the ClassIn WeChat official account and the ClassIn app, sent at 15-minute intervals.

"Copy Roster" copies a text-and-link list for manual reminding.

### Related Articles
"Enabling WeChat Notifications"

1. Go to Not Submitted.
2. Click Notify.

## IX. Students Submitting an "AI Speaking Card"

Once a teacher publishes an AI Speaking Card, students can find it in the ClassIn class or their to-dos, view it, and record and submit their reading.

On the AI Speaking Card reading screen, students can view each question, play the system's reference audio, and record themselves reading it aloud. After reading a given question, the system automatically gives a star rating and highlights inaccurately pronounced words in color (red for poor pronunciation or a skipped word, yellow for good, and green for excellent — see the image below); students can also play back their own recording, or choose to re-record or move on to the next question.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa961be4d21bccf95ac4457c976a94ed1cc3245f88a29868fa7ad39dd2b51d0c9_13405?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f5556b5b9c6afb98a686330e913bfb42c9354f8f)

If a student exits the reading page without submitting, the system saves their progress so they can continue recording the remaining questions next time.

Once a student finishes recording all questions, they can tap Submit; if grading is enabled, the score will be shown after submission.

Once a student submits their AI Speaking Card, they can still re-record and resubmit as long as the teacher hasn't manually graded it yet. If the teacher requests a re-recording when grading, they can mark the student's card as "Sent Back for Revision" — the student can then re-record their submitted card and resubmit it.

1. View the reading content.
2. Tap Start Reading.
3. On the reading page, start/end recording, view the star rating for the question, and play the system's or your own audio.
4. Once finished with a question, tap to switch to the next one.
5. Once all questions are recorded, tap Submit.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7d602e879fc4b16824903498f3225ddcfd0368e752147f0bfb1424e1d3894279_905607?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=87b560fae648a323bad8fe8b2aeab51e014474a9)

Once finished with a question, swipe left to switch to the next one.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa9f7a23d124f122b1183da1976fb70ef92dd979ec4f458d866fd839e76bff22f_3288745?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=8e93a323a81f57fb5f5f6c95f92604c8c01ee210)

## X. Students Resubmitting an "AI Speaking Card"

## 1. Re-Recording an Already-Submitted Card

Once a student submits an AI Speaking Card, they can still re-record and resubmit as long as the teacher hasn't manually graded it yet. Submission and grading history can be viewed on the activity details page.

1. Tap Read Again.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3d6b6e4ba4306054fd930bedfbfd73b18f97edd0ad3116f2f19bbd08086f378e_553934?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5b6ac68f70f45dc55dad4cb70f881fe2f6c5d08c)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F345ea8311ca70270e77746581f926c7231c403beb12d53aa7363271c82f7713a_2228275?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=83e4fd84c8f5b608eff3900e7f9dcb92d9b8e0b5)

## 2. Resubmitting a Card That Was Sent Back for Revision

If a teacher marks a student's AI Speaking Card as "Sent Back for Revision" when grading, the student can find it under the class's course tab, re-record the questions, and resubmit.

Once a student submits a card that was sent back for revision, they can no longer re-record it again.

1. Tap Go Revise.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fe2e670cd3d6661fcc557bf4490382563e16f8b2801065d6b7ad70de90c454e11_551019?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4bbc1a039cc0dae9e11de8965dc3d4f1c4afbff1)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F32538e1497aa35bc7626c2d758e7046f7c5365f5769dbaaceba98de61e88d13e_2229812?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=1818b63474923c3f0f53f915fff0b8d99cfbf77f)

## XI. Grading an "AI Speaking Card"

Once a student submits an AI Speaking Card, teachers can find it in the class or their to-dos to grade.

If the AI Speaking Card has a grading scheme set, the system automatically generates a score based on the student's reading results (see the image below — the system automatically gives a star rating for every question and highlights inaccurately pronounced words in color), and teachers can re-review the student's card under "Graded." If the AI Speaking Card doesn't have a grading scheme set, teachers can grade the student's card under "Pending Grading."

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F66731356977d1622a2c41805a381bde7ebced23b9b6e3dd9d5d3ca08b9a89672_21288?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a73e36898ebc259d418351f1739f64ef0587764c)

While grading, teachers can play a student's recording for each question and comment based on it; comments support both text and voice recordings. If a student's reading is exceptional, teachers can mark it as "Excellent," and can also assign a grade if grading is enabled.

Once teachers finish grading, they can click Submit. If a student needs to re-record and resubmit, teachers can click Send Back for Revision.

Teachers can grade a student's submitted card multiple times; the student's history retains records of their submissions, the system's automatic grading, and the teacher's grading. If teachers don't want a student to see certain grading records, they can delete them from the student's history.

1. Go to Pending Grading or Graded.
2. Click Grade or Re-Grade.
3. Play the student's recording, then leave a comment.
4. Click Send Back for Revision, or Submit Grading.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa487571e2c846497e554a5d43363cf602e3986212b9f628f3bb90c09c9f7793c_1182407?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ae343f7c04653a9d17d03fa53d4f8593f7e30c4e)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F58b64b6f40d769157d0f9f547a1d492b3fa3e6f32f28c9471e6c4cc5c7cce6be_3721984?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=977dde57849ab08e80eca0f6258035bf5f22869a)

## XII. Viewing/Downloading "AI Speaking Card" Data

On the AI Speaking Card's details page, teachers can view overall reading analysis and student data for the current card; on computer, they can also download detailed student data.

**Reading analysis:** teachers can click on the bar chart to jump directly to a specific question card, making it easier to identify problems common across the class. On phone, reading analysis appears under "Reading Content & Data" on the activity details page.

**Student data:** includes the current AI Speaking Card's overall submission rate, highest score, average score, and number of "Excellent" ratings.

Teachers using a computer can download all data — that is, detailed student data — locally after the student data section; the data includes each student's submission, grading, and score information.

Phone and tablet can only view reading analysis and student data, without downloading detailed student data.

1. View Student Data and Reading Data.
2. Download detailed student data.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3bb3f3241adfb67eeb7a8cfda7f31bb18f3835e0d4bf1247a3b6c0e3f52b748f_582263?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c605bf2f71fd691ed7f4470bdcfe70bb18edf304)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb425930bc0fe78dc73507bcc825b6f4293b57c6b2d939f7e19370f316c051f60_2780462?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=bd6330ba19220ca00151192e126b91bc03e690f9)

# 5. Class Teaching Activities (Class Sessions)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Class Sessions"
source_title_zh: "课堂"
```

## Class Sessions

## I. What Is a "Class Session"?

On the ClassIn platform, a "class session" is the dedicated place where a teacher delivers knowledge to students — also called a lesson or live classroom. In a class session, the teacher carries out teaching activities through explanation, demonstration, and questioning, aiming to promote student learning and development. How the classroom environment is designed and organized is critical to improving teaching outcomes and student engagement. Common features within a class session include on-stage seats, the blackboard, and various teaching tools, ensuring the teaching process runs smoothly.

## II. Creating a "Class Session"

### Applies to
Head teachers.

Class teachers, once "Allow Teachers to Create Class Sessions" is enabled.

### Usage Notes
When creating a class session within a class, the following can be configured:

| Setting | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Class session name | Give the class session a clear name so students and teachers can easily identify it. |
| Start time and duration | Set the class session's start time and duration. The earliest the start time can be set is the current time; the duration can be set to as short as 15 minutes and as long as 23 hours 55 minutes. |
| Publish to | The "class session" can be published to a specific class, to some group members or specific students within a class. |
| Lead teacher | The creator is the lead teacher by default; the head teacher can assign other class teacher members as the lead teacher. Only one lead teacher can be set per class session. |
| Co-teacher(s) | Teachers in the class can be selected as co-teachers. Up to 6 co-teachers can be added per class session. When one co-teacher goes on stage to show their camera, it doesn't take up a lead-teacher or student seat, but when multiple co-teachers go on stage, they do take up student seats. |
| Select course | Choose which course the "class session" belongs to. Defaults to the current course. |
| Unit topic | Choose which unit topic the "class session" belongs to. If not selected, it goes into the default unit. |
| OMO livestream broadcast | Lets students watch the teacher's livestream broadcast feed, which students can choose to view; suited to blended in-person/online teaching scenarios. This feature must be enabled in the Backend Management System before it can be selected. |
| On-stage headcount | The number of people that can appear on the on-stage seats at the top of the classroom at the same time. Minimum: 1 lead teacher and 0 students; maximum: 1 lead teacher and 12 students. |
| Record ClassIn Classroom | Cloud recording is split into "Record ClassIn Classroom" and "Record On-Site." Record ClassIn Classroom captures the entire class session view. |
| Record On-Site | Cloud recording is split into "Record ClassIn Classroom" and "Record On-Site." Record On-Site only captures the selected teacher's camera feed, showing the full teaching scene. |
| Web live stream and playback permission | With cloud recording checked, you can set the class session's web live stream and playback permission, determining whether users outside the class can watch the live stream and playback via the web. |
| AI class session summary | With cloud recording checked, you can choose to have an AI agent generate an intelligent summary of the class session playback content, including chapter summaries and a subtitle list. |
| Show on-stage seats | Once enabled, it makes it easier for teachers and students to interact online, communicate, and answer questions at any time. Once disabled, class sessions focus on blackboard-based teaching; teachers can also adjust this again from within the classroom. |
| Students auto-join on stage | With "Show on-stage seats" enabled, you can set whether students automatically show their camera on stage when entering the classroom. |
| Allow students to see each other's learning reports | Once enabled, students can view other classmates' learning reports. |

### Notes
When creating a class session within a class, the teacher can choose the on-stage headcount. The system defaults to the option used the last time a class session was created on the current device. If you switch devices, the system won't remember your previous choice, and you'll need to set it again.

If you're unable to add a lesson or course, it may be because the number of lessons under the current course has reached its limit.

Regardless of the class session's scheduled duration, formal classrooms have a 20-minute grace period for running over, while temporary classrooms have a 2-minute grace period.

If the "head teacher" is also the "lead teacher," there's no need to separately set the lead teacher when creating the class session, since the lead teacher defaults to the head teacher when creating a class session on the client.

If "a student was removed from the class by a teacher," "the class was dissolved," or "a student left the class voluntarily," whether the departed student can still view recorded class playback videos in ClassIn depends on the class setting for allowing students who left the class or whose class was dissolved to view course content.

### Steps

**Computer/tablet**
1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Create a new course, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Select Class Session.
6. Configure the class session's parameters.
7. Publish directly, or save as a draft.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F89a34ed5bd5876be88ae273785dc0cc135cb7daf2f3f8d93817c213db20440c5_982056?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=fa9820232a5242dd2ae4e703e7b5a222556a6a1f)

**Phone**
1. Create a Class Session (if not your first time, tap "+" in the bottom-right corner).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8a41d4212d8728748b137efc358604d25e2a0c212918352d39da00d6f84971fa_2487906?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c2035d75c43d097c118799e7fa8c3b61429e456e)

## III. Editing a "Class Session"

Lead teachers with the permission to create class sessions.

In the ClassIn client, the head teacher can edit any class session already created, while a teacher with the permission to create class sessions can only edit class sessions where they are the lead teacher.

Editable information and settings include: class session name, class date, class start time, class session duration, lead teacher, co-teacher(s), on-stage headcount, cloud recording, web live stream, and web playback. Please follow the related rules and time limits below.

Settings that can be changed up to 20 minutes before class starts: class session name, class date, class start time, class session duration, published class/members, OMO livestream broadcast, on-stage headcount, cloud recording (Record ClassIn Classroom, Record On-Site), web live stream, web playback, show on-stage seats, and students auto-join on stage.

Settings that can be changed at any time before the class session ends: changing the lead teacher, adding/replacing co-teacher(s), and web playback.

Settings that can be changed at any time, without time restriction: AI class session summary, web playback, unit topic, and allow students to see each other's learning reports.

Before the class session officially starts (including the pre-entry window), the class session can be deleted at any time. However, once the class session reaches its scheduled start time, it can no longer be deleted.

Class sessions that have ended cannot be deleted.

1. Go to Home.
2. Enter the class.
3. Go to a created course.
4. Find the class session, click "···," then select Edit.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F549a9d3be2f5440d2ab04948d9922a2fd90999349fbf140a022c23bf875432c3_341127?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=dd185894a1aedb1a1cf781fb95b3d6962ecd35e0)

Go to the course, tap the class session, tap the three-dot icon in the top-right corner, and select Edit.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F321da2ceaaacdb9d5416240c614114654d3b62af5d7fcb2dc0941c9d638f1502_1809404?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ea928601713b280056eb268e9ff72d6d5d2bc788)

## IV. Deleting a "Class Session"

The head teacher can delete a class session in the class before it starts; a teacher with the permission to create class sessions can only delete a class session before it starts if they are the lead teacher for that session.

Once deleted, a class session cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

1. Find the class session, click "···," then select Delete.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7b56a0072381e2ecaed0acdf2e236e112f14942246453787c77a67beb1c068fb_344632?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=8bebefff0df2fbf86c4fc5c234cdee84ed582028)

Select Delete.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fccb72d2c4db2d8acf84a16d8eadb717022c9fa2a7a7b63cd8d0ed6eca5327229_1805969?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c49b2215817b1ef40dea031802555db6156026f9)

## V. Duplicating a "Class Session"

Class session activities can be duplicated to the current class whether they're a draft, not started, in progress, or ended. Except for the start time and class duration, the duplicated class session's parameters default to match the original.

1. Find the class session, click "···," then select Duplicate Activity.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff98e6be34065758569db29e864e164ec0afde8605321b14992d9ef043d238f0c_346009?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=78886f38627bba7439ca05da3bf21fcd776ce5e6)

Select Duplicate Activity.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F5fdd7445d52e5ef53bf190191f6013839a35e8714898a7c4fe90e582aad6956e_1812497?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=286dad18993c988d89e80fc4f289da1efaa7bc5f)

## VI. Setting "Co-Teacher(s)"

## 1. Adding a Co-Teacher When Creating the Class Session

### When to use this
If a large number of students are attending class, the head teacher or a teacher with the permission to create class sessions can add "co-teacher(s)" to the class session. Co-teachers can help the lead teacher maintain classroom order and assist with delivering the lesson.

Before a co-teacher can be added to a class session, the head teacher must first add that teacher to the class and set them as a "class teacher" within the class. Only then can the head teacher, or a teacher with the permission to create class sessions, add that class teacher as a co-teacher when creating a class session.

1. Go to Home in the left navigation.
2. Find and enter the class.
3. Create a new course in the top-left corner, or open an existing one.
4. Click New.
5. Create a Class Session.
6. In the creation window, click Expand, then add a Co-Teacher.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fe9782f54a059ec88b52e8b677944473441af0ddf13de20a0f753364ee383285d_477216?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=d6c9ccb1330dca1a325dfe7394baa6fa24b1fede)

Add a Co-Teacher.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F0a17890e9966a018cb6e7a4644f6243da6a0dc670579717b8860324489410f2e_2286119?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f794bb92a559f284342cde54b71f9fa85efedb94)

## 2. Adding/Replacing a Co-Teacher After Class Has Started

Once a class session has already started, if a co-teacher needs to be added or an existing one replaced, the head teacher or a lead teacher with the permission to create class sessions can add another class teacher member as a co-teacher for this class session, or replace an existing co-teacher with someone else.

1. Go to a created course on the left.
2. Find the class session you need to change, click "···" on the right, then select Edit.
3. Click Expand, then set the Co-Teacher(s).
4. Click Confirm.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb6a3c2e27997ac1806ff58fb4d7b860f17d12ef82c159102c1177da164b4bbdb_486604?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=96786d284175f0f77a5c7a1f3f785f2ddc14d2eb)

Set the Co-Teacher(s).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff229f0facf692b24d79223705b44f8bebfafd8622f1276fc37838cd1d95c8a2f_2299809?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=fc66e0da598cdbb98ad67c11dbaf3bb830c66fbf)

## VII. Changing the "Lead Teacher"

Once a class session has already started, if the lead teacher has something else come up and someone needs to temporarily take over the class session, the head teacher can temporarily swap in a different lead teacher for that classroom.

Before changing the lead teacher for a class session, the head teacher must first add the new lead teacher to the class and set the newly joined teacher as a "class teacher" within the class. Only then can that teacher be set as the class session's lead teacher when making the change.

1. Select the teacher, check the new lead teacher, then click Confirm.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8d05b58c14439448b6247818fbc8bd844a10996835b9a2c87f8fcf0dfa9769a3_477418?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=613fc8460385fd0b8c0ba5d80771c342105219cd)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3f1a85e3c35686fb6638fbdc6ad34d83286dd899163e8595449b47e9b54060cb_2275843?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=9eb90f4983e96a2ce14d65ebd25fe30d73d2f586)

## VIII. Getting the Web Live Stream/Playback Link

Applies to this class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and the class's head teacher.

Once "Allow Teachers to Get the Web Live Stream/Playback Link from the Client" is enabled in the Backend Management System at www.eeo.cn, the class's head teacher and the class session's lead teacher/co-teacher(s) can go to the class session details in ClassIn and get the web live stream/playback link for that class session or class.

1. Click "Class Sessions Only."
2. Find the class session, then click into the class session details.
3. Click the class session info, then copy or forward the web live stream/playback link for the class session or class.

## IX. Watching "Recorded Class Playback Videos" in the Class

### What is a playback video?
A "playback video" refers to when a class session was created in the class with "Record ClassIn Classroom" or "Record On-Site" checked (i.e. cloud recording), and the lead teacher entered the formal classroom to teach and record the entire class session. These videos are automatically turned into "playback videos" about 30 minutes after the class ends.

### What's the difference between "recorded class playback videos" and "recorded courses"?
"Recorded class playback video" refers to a video the lead teacher records of the entire teaching process, from the teacher's point of view, using ClassIn's cloud recording feature. These videos are automatically generated and available for playback about 30 minutes after the class session ends. "Recorded course," by contrast, refers to a specific teaching activity the head teacher or a teacher creates within the class, where the teacher can upload a video from their local computer to the "recorded course" for students and teachers to watch and learn from at any time.

Applies to class teachers and class session students.

As long as the lead teacher's recording during the class session went normally, half an hour after class, all teachers in the class and the class session's students can find the class session in the class and watch the playback video.

While watching the video, based on the recording settings, you can choose to play either the recorded video or the recorded on-site video; if the playback includes multiple video segments, you can switch between segments while watching.

Playback video supports windowed playback, variable playback speed, volume adjustment, and dragging the progress bar for flexible viewing.

If the chapter summary and subtitle list under "AI class session summary" were checked when creating the class session, you can also view the AI-generated summary and subtitle list for the class session while watching the playback, and can copy them.

If "Record ClassIn Classroom / Record On-Site" and "AI Teaching Analysis" were checked when creating the class session, and the lead teacher's recording completed successfully with normal audio, the lead teacher can view AI Teaching Analysis for that class session in the class session playback after class, and can also download the analysis as a PDF to keep.

Transfer students can watch the "playback video" of class sessions they took part in.

To grant newly joined students access to view the class's historical playback videos, enable "Allow Students Newly Added to the Course to Watch Playbacks of Historical Class Sessions" in the "Backend Management System," then add the student to the class.

To prevent students removed from the class from continuing to watch historical class session playback videos, enable "Students Removed from the Course Cannot Watch Historical Playback Videos" in the "Backend Management System," then remove the student from the class.

Only teachers with Backend Management System access, or organization administrators, can download playback videos from the www.eeo.cn Backend Management System — teachers and students cannot download them within ClassIn.

1. Go to a created course.
2. Find the class session, then click Playback.

## X. Viewing "Whiteboard Courseware" in the Class

### What is "whiteboard courseware"?
When a teacher types text or draws annotations on the blackboard or courseware while teaching, ClassIn automatically saves the teacher's whiteboard writing and courseware. These auto-saved items can be viewed after class in "Class Session Details" or the "Schedule." Teachers and students can easily review and revisit class session content.

"Whiteboard courseware" includes both "classroom whiteboard" and "annotated courseware." "Classroom whiteboard" is the writing on the blackboard in a formal classroom; "annotated courseware" is courseware opened in a formal classroom. As long as either the "classroom whiteboard" or "annotated courseware" is generated, a "whiteboard courseware" entry point will appear after class.

There are certain conditions for generating "whiteboard courseware":

First, whiteboard courseware retention must be enabled in the Backend Management System at www.eeo.cn.

Second, while teaching in a formal classroom, if the teacher types any amount of text on the blackboard, or on an opened PPT/PDF/Word (docx/doc)/Epub courseware (including courseware authorized for saving), or annotates with the pen tool across more than 10 elements (for PPT courseware, more than 10 pen-annotated elements on a single slide), ClassIn will automatically save the whole annotated whiteboard content and the entire courseware after class.

Teachers in the class and the class session's students can view that class session's "whiteboard courseware" in the class after class; the class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students can also view that class session's "whiteboard courseware" in the Schedule.

The class session's lead teacher and co-teacher(s) can share "whiteboard courseware" to a ClassIn class/friend, or to WeChat; on phone or tablet, they can also share to Weibo, QQ, and so on, or copy the link to send to others. Saving the generated "classroom whiteboard" as a JPG image to your personal ClassIn cloud drive is also supported.

After meeting the save conditions on the blackboard or in the courseware, pressing Ctrl+N or using one-click clear on the whiteboard will preserve the whiteboard content from before it was cleared.

"Annotated courseware" is ultimately saved as a PDF, with the preview thumbnail showing the first page of the courseware.

"Whiteboard courseware" is only generated after class for formal classrooms that meet the conditions.

1. Find the class session, then click Whiteboard Courseware.

## XI. Viewing the "Teaching Report" in the Class

As long as the lead teacher or co-teacher(s) in a formal classroom attended normally, a "teaching report" for that class session is generated about half an hour after class ends. The class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and head teacher can view the "teaching report" within the ClassIn class; the lead teacher and co-teacher(s) can also view it in the Schedule.

The "teaching report" defaults to showing the new-version report, with an option at the top to switch to the old version; it supports viewing content in 12 languages; and it displays class session info, including the lead teacher's avatar and class nickname, the class session's start time, and its duration.

The "teaching report" data includes five parts: attendance, class participation rate, class activity time distribution, class records, and class achievements.

**Attendance:** view the number of students who were present, late, and left early for this class session; viewing the details also shows each student's specific attendance status, class duration, and learning report — and on computer, attendance data can be exported.

**Class participation rate:** shows the participation rate for students using the answer clicker, small blackboard, interactive messages (chat within the classroom), and buzzer in the classroom; viewing the details shows each student's specific participation, and on computer, the detailed data can be exported.

**Class activity time distribution:** shows how much time the teacher spent using teaching tools in the classroom, split into four parts — formative assessment (including answer clicker, small blackboard, buzzer), teaching interaction (including random student picker, raise hand, group discussion, interactive messages, timer/countdown, etc.), and classroom incentives (trophies given to students); viewing the details gives a clearer view of how long and how often each tool was used.

**Class records:** includes classroom whiteboard, highlight moments (monitoring images), and class notes from within the classroom.

Classroom whiteboard is the writing on the blackboard; the condition for generating a classroom whiteboard image is that the blackboard has pen-marked elements exceeding 10, or contains typed text input — pressing Ctrl+N or using one-click clear will also save the whiteboard image from before it met the generation condition.

Highlight moments (monitoring images) are images automatically saved from the teacher's classroom window, useful for reviewing the teaching process within the classroom.

Class notes are note images saved after a teacher using a computer uses the class notes feature within the classroom.

If a teacher views images in class records using a phone or tablet, they can press and hold to save the image to their local photo album.

**Class achievements:** includes the accuracy ranking for students' answer clicker (in-class practice) answers, and the ranking based on trophies awarded by the teacher; viewing the details shows each student's data, and on computer, the detailed data can be exported.

The teaching report also supports sharing: on computer, it can be shared to a ClassIn class/friend; on phone or tablet, it can also be shared to Weibo, QQ, and so on, or the link can be copied to send to others.

The teaching report template looks like this:

## XII. Viewing the "Learning Report" in the Class

## 1. Students Viewing Their Own "Learning Report"

Applies to class session students.

A "learning report" for a student in that class session is generated about half an hour after class ends. Class session students can view their "learning report" within the ClassIn class, or in the Schedule.

The "learning report" can be viewed in 5 languages, and supports 2 display templates — which one is shown depends on the class report settings in the Backend Management System.

The "learning report" shows the student's personal nickname (if present) / their name from the Backend Management System (if absent), and includes: the teacher's rating and comments, class achievements, answer accuracy rate, activity level, attendance stats, classroom whiteboard, class notes, and highlight moments.

**Teacher's rating and comments:** the star rating and comments the lead teacher/co-teacher(s) gave the student for this class session, with the star rating shown under the student's personal nickname/Backend Management System name.

**Class achievements/My rewards:** shows how many trophies the student earned in this class session, and how they rank against classmates by trophy count.

**My answer accuracy rate:** shows the student's answer clicker breakdown for this class session, their personal accuracy rate, and the class average accuracy rate.

**Activity level:** shows how long the student spent on stage, speaking (not muted by the teacher), and authorized during this class session.

**Attendance stats:** includes this class session's attendance status, as well as the student's attendance record for other ended class sessions in this class.

**Classroom whiteboard:** an image of the writing on the blackboard, automatically generated once the save condition is met; when a student views the whiteboard image on a phone or tablet, they can tap the image and save it to their local photo album.

**Teacher's class notes:** note images saved after a teacher using a computer uses the class notes feature within the classroom; when a student views these on a phone or tablet, they can press and hold to save the image to their local photo album.

**My class notes:** note images saved after the student, using a computer, uses the class notes feature within the classroom; when viewed on a phone or tablet, students can press and hold to save the image to their local photo album.

**Highlight moments:** images automatically saved from the teacher's classroom window, useful for reviewing the teacher's explanations during class; when a student views these on a phone or tablet, they can press and hold to save the image to their local photo album.

The learning report also supports sharing: on computer, it can be shared to a ClassIn class/friend; on phone or tablet, it can also be shared to Weibo, QQ, and so on, or the link can be copied to send to others.

If a teacher needs to fill in or edit an evaluation after class, they can go to Post-Class Evaluation in the class session details and click "Evaluate Student" to view or edit the evaluation — evaluations can be edited and submitted multiple times.

## XIV. Exporting Class Session Data

Applies to class teachers and head teachers.

Besides being able to download class session data from the Backend Management System at www.eeo.cn, class teachers can also export it within ClassIn. The Backend Management System offers two data types for download — "teaching analysis" and "learning analysis" — but ClassIn only supports downloading "learning analysis" data.

The class session's "learning analysis" data includes: lesson name, lesson ID, start time, end time, lesson duration, student name, student's actual class duration, whether the student was present/late/left early, teacher's rating (teacher's rating of the student), teacher's comment (teacher's comment on the student), student's rating (student's rating of the teacher), student's comment (student's comment on the teacher), the number of valid times and total duration the student watched the playback within the ClassIn client, this class session's total playback video duration, the student's speaking duration, how many times the student went on/off stage and for how long, how many times the student was removed from the classroom by the teacher, how many times the student was rewarded, how many times the student raised their hand, how many times and for how long the student was authorized, how many times the teacher used the buzzer, how many times the student took part in buzzer questions, how many times the student answered first, the student's total answer clicker attempts, number of correct answers, answer breakdown, and how long the student's camera was on. This data is broken down in detail for every student.

Phone and tablet do not support exporting class session data within the ClassIn class.
