## XV. Viewing "AI Teaching Analysis" in the Class

ClassIn's AI Teaching Analysis is based on a class session's recorded video. It analyzes the teacher's delivery and classroom interaction, reconstructs the teaching process, and provides AI evaluation and scoring across multiple dimensions of teaching performance.

Once an eeo Backend Management System administrator turns on the AI Teaching Analysis switch under "School Settings → Value-Added Services," and both "Record ClassIn Classroom/Record On-Site" and "AI Teaching Analysis" are checked when creating a class session in a class, then — provided the lead teacher's recording completed successfully with normal audio — the lead teacher can view AI Teaching Analysis for that class session in the class session playback after class, and can also download the analysis as a PDF to keep.

The AI Teaching Analysis report includes: a class session overview; a reconstruction of the class session (teaching time allocation, a time-allocation timeline chart, a classroom keyword cloud, and a table of high-frequency classroom terms); detailed class session data (analysis of speech delivery effectiveness, analysis of the logic and structure of teaching language, and interaction analysis); and an overall AI evaluation of the class session with optimization suggestions. The AI Teaching Analysis report is only available in Chinese and does not support other languages.

The AI Teaching Analysis template looks like this:

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fab01f9c31c5f81e9f78226b5d0f05e2bbd30ce30ec37584ed363af12641c4277_911303?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=28b0a6525701f612c41242542aacaa97f7a3cf96)

Only the lead teacher can view AI Teaching Analysis in the class session playback within the ClassIn app; in addition, an eeo Backend Management System administrator can view it under "Backend → Teaching Management → Teacher Development."

The analysis only applies to playback generated in real time from a live class session — it does not cover manually uploaded class playback videos or LMS recorded courses.

1. Go to the class session playback page, then view/download the AI Teaching Analysis.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fd92cd912296064e92d4265e763a75a7233e1333205edb1720cb4e10979baada7_641788?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=271f1f5cacb12aa27235115c6f5fce6da2a91949)

# 6. Class Group Chat

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Class Group Chat"
source_title_zh: "班级群"
```

## Class Group Chat

## I. Sending Class Messages

### Applies to
All class members.

### When to use this
The "Chat" section within a class is an area for students to communicate, discuss, and share outside the classroom. Here, students can discuss course-related topics, academic questions, or personal interests, and share their learning experience and resources with each other. The purpose of this section is to encourage communication and collaboration among classmates, supporting their learning and personal growth.

### Usage Notes
Within a class, members can communicate in the class group chat in several ways:

**Text messages:** teachers and students type text to communicate and share ideas in the class group.

**Voice messages:** teachers and students can communicate via voice on the ClassIn phone app — a quicker, more convenient way to talk.

**Image sharing:** teachers and students can send images to the class group to show or share something.

**File sharing:** teachers and students can send local files from their computer or phone, or files from their ClassIn cloud drive, to the class group, making it easy for other class members to view and download.

**Emoji:** teachers and students can use emoji in the class group to express and convey emotion, adding warmth to the conversation.

### Notes
Sending voice messages is not supported on computer.

Users who newly join a class can see the previous chat history.

### Steps

**Computer**
1. Go to Messages in the left navigation.
2. Find the class in the message list and go into it.
3. Go to the class chat area on the right.
4. Below, you can send text, stickers, @mention other members, send a screenshot, send a file, send a friend's contact card, or start a temporary classroom.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F099d42d580e9f75751b0fd61d1b9724338e5d86e6797e596621e4bac8d514be7_145852?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=3751628044444c19ca7fee440ed70ed60fb15f47)

**Phone/tablet**
1. Go to Messages in the bottom navigation.
2. Enter the class group.
3. Go to the Chat module.
4. Below, you can send text, voice, images, files, and more.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F0573fa917b4635d3144ce04c6a46d5ee56b05f116f36af2500898bb330c647c5_498163?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=1de0b36fa4d6ffbab369ea6fc712a7d0422158f7)

## II. Recalling a Class Message

Applies to all class members.

If a user sends an incorrect message in the class group chat, they can use the message recall feature. Recalling a message means the user can, within a certain window of time, withdraw a message they've sent so it no longer appears in the class group chat. This gives users a convenient way to correct any incorrect or inappropriate content.

The "head teacher" and "teacher" in the class group chat can recall their own sent messages at any time, with no time limit.

Students in the class group chat can only recall messages they sent within the last 24 hours; after that window, they can no longer recall them.

1. Right-click a message you sent, then select Recall.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb7b4d51a820ba54af273d37c174a5ecbe4508cfaf43726628c24fe193e38afd1_143753?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a3e03c9da761194760ea24e5d1a7f065037f05a4)

Press and hold a message you sent, then select Recall.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F1106fd5ed9797eae8ee1751c2d242a3565d43a209303fcbc649a519da6292fdf_509155?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b25dee7b235c3211d10682c5cb52dfd17e100811)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Forwarding/Saving Files from the Class Group"
source_title_zh: "转发/保存班级群中文件"
```

## III. Forwarding/Saving Files from the Class Group

If you want to forward a file — one you sent or one sent by someone else — from the class chat to a friend or another class, you can use the multi-select feature. In the class group chat, right-click a file, select "Multi-Select," check the items you want to forward, then click "Forward One by One." If you want to save multiple files from the class, you can also use multi-select to check the files and save them locally on your computer or to your personal cloud drive.

Only images, videos, and files can be saved locally to your computer or to your personal cloud drive.

Multi-selecting files in the chat group is not currently supported on phone or tablet.

1. Go to Messages in the left navigation.
2. Right-click the image/file you want to forward or save.
3. Select Forward or Save As.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8e2a8d37aa7eb9dfc474ca72870552ba821a11f5d007781aea0b1bb47e5eecac_197526?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=78c0cde16f7f3c9cea034db157683a21017df343)

Press and hold the image or file you want to forward or save.
2. Select Forward.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F180dc3b824b642738d2906d54e633303009e645c3f8a2883672a936220923e58_495596?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=2de465d2b5844078af313f3cc70a71dc44d7723c)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Muting a Student in the Class"
source_title_zh: "班级禁言学生"
```

## IV. Muting a Student in the Class

Applies to "head teachers" and "teachers."

This feature is mainly used to prevent an individual student from posting inappropriate remarks or images in the class, or from creating a temporary classroom that disrupts class order — helping keep the class running smoothly and preventing the spread of inappropriate content. Teachers can mute a student from within the class settings.

Teachers can mute a student's chat; once muted, that student can no longer send content in the class group.

1. Right-click a member.
2. Select Mute.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff5c266e6d326de54170e68fa73265cf47045bd2bf16870efb7fb49b727c2502a_140946?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=197a135423315409d5640ca3c4ba8467ca5308ed)

Go to the Chat module.
2. Press and hold a message sent by the student, then select Mute.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F84ba03ee15367b5c58422adcaa292dfa1af4bec427a702b81ed7f83866aa20a8_498679?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=0b589b9525e8fbb501b2c1796f85a5180594c23a)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Muting All Students in the Class"
source_title_zh: "班级全体学生禁言"
```

## V. Muting All Students in the Class

When students in a class post inappropriate remarks or unsuitable topics to the whole group, or students create temporary classrooms without permission and disrupt class order, the class teacher can enable "Mute All Students" in the class settings to prevent inappropriate content from spreading, and to maintain class order and a good learning atmosphere. This measure helps teachers maintain class discipline and protects students' right to learn.

Teachers can mute an individual student's chat, or mute all students in the class at once; once muted, students can no longer send content in the class group.

1. Click Home in the left navigation.
2. Find and enter the class.
3. Click the class name in the top-left corner.
4. In Class Settings, go to Class Management.
5. Turn "Mute All Students" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fc5d4f29096709290b7eaa2d9e9fbc713f111ef9fb65850f95185c266b9d89989_329102?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=55db610f19300aadd01ac900baecced43db6589f)

Go to Home in the bottom navigation, find and enter the class.
2. Tap ">" to the right of the class name.
3. Tap Class Management.
4. Turn "Mute All Students" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7d2d840ea92859a02c0a9dff7fdaedac34f66433e471264e075667f8b33930dc_302070?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a63a3acf074f665060711e8cc886d34b3ce3bf28)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Class Chat History"
source_title_zh: "班级聊天记录"
```

## VI. Class Chat History

If you want to forward multiple messages from the class chat to a friend or another class, you can use the multi-select feature. In the class group chat, right-click a message, select "Multi-Select," check the messages you want to forward, then click "Forward One by One."

Chat history cannot be saved — only forwarded.

Multi-selecting chat history is not currently supported on phone or tablet.

1. Go to Messages.
2. Go to the class group.
3. Right-click a message.
4. Select Multi-Select.
5. After multi-selecting messages...
6. Click Forward, Save As, or Save to Cloud Drive.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F74633b70fdcf24aab9ffc89b2f20c5f914a77b83ea1220c21ae8e90acd8f029d_194670?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a9520a08e9bdbd39760f610525209a7159d0f379)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Class Temporary Classroom"
source_title_zh: "班级临时教室"
```

## VII. Class Temporary Classroom

A class temporary classroom can meet a variety of specific needs, including but not limited to temporary meetings, course discussions, supplementary teaching, and after-class communication.

Any member of a class (including teachers and students) can create a temporary classroom in the class chat area. Whoever creates the temporary classroom — teacher or student — takes on the role of lead teacher within that temporary classroom, while the other class members (teachers and students alike) join as students to listen in. A class temporary classroom only supports 1v6 teaching mode — one lead teacher and six students shown with camera video on stage, with other students listening in below the stage.

Both class teachers and students can start a temporary classroom. If you need to prevent students from creating temporary classrooms freely, class teachers can apply "Mute Individually" or "Mute All" to students in the class settings — muted students will not be able to send any messages in the class chat area or create a temporary classroom.

The temporary classroom does not have a "class notes" feature.

The temporary classroom's grace period for running over is 1–2 minutes; after the same person creates a temporary classroom, they must wait until the grace period ends before they can create another one.

If teaching staff want to configure the default state for whether newly created classes allow or prevent creating temporary classrooms, this can be set in the Backend Management System under "Default State: Allow Members to Create Temporary Classrooms."

1. Start a Temporary Classroom below.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fefd71e8e4dce39f94423855adf8cab6fb75f0c60e9174d199a6f8c42dee3dc4e_145686?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=23f0afc05d90fd2352831ebdcfe5b37e2b7c6624)

Tap "+" below, then create a Temporary Classroom.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F11fe6d077dec5ab71508aebd43b5eac2490ed63a56a6349b3b7fa5727549cf65_474845?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=52e889c62774773779c7d8daa0b638db29d6a1a1)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Pinning a Class Message"
source_title_zh: "置顶班级消息"
```

## VIII. Pinning a Class Message

Teachers in a class can right-click (or press and hold, on phone or tablet) a message — their own or one sent by another class member — and pin it to the top of the class, so it's prominently visible to all class members.

1. Right-click a message you or someone else sent, then select Pin (click the "x" to the right of a pinned message to unpin it).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7ea4be50a3f713297e7e491ae964876f476577998d9a82113c156b8df009e763_163916?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cbd128e02ed020cc2b402cdfab5e8803b613eabe)

Press and hold a message you or someone else sent, then select Pin.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F9cddd719ef296109e18f0ab3952d7353886cb77fbf5824f03c119f00f1551d9a_510497?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f5ca9ac4355aa25840f1c67bfab4bfd09fbd19fc)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Hiding a Student's Message"
source_title_zh: "屏蔽学生消息"
```

## IX. Hiding a Student's Message

"Head teachers" and "teachers" can hide messages sent by students.

"Head teachers" can hide messages sent by teachers.

When a student posts an inappropriate remark or image in the class, the class's "head teacher" or "teacher" can hide that student's message to help maintain class order. A hidden message cannot be recovered, and other class members will no longer be able to see its content.

1. Right-click a message sent by a student, then select Hide.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F924cfa605c4a2d60ab58d99c0755aa41556496eb72232dfda558882cfa8253c8_144519?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a9c6f4ee53fdc04a362d9799b4a4af99c2213a33)

Press and hold a message sent by a student, then tap Hide.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Faef93c2f14854b8ec102005fa78e588c454f69e1afe2c32629adb59b916f1140_515609?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c8aa38a3942bb5fcaff01369adc92c9ec0e0f6ee)

# 7. Classroom (Part 1: Entering Class, Student Trophies, Student Tools)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Entering the Classroom for Class"
source_title_zh: "进入教室上课"
```

## Entering the Classroom for Class

## I. Entering the Classroom for Class

## Applies to
Lead teachers, co-teachers, class session students, auditors, and transfer students.

## Usage Notes
The class session's lead teacher or co-teacher(s) can enter the classroom 20 minutes before the official start time; students can enter 10 minutes before. For example: if class officially starts at 16:00, the teacher can enter as early as 15:40, and students as early as 15:50.

Between when the class session is created and 20 minutes before the official start time, the classroom is a preparation room, not the formal classroom. If the time to enter the formal classroom arrives while the teacher is still in the preparation room, the teacher needs to leave the preparation room and enter the formal classroom before they can interact and teach with students.

Teachers and students can enter the classroom by tapping the "Start Class" button on the ClassIn home page, or by finding the class session in the Schedule and tapping "Start Class."

Note: if a teacher or student exits the classroom during the grace period for running over, they cannot re-enter — there is no entry point available. (For example, if a class session is set to officially start at 16:00 with a 30-minute duration, 16:30–16:50 is the grace period; once the grace period ends, the classroom closes automatically.)

## Steps

### Computer
1. Click the Dynamic Island at the top of the client.
2. In the pop-up window, click Start Class.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fe5e0c5809ea0f0e45d9bae70b12d9bfa25be0212ad4ebad5afe45b51aae9ae23_125600?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cf85d8b6707c9b8e883fa20ed439893c7fccca7b)

### iPad
1. Tap the Dynamic Island at the top.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fe8aee9f3b6d13b5b7d81f2ba8167a4d2d5223547eb732864ca2425e74ea1e94c_557141?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4de7eb404688fb92805eedd721d9b268094b5c70)

### Phone/Android tablet
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation bar.
2. In the pop-up window below, tap Start Class.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F15a41613a0b11fdbeabea46deeea735ea075f7592ea24d510eeeb802c4c13b2f_532893?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b371620566cf044a9606424f9d2c54217ac3f84c)

## II. Entering the Classroom on Two Devices

Applies to "lead teachers" and "co-teachers."

## When to use this
If a teacher needs to draw or write on the whiteboard but doesn't have a graphics tablet handy, they can enter the classroom on a computer, then log into ClassIn on an iPad or phone and enter the same classroom to temporarily use it as a writing tablet.

In a class session, a "lead teacher" or "co-teacher" can use two devices for teaching at the same time. Once a teacher enters the classroom, they can choose, in settings, whether the primary or secondary device's camera, microphone, and speaker are in use. Note: only the lead teacher or co-teacher(s) can enter the classroom on two devices — students cannot use this feature.

### Computer: switching audio/video between two devices

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F9e55c3647f07c30d84bbf52019d2da76209591aa108715bd7a9a929ef18e044f_284136?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=57c82449c928ae71e3d98aa85957c61e5844ad65)

### iPad: switching audio/video between two devices

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fce5b83a4bc1ec72e97e044ca80fad4b9dbf59df5a5ef92dc58fc2342aeb6771c_649721?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f2abb025d1aded5044bfc16323be0f16c3e21420)

### Phone/tablet: switching audio/video between two devices

## Student Trophies

## I. Giving a Trophy to a Student

### Applies to
Lead teacher, co-teacher(s).

### When to use this
When a student performs exceptionally well in class, the teacher can send them a trophy as a reward.

### Notes
Teachers using an Android phone or Android tablet don't have quick-action buttons below the classroom camera view; they can award trophies using the roster tool in the classroom instead.

If "Trophy" doesn't appear among the buttons below a student's camera, go to "Change Buttons Below Student Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

### Related Articles
"Changing the Trophy Style"

### Steps

#### Computer/iPhone/iPad
1. Click a student's camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, click Trophy.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa88afabbc01043e4a566f76d1afffa098779ed4a57a9dc6583406e17e81e2469_106925?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a886285ffd0e78c015763882f7703555164c644a)

## II. Trophy for All Students on Stage

Android phones and Android tablets do not have an "All-Student Trophy" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "All-Student Trophy" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Click your own camera.
2. In the buttons that pop up below, click the All-Student Trophy button.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fdfe1fa9f608ec33a8ca45126aaff85a972df630bc93dd12b65c3d596c6decbe5_101334?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=550ac5efe46ce2c3f04a4ab62ffbc86fbe8ea35d)

## III. Giving a Trophy to a Student from the Roster

### Usage Notes
How students can check how many trophies they've earned in the classroom:

**Method 1:** if a student is on stage, they can see their trophy count in the bottom-right corner of their own camera feed.

**Method 2:** if a student is off stage, they can open the roster on the right side of the classroom, and find the trophy count column to see their specific count.

#### Computer
1. Click Roster on the right side of the classroom.
2. Find the student.
3. Click Trophy on the right.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F855edbcd82c238d1513a43a0395e6116205f4a5d17b4db7e3f8eacaf6faa122d_149948?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=bc04b8ff87cad669784f99484bebcc79faeeedc5)

#### iPad
1. Click Roster in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Feab104451ec6647bbde9258bd50f38455154e1864615676f5da8c64b6eea15ac_239503?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=20b9f6edaa9ffc2b1c61565624be261492b9a247)

#### Phone/Android tablet

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fbbe2f7f8c7c63a78670899059db837251e0c35f0279f6a99690321353f7c27d9_170607?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ca3fe27d442bdc38c3d164a22e4703c620f22422)

## IV. Deducting a Student's Trophies

Deducting a student's trophies is not supported on phone or tablet.

If "Authorize" doesn't appear among the buttons below a student's camera, go to "Change Buttons Below Student Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Click the student's camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, right-click Trophy.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F2e59429ee7f0a6ef888ac69bca4bfe9e664d6ed72bc904e07862de5ca1f87af0_107539?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=66322724a4e62d74bfce7eea3f0f097650eca9d7)

```yaml
title: "Student Tools"
```

## Student Tools

## I. Tool Comparison Before and After Student Authorization

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7ea7238f4789306d5db78fb39f763887fb46e0f97c31ba945a4c1a756490003d_310627?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b9ccfbde49d7f25b725400f82aac430a3bc1357c)

## II. Authorizing a Student

### Applies to
Lead teacher, co-teacher(s).

### When to use this
In the classroom, to keep students actively engaged and improve teaching effectiveness — for example, when a student needs to draw or type on the whiteboard, or trigger a PPT animation — the teacher can individually authorize that student to use teaching tools, so they can complete a learning task or present their work more easily.

### Notes
Teachers using a phone or tablet (Android or HarmonyOS) don't have quick-action buttons below the classroom camera view; they can authorize students to use teaching tools using the roster tool in the classroom instead.

A student can be authorized by the teacher whether they're in a seat on stage or off stage.

Up to 15 students can be authorized in the classroom at the same time. Once that limit is reached, authorizing another student automatically revokes authorization from whichever student was authorized first.

If a student scribbles carelessly on the whiteboard, it may disrupt the teacher's lesson. If this becomes a problem, the teacher can revoke the student's whiteboard drawing permission — i.e. revoke their authorization.

If "Authorize" doesn't appear among the buttons below a student's camera, go to "Change Buttons Below Student Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

There's no separate teaching toolbox on the student side — once a teacher opens certain tools within the toolbox, students can use them at the same time.

### Related Articles
"Preventing Authorized Students from Scrolling the Whiteboard"
"Automatic Authorization for Whiteboard Area"

### Steps

#### Computer/iPhone/iPad
1. Click the student's camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, click Authorize (click again to revoke authorization).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fadc87d20a0e4fc20dea88104bc2882c2b3215d07588cdf35274dedac7f4f69c8_159327?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=63c54a1f5ef05c06df019583bfa2571166f890ed)

## III. Auto-Authorizing Students Who Join the Stage

In the classroom, to encourage teacher-student interaction, teachers can enable "Auto-Authorize on Stage." Once enabled, as soon as a student joins the stage, they're automatically authorized by the system to use teaching tools — without needing to wait for the teacher to manually authorize them; and when the student leaves the stage, the system automatically revokes their authorization. This significantly improves classroom interaction efficiency, freeing up more time for teaching and discussion. It also saves teachers the time and effort of manually authorizing students, improving teaching efficiency. Once "Auto-Authorize on Stage" is enabled, a gold rotating crown icon appears in the top-right corner of the teacher's camera; once disabled, the icon disappears automatically.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have the "Auto-Authorize Students on Stage" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Auto-Authorize Students on Stage" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Click your own camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, click Auto-Authorize on Stage.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F201818bb4ab928484cb360c6494a2752f8cca1108d565780a4e3db18168b1f54_163602?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=89ff18eb5ad2971493b5958a9c96e64c6089603f)

## IV. Authorizing All Students on Stage

### Usage Notes
When the lead teacher wants all students on stage to join in drawing or typing on the whiteboard, triggering PPT animations, or otherwise taking part in classroom interaction, they can use the "Authorize All" feature to make this happen more efficiently.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have the "Authorize All" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Authorize All" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons below the camera, click Authorize All (click again to revoke).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff2c1d0ae32a29a80ccf0232f1ee2179d21f1a20a7ffbf4b9450fa0cae48728e7_150746?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cc82abb8cf730619bf952aa9cb2fdd0d27c87539)

## V. Revoking All Students' Authorization

If a teacher notices during class that a student has been messing with courseware or elements on the whiteboard without permission, and can't tell exactly who's responsible, they can use "Revoke All Authorization." This turns off teaching tool access for every authorized student in the classroom, both on stage and off. This effectively prevents students from disrupting the lesson content without permission.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have the "Revoke All Authorization" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Revoke All Authorization" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons below the camera, click Revoke All Authorization.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F51fe2038c735cb45a94e936a6e313b512124e65107558ea3547c6a09c4b0e4ed_138292?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=682cdbdbf532a408c68d54279b3c411e1520cb00)

## VI. Authorizing a Student from the Roster

#### Computer
1. Open Roster on the right side of the classroom.
2. Find the student.
3. Click Authorize on the right (click again to revoke).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F90ceb6b7b867d87a5fecb8e56ef9ecc2d4811e79ab4d84f64ebb7c3af11229c3_143906?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=7b6ced3dd21533594eeaf3ba7d927f2e367fc91f)

#### iPad
1. Open Roster in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.
2. Click Authorize (click again to revoke).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb0dff1c45626e26027f7978bcd19443d62212b7fc8302f50ad7aed52d26b3521_158772?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=76e2fc0fbbc35a9dd4a970bbeeecab4921df5b67)

#### Phone/Android tablet

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F1dcd6b0b93c36bb15252a7acb85378132d11dc426cad5f0d91dc3d84dea3069b_124699?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=e703a1ca3e281cc5200993e307bda4673153dc0d)

# 7. Classroom (Part 2: Personal Audio/Video Settings — Microphone)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Microphone"
source_title_zh: "麦克风"
```

## Microphone

## I. Microphone Mode

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
While using ClassIn, users may run into the following microphone issues:

A computer user turns on their microphone in the classroom, the microphone icon shows green, but there's no sound when they speak — even after using "Fix Hardware Driver," and even though the microphone works fine in other software.

A computer user turns on their microphone in the classroom, but the microphone toggle keeps automatically switching back to "disabled."

An Android phone or Android tablet user turns on their microphone in the classroom, but there's no sound when they speak.

For the cases above, computer users experiencing this issue are advised to try checking "Legacy Mode 1" or "Legacy Mode 2" under "Microphone Mode" in ClassIn settings. Android phone or tablet users can enable "Microphone Mode" in settings.

### Notes
After a computer user changes "Microphone Mode," ClassIn must be restarted for the change to take effect.

After an Android phone or tablet user enables "Microphone Mode," they should tap the "Start Class" button again to re-enter the classroom.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change Microphone Mode.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F6ffce8b5878b2d1c0fda26d3d505a7ef03e1c839d57e87237c62dae45611ce0f_140092?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=460596919b8c37c9d2050a8b8fed6c6edc9009dc)

#### Phone/tablet (Android)
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Go to App Settings.
4. Go to Advanced Settings.
5. Turn Microphone Mode on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7016953bd6f18ddf3a8e44d3759f8be831bc27b005001c5ff2c90593f60df6e1_265628?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5fe186c3d538618fd14a57269a0b37f1ed735db4)

## II. Fixing the Microphone

If a user's built-in Windows sound recorder works fine locally, but they run into these microphone issues in a ClassIn classroom, this feature can also help fix the microphone:

No waveform movement while speaking.

Waveform moves while speaking, but there's no sound.

We recommend restarting your computer after fixing the microphone.

Phones and tablets don't have "hardware driver fix" — if you run into this kind of issue on phone or tablet, try restarting the device instead.

Mac computers don't have a "Fix Hardware Driver" feature. If this happens on a Mac, first check whether "Microphone" access is authorized for ClassIn in your Mac's local settings, and grant authorization if not. If it's already authorized and the issue persists, try restarting your computer.

#### Computer (Windows)
1. Go to System Settings.
2. Scroll the right-side scrollbar all the way down.
3. Under Hardware Driver Fix, click Fix.
4. (If a firewall prompt blocks it, click Allow or Yes.) Click Fix Microphone; once it reports the fix is complete, we recommend restarting your computer.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F568f4ed71d6913ec92663110d17f926ee601dcfe739b35d04aec64f4d000e9fe_383168?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4d08f4532f3c9dcae9b12a49f1ce0b94601dcb85)

## III. Microphone Gain

When taking class on a phone or tablet, if your own voice sounds too quiet, note that the device's physical volume buttons only adjust speaker volume, not microphone gain. In that case, exit the classroom and enable "Auto Microphone Gain" in the app settings to boost your speaking volume, then re-enter the classroom.

On computer, the classroom supports adjusting microphone volume directly.

#### Phone
1. Turn Auto Microphone Gain on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fab7e3ed13cc8cdfa0918d517bb84665ce4f3ae891d1d4e705b031857a0c23bb5_268786?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=6c1774149199d068a53bd2f6fea575491df3b8b3)

#### Tablet
1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F229c5fd2073bf5e43a3e6d95cc719099cffad1cd8328a5c5f0483c73ec0d00a9_525749?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=de8b3901efb7440c647ee3ae4b391027b7565b30)

## IV. Enabling Microphone Boost in Music Mode

If the teacher in a classroom has enabled Music Mode, and a Windows computer user's voice sounds too quiet, that user can enable "Enable Microphone Boost in Music Mode" in classroom settings. Once enabled, ClassIn must be restarted and logged back in for it to take effect.

### Usage Notes
This feature only supports Windows computers.

1. Turn "Enable Microphone Boost in Music Mode" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F66a06be44e84030f34c3ef23d545bcfcf8a2d495a3d6b5c293df916f51ba3b48_179367?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=10541920c48b7bfca36c1b799879a13299e7e6c1)

## V. Microphone AI Noise Reduction

If a user's surroundings are too noisy while taking class on a phone or tablet, making it hard for others in the classroom to hear them clearly, they can try enabling "AI Noise Reduction" in app settings to improve this.

On computer, the classroom supports enabling background noise reduction.

Once a teacher enables Music Mode in the classroom, noise reduction for classroom users won't take effect, in order to ensure instrument sound comes through properly. Conversely, if Music Mode isn't enabled in the classroom, users' noise reduction will work as expected.

1. Turn AI Noise Reduction on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff00c3a2b0ab2ea6dd96ebaa97318a05b885bde949e87a010d763ded586842dc2_266281?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cc9a17943d5f9328184e60acd2471d32282d7e5c)

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fca7bb27ef2367090386b763d054c8688ce2962a6e96ac44946bed727288aa5ac_516282?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4331bdc9e02403bb36c4d4cbee5e933f1a5c2206)

## VI. Opening Audio a Different Way

For iOS iPhone or iPad users, in certain situations while using ClassIn, and with AI Noise Reduction already enabled, you can try turning on "Open Audio a Different Way." Specific situations include:

**Screen-mirroring issue:** if you mirror the ClassIn screen from your iPhone or iPad to a TV, but the TV can't play ClassIn's audio properly even though other apps on your phone or tablet play sound fine, you can try turning on "Open Audio a Different Way" (with AI Noise Reduction already enabled).

**Microphone issue:** if your voice sounds too quiet in the classroom on iPhone or iPad after enabling AI Noise Reduction, you can try turning on "Open Audio a Different Way" (with AI Noise Reduction already enabled).

"Open Audio a Different Way" can only be enabled on iPhone or iPad after AI Noise Reduction has been enabled in Advanced Settings.

Computers and Android phones/tablets do not have an "Open Audio a Different Way" feature.

#### iPhone
1. Tap Home in the bottom-left corner.
2. First enable AI Noise Reduction, then turn "Open Audio a Different Way" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fd7f172416f2fbfa2ad14ef2b24663fa1cfd66b53173ebab7a0e5115788683b51_1132561?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=08322619d18bf16aac3d69f1e86aa7b3838ddabb)

#### iPad
1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. First enable AI Noise Reduction.
3. Toggle "Open Audio a Different Way."

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb968a121ca20eca413649f956a0091b4f5eef4a5a07e5a2580fce85cb75d19de_526165?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f34540ef66e51939e0d59dc74ab8b6a5a635ed74)

# 7. Classroom (Part 3: Managing Student Audio/Video)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Managing Student Audio/Video"
source_title_zh: "管理学生音视频"
```

## Managing Student Audio/Video

## I. Camera

## 1. Inviting a Student on Stage

### Applies to
Lead teacher, co-teacher(s).

### When to use this
During teaching, to encourage students to interact and share their answers, teachers can quickly invite a student on stage to answer a question using the roster tool. If the student has their camera enabled, their live camera feed will show once they're on stage — a more direct way to see the student's performance and answer.

### Usage Notes
Once the on-stage seats are full, inviting another student on stage from off-stage will bump the student who joined the stage earliest back off stage.

Students cannot be invited on stage in a 1v0 class type.

### Notes
In the classroom, the "lead teacher" or "co-teacher" can only control whether a student's camera feed is shown on stage — they cannot control whether the student's camera itself is turned on or off. Only the student can turn their own camera on or off.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Open Roster on the right side of the classroom.
2. Find the student.
3. Click Go on Stage (click again to bring them off stage).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb277e5bfb9be79fb780e81298dc1d2e82d41a62684433f243e60b78be47f2856_141677?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=862d73134eab1b3622cf0aadeabfc29a84503cee)

#### iPad
1. Open Roster in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fde207d3e1d4a1a190bafaf0159ee43c7129b9212223e981eeda7b5bc59aa7cda_157150?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=df7ce81ae524e8f4492a81de8cf2f6ec9c36eccc)

#### Phone/Android tablet

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8e9f21adb3cbd5a586a974915a5c1ecec95ed07ccf5fe9de7800451b1f4c91a8_129500?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=e9227535fb5c3c981fe02271e080d8a837719817)

## 2. Sending a Student Off Stage

Once a student has finished answering on stage and there's no longer a need to show their camera feed, teachers can send the student off stage using the quick-action buttons below their camera. If a student is being disruptive while on stage, the teacher can similarly send them off stage.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have an "Off Stage" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below a student's camera. If "Off Stage" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Student Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

#### Computer/iPhone/iPad
1. Click the student's camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, click Off Stage.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F760d35587d7fa6dd9150023771a6c24d45655001b4e7f22371935f0eaaa54e40_60338?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=5b4023e6601c0260b475da1374f8e70f61b9b551)

## 3. Sending All Students Off Stage

Android phones and Android tablets do not have an "All Off Stage" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "All Off Stage" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Click your own camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, click All Off Stage.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F19106b6d46bfd598b3a3d2ad544c5b2e5561b9d2056d5d04ebe36a13a609f9d9_107336?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=0f361761c9a0d9f5a246c333cb2fee6fcd1ab69c)

## 4. Swapping Students on Stage in One Click

Once a group of students has finished answering questions or presenting their work, teachers can use the "Swap Students on Stage" quick-action button to send all current on-stage students back off stage and invite the next group on — improving classroom efficiency.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have a "Swap Students on Stage" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Swap Students on Stage" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons below the camera, click Swap Students on Stage.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F5ee0e2ec9318a6f1868efff5aa10acd05391a6428100fddae598f6cb460b9557_117383?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4a550bc142542e6e3ddfbb6d5b32ccf081be6d91)

## 5. Rotation

If a teacher wants students' cameras to rotate through display on stage, they can enable the rotation feature in the roster.

Enabling rotation lets students take turns showing their camera on stage.

On mobile, only iOS phones and tablets support rotation (i.e. rotating students automatically onto the stage); Android and HarmonyOS phones/tablets do not have this feature.

1. Turn Rotation on/off in the bottom-right corner.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ffed48fd8d3ec48f8788e8f6d97c9e15e3d48ba400307432b15101f5076d7b718_160386?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=c18479d1fd3ad75080cc0e79f515a90ef5f08abf)

## 6. Inviting a Student with Their Hand Raised on Stage

### Related Articles
"Hiding the Student Raise-Hand Button"

When a student raises their hand, the raise-hand button in the bottom-right corner of the classroom (from the teacher's view) starts blinking. The teacher can hover over the raise-hand button and then invite the student who raised their hand on stage.

## 7. Auto-Invite on Raised Hand

Once a teacher enables "Auto-Invite on Raised Hand," any subsequent student who raises their hand will be automatically invited on stage by the system — without the teacher needing to do this manually.

iPhone/Android phones/Android tablets do not have an "Auto-Invite on Raised Hand" feature.

1. Tap the Raise Hand button in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.
2. Turn "Auto-Invite on Raised Hand" on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F29fe06b52be0f0cb182dc828ce6dacf0a140e8b34394ace8fb0f306ec09a0f95_100834?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=8cae544ce88a2245c9b56fafbc602ce7b75457a4)

## 8. Private Video Chat Between Teacher and Student

While teaching, if you need to address a specific student's issue privately — for example, to redirect a student who's being disruptive — a co-teacher can use the 1-on-1 private chat feature to temporarily pull themselves and that student into a separate room. In this room, only the teacher and the pulled-in student are present, which avoids disrupting the lead teacher's pacing. The lead teacher can also use this feature to communicate privately with a student and resolve something that needs to be handled one-on-one.

The private chat feature in the classroom is actually implemented via a breakout room. In the breakout room, you can use the same set of tools for communication and discussion. For details on how to use these tools, see the "Group Discussion" usage guide.

Phones and Android tablets cannot initiate a private chat invitation — they can only receive one sent by someone else.

Up to four buttons can display below a student's camera. If "Private Chat" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons below the camera, click Private Chat.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F788cc3d2854f063f8bc07c81effa5a05fd541482b79a8f117fc47496d5e74e26_325411?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a374bd83d7291508067c4e7d90d2c5ddf0806d80)

## II. Microphone

## 1. Muting All Students' Microphones

If several students' microphones are producing interference noise while they aren't speaking, the teacher can mute all students' microphones to prevent it from disrupting the lesson or other students' experience.

If echo occurs during teaching and the teacher can't pinpoint which student is causing it, the teacher can mute all students' microphones to eliminate the interference and its impact on teaching.

**How to tell whether the teacher has enabled "Mute All Students" in the classroom:** check whether there's a red microphone icon in the bottom-right corner of the teacher's camera feed. If not present, the teacher hasn't enabled mute-all; if present, they have.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have a "Mute All" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Mute All" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons that pop up below the camera, click Mute All (click again to unmute all).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8fa7273fb50692d98ad031ae5410402dc3870875105b622f60445d50413c86e7_123535?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=54935191b431d542d82223e68e33847963e9ca71)

## 2. Muting a Student's Microphone

When there are many students in on-stage seats, teachers can mute an individual student's microphone to help maximize teaching effectiveness and maintain good classroom order.

If a student's microphone produces interference noise while they aren't speaking, the teacher can mute that student's microphone to prevent it from disrupting the lesson or other students' experience.

If echo occurs in the classroom, the teacher can mute the microphone of the student causing it, eliminating the interference and its impact on teaching.

If a student on stage makes an inappropriate remark or disrupts the lesson, the teacher can mute that student's microphone to maintain classroom order and a good teaching atmosphere.

Teachers using an Android phone or Android tablet, which don't have quick-action buttons below the classroom camera view, can mute a student's microphone from the roster instead.

If "Mute" doesn't appear among the buttons below a student's camera, go to "Change Buttons Below Student Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons below the camera, click Mute (click again to unmute).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F606cbd83fd2929d8ff32dd2ac5cf712f640163b434ec48cceae047184dd42e67_156518?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=41c613f0af81502133b390e840c1df8155fddd9c)

## Classroom Courseware

## I. Opening Courseware

### Applies to
Lead teacher, co-teacher(s), authorized students.

### Usage Notes
In the ClassIn classroom, you can open courseware already uploaded to your cloud drive — for example, opening a Word document, playing an audio file (music, MP3), or playing a video file (MP4) all count as opening uploaded courseware.

### Notes
The classroom only shows organization cloud drive files belonging to the current class session's school.

### Steps

#### Computer
**Personal courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to My Cloud Drive, and open locally uploaded courseware.

**School/institution-authorized courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to Organization Cloud Drive, go to School Materials, and open the authorized courseware.

**Organization courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to Organization Cloud Drive, and open organization courseware.

**Resource Center courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to Resource Center, go to My Resources, and open courseware obtained from the Resource Center.

## II. Opening Resources for This Class Session

Lead teacher, co-teacher(s).

In the ClassIn classroom, teachers can open school-authorized courseware that can only be opened within this specific class session.

1. Open the Cloud Drive.
2. Go to This Session's Resources.
3. Find the authorized courseware under This Session's Resources.

## III. PPT Animations and Video Playback

## Applies to
## Usage Notes
In the classroom, if you need to play a PPT's animation effects or an embedded video, use the "Click Tool." Specifically: for animation effects, click the location in the PPT where the animation is, or click anywhere on the PPT slide to trigger it. For an embedded video, you need to click the play button inside the video frame to play it. If you don't click the play button inside the video frame, ClassIn won't trigger playback, and may jump straight past the current page to the next one.

## Steps

### (1) Playing an animation effect
1. Select the Cursor tool from the classroom's right-side toolbar.
2. Click the PPT's animation location, or click anywhere on the PPT slide, to trigger the animation.

Phone and tablet cannot view PPT thumbnails.

Only the user who opened the PPT can open its notes — other participants cannot see them.

PPT notes cannot be viewed on phone or tablet.

## V. PDF Page Navigation, Thumbnail Browsing, and Synchronized Scrolling

## When to use this
The following scenarios call for the PDF thumbnail feature:

In the classroom, when a user opens a PDF courseware document with many pages, they can use the PDF thumbnail feature to more easily see the document's outline. By showing PDF thumbnails, users can quickly get a sense of the whole document's content structure and jump directly to a specific page. This makes it easier to navigate and locate the information you need, improving the experience of using PDF courseware.

When a user is showing a PDF courseware document in the classroom that wasn't fully covered last time, they can use the PDF thumbnail feature to quickly jump back to where they left off. By clicking the relevant thumbnail, users can quickly jump to the page they need and precisely resume content that wasn't fully shown before. This significantly reduces the time spent searching for a particular page, improving classroom presentation efficiency.

On phone and tablet, once a PDF is opened, page navigation is not supported.

Phone and tablet cannot view PDF thumbnails.

## VI. Adjusting Courseware Volume

Everyone.

In the classroom, if a video courseware's volume sounds too quiet, you can adjust the volume for that audio/video courseware in the classroom, no matter who opened it — every classroom member can adjust its volume independently, since the adjustment only affects what you personally hear and doesn't affect anyone else.

Adjustments a user makes to audio/video courseware volume only take effect for that user, and won't affect what other classroom members hear.

On phone and tablet, the only way to make video sound louder is by adjusting the device's own volume.

## IX. Adjusting Courseware Display Size

Lead teacher, co-teacher(s), authorized students.

### When to use this
After a user opens a piece of courseware in the classroom, if the courseware window feels too small or too large, they can resize it. Resizing the window lets users browse the courseware more comfortably and enjoy a better visual experience. Resizable courseware includes: PDF courseware, PPT courseware, audio, video, Word documents, Excel spreadsheets, and any other file type the classroom supports opening.

#### Computer:
**Drag to resize:** hover the mouse over the edge of the courseware window; once the cursor turns into a double-headed arrow, click and drag the border to resize the window.

**Maximize window:** if the courseware window isn't already maximized, click the "Maximize" button in the top-right corner of the window to maximize it.

**Restore window size:** if the courseware window is already maximized, click the "Restore" button in the top-right corner of the window to return it to its non-maximized size.

#### Phone/tablet:
**Two-finger pinch:** place two fingers on the courseware area of the screen and pinch in or spread out to shrink or enlarge the courseware window.

# 7. Classroom (Part 5: Classroom Settings)

```yaml
title: "Classroom Settings"
source_title_zh: "教室设置"
```

## Classroom Settings

## I. Classroom Mode

## What is Classroom Mode?
"Classroom Mode" is a commonly used classroom setting. There are two modes: "Standard Mode," suited to purely online teaching, offering a clearer and more complete learning experience; and "Big Screen Mode," better suited to blended in-person/online teaching or touchscreen computers, offering a more intuitive and convenient way for teachers to operate.

## Applies to
Everyone.

## Usage Notes
On computer, ClassIn offers two interface styles for the classroom: "Standard Mode" and "Big Screen Mode."

In "Standard Mode," teaching tools sit on the right side of the classroom interface, and classroom settings sit in the top-right corner.

In "Big Screen Mode," teaching tools appear as a radial dial tool on the whiteboard, and classroom settings move to the bottom-left corner. On a touchscreen computer, you can four-finger-touch anywhere on the whiteboard to summon the radial tool to that location.

In the classroom, each user can set their own classroom mode; this setting only affects that user and doesn't affect anyone else in the classroom.

Switching classroom mode is equivalent to leaving the current classroom and re-entering. If a teacher switches classroom mode while recording, the recording will stop; once the switch is complete, the teacher needs to click Record again, and so on.

Besides switching within the classroom, users on computer can also switch mode from the local whiteboard, temporary classroom, or preparation room.

## Notes
"Classroom Mode" cannot be changed on phone or tablet.

## Steps

### Computer

#### Switching from Standard Mode to Big Screen Mode
1. Click More in the top-right corner of the classroom, then click Settings.
2. Go to General.
3. Check Big Screen Mode.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F7622c8b5a2d484cd9915109e029e4d51c4d7a376df70264927386ae98f6f5c16_162876?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=23c779e132fc9a7fd63d56c1960a9a1638eb800f)

#### Switching from Big Screen Mode to Standard Mode
1. Click More in the bottom-left corner of the classroom.
2. Click Settings.
3. Check Standard Mode.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fd5651f1640f733036bcca47681f276f7d333f3258f30469ee0b7e60312632b23_264964?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=870453ad753431fb5115aff570d169d2ea1a7cc2)

## II. Showing/Hiding the On-Stage Seats Area

## What is the classroom's on-stage seats area?
The on-stage seats area is the row at the very top of the whiteboard. It's used only to display teacher and student camera feeds — you cannot write on it.

"Lead teacher" and "co-teacher."

Besides choosing whether to show the on-stage seats area when creating a class session, once inside the classroom, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also show or hide the on-stage seats area under the classroom's More settings.

When the classroom shows the "on-stage seats area," a row of camera feeds appears at the top of the classroom, including the "teacher" and any "students the teacher has invited on stage." Even if the "teacher" or those "students" haven't turned on their own camera, their camera tile will still appear in the row.

When the classroom hides the "on-stage seats area," no camera feeds display at the top of the classroom (including the teacher's), and the entire interface becomes the whiteboard, which can be used for writing and similar actions, or for showing courseware full-screen. In this state, other classroom members can still hear the lead teacher speaking; if the lead teacher wants to show their own camera, they can quickly turn it on from the top-right corner of the classroom, and it will appear in the top-left area of the classroom. To show a student's camera, the teacher needs to invite the student on stage from the roster.

Both co-teachers and the lead teacher have permission to hide the on-stage seats area. Once either one hides it, the on-stage seats area disappears from every other teacher's and student's screen in the classroom.

Also, the teacher's on-stage seat rotation setting only takes effect while the on-stage seats area is shown.

On phone or tablet, this feature is called "Camera Area."

#### Standard Mode
1. Choose to Show or Hide the on-stage seats area.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F6951d9272d28449eb71cf1363cf4edbfbd8f1b8ece1b91d5b5a6f3df0d856c48_174465?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=361d6923afac1aceb973fdc2e6223e0c97376f5b)

```yaml
title: "Focus Mode"
source_title_zh: "专注模式"
```

## III. Focus Mode

## What is Focus Mode?
"Focus Mode" is a commonly used classroom setting. It's a classroom-management feature ClassIn designed specifically for classroom discipline, effectively preventing students from switching away from the classroom to play games, browse the web, or similar.

Backend administrators can apply a skin with "Enable Focus Mode" checked to a class, and formal classrooms under that class will have Focus Mode enabled by default. In addition, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also turn Focus Mode on or off under the classroom's More settings once inside the classroom.

Once Focus Mode is enabled: if a student enters the classroom on a Windows computer, the classroom window will stay maximized and pinned on top, unobstructed by other windows. If a student enters the classroom on a phone or tablet, switching to another app will automatically exit the classroom.

Focus Mode set by the lead teacher or co-teacher within the classroom only applies to the current classroom.

Only teachers using a computer or iPad can turn Focus Mode on or off in the classroom.

Focus Mode does not take effect for students using a Mac.

Focus Mode does not take effect for auditors.

If a student's device supports split-screen or similar features, Focus Mode may also fail to take effect.

1. Turn Focus Mode on or off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F29d25dd2ee8ae901e0544f5defbe8e4dcd62fcd24cffb4577d507847bc20fe11_164995?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=79506689ee3dd59f18c40c17c27276952eb282ce)

```yaml
title: "Raise Hand Sound Alert"
```

## IV. Raise Hand Sound Alert

## When to use this
When a student raises their hand in the classroom, the teacher's side automatically plays a raise-hand alert sound, so the teacher can still notice a student's raised hand while focused on teaching, writing on the board, or viewing courseware, and won't miss a chance to interact.

Once inside the classroom, the lead teacher and co-teacher can each set their own raise-hand alert sound independently, with no effect on each other.

In raise-hand alert settings, teachers can choose no alert sound, or select a "ding," "tick-tock," or "ding-dong" sound as the alert.

The alert sound is only audible to the teacher themself — students in the classroom won't hear it.

Only teachers using a computer can set "Raise Hand Sound Alert" in the classroom.

1. Select a Raise-Hand Alert Sound.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fb3452805b09249aa67a07dd498ad286062d24e6b4b672d1b22f8918f2ea9b493_171909?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=d5966fdfdf7bdbcdac682af4ad8148b4a5959136)

```yaml
source_title_zh: "进出教室通知"
```

## V. Entry/Exit Notifications

Once inside the classroom, if the teacher enables entry/exit notifications in classroom settings, a pop-up notification will appear on the teacher's screen whenever a student joins or leaves the classroom, helping the teacher track attendance status in real time. (In Standard Mode, this notification appears next to the roster on the right; in Big Screen Mode, it appears in the bottom-left corner.)

The lead teacher and co-teacher can each set their own entry/exit notifications independently, with no effect on each other.

If the lead teacher has this feature enabled, they'll also be notified when a co-teacher joins or leaves.

Only teachers using a computer can set entry/exit notifications in the classroom.

1. Turn entry/exit notifications on or off.

## VI. Changing the Classroom Background

A classroom background can be set in advance in the Backend Management System; once inside the classroom, teachers can also set it themselves under the classroom's More settings. Once a teacher changes the classroom background, the new one takes effect immediately.

Teachers can choose from the system's built-in background images, or upload a local image as the classroom background. Uploaded images must be JPG format and no larger than 1MB.

A classroom background changed within classroom settings only applies to the current classroom.

Only teachers using a computer can set the classroom background in the classroom.

1. Go to Classroom Background.
2. Select or upload a classroom background image.

## VII. Window Layout

Dragging cameras, courseware, and widgets to preset positions with automatic resizing helps teachers quickly organize the classroom whiteboard interface, efficiently switch teaching scenarios, and stay focused on instruction and interaction.

Once inside the classroom, teachers can go to Window Layout under classroom settings to choose an existing layout template. Custom layout templates are also supported — you can add a template using either tiled mode (pane size and position are fixed and cannot be freely adjusted) or free-pane mode (pane size and position can be freely adjusted).

Once you've selected a template, drag a camera, courseware, or widget with the mouse while holding Shift on the keyboard to enter layout mode. In Big Screen Mode on a touchscreen, dragging a camera/courseware/widget with one finger and holding for 0.5 seconds also enters layout mode.

Only teachers using a computer can set the window layout in the classroom.

1. Click More in the top-right corner of the classroom.
2. Click Window Layout.
3. Select or add a layout template.
4. Drag a camera/courseware/widget with the left mouse button while holding Shift on the keyboard; once the yellow layout frame appears, you're in layout mode.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fe83f1aa3e2bc30e31fd57e0b62ce4a11f7b3e46828580d0c8cfaacf149eef79c_520968?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b01a56497c2de0333c6c48635478367a8113e384)

## VIII. Quick Help Request

"Lead teacher," "co-teacher," "student" (excluding auditors).

When a teacher or student in the classroom runs into an issue they can't resolve on their own, they can request assistance from the academic administrator in the "Backend Management System."

Once inside the classroom, teachers can check off the relevant teacher(s)/student(s) involved under Quick Help Request, describe the issue, and submit it. The academic administrator can view the issue details, an automatically captured screenshot from the teacher's/student's perspective, and the tagged individual(s) under classroom monitoring in the backend. Once the administrator replies, a reply window will pop up for the teacher in the classroom.

Once the class has a custom skin applied that includes the "Allow Students to Send Help Requests to the School Backend" setting, students in the classroom can also use the Quick Help Request feature on iPad or computer. Students describe the issue and submit it; the academic administrator can view the help request content and an automatically captured screenshot from the student's perspective under classroom monitoring in the backend. Once the administrator replies, a reply window will pop up for that student in the classroom.

Sending a help request is not currently supported on phone or Android tablet.

## IX. Pinning the Classroom Window

## What is pinning the classroom window?
Pinning the classroom window is a commonly used classroom setting. Computer users who want the ClassIn classroom window to always stay unobstructed by other software can pin the classroom window.

Users entering the classroom on computer, in Standard Mode, can click Pin under More in the top-right corner; once pinned, the classroom window will by default display above every other app; clicking again unpins it. In Big Screen Mode, the classroom window is full-screen by default, so this feature doesn't apply.

Phone and tablet cannot pin the classroom window — it's full-screen by default.

1. Click Pin or Unpin.

## X. Leaving the Classroom

For users entering the classroom on computer: in Standard Mode, click the "X" in the top-right corner of the classroom window to leave the current classroom; in Big Screen Mode, click "Exit" under More in the bottom-left corner. On phone or tablet, tap "Leave Classroom" under the Settings button.

For the lead teacher entering the classroom on computer: in Standard Mode, after clicking the "X" in the top-right corner of the classroom window, you also need to click "Leave (Just Me)" to actually leave the current classroom; in Big Screen Mode, click "Exit" under More in the bottom-left corner. On phone or tablet, first tap the Settings button, then select "Leave (Just Me)."

As long as you leave before the grace period for running over, you can re-enter the classroom for class. Once the grace period begins, you can no longer re-enter.

## XI. Ending Class for Everyone

"Lead teacher."

### When to use this
If a teacher finishes covering the lesson content earlier than expected, they can use "End Class for Everyone" in the classroom to end the class session early.

Provided the class skin applied to the classroom setting has "Allow Teachers to End Class Early" checked, once the lead teacher has started the formal classroom, they can click "End Class for Everyone" to end the class session early.

Once "End Class for Everyone" is triggered, all users in the classroom are automatically removed, the classroom is closed, and neither teachers nor students can re-enter it.

## XII. OMO Livestream Broadcast

## Prerequisites
A backend administrator must first enable the OMO livestream broadcast feature under School Settings → Value-Added Services in the backend, and then check "OMO Livestream Broadcast" when creating the class session.

If online students only need to watch the teacher's livestream broadcast feed within the classroom, without needing cloud recording, we recommend checking "OMO Livestream Broadcast" when creating the class session.

OMO livestream broadcast mode is a high-definition mode for recording the live scene. Once the lead teacher selects which camera feed to display in the OMO livestream broadcast settings, online students in the classroom can open the OMO livestream broadcast window in the bottom-right corner to watch the teacher's on-site broadcast more clearly. The lead teacher can also turn off OMO livestream broadcast mid-class; once turned off, online students in the classroom will no longer be able to see the broadcast feed.

When on-site recording mode and OMO livestream broadcast mode are both enabled, they cannot use different cameras separately — when the lead teacher selects a camera in on-site recording mode, OMO livestream broadcast automatically switches to that same camera, and vice versa.

On-site recording and OMO livestream broadcast are only supported for lead teachers using a computer or big screen (Windows) — other devices (such as phone/tablet) don't support them.

1. Enter the classroom.
2. Click OMO Livestream Broadcast in the top-right corner (bottom-left corner in Big Screen Mode).
3. In the settings at the top-right of the OMO livestream broadcast window, select a camera, then click Done; view the broadcast feed.
4. Shrink the OMO livestream broadcast window.

# 7. Classroom (Part 6: Personal Audio/Video Settings)

```yaml
title: "Personal Audio/Video Settings"
```

## Personal Audio/Video Settings

## I. Camera

## 1. Turning the Camera On/Off

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
When the on-stage seats area is shown, users can click the camera icon in the top-right corner of the classroom (bottom-left corner in Big Screen Mode) to quickly turn their own camera on or off. When the on-stage seats area is hidden, the lead teacher or co-teacher can click this same spot to quickly go on or off stage themselves.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click the camera icon in the top-right corner of the classroom to quickly turn your camera on/off.

## 2. Turning Dual Cameras On/Off

### What is dual-camera mode?
Dual-camera mode refers to a teacher choosing "1v1 Dual Camera" mode when creating the class session. In this mode, every on-stage user in the classroom can display two camera feeds at once, enabling multi-angle demonstration and teaching. This mode offers a more professional filming experience for teaching, letting students observe the subject more clearly and improving learning outcomes.

### When to use this
In teaching scenarios, dual-camera mode is commonly used for art classes, instrument lessons, calligraphy classes, arts-and-crafts classes, and similar. For example, in a piano lesson, both the teacher and student can turn on dual-camera mode at once — one camera captures the teacher's or student's face, and the other captures their hands on the instrument. This lets students see the teacher's fingering technique more clearly, and lets the teacher notice how the student is playing in time to give more targeted guidance.

Dual-camera mode only supports "1v1 class types" — that is, only one lead teacher and one student can show their cameras on the platform at the same time. The classroom will then show two cameras each for the lead teacher and the student. Note: to use dual-camera mode, the user's device must have two cameras in order to properly turn on two camera feeds in the classroom. This means users on phone or tablet cannot enter a dual-camera classroom for class.

### Notes
Teachers in a dual-camera mode classroom cannot use the "Auxiliary Camera" tool from the teaching tools.

1. Click the square icon in the top-right corner of the classroom.
2. Go to Primary Settings to turn the first camera on/off.
3. Go to Secondary Settings to turn the second camera on/off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F9f1884d9050fd2aacdf509b69ffdd107edf511029b475eae92c6cca9f9ce3c01_105811?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=1947401f8caaf35eb09f92d94530a56d01c76b1c)

## 3. Showing/Hiding the Co-Teacher's Camera

Lead teacher, co-teacher.

Once a co-teacher enters the classroom, their camera is hidden by default. The classroom's lead teacher can invite the co-teacher on stage to show their camera; the co-teacher can also invite themself on stage. Note that when a co-teacher goes on stage, they don't take up a spot in the on-stage seats meant for students or the lead teacher.

1. Open Roster on the right side of the classroom.
2. Go to Co-Teachers.
3. Click Go on Stage to send the co-teacher on stage or bring them back off stage.
