## 4. Switching Cameras

When a user takes class on computer with multiple cameras connected, they can switch cameras in classroom settings at any time.

When a user takes class on phone or tablet with the camera turned on, it defaults to capturing what's behind the device. Users can switch from the rear camera to the front camera in classroom settings.

In the ClassIn classroom, "front-facing" and "rear-facing" are the two common camera orientations. Front-facing means the camera points toward the person using the device; rear-facing means it points away, toward what's behind the device. Normally, when entering the classroom, the camera should point at yourself to ensure a correct video feed. If you find the video orientation is reversed after entering class, try adjusting the front/rear camera setting.

1. Click the arrow next to the camera icon in the top-right corner of the classroom.
2. Select the camera to switch to.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F9df8d0d12a9ca5a41d4f0be038e6a4aa2bca4ac34fedc2740c59a1eb6e59946a_58557?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=3f387501eeb8862c159f2a75291a65760566ce84)

Click the gear icon in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.
2. Under Orientation, switch between the front and rear cameras.

## 5. Rotating the Camera

Rotating the camera is supported for users on computer in the classroom. Once "Mirror Mode" is enabled, camera rotation is also supported.

Rotating the camera is not supported on phone or tablet.

1. Go to Settings.
2. Go to Video.
3. Rotate the camera angle in the top-right corner (rotation options: No Rotation, Rotate 90°, Rotate 180°, Rotate 270°).

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F91839ebaec837664ff878f4a2341768e8e60d01718476c7302bfa1d8dfdbecdc_133603?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=49d3b63acab2410b7170bf7aa6762713d1394848)

## 6. Camera Mirroring

There are two common scenarios in teaching where you'd need to consider toggling "Mirror Mode."

**Scenario one:** if a user is showing text or an illustration in a book via their camera, and other classroom members see the text or image reversed, the presenter needs to turn off camera "Mirror Mode" so it displays correctly.

**Scenario two:** while taking class, a user may notice that their own body movements appear reversed when they watch their own camera feed. Some users find this disorienting, in which case they can turn on camera "Mirror Mode" so their movements match what they see in their camera. Once this mode is on, the user's actual movements and the movements shown in their camera will match direction. Toggling camera mirror mode appropriately in these situations helps users present themselves more effectively.

1. Turn Mirror Mode on/off in the top-right corner.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fa97e2a6900b0033d72c6eaa6e7146f567d3df0c810f633f81f2ee3d41a008bbc_185525?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=bbdd397d3fba5154f95bc10cdee2137129dd17c7)

Turn Mirror Mode on/off under Mirroring.

## 7. Camera Virtual Background

Users on computer can use a virtual background for their camera.

The uploaded local image for a virtual camera background must be in PNG format.

Up to 10 local images can be uploaded; there's no size requirement for local images, and you can resize them after uploading.

Images larger than 2MB will have their resolution compressed to 0.6x.

Setting a virtual camera background is not currently supported on phone or tablet.

1. Go to Virtual Background.
2. Set the camera background.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fc4820045c583e7e59e7c8b597e0a7e942e8546583e4442d0d3cfe084b67b2880_123769?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=87f338d0b617b1c25a7f137c16a6d79bd478f273)

## 8. Moving the Camera Window

Teachers can drag or double-click their own or a student's camera to reposition it.

**Double-clicking a camera:** the teacher double-clicks their own or a student's camera to enlarge it from the on-stage seats onto the main whiteboard; double-clicking it again returns it to the on-stage seats.

**Dragging a camera:** the teacher drags their own or a student's camera from the on-stage seats onto the main whiteboard, and can drag it back to the on-stage seats too. Dragging a camera while holding Ctrl keeps its size unchanged as it moves from the on-stage seats to the whiteboard.

#### Computer/Phone/Tablet
1. The teacher double-clicks or drags their own or a student's camera onto the main whiteboard.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F0323efd614d1c67a67c5972f45f899ff1b28cf150ef80fee4a40510b5bdd5234_60624?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=85ad10ee96721103922854d432d82634e5cda5e6)

## 9. Resizing the Camera Window

Teachers can resize their own or a student's camera on the main whiteboard.

**Method 1:** teachers taking class on computer can hover the mouse over the edge of a camera; once the cursor turns into a double-headed arrow, click and drag to resize the camera. On phone or tablet, drag the camera's edge with your finger to enlarge or shrink it.

**Method 2:** while a camera is on the main whiteboard, the teacher can click and hold the camera and drag it toward the bottom-left or bottom-right corner of the classroom to shrink it.

1. Drag the edge of a camera on the main whiteboard to resize it.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F3abee7503b0490e3fa960a1549cf8aa71ed12563a0435310be5f4dbad70091ec_79480?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=7a8603563665273efb87a774723ce29b51c866da)

## 10. Tiling Camera Windows

Teachers on computer/iPhone/iPad can use the "Tile Cameras" feature from the quick-action buttons below their own camera to arrange all on-stage seat cameras evenly across the classroom whiteboard.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have a "Tile Cameras" feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Tile Cameras" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

#### Computer/iPhone/iPad
1. The teacher clicks their own camera.
2. Among the buttons below the camera, click Tile Cameras.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F79b71a41889970fd51df053796715d56722b88f17c729a7a6ca88699e7c74efd_126164?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=0f2a03cdf1c9d482b09565bdfdbc2ce76b3990c6)

## 11. Restoring Camera Windows

Teachers on computer/iPhone/iPad can restore all camera windows on the classroom whiteboard back to the on-stage seats.

Android phones and Android tablets do not have a camera restore feature.

Up to four buttons can display below the teacher's camera. If "Restore Cameras" doesn't appear, go to "Change Buttons Below Teacher Camera" in the "Backend Management System."

1. Among the buttons that pop up below the camera, click Restore Cameras.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ff0ff27756044c12414c20d5ed52721a65090db8e161d509196bb95662f94706e_108355?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=57577ad89907a47d81b3ea62dfb7e61df1800040)

## 12. Network Camera

When you need to show a live stream from a streaming platform in the classroom, you can use "Network Camera" to input the stream's pull URL as the video source, sharing the livestream with the rest of the classroom.

Teachers on computer can choose to use a network camera.

Phone and tablet do not have a "Network Camera" feature.

1. Switch from Local Camera to Network Camera.
2. Click Add Network Camera.
3. Enter the stream pull URL.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F49c9fdad22d92d3953f21f38743999169ce55382324943f96d15b433d0211f58_90452?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=0daf55b96bed663649270374f07897f80ff2f4aa)

## 4. Background Noise Reduction

When a computer user speaks using their microphone in the classroom, if other classroom members hear a lot of background noise mixed into their voice, the user experiencing the noise issue can enable "Background Noise Reduction" in classroom settings, reducing interference and improving voice call quality. If the user is on phone or tablet, they need to enable "Microphone AI Noise Reduction" in App Settings → Advanced Settings outside the classroom.

Once a teacher enables noise reduction, Music Mode is automatically disabled and won't take effect; conversely, if the teacher enables Music Mode, students' noise reduction won't take effect either.

1. Turn Background Noise Reduction on/off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F8eb3aff93fdc2bd06e604e340b82c56ef12115f270e7bb92458cfb02d4f92752_99953?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=e97c71efcdc41b343e2ca15d89699de003327ab4)

## 5. Music Mode

### What is Music Mode?
"Music Mode" in the classroom is a commonly used setting. Once a teacher enables "Music Mode," teachers and students in the classroom can experience a more authentic reproduction of instrument sound, making it come through more clearly, naturally, and true-to-life for every classroom member.

"Lead teacher" and "co-teacher."

Once a teacher on computer enables "Music Mode," to achieve a more authentic musical effect, both background noise reduction and echo suppression in the classroom will be disabled (the teacher's background noise reduction is turned off, and students enabling their own background noise reduction or AI noise reduction has no effect). Phone and tablet do not have Music Mode.

1. Turn Music Mode on/off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F1e50761335a509869b3d6dc3affd46a75952118bd22861a18d3daad084c22dbb_158156?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a9169122abda30eb58f295ea684b89689fe955fd)

1. Turn the Speaker on/off.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F07337892610cba2fbc947d99be10d376f2278f343f334964750e7601b6ab2e1e_236034?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=fcf89cbc58905edecc0bf02a64ae2bf2fb26c197)

## 2. Speaker Volume

If the sound you hear in the classroom is too quiet, you can adjust it in the following ways:

Users on computer can adjust the classroom speaker volume, or adjust it through the computer's system settings.

Users on phone or tablet can adjust volume using the physical volume buttons on the side of the device.

1. Adjust the classroom speaker volume.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Facf62bb66813f25f42299f29a6e3abffa94445eadbd96a4a4248c1b059ef8fae_91351?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=63286ffaad164bf5e70b6cad4c7edf14ef3800dc)

#### Phone/tablet
1. Adjust the speaker volume using the physical volume buttons on the side of the phone or tablet.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F074168a5e00d40f1146a6fc16a184663949a96847b6f78042a790fb8c7d18b86_302715?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=829c20fe3c526d0dbfd0938406dd1c1f737eac23)

## 3. Switching Speakers

Try switching speakers in the classroom in the following situations:

**Multiple speaker devices connected:** for users taking class on computer, if multiple speaker devices are connected simultaneously — for example, Bluetooth headphones, a wired headset, and speakers — you can switch speakers in the classroom to choose which device the sound comes from.

**No sound from an HDMI external display:** for users taking class on a laptop, if you've connected an external display via HDMI but find you can't hear any sound during class, and you've confirmed both the classroom's and the computer system's speaker volume are turned up, this may be because the external display doesn't have speakers, while the computer's audio output is set to the display. In this case, you can switch speakers in the classroom back to the laptop's built-in speakers.

**Wanting sound from an HDMI-connected TV:** for users taking class on a laptop, if you've connected to a TV via HDMI and want sound to come from the TV, you can switch speakers in the classroom to the TV's speaker.

Mac computers do not support switching the classroom speaker — the classroom's default speaker is the computer's local speaker.

Switching speakers is not supported on phone or tablet.

1. Under Select Speaker, choose the speaker to use.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F46fac9cefebdbfc105fd9a6015318ad6126223e8ca5d87f098b56cd186d52263_69470?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b4912efd07d2e8c5b501599e17b1a8e31c57e3bc)

## IV. Checking and Fixing Audio/Video

## 1. Checking the Microphone

All classroom members.

Users can check their microphone either inside the classroom or on the self-check page when entering the classroom, to make sure it's working properly.

Users on computer can go to classroom settings after entering the classroom, select the Audio tab, then select the microphone device to use. Then click the "Test" button on the right; a 10-second countdown begins, during which you can count from 1 to 10 while watching the sound-wave indicator below — if the indicator responds, the microphone is working properly.

Users on phone or tablet can, on the self-check page when entering the classroom, turn on their microphone, start speaking, and watch the sound-wave indicator below — a green wave indicates the microphone is working properly.

1. Select the microphone device to check.
2. Click the Test button on the right.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fac18a464b9521c92e76e146014aa22c528b086c38be583eb816b31c496dc1225_114924?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=dc05d58942b59074d9a7c18cbbc6e63bc8e21ac2)

After tapping Start Class, go to the Self-Check page.
2. Turn on the microphone, start speaking; a green wave indicates the microphone is normal.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fdc0c0cff5cd383de8413c23fd1d9c818f5e9e6ab73a82f9314c3880e06a551ef_392468?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=e927888e17cb302926f3b8be5c2667583a34f7a8)

## 2. Checking the Speaker

Users can check their speaker either inside the classroom or on the self-check page when entering the classroom, to make sure they can hear sound properly.

Users on computer can go to classroom settings after entering the classroom, select the Audio tab, select the correct speaker device, then click the "Test" button on the right — if the user can hear a drum sound, the speaker is working properly.

Users on phone or tablet can, on the self-check page when entering the classroom, turn on the speaker and click the test button — if they can hear sound, the speaker is working properly.

1. Click Check.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Ffe8a06567790f3ebc2acf7eb6676686ea39423cddf60d0b4957dac1381480142_111343?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=ab211781d33ae5acf574828cc5cf2cd241ef5a21)

Turn on the speaker, then click Test; if you can hear sound, the speaker is working normally.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F0a30abf1339d803422de385eadc96f6d7041b991a0ddc55f1b2ebe4ec16c55b8_399034?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=4d1bcd1ad34aac6f05d80c93479868bdd93d7435)

## 3. Fixing Audio/Video

All members.

When a user turns on their microphone in the classroom but there's no sound when speaking, they can try using the "Hardware Fix" feature in the classroom.

When a user's microphone option keeps automatically switching back to muted after they turn it on in the classroom, they can try using the "Hardware Fix" feature in the classroom.

When a user can't hear any other classroom member speaking, they can try using the "Hardware Fix" feature in the classroom.

When a user's camera video isn't displaying properly, they can try using the "Hardware Fix" feature in the classroom.

We recommend restarting your computer once the fix is complete.

Phone and tablet don't have a "Hardware Fix" feature in the classroom — if you run into the issues above, try restarting your phone or tablet instead.

Mac computers do not have a "Hardware Fix" feature.

1. Click Hardware Fix in the bottom-left corner.
2. Fix the relevant feature based on the symptom.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2F66b9a1db1b0ca71952d446d45a9a46713c81865896ab562a0535ba8479def35b_127385?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=1dc79f95076f5a58a82fecc040dd4400d88d27ca)

## Teaching Tools

## I. Click Tool

### What is the Click Tool?
The "Click Tool," also called cursor mode, is one of the commonly used tools in the classroom toolset. Teachers can use it to trigger animation effects in PPT courseware, play embedded audio and video in PPT courseware, and click through content on a webpage in the browser. It's also used to operate equipment in the virtual "Chemistry Lab" and "Physics Lab." When a teacher uses the "Student Screen Share" tool, the Click Tool can also control file operations on the student's desktop. Using the Click Tool lets teachers teach more flexibly and efficiently, improving teaching outcomes.

### Applies to
Lead teacher, co-teacher, authorized students.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Select the Cursor tool from the classroom's right-side toolbar.

## II. Select/Move

### What is the Select/Move Tool?
The "Select/Move" tool is one of the commonly used tools in the classroom toolset. Users can use it to single-select, multi-select, and move various whiteboard elements — images, shapes, text, and so on. Once you select an element on the whiteboard, a "secondary editing" bar pops up below it. Users can use the shortcuts in this bar to modify and adjust the selected element(s).

### Usage Notes
With the "Select/Move" tool, you can single-select or multi-select images, text, shapes, and other elements in the classroom, and further edit these elements once selected. "Box-select mode" lets you draw a rectangle on the whiteboard, selecting every element inside it. "Free-select mode" lets you draw a freeform lasso, selecting every element it encloses.

To use the "secondary editing" feature of the "Select/Move" tool, first click an element on the whiteboard; a row of functions for further editing the selected element appears below it. Users can use these functions to further modify and edit the currently selected element.

When multiple whiteboard elements are selected at once, you can change the color of all of them at the same time.

**(1) Secondary edits supported for image elements:**

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Cutout | Uses the secondary editing cutout feature to separate the subject in an image from the original background, making the background transparent. |
| Lock image position | Fixes an image at a specific spot on the whiteboard, preventing it from being accidentally dragged or deleted. The image must be unlocked before it can be moved, edited, or deleted. |
| Resize image | Changes the image's size on the whiteboard. |
| Change image layer | Adjusts the image's display layer on the whiteboard. When multiple images, shapes, or text overlap in the same spot, the one on a higher layer displays in front, unobstructed by other elements. |
| Duplicate image | Creates multiple copies of the image on the whiteboard. |
| Delete image | Removes the image from the whiteboard. |

**(2) Secondary edits supported for shape elements:**

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Change shape border color | Changes a shape's border color, making it stand out and stay distinguishable from other elements. |
| Add or change shape fill color | Adds a fill color to a shape on the whiteboard that doesn't have one, or changes the fill color of a shape that already does. |
| Lock shape position | Fixes a shape at a specific spot on the whiteboard, preventing it from being accidentally dragged or deleted. The shape must be unlocked before it can be moved, edited, or deleted. |
| Resize shape | Changes the shape's size on the whiteboard. |
| Change shape layer | Adjusts the shape's display layer on the whiteboard; a shape on a higher layer displays in front, unobstructed by other elements. |
| Duplicate shape | Creates multiple copies of the shape on the whiteboard. |
| Delete shape | Removes the shape from the whiteboard. |

**(3) Secondary edits supported for text elements:**

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Change text size | Changes the font size of text on the whiteboard. |
| Change text color | Changes the color of text already entered on the whiteboard. |
| Lock text position | Fixes text at a specific spot on the whiteboard, preventing it from being accidentally dragged or deleted. The text must be unlocked before it can be moved, edited, or deleted. |
| Change text layer | Adjusts the text's display layer on the whiteboard. When multiple images, shapes, or text overlap in the same spot, the text on a higher layer displays in front, unobstructed by other elements. |
| Duplicate text | Creates multiple copies of the text on the whiteboard. |
| Delete text | Removes the text from the whiteboard. |

### Notes
Secondary editing of elements is not supported on phone or Android tablet.

"Free-select" mode is not currently supported on phone or tablet.

1. Select the Select/Move tool from the classroom's right-side toolbar.
2. Single-select or multi-select whiteboard elements.
3. Once elements are selected, you can move them or apply secondary edits.

## III. Pen

### When to use this
The Pen tool is one of the classroom's commonly used teaching tools, packed with features that let users mark up, write, and draw on the whiteboard, courseware, and images. It supports drawing several shapes — circles, ellipses, squares, rectangles, irregular triangles, equilateral triangles, straight lines, and curves — as well as writing text.

Users can choose either the regular pen or a highlighter pen. The regular pen behaves like chalk, while the highlighter pen is semi-transparent, suited to highlighting key points on text, courseware, or images. Users can also choose between solid and dashed line styles.

The Pen tool also lets users freely adjust pen color and thickness, to meet different drawing and annotation needs. For users, the Pen tool substantially improves teaching interaction and classroom outcomes.

When a user selects "curve" mode and draws an irregular shape on the whiteboard (like a circle, square, straight/vertical line, or triangle), the system automatically performs shape recognition about 1.5 seconds after the user stops drawing. If recognition succeeds, the system converts the user's irregular shape into a regular one.

**(1) Pen modes and shortcuts:**

**Curve mode:** hold Shift to draw a straight line.

**Line mode:** hold Shift to draw a horizontal straight line.

**Square mode:** hold Shift to draw a perfect square.

**Circle mode:**
- Hold Shift to draw a perfect circle.
- Hold Ctrl to draw a circle centered on the point where you started drawing.
- Hold Shift+Ctrl to draw a perfect circle centered on the point where you started drawing.

**Shortcuts:**

Hold Alt and press "1," "2," "3," or "4" on the number pad to switch the pen to "curve," "line," "circle," or "square" mode, respectively.

Hold Alt and press "q," "w," "e," "r," "a," "s," "d," "f," "z," "x," "c," or "v" on the keyboard to change the pen color.

Hold Ctrl and press Z to undo the last drawing action.

Note: shortcuts and settings may vary across different software and operating systems. The above describes the general case — actual behavior may vary depending on your specific software and OS. (The "Ctrl" key on Windows corresponds to "Command" on Mac; "Alt" on Windows corresponds to "Option" on Mac.)

In highlighter pen mode, the pen defaults to a solid line and cannot be switched to dashed. The pen shape defaults to curve and cannot be selected or changed.

Shapes already drawn on the whiteboard cannot have their color changed using shortcuts — only via the secondary editing feature.

A shape that has been auto-converted into a regular shape cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z.

When a teacher or student draws or writes using the Pen tool in the classroom, everyone in the classroom can watch the drawing and writing happen in real time.

1. Select the Pen tool from the classroom's right-side toolbar.

## IV. Eraser

The eraser is one of the classroom's commonly used teaching tools. Users can use the eraser to erase content drawn or written with the Pen tool on the whiteboard, and it also includes a "one-click clear" feature — if you encounter whiteboard elements that can't be erased normally, use "one-click clear" to wipe the entire whiteboard clean.

The eraser cannot erase text entered with the "Text" tool.

The eraser cannot erase locked shape elements.

Students' eraser tool doesn't have the "one-click clear" feature.

Using "one-click clear" cannot be undone.

If a user accidentally deletes whiteboard content while teaching, they can try pressing Ctrl+Z on the keyboard to undo the last deletion.

The eraser cannot erase straight lines drawn using the Pen tool's "line" mode. To delete a straight line, first select it with the "Select/Move" tool, then delete it.

1. Select the Eraser tool from the classroom's right-side toolbar.

![](https://cofile.eeo.cn/res-store%2Fedaba5256e9acdbd1c518fd52e40ec301305afe1515b701db660f4914b5a2e69_70667?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDJQGsEOK2TfbFdEZifMnxrWx85mpdHj6H&q-sign-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-key-time=1773936000;1774540800&q-header-list=host&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=3f873fdb78c25e42ab7f3d2acc041e6a82540c08)

## V. Text Input

The Text tool is one of the classroom's commonly used teaching tools; users can use the "Text" tool to type any text, letters, or numbers onto the whiteboard or courseware. You can set font color and size before typing.

**(1) Text input shortcuts:**

Hold Alt on the keyboard, then press any of "1," "2," "3," or "4" on the number pad to adjust the font size.

Hold Alt on the keyboard, then press any of "q," "w," "e," "r," "a," "s," "d," "f," "z," "x," "c," or "v" to preset the font color.

When a teacher or student types using the Text tool in the classroom, everyone else in the classroom can watch the typing happen in real time.

The font-color and font-size shortcuts cannot modify content already written on the whiteboard.

Shortcuts and settings may vary across different software and operating systems. The above describes the general case — actual behavior may vary depending on your specific software and OS. (The "Ctrl" key on Windows corresponds to "Command" on Mac; "Alt" on Windows corresponds to "Option" on Mac.)

1. Select the Text tool from the classroom's right-side toolbar.

## VI. Screenshot

The Screenshot tool is one of the classroom's commonly used teaching tools. When you need to capture what's displaying in the classroom, use the Screenshot tool to grab a shot of the classroom. If you want to capture something on your computer desktop, use the "Hide Classroom Screenshot" feature within the Screenshot tool to capture your computer desktop outside the classroom. If you want to share an image or photo from your phone or tablet into the classroom, use the "Scan QR Code to Upload Image" feature within the Screenshot tool. If you're a computer user who wants to directly open a local image in the classroom, use the "Open Local Image" feature within the Screenshot tool.

On iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet, only the "Open image from local album" and "Take photo" features are available.

The "Laser Pointer" is one of the classroom's commonly used tools. When there's a lot of content on the whiteboard, teachers can use it to draw students' attention to a specific point, improving learning outcomes.

## VIII. Cloud Drive

"Cloud Drive" is available both on the ClassIn main interface and inside the classroom, and data between the two is fully synchronized. It's one of the classroom's commonly used tools — teachers and students can upload various local courseware resources (audio, video, documents, etc.) to Cloud Drive for safe, reliable storage, ready to be flexibly recalled during class. In the classroom, users can quickly find and display courseware they've uploaded via "My Cloud Drive → Documents." Public courseware the school has authorized for a lead teacher can be found and used under "Authorized Resources," and related textbooks a teacher obtained from the Resource Center will also appear under "Authorized Resources."

The classroom only shows organization cloud drive files belonging to the current class session's school.

**Personal courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to My Cloud Drive, and open locally uploaded courseware.

**School/institution-authorized courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to Organization Cloud Drive, go to School Materials, and open the authorized courseware.

**Organization courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to Organization Cloud Drive, and open organization courseware.

**Resource Center courseware:** open the cloud drive, go to Resource Center, go to My Resources, and open courseware obtained from the Resource Center.

## IX. LMS

## Applies to
## When to use this
The classroom's Learning Management System (LMS) is one of its commonly used tools. Through LMS, teachers can assign in-class assignments, quizzes, and answer sheets, and promptly grade what students submit. In addition, assignment, quiz, and answer sheet data within the classroom syncs seamlessly with data outside the class, improving teaching management convenience. Teachers can also use LMS to assign after-class homework, grading it on the fly during teaching and providing real-time feedback. This significantly improves teaching efficiency and the student learning experience.

## Notes
iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the classroom LMS feature.

## X. Class Notes

Everyone.

Class Notes is one of the classroom's commonly used tools. Its main function is to record important notes and highlight moments during class via screenshots, supporting the saving of annotations and analysis on classroom courseware (PDF, PPT, Word, etc.), and letting you further edit saved images and add text captions, to more clearly express and record key knowledge points. Class Notes also lets you download note images locally to save and share.

Notes must be at least 10 seconds apart from each other.

Phone and tablet do not have the "Class Notes" feature.

Each user can record up to 100 notes at a time.

## XI. Chat Tool

The Chat tool is one of the classroom's commonly used teaching tools. It includes two main modules: the Chat module and the Questions module. In the Chat module, teachers and students can freely type messages, and either side can recall a message they've sent; translating the other person's message is also supported. Teachers additionally have permissions to mute a student's chat, or delete a message a student has already sent. In the Questions module, students can ask the teacher questions, and the teacher can view students' questions and respond accordingly.

Once you exit the classroom after class ends, the chat records in the classroom's chat box are cleared and cannot be saved.

## XII. Roster

#### Class Students Section
**Go on stage/off stage:** the teacher controls whether a student shows their camera on stage, or sends them off stage so they listen to the lesson without showing their camera.

**Authorize:** grants a student permission to use teaching tools, or revokes that permission.

**Mute:** prevents a student from typing messages in the chat window.

**Microphone:** mutes or unmutes a student's microphone.

**Camera:** view a student's camera status.

**Reward:** give a student a trophy.

**Raise hand:** view a student's raised-hand status.

**Private chat:** the teacher and student enter a 1v1 camera private-chat classroom.

**Remove:** removes a student from the classroom.

**View other devices:** view what type of device a student is using for class.

**Rotation:** rotate through displaying different students' cameras.

#### Co-Teacher Section
**Co-teacher go on stage/off stage:** the lead teacher invites the co-teacher to show their camera on stage, or sends them off stage so their camera no longer shows (the co-teacher can also control their own on-stage status).

## ClassIn Recording Tutorial

## I. Recording Notes

## 1. Recommended Recording Devices

### 1.1 Computers & Laptops

Note: Chromebooks do not support recording.

Recommended device specs for computers and laptops:

| | Minimum Requirements | Recommended Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processor | Intel i5 8th gen or higher; AMD Ryzen 5 1st gen or higher | Intel i7 9th gen or higher; AMD Ryzen 7 2nd gen or higher |
| OS | Windows 7 or higher; macOS 10.13 or higher | Windows 10 or higher; macOS 11 or higher |
| Memory | Windows: 4GB RAM; Mac: 4GB RAM | Windows: 8GB RAM; Mac: 8GB RAM |
| Display | At least 1280 x 720 resolution | At least 1920 x 1080 resolution |
| Network | At least 4Mbps | At least 6Mbps |

| RAM | iPad/iPhone: 2GB or higher; Android/HarmonyOS: 8GB or higher | iPad/iPhone: 3GB or higher; Android/HarmonyOS: 8GB or higher |
| Processor | iPad/iPhone: A11 or higher; Android/HarmonyOS: Qualcomm Snapdragon 855 or higher, Kirin 980 or higher, Dimensity 1000 or higher | iPad/iPhone: A12 or higher; Android/HarmonyOS: Qualcomm Snapdragon 865 or higher, Kirin 9000 or higher, Dimensity 1100 or higher |

## 2. Setting the Recording Area

### 2.1 Recording Only the Classroom View

Usage Notes: If you checked "Record ClassIn Classroom" when creating the class session, or you need to do a local recording, and the teacher on computer only wants to record what's inside the classroom, they can select this under "Recording Area" in ClassIn's classroom settings.

Choose "Minimum-Size Classroom Window" (once recording starts, the classroom window shrinks to 1280 x 720 and cannot be resized), or "Current-Size Classroom Window" (once recording starts, the classroom window can be resized by dragging, and cannot be minimized but can be maximized).

Notes:

If you choose to record the minimum-size or current-size classroom window, and the teacher then uses the screen share tool, or clicks the minimize button in the bottom-left corner while in Big Screen Mode, the entire computer desktop will be recorded instead.

This setting only applies to the current computer. When taking class on phone or tablet, the classroom window is full-screen by default, so the recording captures the phone or tablet's entire screen.

### 2.2 Recording the Entire Computer Desktop

Usage Notes: If you checked "Record ClassIn Classroom" when creating the class session, or you need to do a local recording, and the teacher on computer wants to record their entire computer screen, they can check "Entire Computer Desktop" under "Recording Area" in ClassIn's classroom settings. Once recording starts, everything inside and outside the classroom will be recorded; note this demands more from your computer's performance when using a larger display.

Notes: this setting only applies to the current computer. When taking class on phone or tablet, the classroom window is full-screen by default, so the recording captures the phone or tablet's entire screen.

## 3. Setting Recording Resolution

Usage Notes: If you checked "Record ClassIn Classroom" when creating the class session, or you need to do a local recording, and the teacher on computer wants to increase the recording's resolution, they can select it under "Recording Video Resolution" in ClassIn's classroom settings.

In HD mode, the recorded class video resolution is 1280 x 720; in Full HD mode, it's 1920 x 1080.

Notes: if the teacher's "Recording Area" is set to the minimum-size classroom window, Full HD resolution cannot be selected under "Recording Video Resolution." This setting only applies to the current computer.

## 4. Setting Recording Audio

Usage Notes: If you checked "Record ClassIn Classroom" when creating the class session, or you need to do a local recording, and the teacher on computer:

wants to record all sound from the entire computer, they can select "System Sound" under "Recording Mode" in ClassIn's classroom settings. Once "System Sound" is checked, the recording captures all sounds on the computer, both inside and outside the classroom — for example, a video playing or music, or notification sounds from messaging software outside the classroom, will all be captured.

only wants to record sound from within the classroom, they can select "Software Sound" instead. Once "Software Sound" is checked, only sound from within the classroom is recorded, and sound from outside the classroom is not captured.

Notes: this setting only applies to the current computer.

## 5. Common Recording Issues

### 5.1 Preventing the Classroom Window from Shrinking After Recording

Once a teacher on computer checks "Current-Size Classroom Window" under "Recording Area" in ClassIn's classroom settings, the classroom window will no longer automatically shrink the next time they record.

### 5.2 Avoiding Recording What's Outside the Classroom

Once a teacher on computer checks "Minimum-Size Classroom Window" or "Current-Size Classroom Window" under "Recording Area" in ClassIn's classroom settings, the next recording will only capture what's inside the classroom, not what's outside it.

In addition, teachers on Windows 7 also need to set the system theme to the Aero theme.

### 5.3 Avoiding Recording Sound from Outside the Classroom

Once a teacher on computer checks "Software Sound" under "Recording Mode" in ClassIn's classroom settings, the next recording will only capture sound from within the classroom, not sound from outside it.

### 5.4 Preventing Recording Interruptions

While recording is in progress, don't plug or unplug speaker devices like headphones or external speakers — make sure the classroom's speaker output stays audible normally.

Don't voluntarily exit the classroom while recording is in progress.

Don't switch classroom mode (Standard Mode or Big Screen Mode) while recording is in progress.

Make sure the classroom microphone works normally while recording is in progress.

Make sure your network connection is stable while recording is in progress.

When recording on-site, make sure the selected camera feed in the on-site recording window is displaying properly.

## 6. Recording Status

### 6.1 Lead Teacher Checking "Record ClassIn Classroom" Status

Once a class session has "Record ClassIn Classroom" checked, once the lead teacher enters the classroom, they can tell whether recording is working properly based on the different recording-status indicators in the classroom.

Once recording starts, on computer (phone/tablet), a "TV" icon appears in the top-right (top-left) corner of the classroom window, from the lead teacher's view. When this icon is "green," it means the classroom recording is working normally; when "red," it means recording has been interrupted. (If Big Screen Mode is selected, check the recording status in the bottom-left corner of the classroom window instead.)

### 6.2 Lead Teacher Checking "Record On-Site" Status

Once a class session has "Record On-Site" checked, once the lead teacher enters the classroom, they can tell whether recording is working properly based on the different recording-status indicators in the classroom.

The Record On-Site feature is only supported for lead teachers on computer, so once recording starts, a "TV" icon containing the number "2" appears in the top-right corner of the classroom window, from the lead teacher's view. When this icon is "green," on-site recording is working normally; when "red," it has been interrupted. (If Big Screen Mode is selected, check the recording status in the bottom-left corner of the classroom window instead.)

### 6.3 Checking Local Recording Status

Once local recording starts, on computer (phone/tablet), a "camera" icon appears in the top-right (top-left) corner of the classroom window, from the lead teacher's view. When this icon is "green," it means the classroom recording is working normally; when "red," it means recording has been interrupted. (If Big Screen Mode is selected, check the recording status in the bottom-left corner of the classroom window instead.)

## 7. Recording-Related Parameters

### (1) Bandwidth Requirements by Class Type

| Class Type | Downlink Bandwidth Requirement | Corresponding Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1V6 | ≥2Mbps | 250KB/s |
| 1V12 | ≥4Mbps | 500KB/s |

### (2) Camera Bandwidth Requirements

| Configuration | Uplink Bandwidth Requirement | Downlink Bandwidth Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1v1 HD | ≥1.5Mbps | ≥1.5Mbps |
| 1v1 Full HD | ≥3Mbps | ≥3Mbps |
| 1v1 Dual-Camera Full HD | ≥6Mbps | ≥6Mbps |
| 1v6 HD | ≥8Mbps | ≥8Mbps |
| 1v6 Full HD | ≥15Mbps | ≥15Mbps |

### (3) Additional Feature Bandwidth Stacking Rules

Cloud recording / livestreaming (affects only the teacher side):
- HD video: uplink bandwidth +1Mbps
- Full HD video: uplink bandwidth +2Mbps

Screen sharing:
- Presenter: uplink bandwidth +2Mbps
- Viewer: downlink bandwidth +2Mbps

Video wall mode:
- Bandwidth requirement = base class-type requirement × 2

### (4) Recording Technical Specifications

| Parameter | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| File format | MP4, FLV |
| Aspect ratio | 16:9 |
| Video codec | H264 @ 15fps |
| Resolution & bitrate | 1080P (2Mbps) / 720P (1Mbps) |
| Audio bitrate | 64kbps (customizable) |

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "The Difference Between Recording the Classroom, Recording On-Site, and OMO Livestream Broadcast"
source_title_zh: "录制教室、录制现场和OMO站播的区别"
```

## II. The Difference Between Recording the Classroom, Recording On-Site, and OMO Livestream Broadcast

Cloud recording comes in two modes: "Record ClassIn Classroom" and "Record On-Site." These two recording modes can be enabled individually or together.

**Record ClassIn Classroom:** classroom recording mode has two view options — the first records only what's in the lead teacher's classroom window; the second records the lead teacher's entire computer desktop, including the classroom window and anything the user does on the desktop. Both view options can be configured under Recording Area in App Settings. If the lead teacher only wants to record what's inside the classroom window, they can check "Current-Size Classroom Window" under Recording Area. If the lead teacher wants to record both the ClassIn classroom view and everything happening on the computer desktop, they can check "Entire Computer Desktop" under Recording Area. When taking class on phone or tablet, the classroom window is full-screen by default, so the recording captures the phone or tablet's entire screen.

**Record On-Site:** this mode means that while the lead teacher is recording class, only the camera feed they've selected for on-site recording is captured — anything outside that camera view is not recorded. Online students in the classroom can open the on-site recording view window to watch the teacher's lesson enlarged and more clearly. Users watching class via the web livestream link can also directly switch to view the on-site recording feed. In addition, students watching the class playback afterward can likewise switch to on-site recording mode, for a better review and understanding of the teacher's explanation.

**OMO Livestream Broadcast:** if students only need to watch the teacher's livestream broadcast feed within the classroom, without needing cloud recording, we recommend using the OMO livestream broadcast feature. OMO livestream broadcast mode is a high-definition mode for recording the on-site scene — in this mode, only the camera feed the lead teacher selected in the OMO livestream broadcast settings is recorded in the classroom; anything outside that camera view is not recorded. Online students in the classroom can open the OMO livestream broadcast window to watch the teacher's lesson more clearly. This mode is especially suited to teaching scenarios that call for high-definition video.

When on-site recording mode and OMO livestream broadcast mode are both enabled, they cannot use different cameras separately — when the lead teacher selects a camera in on-site recording mode, OMO livestream broadcast automatically switches to that same camera, and vice versa.

On-site recording and OMO livestream broadcast are only supported for lead teachers using a computer or big screen (Windows) — other devices (such as phone/tablet) don't support them.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassIn Classroom Recording"
source_title_zh: "ClassIn录制教室"
```

## III. ClassIn Classroom Recording

## What is "Cloud Recording"?
"Cloud Recording" includes two recording modes: "Record ClassIn Classroom" and "Record On-Site." Once recording is checked when creating the class session, ClassIn's built-in recording feature fully records the entire class from the lead teacher's point of view while they teach. These recorded videos are automatically uploaded and stored on ClassIn's servers. About half an hour after class ends, the recorded video is turned into a "class playback video" for students and teachers to review and watch afterward.

## Applies to
Lead teacher.

## Prerequisites
"Record ClassIn Classroom" under "Cloud Recording" must be checked when creating the class session before the lead teacher can use the "cloud recording classroom recording" feature during class.

## Usage Notes
Recording ClassIn Classroom means recording what's happening inside the classroom itself, from the lead teacher's view.

If the lead teacher on computer selects the current-size or minimized classroom window as the recording area, the classroom view is recorded; but if the lead teacher uses the screen share tool, or minimizes the window from the bottom-left corner in Big Screen Mode, the entire computer desktop where the ClassIn classroom window is located gets recorded instead.

If the lead teacher on computer selects the entire computer desktop as the recording area, the entire computer desktop where the ClassIn classroom window is located is recorded.

Every time the lead teacher enters the classroom, they receive a recording prompt; after clicking Confirm, a "recording countdown" prompt appears. The lead teacher can manually click "Start Recording Now" on the countdown prompt to begin right away, or wait for the countdown to finish and let recording start automatically. The default recording countdown is 10 minutes; to change this, please have a teacher with "Backend Management" access change the countdown time in the "Backend Management System."

Recording cannot be stopped once class has started; if you don't want to record, you can only turn off "Record ClassIn Classroom" the next time you create a class session. Recording stops automatically once the lead teacher exits the classroom, and starts prompting again once they re-enter.

If the lead teacher forgot to enable "Record ClassIn Classroom" before class, they can use the "Local Recording" feature to record and save the teaching session locally on their computer or big screen, or create a new class session and check "Record ClassIn Classroom" this time.

## Notes
An unstable network connection for the lead teacher may cause recording to fail.

If recording fails, ClassIn will automatically retry; after 3 consecutive failed attempts, a prompt appears in the classroom offering to switch from cloud recording to local recording, which the lead teacher can accept manually (only computer supports this switch — phone and tablet cannot). Once switched to local recording, the recorded file is by default stored in a new folder under ClassIn file, in mp4 format by default; local recording can be manually stopped and restarted. If you don't click to switch to local recording, cloud recording continues and ClassIn keeps retrying; the switch prompt won't reappear, but you can reopen it by clicking the red "recording failed" icon.

Also, if the lead teacher exits and re-enters the classroom, ClassIn will retry cloud recording again.

If the lead teacher plugs or unplugs a speaker device on their computer, or the speaker disconnects due to an unstable connection, this can also stop the recording. In that case, the lead teacher will see a "Recording Interrupted" prompt; to keep recording, reconnect the speaker device or switch to a more stable one, then click Retry in the classroom's "Recording Interrupted" prompt window.

While recording, if the lead teacher uses the "Screen Share" tool in the classroom, or clicks "Minimize" in the bottom-left corner in Big Screen Mode, everything on the computer desktop where the ClassIn classroom is located will be recorded.

On Android devices, close features like split-screen, floating windows, or landscape mode before recording — if these features are left on, recording may fail.

## Related Articles
"Changing the Recording Countdown"

## Steps

### Computer
1. Enter the classroom.
2. Read the recording prompt, then click Confirm.
3. Click "Start Recording Now" next to the recording countdown, or wait for the countdown to end and let recording start automatically.
4. Check the recording status.

### iPhone/iPad
1. When prompted to allow screen capture in ClassIn, tap Allow.

### Android Phone/Tablet
1. When prompted to request the floating window permission, tap Confirm.
2. Enable "Display over other apps," then tap Back.
3. When prompted to allow ClassIn to record/project the screen, tap Allow.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassIn On-Site Recording"
source_title_zh: "ClassIn录制现场"
```

## IV. ClassIn On-Site Recording

"Record On-Site" under "Cloud Recording" must be checked when creating the class session before the lead teacher can use the "cloud recording on-site recording" feature during class.

On-site recording means that while a lead teacher on computer is recording class, only the camera feed they've selected in the on-site recording window is captured — anything outside that camera view is not recorded, so make sure the selected camera feed is displaying properly.

Every time the lead teacher enters the classroom, they receive a recording prompt; after clicking Confirm, they'll see the on-site recording window along with a "recording countdown" prompt.

In this window, you can view the current on-site recording feed, and switch which camera device to record using settings in the top-right corner of the window; recording only works properly if the on-site recording feed is displaying normally.

Once the lead teacher has adjusted the on-site recording camera feed, they can manually click "Start Recording Now" on the countdown prompt to begin right away, or wait for the countdown to finish and let recording start automatically. The default recording countdown is 10 minutes; to change this, please have a teacher with "Backend Management" access change the countdown time in the "Backend Management System."

Recording cannot be stopped once class has started; if you don't want to record, you can disable the camera in the on-site recording window, or turn off "Record ClassIn Classroom" the next time you create a class session. Recording stops automatically once the lead teacher exits the classroom, and starts prompting again once they re-enter.

In addition, online students in the classroom can also view the "Live Broadcast" feed (i.e. the on-site recording feed) in the bottom-right corner.

On-site recording is only supported for lead teachers on computer.

An unstable network connection for the lead teacher may cause recording to fail. The recording icon will turn red, and ClassIn will automatically retry recording.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Local Recording"
source_title_zh: "本地录课"
```

## V. Local Recording

### What is "Local Recording"?
"Local Recording" refers to a teacher using ClassIn's screen recording feature (recording the classroom window) to record the teaching session and save it locally to a computer, or to the system photo album on a phone or tablet.

### Prerequisites
As long as either "Record ClassIn Classroom" or "Record On-Site" is enabled (or both), the class session's co-teacher can use local recording.

If neither "Record ClassIn Classroom" nor "Record On-Site" is enabled, the class session's co-teacher can still use local recording.

An academic teacher who enters classroom monitoring via the "Monitor Classes" module in the "Backend Management System" can use local recording.

Anyone who enters the "Whiteboard" from the ClassIn main interface can use "Local Recording."

Local recording can be used after creating and entering a temporary classroom in a class or friend chat.

A teacher who enters the preparation room can use "Local Recording."

### When to use this
If a class session has a co-teacher, and the lead teacher's cloud recording of the classroom becomes unstable (for example: recording is interrupted, and the recording-status icon in the classroom turns "red"), the co-teacher can use local recording in the classroom to make sure the lesson gets fully recorded without gaps. Afterward, the academic teacher can upload the co-teacher's local recording video to the "Backend Management System" to replace the lead teacher's incomplete recording of that class session.

If a class session has no co-teacher, and the lead teacher's cloud recording becomes unstable (for example: recording is interrupted, and the recording-status icon in the classroom turns "red"), the academic teacher can log into the "Backend Management System," go to classroom monitoring under "Monitor Classes," and do a local recording. Afterward, the academic teacher can upload their own local recording video to the "Backend Management System" to replace the lead teacher's incomplete recording of that class session.

For a classroom where neither "Record ClassIn Classroom" nor "Record On-Site" is enabled, but you need to record the classroom content during class, the lead teacher or co-teacher can use local recording, then send the local playback video afterward to whoever needs to watch it.

### Usage Notes
Once the prerequisites for local recording are met, the lead teacher clicks the recording icon, selects a save location and file type (flv/mp4, default flv) in the save-path window, and recording begins. Local recording captures what's happening inside the classroom.

If the teacher on computer selects the current-size or minimized classroom window as the recording area, the classroom view is recorded; but if the teacher uses the screen share tool, or minimizes the window from the bottom-left corner in Big Screen Mode, the entire computer desktop where the ClassIn classroom window is located gets recorded instead.

If the teacher on computer selects the entire computer desktop as the recording area, the entire computer desktop where the ClassIn classroom window is located is recorded.

Clicking the recording icon again ends local recording. You can start local recording again afterward.

### Notes
Requirements for local recording on phone or tablet: iOS 11 or higher; for Android, the processor must be Qualcomm Snapdragon 700 series or higher, or an equivalent-performance processor. In addition, the recorded video file grows by about 12MB per minute, so make sure your phone or tablet has enough storage space. We also recommend keeping classroom sound enabled and working properly.

An unstable teacher network connection may cause recording to fail. You can manually try restarting the recording if it fails.

If the teacher plugs or unplugs a speaker device on their computer, or the speaker disconnects due to an unstable connection, this can also stop the recording. In that case, the lead teacher will see a "Recording Interrupted" prompt; to keep recording, reconnect the speaker device or switch to a more stable one, then click Retry in the classroom's "Recording Interrupted" prompt window.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. In Standard Mode, click the recording icon in the top-right corner of the classroom (in Big Screen Mode, click Record under More in the bottom-left corner).
2. Read the local recording prompt, then click Start Recording.
3. Select a save path and file type, then click Save.
4. Check the recording status. Click the recording icon again to End the recording.

#### Android Phone or Tablet
1. Click the recording icon in the top-left corner of the classroom.
2. Click the recording icon in the top-left corner again to stop recording; recording also stops if you exit the classroom.
3. Go to your local photo album to watch the local recording's playback video.

#### iOS Phone or iPad
1. Read the local recording prompt, then click Confirm.
2. Click Screen Recording.
3. Check the recording status (the icon in the top-left corner turns green when recording).
4. Go to your local Photos app to watch the local recording's playback video.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Switching to Local Recording When ClassIn Classroom Recording Fails"
source_title_zh: "ClassIn录制教室失败时切换本地录课"
```

## VI. Switching to Local Recording When ClassIn Classroom Recording Fails

When an unstable network connection for the lead teacher causes classroom recording to fail, ClassIn will automatically retry; after 3 consecutive failed attempts, a prompt appears in the classroom offering to switch from cloud recording to local recording, which the lead teacher can accept manually (only computer supports this switch — phone and tablet cannot). Once switched to local recording, the recorded file is by default stored in a new folder under ClassIn file, in mp4 format by default; local recording can be manually stopped and restarted. If you don't click to switch to local recording, cloud recording continues and ClassIn keeps retrying; the switch prompt won't reappear, but you can reopen it by clicking the red "recording failed" icon.

After class ends, when the teacher checks the playback under "Schedule" or "Class" in ClassIn, a small red dot appears on the playback button, and clicking it shows: "You have a local recording file pending upload — please contact an administrator to upload the recording video." Clicking "Local Recording File" opens the file's storage location. You can send the locally recorded video to an academic teacher, who can log into the Backend Management System and upload it to the corresponding class session's playback slot. If there's no local recording file (for example, it was deleted), no such prompt appears.

1. Read the recording error prompt, then click Switch Now.
2. When checking the class playback afterward, find the video and give it to the academic teacher.

# 7. Classroom (Part 9: Teaching Toolbox)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Teaching Toolbox"
source_title_zh: "教学工具箱"
```

## Teaching Toolbox

## I. Screen Share

## 1. Teacher Screen Share

### Applies to
Lead teacher, co-teacher.

### When to use this
"Screen Share" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Through the "Screen Share" feature in the ClassIn classroom, teachers can show teaching content in real time so students can watch and learn along, improving teaching outcomes and interactivity. Teachers can also remotely control a student's desktop, quickly resolving issues the student runs into, significantly improving the student's learning experience and teaching outcomes.

In ClassIn, screen sharing comes in two modes: "Teacher Screen Share" and "Student Screen Share." "Teacher Screen Share" refers to a teacher sharing their own computer screen content with students in real time. This is widely used in online education and blended teaching. Through screen sharing, teachers can show textbooks, courseware, demonstrate operating steps, or explain complex concepts, helping students watch and learn along in real time.

### Usage Notes
While sharing their screen, a teacher can share their computer desktop and sound, or choose to share a specific software window. During sharing, the teacher can still use the "Roster" and "Chat" tools, and can turn on their camera and microphone for better interaction with students.

In addition, teachers can use the "Pen," "Click Tool," "Select/Move," "Eraser," and "Text" tools to mark up and annotate the shared window. Teachers can also switch student permissions, specifically:

**Don't allow student control:** students can only watch — they cannot mark up or write in the teacher's shared window.

**Allow authorized students to control the view:** authorized students can collaborate with the teacher writing or drawing in the shared window.

**Allow authorized students to control the computer:** authorized students can use the "Click Tool" to control the teacher's computer.

### Notes
Phone and tablet only have "Screen Share" mode, which can only share what's on that device itself — students cannot draw on the teacher's device, etc.

"Teacher Screen Share" can only share a single software window separately if the system is Windows 8, Windows 10, or Mac; there's no limit on the maximum shared area (anything larger than 1920 x 1080 is automatically compressed down to 1920 x 1080).

Once cloud recording is used together with screen sharing in the classroom, the resulting playback shows the entire computer desktop — so the recorded playback footage isn't limited to just the window that was shared; other windows or the taskbar may also appear.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Open the Teaching Toolbox on the right side of the classroom.
2. Select Screen Share.
3. Select Teacher Screen Share.
4. Click Share in the bottom-right corner to start sharing.

#### iPad
1. Open the Teaching Toolbox in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.
2. Click Start Live to begin sharing.

#### Phone/Android tablet
1. Select the Screen Share tool from the toolbox in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.
2. Click Start Sharing to begin sharing.

## 2. Student Screen Share

Lead teacher, co-teacher, the student whose screen is shared.

In ClassIn, screen sharing comes in two modes: "Teacher Screen Share" and "Student Screen Share." "Student Screen Share" refers to sharing what's on a student's computer, phone, or tablet screen with the rest of the classroom in real time. If the student shares their computer desktop, the teacher can also remotely operate the student's computer.

Teachers can share the screen of any student's computer, phone, or tablet in the classroom; if a teacher wants to control files on a student's computer, they can use the "Click Tool" from the teaching tools to open or move files on the student's computer.

Phone and tablet do not have "Student Screen Share" mode.

Phone and tablet cannot initiate "Student Screen Share."

Phone and tablet can accept being screen-shared.

1. Select Student Screen Share.
2. Click Send Request below to start sharing.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Screen Projection"
source_title_zh: "投屏"
```

## II. Screen Projection

Everyone (only the lead teacher or co-teacher can open this tool; once opened, others can use it too).

During class, if a teacher or student wants to show what's on their phone/tablet or another computer's screen in the classroom, they can use the classroom's screen projection tool.

For projection to work, the projecting device and the receiving device must be on the same network.

**(1) Projecting from another computer to the classroom:** log into ClassIn on the projecting device, click Screen Projection in the left navigation, enter the receiving device's projection code and click Project, or select the receiving device's name to complete projection. The four green corners on the projecting device's screen indicate the projection area, which cannot be adjusted — the entire screen is always used.

**(2) Projecting from an Apple phone, tablet, or computer:** you can use the device's built-in mirroring/AirPlay feature and select the receiving device's name to complete projection; you can also use the ClassIn Screen Projection app, entering the projection code from the device to be projected and clicking Project, or selecting the receiving device's name.

**(3) Projecting from an Android phone or tablet:** you need to use the ClassIn Screen Projection app — enter the receiving device's projection code in the app and click Project, or select the receiving device's name to complete projection.

**(4) Projecting from other video apps that support projection:** open the video app, play the video, and tap the app's own projection button to select the receiving device's name to complete projection.

While using the screen projection tool, the top-right corner of the projection tool window offers more settings for this projection session:

**Sharing settings:** play the projecting device's sound through this device's speaker; share the projecting device's sound with everyone else in the classroom.

**Privacy settings:** allow receiving projections from all devices; once the projection window is open, allow receiving projections from all devices.

In addition, multiple devices can project into the classroom at once — once projection succeeds, the teacher can switch between viewing different devices' projected content in the bottom-right corner of the projection tool window.

Android phones and tablets need Android 6.0 or higher to download and install the ClassIn Screen Projection app; iPhones and iPads need iOS 12.0 or higher.

The screen projection tool can only display content from a phone/tablet or another computer onto the whiteboard — it cannot be used as a handwriting tablet. If a teacher wants to use their phone or tablet as a handwriting tablet, try the "Two-Device Classroom Entry" feature instead.

Screen projection in the classroom is only available to teachers taking class on computer.

1. Select Screen Projection.

title: "Auxiliary Camera"
source_title_zh: "辅助摄像头"
