## III. Auxiliary Camera

Lead teacher, co-teacher.

"Auxiliary Camera" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Its main purpose is to give teachers a second camera feed to display. It's typically used in music teaching scenarios, where a teacher can use two cameras at once to show both their facial expressions and their hand movements controlling an instrument. In addition, if a teacher uses a document camera device, the Auxiliary Camera can also be used to display what the document camera is capturing.

Phone and tablet do not have the "Auxiliary Camera" feature.

The "Auxiliary Camera" feature is not available in "1v1 Dual Camera" class type mode.

1. Select Auxiliary Camera.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Small Blackboard"
source_title_zh: "小黑板"
```

## IV. Small Blackboard

## 1. Whiteboard Small Blackboard

Lead teacher, co-teacher, students.

"Small Blackboard" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It gives each student the equivalent of a personal mini blackboard, making it easy for them to complete tasks the teacher assigns on their own small blackboard. Small Blackboard has two modes: "Whiteboard Small Blackboard" and "Text Small Blackboard." "Whiteboard Small Blackboard" is mainly for drawing and writing. Once the teacher distributes small blackboards, students can create, draw, and write on their "Whiteboard Small Blackboard." Teachers can also enter any student's small blackboard at any time to collaborate with them directly.

| Stage | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Preparation | In this stage, the teacher can use the teaching tools in the bottom-left corner to set up the small blackboard's content; students cannot see this content yet. Once ready, click "Distribute" to move into the Answering stage. |
| Answering | In this stage, the teacher can use the search feature in the top-right corner of the small blackboard to search for a student by name, and can view any student's small blackboard at any time, including collaborating with them directly. The teacher can also switch the display mode above the small blackboard, choosing a single board, a 2x2 grid, or a 3x3 grid. In multi-board display mode, the teacher can click a student's small blackboard to jump straight into it. The teacher can also send students on/off stage, and click "Recall" to end the answering stage. |
| Grading | Once in the grading stage, the teacher can view any student's small blackboard (all students follow the teacher's view together), and can send students on/off stage and mark up or type on a student's blackboard. |

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the small blackboard tool, so teachers on these devices cannot initiate "Small Blackboard" for classroom members; however, students on phone or tablet can still normally take part in small blackboard activities.

The small blackboard's window size can be adjusted before it's published, but not after.

1. Select Small Blackboard.
2. Select Whiteboard.

## 2. Text Small Blackboard

"Small Blackboard" is an important teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It gives each student the equivalent of a personal mini blackboard, making it easy for them to complete tasks the teacher assigns. Small Blackboard has two modes: "Whiteboard Small Blackboard" and "Text Small Blackboard." "Text Small Blackboard" is mainly for text input and writing code. Once the teacher distributes small blackboards, students can write code or do other text-based work on their "Text Small Blackboard." Teachers can also enter any student's small blackboard at any time to guide and communicate with them directly.

| Stage | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Preparation | In this stage, the teacher can use the teaching tools in the bottom-left corner to set up the small blackboard's content; students cannot see this content yet. Once ready, click "Distribute" to move into the Answering stage. |
| Answering | In this stage, the teacher can view any student's small blackboard at any time, including sending students on/off stage and typing together with them on their small blackboard. To end the answering stage, the teacher can click "Recall." |
| Grading | Once in the grading stage, the teacher can view any student's small blackboard (all students follow the teacher's view together), and can send students on/off stage and mark up or type on a student's blackboard. |

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the small blackboard tool.

If more than 50 students are online in the classroom, the small blackboard tool cannot be used; the "Small Blackboard User Limit" can be changed in the Backend Management System.

1. Select Text.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Collaboration"
source_title_zh: "协作"
```

## V. Collaboration

## 1. Text Collaboration

Lead teacher, co-teacher, students authorized by the teacher.

"Collaboration" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox, designed to help teachers and students jointly type into a shared document during class. "Collaboration" has two modes: "Text Writing" and "Document Writing." "Text mode" is designed specifically to handle multi-language input needs. In text mode, teachers and students can jointly type into the shared document.

In text mode, teachers can switch the text format in the bottom-left corner of the "Collaboration" window; supported input formats include: Text, C, C++, CSS, Go, HTML, Java, JavaScript, Markdown, Pascal, Perl, PHP, Python, R, Ruby, Rust, SQL, and Swift. When closing the Collaboration window, you can also save the collaborative content locally or to your personal cloud drive.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the text collaboration tool.

1. Select Collaboration.

## 2. Document Collaboration

"Collaboration" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox, designed to help teachers and students jointly type into a shared document during class. "Collaboration" has two modes: "Text Writing" and "Document Writing." "Document mode" is nearly identical to the Word processor most people use daily.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the text collaboration tool.

The Collaboration tool on iPad does not have Document mode — only Text mode.

1. Select Document.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Group Discussion"
source_title_zh: "分组讨论"
```

## VI. Group Discussion

"Group Discussion" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox, designed to help teachers better organize classroom activities. By splitting students into different groups, students can discuss and learn together in breakout rooms, sparking interest and enthusiasm for learning. Teachers can adjust student groupings at any time, and can join in or silently monitor a group to understand their learning progress, improving teaching outcomes.

The classroom's "Group Discussion" and the class's "Discussion" feature are two entirely different features — a class discussion is a learning activity created under the class's course tab for all teachers and students in the class to discuss, while a classroom group discussion can only be created within the classroom, taking the form of multiple small breakout-room classrooms for students to discuss in.

On phone, you cannot initiate a group discussion — you can only receive one someone else has sent.

1. Select Group Discussion.

### Teacher Guide

**Copy classroom content:** to copy the content from the main classroom into every breakout room, check "Copy Classroom Content to Discussion Groups" in the bottom-left corner before starting the discussion.

**Synchronize audio/video:** once discussion starts, you can check "Sync Teacher Audio/Video to Discussion Groups" in the bottom-left corner, so students in every group can see the teacher's demonstration and explanation.

**Silently monitor a group discussion:** click "Silent Monitor" above a group window — the teacher can hear the discussion and see the video, but their own audio/video won't appear in that room.

**Join a group discussion:** click "Join Group" above a group window — the teacher's audio/video moves into that breakout room to interact normally with group members, and their audio/video will no longer appear in the main classroom.

**Show/hide the group window:** control this in the top-right corner.

**View group member info/adjust members:** hover the mouse over a group window to view member info; to adjust members, drag and drop them between groups.

### Student Guide

**Group leader permissions:** the group leader has the same permissions as a teacher — they can use the buttons below the camera and the tools in the teaching toolbox, and can operate the roster to send group members on/off stage, authorize them, mute their microphones, and so on. However, the group leader cannot award trophies, and cannot remove students from the classroom.

**Group member permissions:** group members have the same features as a regular classroom student, but are authorized by default.

### Post-Discussion Guide

**End discussion:** the teacher clicks "End Discussion" in the bottom-right corner to end the group discussion.

**Copy group content back to the main classroom:** to copy the content from a specific group room into the main classroom, click "Copy Discussion Group Content to Classroom" above that group's window. Note: this clears the main classroom's existing whiteboard content first.

**Bring a group's members on stage:** click "On Stage" above a group's window to bring all members of that group on stage.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Random Student Picker"
source_title_zh: "随机选人"
```

## VII. Random Student Picker

"Random Student Picker" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It ensures fairness and objectivity when choosing students, removing subjective bias from the selection process. By using the Random Student Picker, every student has an equal chance of taking part in classroom activities, effectively boosting participation and enthusiasm. This tool plays an important role in teaching practice, creating a fair, equitable learning environment and promoting well-rounded student development.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Random Student Picker feature.

Once a student is selected using the Random Student Picker, the teacher can find the student's name who needs to come on stage right within the tool, and click the "on stage" button next to the student's name to directly invite them on stage — no need to manually drag the student on stage, and students won't automatically come on stage either.

1. Select Random Student Picker.
2. Set the participation criteria.
3. Shake to randomly select a student.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Buzzer"
source_title_zh: "抢答器"
```

## VIII. Buzzer

"Buzzer" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. The buzzer can boost student participation and interaction in the classroom, spark students' enthusiasm to answer, and improve classroom atmosphere.

Once the teacher activates the buzzer and clicks "Start Buzzer," the buzzer immediately enters buzzer mode. The teacher's view shows "Buzzer Active," and the bottom of the screen shows the important stats "number of students taking part" and "total number of students online in the classroom." In students' view, the buzzer appears on the whiteboard and starts a 3-second countdown; once the countdown ends, the buzzer lands randomly at a spot on the whiteboard. Students can then start tapping the buzzer. The first student to buzz in successfully is automatically brought on stage to show their camera.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Buzzer tool.

During buzzing, if multiple students buzz in within 0.5 seconds of each other, the system randomly selects one of them as the winner; if no student buzzes in within 0.5 seconds, the system selects whichever student buzzed in first, based on timing order.

1. Select Buzzer.

## IX. Dice

Lead teacher, co-teacher, authorized students.

"Dice" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It sparks students' interest in learning, adds fun and interactivity to the classroom, and encourages students to actively take part in classroom activities. Using dice, students can more actively participate in the learning process — exploring and practicing — leading to a deeper learning experience. Dice not only grab students' attention, but also make the learning process more fun and motivating.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Dice tool.

1. Select Dice.
2. Click the dice to roll it.

"Timer" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Teachers can use the timer to precisely control the timing of classroom activities and effectively manage the pacing as students take part in different learning activities. Using the timer, teachers can set up learning challenges or competitions, sparking student motivation.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Timer feature.

1. Select Timer.

## XI. Countdown Timer

Lead teacher, co-teacher, students authorized by the teacher.

"Countdown Timer" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It's widely used in the classroom to precisely control the pacing of teaching segments, ensuring reasonable time allocation for each part of the lesson. By setting a countdown in advance, teachers can precisely manage class time, ensuring learning activities run smoothly.

Minimum settable time: 00:00 minutes.

Maximum settable time: 59:59 minutes.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Countdown Timer tool.

1. Select Countdown Timer.
2. Set the time, then click Start to begin the countdown.

## XII. Browser

## 1. Browser

"Browser" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Users can freely visit various webpages within the classroom browser, and play video and audio from webpages for the rest of the classroom to watch.

To interact with and click content on a webpage in the browser tool, users need to first select the classroom's "Click Tool" before they can effectively click content in the browser.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Browser feature.

### Related Articles
"Presetting Browser Bookmarks"

1. Select Browser.

## 2. Multi-Directional Browser

In programming teaching scenarios, besides watching the teacher explain and write code, students also need hands-on practice, which usually needs to be completed independently in a web browser. ClassIn's toolbox added the "Multi-Directional Browser" — in this browser, students can write and run their own programs, while teachers can check in on and guide them.

The "Multi-Directional Browser" feature works similarly to the "Small Blackboard" tool. First, the teacher opens the Multi-Directional Browser, enters the correct URL, and clicks "Start Learning." Once this is done, every student in the classroom can work in their own Multi-Directional Browser on the whiteboard. Any action a student takes in their Multi-Directional Browser only shows in their own personal view — students cannot see each other's Multi-Directional Browser content. Teachers can switch between student names above the Multi-Directional Browser window to check each student's work. In addition, if a student is taking class on computer, the teacher can enter that student's Multi-Directional Browser to work with them directly.

Teachers taking class on phone or tablet do not have the Multi-Directional Browser tool.

If a student is taking class on a non-computer device, once the teacher opens their Multi-Directional Browser, the teacher can only watch — not operate that student's browser.

1. Select Multi-Directional Browser.

```yaml
title: "Save/Share Whiteboard"
source_title_zh: "保存/分享板书"
```

## XIII. Save/Share Whiteboard

The "Save/Share Whiteboard" tool is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Teachers can use it while preparing lessons or teaching to save the whiteboard's content locally on their computer or to their cloud drive space.

When saving the whiteboard, the teacher can choose to save it locally or to the cloud drive. If saving locally, the teacher can simultaneously save it in multiple formats — EDB, PNG, and PDF. In addition, the teacher can choose whether to compress images in the whiteboard content, and set the whiteboard's background color. However, if saving to the cloud drive, only one format can be chosen at a time — EDB, PNG, or PDF.

Teachers can also share the whiteboard with a ClassIn friend or to a ClassIn class. Students can also get the whiteboard image by scanning the generated QR code.

When saving the whiteboard on phone or tablet, you cannot select a whiteboard background color.

Only computer users have the QR-code-to-generate-whiteboard-image feature — phone and tablet do not.

When a computer user saves the whiteboard locally, they can select edb, png, and pdf simultaneously, producing three different whiteboard file types locally; when saving to the cloud drive, only one file type can be selected at a time.

1. Select Save/Share Whiteboard.
2. Set the whiteboard background color in the bottom-left corner.
3. Select a save method or sharing method in the top-right corner.

Select Save Whiteboard.
Select a save method or sharing method on the right.

Select the Save Whiteboard tool from the toolbox in the bottom-right corner of the classroom.

## XIV. Video Wall

"Video Wall" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It gives teachers a way to view every student's camera feed in real time. If a teacher wants to observe all students' cameras in the classroom without bringing them on stage, the Video Wall lets the teacher quietly monitor each student's status during class, for better teaching and classroom management. In addition, the "Video Wall" can also be used for proctoring in the classroom.

The "Video Wall" control interface is only visible to the teacher — students cannot see it. From a student's view, they only see a small window in the bottom-left corner of the classroom showing their own camera. If a student sees this small window during class, it means the teacher is using the Video Wall feature.

In the "Video Wall" interface, the teacher can drag and drop to directly reposition students' cameras. Double-clicking a student's camera enlarges it to fill the entire Video Wall interface; double-clicking again restores its original size. To bring a student on stage or start a private video chat with them, the teacher can hover the mouse over the student's camera and click the quick-action buttons below it.

In addition, in the top-right corner of the Video Wall interface, teachers can set "Auto Page Turn," "Page Turn Interval," and "Layout," and can also take a group photo.

Tip: we recommend using the Video Wall with a dual-monitor setup — move the Video Wall to a secondary display so you can teach while keeping an eye on it at the same time.

**(1) Video Wall device requirements**

Phone and tablet do not have a Video Wall feature.

If a teacher is using two monitors for class, once Video Wall is opened, the Video Wall window automatically floats on the secondary display.

1. Select Video Wall.

## XV. Teaching Materials Library

The "Teaching Materials Library" tool is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. The Teaching Materials Library offers a wealth of subject-specific materials — teachers can browse and select materials suited to their teaching needs and apply them directly to their lesson. By showing these materials on the whiteboard, teachers can present knowledge more professionally, improving student learning outcomes.

**(1) The Teaching Materials Library includes materials across many subjects; below is what each subject includes:**

**Interactive Fun:** interactive games better suited to students.

**Chinese:** grid paper for character practice, pinyin, character structure, and so on.

**Math:** grid lines, solid geometry, plane geometry, functions, numbers, tangram pieces, playing cards, time tools.

**English:** English ruled lines, uppercase letters, lowercase letters, IPA phonetic symbols.

**Physics:** magnetism, electricity, optics, mechanics, thermodynamics, acoustics, modern physics.

**Chemistry:** various pieces of lab equipment.

**Biology:** animals, plants, microorganisms, human body, single-celled organisms, cells.

**History:** timelines.

**Music:** notation symbols, instruments, sheet music, notes.

**Art:** articulated figures.

**Calligraphy:** calligraphy ruled lines.

**General Studies:** experiments, human body, animals, plants.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the "Teaching Materials Library" tool.

1. Select Teaching Materials Library.

"Livestream Chat" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Once a classroom has "Cloud Recording" and "Web Livestream" enabled, when a user watching via the "Web Livestream Link" posts a comment in the discussion area, the teacher can use the classroom's "Livestream Chat" tool to communicate and interact with that user in real time via text. Teachers can also delete or mute comments from users watching via the "Web Livestream Link" using the "Livestream Chat" tool.

Phone and tablet do not have the "Livestream Chat" feature.

"Trophy Leaderboard" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It tallies how many trophies each student in the classroom has earned and provides a ranking of students by trophy count. It can also calculate the total number of trophies across all students in the classroom, giving teachers a more comprehensive view of reward data.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the "Trophy Leaderboard" tool.

If multiple students have the same trophy count, whoever has been online longest ranks higher.

When a teacher needs to point the laser at multiple spots on the whiteboard, and finds the regular laser pointer no longer sufficient, they can consider using the drag-and-point laser pointer tool to improve pointing precision and efficiency.

"Answer Clicker" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. It's mainly designed to pair with questions on the whiteboard. Teachers can use the answer clicker in the classroom to preset answers in advance, presented as letters, covering both single- and multiple-choice formats. Once the answer is set, the teacher can distribute the answer clicker to students to answer by selecting the corresponding letter.

iPhone, Android phone, and Android tablet do not have the Answer Clicker feature.

```yaml
title: "VNC"
```

## XX. VNC

### What is "VNC"?
VNC (Virtual Network Console) is a great remote control software tool.

ClassIn's VNC feature integrates a VNC client — teachers just need a separate computer set up as the VNC server, and can then use ClassIn's VNC feature to connect to that computer and use ClassIn's rich teaching features to teach through it.

Note: the computer with the VNC server installed needs a public IP address.

The classroom's "lead teacher" or "co-teacher" can use the VNC tool in the classroom.

### Configuration Notes
For the cloud server configuration you purchase, we recommend the following:

**(1)** If your class type is 1v6, the machine needs at least 2 cores and 4GB RAM. We strongly recommend choosing a bandwidth plan billed by actual usage, with a bandwidth requirement of at least 10Mbps.

**(2)** If your class type is 1v12, the machine needs at least 4 cores and 8GB RAM. We strongly recommend choosing a bandwidth plan billed by actual usage, with a bandwidth requirement of at least 20Mbps.

In addition, after purchasing a cloud server, you'll need to log into the cloud platform's management backend to modify the security policy and open the relevant ports (we recommend not using default ports like 3389, 5900, or 22 — port security needs to be configured separately).

Below are the steps for setting up a VNC server on Windows and Mac.

**2.1 Setting Up a VNC Server on Windows**

**(1)** First, download the VNC installer. Using TightVNC as an example: follow the installation wizard — choosing "Typical" installs both the client and server by default. To install only the client, choose "Custom" as shown below.

**(2)** In the TightVNC installation directory, launch tvnserver.exe to configure the VNC server: set a port number (default 5900) and password (note: the password cannot exceed 8 characters). This port number and password are what you'll need to enter when connecting via ClassIn's VNC feature.

**2.2 Setting Up and Using Screen Sharing (VNC Server) on Mac**

Please visit this link for details: https://support.apple.com/en-us/guide/mac-help/mh11848/mac

Click the VNC feature in the Teaching Toolbox, and log in by entering the configured VNC server's IP, port number, and password.

Once connected, the teacher and students connect to the VNC server computer at the same time; the teacher can use the authorization feature to authorize students to operate the VNC server computer.

Phone and tablet do not have the VNC feature.

1. Click the Teaching Toolbox on the right side of the classroom.
2. Select the VNC tool.

## 1. Chemistry Lab

"Chemistry Lab" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. The Chemistry Lab can simulate realistic chemistry experiment scenarios and results, helping students practice experiments and build chemistry lab skills outside of a physical lab. Through virtual reality technology, it gives users a realistic visual and auditory experience, and automatically records and analyzes data during operation. This tool is widely used in colleges, secondary schools, training institutions, and other educational settings, offering students a safe, convenient, low-cost way to learn.

"Physics Lab" is a professional teaching tool in the classroom's teaching toolbox. Through virtual reality technology, it gives users a realistic visual and auditory experience, and automatically records and analyzes data during operation. This tool is widely used in colleges, secondary schools, training institutions, and other educational settings, offering students a safe, convenient, low-cost way to learn.

In teaching, they're widely used for drawing and measuring in geometry and graphics, and for helping students understand and apply geometric concepts.

Shapes added to the whiteboard support resizing, border color, and fill color adjustments — through this tool, teachers can easily choose different types of shapes, such as circles, rectangles, and triangles.

## XXV. TI Store

During a livestream, teachers or teaching assistants can go to "Teaching Tools → TI Store" in the ClassIn livestream classroom, or academic teachers can go to "Class Product Management Settings" in the backend, to set a product's status to "Live for Sale," letting students purchase it directly while watching the livestream.

Product management and the TI Store are value-added services, available only to enterprise customers — please contact your dedicated account manager to enable them.

During a livestream, teachers, teaching assistants, and backend academic staff can only have 1 product listed at a time; once a new product is listed, the previous one is automatically taken down.

# 8. Cloud Drive Space (Part 1: Lesson Packs, EDX, CamIn, Nobook, TeacherIn, Flowin, Resource Center)

```yaml
title: "Lesson Pack (Multi-Courseware Bundle)"
source_title_zh: "备课包（多课件整合）"
```

## Lesson Pack (Multi-Courseware Bundle)

## I. What Is a Lesson Pack?

A lesson pack is a tool that bundles multiple teaching resources together, helping teachers find and use the resources they need more conveniently. By merging several pieces of courseware into a single lesson pack, teachers can organize and curate courseware while preparing lessons, making it easier to use in class.

## II. Creating a New Lesson Pack

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
Teachers on computer can create a lesson pack in My Cloud Drive and select the files they need. During a formal class, they can then use it by opening Classroom → My Cloud Drive → Lesson Pack.

### Notes
Phone and tablet cannot create a "Lesson Pack."

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Go to Space.
2. Click New.
3. Select Lesson Pack.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "EDX Authoring Tutorial"
source_title_zh: "EDX制作教程"
```

## EDX Authoring Tutorial

### I. What Is an EDX File?
An EDX file is a special file that contains a website address. When a teacher opens an EDX file during class, it launches the Multi-Directional Browser to open the URL inside the file; the way students and the teacher interact with it is the same as when the teacher opens the Multi-Directional Browser tool directly.

### II. Creating an EDX File

**Step 1:**

Get the URL of the website you'll need during class — for example, www.eeo.cn.

**Step 2:**

Create a new EDX file, and fill in the file's name and the website address.

Note: once created, you can open it directly for a preview to check whether the webpage displays correctly.

**Step 3:**

During a formal class, the teacher can open this EDX file from the cloud drive; once opened, class can proceed exactly as with the Multi-Directional Browser.

Note: within the classroom, this file type can only be opened by the teacher — no other role has permission to open it. Outside the classroom, there's no such restriction, and it can be previewed normally.

Student-side view is as follows.

## CamIn

## I. What Is CamIn?

CamIn is an all-in-one, easy-to-use video creation tool. It combines a virtual camera, video production, and live streaming push features. It's designed to help every user easily create polished videos.

CamIn supports use on computer, and CamIn's cloud space can be viewed within the ClassIn software's Space.

### Related Articles
CamIn Help Center

CamIn Official Website

## II. Uploading a Video / Creating a New Folder

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
Users on computer or tablet can view and use Flowin's cloud space within Space, where they can upload videos and create new folders. Videos support sharing, renaming, editing the cover, moving, duplicating, downloading, and deleting; folders support sharing, renaming, moving, and deleting.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to CamIn.
3. Click New → Upload Video / New Folder.
4. Select the video or folder action.

## III. Team Space

CamIn's cloud space supports creating and managing a team space; the team edition is a video production and management tool suited to multi-person collaboration. Users on computer or tablet can switch teams, invite and manage members, and upload videos or create new folders within the CamIn module of the ClassIn software.

1. Expand the side toolbar.
2. Switch or create a team.
3. Invite team members.
4. Go to Team Space.
5. Go to Space Management and Space Settings.

```yaml
title: "Nobook"
source_title_zh: "Nobook"
```

## Nobook

## I. What Is Nobook?

Nobook is a smart teaching tool built for teachers and students, designed for hands-on physics, chemistry, and biology experiments in middle and high school, as well as elementary science demonstrations. Teachers can develop courseware online as needed, and freely build and assemble experiments, achieving a cloud-based, intelligent, fully open experiment environment.

Users on computer or tablet can view and use Nobook's middle/high school physics, chemistry, and biology experiments within the ClassIn software's Space.

### Related Articles
NOBOOK Official Website

## II. Switching Subjects and Binding Membership

### Applies to
Everyone, or users with NOBOOK membership privileges.

### Usage Notes
Users on computer or tablet can view and use Nobook within Space. Nobook covers six subjects across middle and high school — physics, chemistry, and biology at each level — and users can switch subjects as needed. If you've purchased a membership on NOBOOK, you can bind your membership account to use VIP experiments; once bound, you can also check the expiration date of your subject-level VIP access.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to Nobook.
3. Switch subject.
4. Bind your NOBOOK membership account.
5. Check your subject VIP expiration date.

## III. Experiments

Users on computer or tablet can find an experiment and view its demo video and description, and can also edit or DIY their own experiment. Within an experiment, you can select the move tool to reposition equipment, fill in an experiment report, equations/tables, and watch the demo video while working through it. Once you finish an experiment, you can save it; saved experiments can be viewed, edited, or deleted under My Experiments.

1. Search for an experiment.
2. View or edit the experiment.
3. Click Save after editing the experiment.
4. Go to My Experiments.

```yaml
title: "TeacherIn"
source_title_zh: "TeacherIn"
```

## TeacherIn

## I. What Is TeacherIn?

TeacherIn is a platform for the education field, mainly offering course publishing, sales, management, and related teaching services, suited to teachers, educational institutions, and independent operators.

TeacherIn integrates deeply with the ClassIn teaching platform — teachers can apply courses from TeacherIn directly to their classes in ClassIn, enabling a seamless connection between online and offline teaching.

### Related Articles
TeacherIn Help Center

TeacherIn Official Website

TI Store

## II. Creating a Course

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
Users on computer or tablet can view TeacherIn within Space. In TI, you can view published courses, and can also go to the workspace to build your own course.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to TeacherIn.
3. Go to the Workspace.
4. Create a course.

## III. Applying/Sharing/Publishing/Deleting a Course

Space supports creating a course, and within a course you can create units and activities. In addition:

Teachers can apply activities from a course to any class where they're the head teacher or a teacher.

Courses support sharing with other users to co-edit.

Courses support publishing — once published, a course can be found and used on the TeacherIn platform.

The course page supports opening it in a browser, course settings (such as file download permissions), and deleting it.

1. Find and enter the course.
2. Create a new unit and activity.
3. Apply / Share / Publish / Delete the course.

## IV. Organization Space

Users can create an organization space in TI, where courses can be jointly managed and created, and also sold. Space also has a certain capacity limit — once exceeded, it can no longer be used. Users on computer or tablet can switch to or create an organization space in My Space, and can also check their personal space capacity.

1. Go to My Space.
2. Switch to / create an organization, or check personal space capacity.

```yaml
title: "Flowin"
source_title_zh: "Flowin"
```

## Flowin

## I. What Is Flowin?

Flowin is a content creation platform for the AI era, designed to help users create content, collaborate as a team, and manage knowledge in a variety of ways. It supports freely combining and dragging to lay out elements like text, images, audio, video, tables, and code blocks, letting users flexibly create rich, polished content. Flowin also offers team collaboration and permission control features, suited to joint creation and project management. In addition, Flowin integrates AI capabilities that can help users create content from scratch or refine existing content, improving creation efficiency and quality. Flowin is used across a wide range of scenarios, including teaching and research, work support, campus life, and content creator work. It also supports publishing and monetizing content, encouraging quality content creators to share knowledge through the platform and earn income.

Flowin offers multi-platform support, including web and mobile (iOS and Android), letting users create and collaborate anytime, anywhere.

Users on computer or tablet can view and use the Flowin web version within the ClassIn software's Space.

### Related Articles
Flowin Help Center

Flowin Official Website

## II. Creating a New Space / Document

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
Users on computer or tablet can view and use Flowin within Space. Once inside a personal or organization space in Flowin, you can view or create documents. Flowin documents support text, headings, tables, emoji, formulas, @mentioning members, AI, and other features.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to Flowin.
3. Enter or create a space.
4. Switch between personal/organization space.
5. View or create a new document.

#### Tablet
1. Choose a personal or organization space in the workspace.
2. Go to the directory.

## III. Personal Storage

Flowin space has a certain capacity limit — once exceeded, it can no longer be used. On computer, users can find Flowin within the ClassIn software's Space and go there to check their personal storage usage.

1. Expand the side toolbar.
2. Click your avatar → Account Settings.
3. Check My Benefits.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Resource Center"
source_title_zh: "资源中心"
```

## Resource Center

## I. What Is the Resource Center?

The Resource Center brings together a wealth of teaching material resources for teachers and students to use. Based on your specific needs, you can search for the textbook you need by choosing conditions such as grade, school level, subject, and publisher. In the Resource Center, you can find textbook materials across every subject — Chinese, math, English, history, geography, physics, and more. You can select the appropriate textbook based on the teaching requirements of different grades. In addition, the Resource Center offers textbooks across multiple school levels — elementary, middle, and high school — for students at different grades. You can select the corresponding school level to find the matching textbook resources. The Resource Center also offers textbooks from different publishers, since publishers' textbooks can vary somewhat, letting you choose the publisher's edition that suits your teaching needs. Through the Resource Center, teachers and students can conveniently access the teaching materials they need, helping improve teaching outcomes and learning results.

## II. Getting Courseware from the "Resource Center"

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
ClassIn offers a rich Resource Center covering online textbooks for every grade and subject across elementary, middle, and high school. These textbooks are available for teachers and students to support their teaching and learning. Besides textbooks, ClassIn also offers curated exam papers and featured topic collections. These exam papers help students practice and test their learning outcomes, while the featured topic collections offer an in-depth explanation and analysis of a specific topic, helping students better understand and master the material.

In addition, ClassIn offers courseware specific to the Beijing Dongcheng district and Shandong Qingyun district. This courseware is produced according to local education requirements and teaching realities, helping local teachers run their lessons more effectively. Users can search for courseware by publisher, or search for resources by keyword. This integration and provisioning makes it easier for teachers and students to access relevant educational resources, improving their teaching efficiency and learning outcomes.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Go to Space in the left navigation.
2. Go to Resource Center.
3. Go to All Resources.
4. Find the courseware by category or search, then click Get once you've found it.

## III. Deleting Courseware Obtained from the "Resource Center"

Delete courseware from your personal cloud drive, or delete courseware obtained from the Resource Center.

### Notes
Phone and tablet cannot delete courseware obtained from the "Resource Center."

## Steps
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to My Resources.
3. Find the resource courseware you want to delete, then click Delete.

# 8. Cloud Drive Space (Part 2: My Cloud Drive)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "My Cloud Drive (File Upload and Related Operations)"
source_title_zh: "个人云盘（文件上传等相关操作）"
```

## My Cloud Drive (File Upload and Related Operations)

## I. Creating/Uploading Files (Folders)

## Applies to
Everyone.

## When to use this
Before class, teachers or students can upload files from their local computer or phone to ClassIn's "Cloud Drive Space," so during class they can show files they've already uploaded to everyone else in the classroom.

## Usage Notes
My Cloud Drive supports creating new folders, as well as new lesson packs, whiteboards, assignment resources, online PPTs, collaborative documents, and other file types. Tablet does not support creating a new online PPT. Phone only supports creating folders, whiteboards, assignment resources, and collaborative documents. Only computer supports uploading a folder.

My Cloud Drive also supports uploading files, such as PPT, Word, PDF, images, audio, and video.

ClassIn has certain limits on uploaded file size: when uploading from a computer, a single file cannot exceed 500MB; when uploading from a phone or tablet, a single file cannot exceed 100MB. For TXT files, we recommend a size under 1MB to ensure normal use in the classroom. In addition, for video files uploaded from a phone or tablet: videos below 720p resolution cannot exceed 100MB, and videos above 720p resolution cannot exceed 3 minutes in length.

## Notes
The total folder limit is 2,000, and each folder is limited to 300 files.

On computer, you can drag and drop files and folders to upload them to My Cloud Drive.

Uploaded files need some time to convert — we recommend uploading in advance.

To use a file in the classroom, it must be opened from the cloud drive within the classroom.

Any file format can be uploaded to ClassIn, but only the file formats listed below can be opened and used normally in the classroom.

The file types supported for use in the ClassIn classroom are as follows:

| Type | Formats |
| --- | --- |
| ClassIn Whiteboard | edb |
| ClassIn Files | edt, edu, edx, eda, edv |
| PowerPoint Presentations | pptx, ppt, pptm |
| Word Documents | docx, doc |
| Excel Spreadsheets | xlsx, xls, csv |
| PDF Documents | pdf |
| Images | jpeg, jpg, png, bmp |
| Audio | mp3, wav, wma, aac, flac, m4a, oga |
| Video | mp4, 3gp, mpg, mpeg, 3g2, avi, flv, wmv, h264, m4v, mj2, mov, ogg, ogv, rm, qt, vob, webm |
| Text Documents | txt, html, htm, css, js, as, cpp, c, cc, cxx, h, java, md, matlab, pascal, pl, php, py, r, rb, ru, sql, swift, rbx, rs, go |
| Go (board game) | sgf |
| Chess/Xiangqi | fen, pgn |

## Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Space in the left navigation.
2. Go to My Cloud Drive.
3. Click Upload or New at the top to create a folder or file.

#### Phone
1. Go to Space.
2. In My Cloud Drive, click "+".
3. Create a folder/file, or Upload a file.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Editing an Uploaded PPT File (Online Editing)"
source_title_zh: "修改已上传的PPT文件（在线编辑）"
```

## II. Editing an Uploaded PPT File (Online Editing)

While using ClassIn, if a teacher needs to edit an uploaded PPT, they can go to My Cloud Drive under Space, find the file, open it, and click "Online Edit." The PPT converts to ClassIn's proprietary eppt format (which supports online editing), and the teacher can then edit and save it.

Phone and tablet do not have an "Online Edit" feature.

An eppt file that's been saved via online editing cannot be downloaded.

#### Computer
1. Go to Space in the left navigation.
2. Find the uploaded PPT file and open it.
3. Select Online Edit.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Forwarding a File"
source_title_zh: "转发文件"
```

## III. Forwarding a File

Files in My Cloud Drive support forwarding to a ClassIn class or friend.

1. Go to My Cloud Drive.
2. Check the file(s) you want to forward.
3. Click Forward below.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Downloading a File"
source_title_zh: "下载文件"
```

## IV. Downloading a File

Computer supports downloading files from My Cloud Drive, such as images, whiteboards, PPTs, PDFs, and Word documents. However, ClassIn's proprietary file formats — such as online slides (eppt format) and documents (edoc format) — cannot be downloaded or opened in other apps.

Phone and tablet support saving images to the local photo album, but for files like PPT and PDF, there's no direct download feature — you can open them in My Cloud Drive, then tap the share feature to open and view them in another app.

1. Check the file(s) you want to download.
2. Click Download below.

#### Tablet
1. Open the image or file.
2. Press and hold the image to save it, or tap the share button on the file page and choose to open it with another app.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Printing a File"
source_title_zh: "打印文件"
```

## V. Printing a File

When you need to turn a teaching file stored in "My Cloud Drive" into a physical printed document, teachers can use ClassIn's print feature; computer supports printing images, PPTs, PDFs, and similar files.

Phone and tablet do not have a "Print" feature.

1. Open the file.
2. Click Print in the top-right corner of the file.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Deleting a File (Folder)"
source_title_zh: "删除文件（文件夹）"
```

## VI. Deleting a File (Folder)

Files and folders in My Cloud Drive can be deleted, and cannot be recovered once deleted.

1. Check the file(s) or folder(s).
2. Click Delete below.
3. Click Delete to confirm.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Editing an Image"
source_title_zh: "编辑图片"
```

## VII. Editing an Image

Images in My Cloud Drive support viewing (including the original image), editing, zooming in/out, saving to the cloud drive/local photo album, or forwarding to a ClassIn class or friend.

Computer additionally supports: fitting/restoring the image to fill the screen and printing; after editing, the image is copied by default so you can paste it into other software.

1. Open the image.
2. Click Edit.
3. After editing the image, click Done.

Press and hold the image, then select Edit.
After editing the image, click Done — you can then choose to Forward or Save the image.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Editing an EDB Whiteboard File"
source_title_zh: "编辑edb板书文件"
```

## VIII. Editing an EDB Whiteboard File

An EDB whiteboard file opened from My Cloud Drive supports editing. On computer, an opened whiteboard supports saving and "save as" in edb, png, or pdf format; on phone or tablet, opening a whiteboard only supports saving to My Cloud Drive.

1. Open the EDB whiteboard file.
2. After editing the EDB, click Save, or click "···" then Save As.

After editing the EDB, click Save.

Open the EDB whiteboard file in My Cloud Drive.

# 8. Cloud Drive Space (Part 3: Organization Cloud Drive)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Organization Cloud Drive (File Upload and Related Operations)"
source_title_zh: "组织云盘（文件上传等相关操作）"
```

## Organization Cloud Drive (File Upload and Related Operations)

## I. Creating a New Organization Drive

## Applies to
The school/institution's primary account.

Backend school/institution administrators with "Organization Cloud Drive" permission.

## When to use this
During teaching research, multiple teachers on a research team often need to share materials and collaborate. Using the Organization Cloud Drive meets this need. Beyond what My Cloud Drive offers, the Organization Cloud Drive also provides a space for multiple people to share and build together.

## Usage Notes
The school/institution's primary account, and backend school/institution administrators with "Organization Cloud Drive" permission, can create an organization drive under "Organization Cloud Drive" in the "Space" section of the ClassIn software. Once the organization drive is created, files and subfolders can be added to it.

## Notes
Phone does not support creating an organization drive within the Organization Cloud Drive.

## Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Space in the left navigation.
2. Go to Organization Cloud Drive.
3. Select the school/institution.
4. Create an organization drive.
5. Enter the organization drive's folder name.
6. Click Create.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Creating/Uploading Files (Folders)"
source_title_zh: "新建/上传文件(文件夹)"
```

## II. Creating/Uploading Files (Folders)

Teachers with operate/manage permission for a folder.

Teachers, administrators, and primary account holders with the relevant permission can create/upload folders and files under the organization drive, and can also upload files from My Cloud Drive to the organization drive.

The organization drive supports creating new folders, as well as new whiteboards, assignment resources, online PPTs, collaborative documents, and other file types. Tablet does not support creating a new online PPT. Phone only supports creating folders, whiteboards, assignment resources, and collaborative documents. Only computer supports uploading a folder.

The organization drive also supports uploading files, such as PPT, Word, PDF, images, audio, and video.

ClassIn has certain limits on uploaded file size: when uploading from a computer, a single file cannot exceed 500MB; when uploading from a phone or tablet, a single file cannot exceed 100MB. For TXT files, we recommend a size under 1MB to ensure normal use in the classroom. In addition, for video files uploaded from a phone or tablet: videos below 720p resolution cannot exceed 100MB, and videos above 720p resolution cannot exceed 3 minutes in length.

The total folder limit is 2,000, and each folder is limited to 300 files.

On computer, you can drag and drop files and folders to upload them to My Cloud Drive.

Uploaded files need some time to convert — we recommend uploading in advance.

To use a file in the classroom, it must be opened from the cloud drive within the classroom.

Any file format can be uploaded to ClassIn, but only the file formats listed below can be opened and used normally in the classroom.

The file types supported for use in the ClassIn classroom are as follows:

| Type | Formats |
| --- | --- |
| ClassIn Whiteboard | edb |
| ClassIn Files | edt, edu, edx, eda, edv |
| PowerPoint Presentations | pptx, ppt, pptm |
| Word Documents | docx, doc |
| Excel Spreadsheets | xlsx, xls, csv |
| PDF Documents | pdf |
| Images | jpeg, jpg, png, bmp |
| Audio | mp3, wav, wma, aac, flac, m4a, oga |
| Video | mp4, 3gp, mpg, mpeg, 3g2, avi, flv, wmv, h264, m4v, mj2, mov, ogg, ogv, rm, qt, vob, webm |
| Text Documents | txt, html, htm, css, js, as, cpp, c, cc, cxx, h, java, md, matlab, pascal, pl, php, py, r, rb, ru, sql, swift, rbx, rs, go |
| Go (board game) | sgf |
| Chess/Xiangqi | fen, pgn |

1. Go to the organization drive.
2. Click Upload or New at the top to create a folder or file.

#### Phone
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to Organization Space.
3. Click "+".
4. Create a folder/file, or Upload a file.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Member Permissions"
source_title_zh: "成员权限"
```

## III. Member Permissions

Backend school/institution administrators with "Organization Cloud Drive — Member Management" permission.

Teachers with manage permission for a folder.

Teachers, administrators, and primary account holders with the relevant permission can add and set members and manage permissions for the organization drive and its subfolders. Members with the appropriate permission can view and use files under the organization drive.

**Member management permission levels for the organization drive and its subfolders:**

| Permission | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Manage | Folder support: setting member management permission (adding, authorizing, and removing members), and uploading, creating, duplicating, moving, renaming, and deleting folders under the organization drive.<br><br>File support: viewing, uploading, creating, forwarding, downloading, deleting, duplicating, moving, saving to cloud drive, renaming, printing, and online-editing PPT/edoc files, plus enabling the file-transfer feature under file permissions. |
| Operate | Folder support: viewing member management permission, and uploading, creating, duplicating, and renaming folders under the organization drive.<br><br>File support: viewing, uploading, creating, duplicating, renaming, printing, and online-editing PPT/edoc files.<br><br>Supports deleting files and folders they uploaded/created themselves. |
| View Only | Only supports viewing the folder and its files. |
| Not Visible | Cannot view the folder or its files. |

**Super Admin:** refers to a backend school/institution administrator with "Organization Cloud Drive" permission. In the Backend Management System, an administrator who only has "Organization Cloud Drive" checked can view, create, and rename organization drives, and view member management, in both the backend and the organization cloud drive in the ClassIn software — but cannot delete folders, nor set folder member permissions. For files, they can view, upload, create, forward, duplicate, move, save to cloud drive, rename, print, and online-edit PPT/edoc files, but cannot download or delete files, nor enable the file-transfer feature.

Additional permissions must be checked separately to: delete files/folders and enable file transfer ("Organization Cloud Drive — Delete"); download files ("Organization Cloud Drive — Download"); set member permissions for the organization drive/folders ("Organization Cloud Drive — Member Management").

Phone does not support viewing or setting member management permission (adding, authorizing, removing members) in the Organization Cloud Drive.

"Enterprise Edition ClassIn" can only add teachers within the same organization.

"School Edition ClassIn" can add both teachers and students from the school as organization folder members (students currently only support being set to "View Only" or "Not Visible" permission).

In the "Backend Management System," a deactivated teacher automatically has their organization cloud drive permission revoked; once reactivated, they must go through the new-member process again to regain access.

For schools using the "K-12 Backend Management System," when a teacher leaves/is deleted, or a student graduates/is deleted, the system automatically revokes their organization cloud drive permission; if a former teacher returns, or a student re-enrolls, they must go through the new-member process again to regain organization cloud drive access.

1. Find the folder you want to grant permission for, then click "···" on the right.
2. Go to Member Management.
3. Add a member, or edit member permissions.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "File Permissions"
source_title_zh: "文件权限"
```

## IV. File Permissions

Backend school/institution administrators with "Organization Cloud Drive — Delete" permission.

If a teacher, administrator, or primary account holder with the relevant permission enables "Allow Operate/View-Only Members to Forward/Download/Save to Personal Cloud Drive" (transfer permission) for a file, members with "Operate" or "View Only" permission can also transfer that file out.

Collaborative documents (edoc), edu, edx, assignment resources, and similar files do not support setting transfer permission.

Phone does not support viewing or setting the file-transfer feature in the Organization Cloud Drive.

1. Go into the folder.
2. Find the file, click "···," then go to File Permissions.
3. Edit the file permissions.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Forwarding a File"
source_title_zh: "转发文件"
```

## V. Forwarding a File

Requires file permission set to allow transfer, and requires the teacher to have view/operate permission for the folder the file is in.

Teachers, administrators, and primary account holders with the relevant permission can find a file in the ClassIn software's Organization Cloud Drive and forward it to a ClassIn class or friend.

1. Check the file, then click Forward.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Saving to Cloud Drive"
source_title_zh: "保存至云盘"
```

## VI. Saving to Cloud Drive

Teachers, administrators, and primary account holders with the relevant permission can find a file in the ClassIn software's Organization Cloud Drive and save it to My Cloud Drive.

1. Find the file, click "···," then click Save to Cloud Drive.
2. Choose a save path, then click Confirm.

Select the file.
Click Save to Cloud Drive.
Choose a save path, then click Save.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Downloading a File"
source_title_zh: "下载文件"
```

## VII. Downloading a File

Backend school/institution administrators with "Organization Cloud Drive — Download" permission.

Computer supports downloading files from the Organization Cloud Drive, such as images, whiteboards, PPTs, PDFs, and Word documents. However, ClassIn's proprietary file formats — such as online slides (eppt format) and documents (edoc format) — cannot be downloaded or opened in other apps.

Phone and tablet support saving images to the local photo album, but for files like PPT and PDF, there's no download feature — you can open them in the Organization Cloud Drive, then tap the share feature to open and view them in another app.

#### Computer
1. Check the file(s) you want to download.
2. Click Download below.

#### Tablet
1. Open the image or file.
2. Press and hold the image to save it, or tap the share button on the file page and choose to open it with another app.

Open the image or file in My Cloud Drive.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Printing a File"
source_title_zh: "打印文件"
```

## VIII. Printing a File

When you need to turn a teaching file stored in the "Organization Cloud Drive" into a physical printed document, teachers can use ClassIn's print feature; computer supports printing images, PPTs, PDFs, and similar files.

Phone and tablet do not have a "Print" feature.

1. Open the file.
2. Click Print in the top-right corner of the file.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Deleting a File (Folder)"
source_title_zh: "删除文件（文件夹）"
```

## IX. Deleting a File (Folder)

Teachers, administrators, and primary account holders with the relevant permission can find a file (or folder) in the ClassIn software's Organization Cloud Drive and delete it. In addition, a teacher with "Operate" permission can delete a folder they created themselves, and can also delete files they uploaded themselves.

Files and folders cannot be recovered once deleted.

1. Find the file or folder you want to delete.
2. Click Delete.

# 8. Cloud Drive Space (Part 4: Question Bank Center)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Question Bank Center"
source_title_zh: "题库中心"
```

## Question Bank Center

## I. What Is the Question Bank Center?

The Question Bank Center gives users a wealth of question resources, including a personal question bank, an organization question bank, and ClassIn's official question bank. Users can choose different question types to add as needed, such as single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, short-answer, and comprehensive questions. A comprehensive question can contain several sub-questions, with sub-question types including single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and short-answer.

Users can add questions one at a time, or in bulk, whichever is more convenient. Once questions are added, users can also create an exam paper and add already-added questions to it, or add questions directly while creating the paper.

For teachers under institution/school teacher management, whether the organization question bank shows up under Question Bank Center in the ClassIn app's Space, and whether they can view and use its content, depends on their member-management permission for the relevant school level and subject.

Whether for personal study or organizational training, the Question Bank Center can meet a wide range of user needs, offering efficient, convenient question management and exam paper creation.

## II. My Question Bank

## 1. Adding a School Level and Subject

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
Users on computer or tablet can set up school levels and subjects in My Question Bank, making it easy to later categorize added questions under a specific school level and subject.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Space.
2. Go to Question Bank Center.
3. Go to My Question Bank.
4. Add a school level / subject.

## 2. Adding Questions

When adding questions in My Question Bank, users can set up knowledge points or chapters as needed, then add questions under the corresponding knowledge point or chapter. When adding questions on computer or tablet, users can add several question types: single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, short-answer, and comprehensive questions (a comprehensive question can contain several sub-questions, supporting single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and short-answer sub-types). When adding questions on phone, only single-choice, multiple-choice, and true/false questions are supported. Once questions are added, users can delete, duplicate, forward, or move them to another subject. Teachers with organization question bank permission can also add questions to the organization question bank(s) they have access to.

When you need to add multiple questions at once, you can use the bulk-add feature on computer. First, download the Excel or Word template from the bulk-add window, then add your questions following the template's format. Once done, upload the completed template back into the bulk-add window. If you're already familiar with the bulk-add format, you can also directly copy and paste correctly formatted questions into the raw-question entry area within the bulk-add window.

#### Computer
1. Select a school level/subject and Questions.
2. Click "+ Add Question" / "Bulk Add Questions."

#### Tablet
1. Click "+ Add Question."

## 3. Adding an Exam Paper

Users can add an exam paper in My Question Bank. When creating a paper, you can select questions from My Question Bank to add to it, or add new questions directly while creating the paper; on computer, bulk-adding questions is also supported. Already-added papers can be duplicated, forwarded, or moved to a different school level or subject; on computer, you can also download a paper locally. Teachers with organization question bank permission can also add a paper to the corresponding organization question bank.

1. Select a school level/subject.
2. Select Exam Papers.
3. Click Add Exam Paper.

Click "+ Add Exam Paper."

Click "+" to add an exam paper.

## 4. Editing/Deleting Questions and Exam Papers

An already-added question can be edited, deleted, duplicated, forwarded to a ClassIn class or friend, moved to a different subject, or added to an organization question bank.

An already-added exam paper can be edited, duplicated, downloaded, deleted, forwarded to a ClassIn class or friend, moved to a different school level, used to create a quiz and publish it to another class, or have its questions added to an organization question bank.

### Notes
Phone only supports editing single-choice, multiple-choice, and true/false questions.

Neither phone nor tablet supports downloading an exam paper.

1. Select a school level/subject, Questions, or Exam Papers.
2. Find the question or paper, click Edit, or click "···" to delete it.

## 5. Adding a Question/Exam Paper to the Organization Question Bank

The school/institution's primary account, school/institution administrators with "Question Bank Center" permission, and teachers with "Operate" or "Manage" permission for the relevant school level/subject in the organization question bank.

Teachers with the relevant permission can add a question or exam paper from My Question Bank to the organization question bank.

1. Find the question or exam paper, then click Add to Organization Question Bank.

## 6. Compiling & Downloading an Exam Paper, and Creating a New Quiz

Everyone, or class teachers.

Questions and exam papers in "My Question Bank" support being added to the Question Basket, where you can view, delete, and reorder questions, and also compile & download a paper or create a new quiz.

**Compile & Download:** jumps to the exam paper page, supporting saving the paper; on computer, you can also download the paper locally.

**Create New Quiz:** jumps to the new-quiz page, where teachers can publish it to a class and save the paper to My Question Bank; on computer, you can also download the paper locally.

In addition, teachers can also download an exam paper's content directly and create a quiz under "My Question Bank → Exam Papers."

Phone does not support compiling & downloading a paper or creating a quiz.

Tablet supports creating a quiz and saving a paper to the "Exam Papers" section under "My Question Bank," but does not support downloading the paper's content.

1. Find the question or exam paper, then click Add to Question Basket, or click "···" next to a paper.
2. Compile & Download, or Create New Quiz.

## III. Organization Question Bank

The school/institution's primary account, and school/institution administrators with "Question Bank Center" permission.

Teachers with the relevant permission can add school levels and subjects, making it easy to later categorize added questions under a specific school level or subject.

Phone does not support creating or configuring school levels/subjects under the organization question bank.

1. Go to Organization Question Bank.
2. Select the school/institution.

## 2. Deleting a School Level/Subject

When a school level/subject's question bank is no longer needed at all, it can be deleted. Once deleted, the questions and exam papers in that bank are also permanently deleted; other users will no longer be able to pull questions or papers from that school level/subject when creating a quiz. This cannot be undone once deleted.

Phone does not support deleting.

1. Go to Manage.
2. Delete the school level/subject.

## 3. Enabling/Disabling a School Level/Subject

The school/institution's primary account, and school/institution administrators with "Question Bank Center" permission.

When a school level/subject's question bank in the organization question bank is temporarily not needed, teachers with the relevant permission can choose to disable it. Once disabled, the questions and exam paper data in that bank aren't lost, but can no longer be viewed or used.

Phone does not support enabling or disabling.

1. Enable or Disable the question bank.

## 4. Setting Members and Permissions

The school/institution's primary account, school/institution administrators with "Organization Cloud Drive" permission, and teachers with "Manage" permission for the relevant school level/subject.

Teachers with the relevant permission can add and set members and manage permissions for a school level/subject in the organization question bank. Member and management permissions are as follows:

| Permission | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Manage | Can manage members and add/edit/delete questions and exam papers.<br><br>Questions: view, add, add to My Question Bank, edit, move to, duplicate, forward, delete, add to Question Basket.<br><br>Exam papers: view, add, add to My Question Bank, edit, move to, duplicate, download, forward, delete, add to Question Basket, create new quiz. |
| Operate | Can add/edit/delete questions and exam papers.<br><br>Questions: view, add, edit, delete, add to Question Basket.<br><br>Exam papers: view, add, edit, delete, add to Question Basket, create new quiz. |
| View Only | Can only use questions and exam papers.<br><br>Questions: view, add to Question Basket.<br><br>Exam papers: view, add to Question Basket, create new quiz. |
| Not Visible | Cannot view content under the organization question bank. |

**Super Admin:** refers to a backend school/institution administrator with "Question Bank Center" permission.

Phone does not support setting members and permissions.

1. Go to Member Management.
2. Add a member, or edit member permissions.

## 5. Adding Questions

The school/institution's primary account.

School/institution administrators with "Organization Question Bank" permission.

Teachers with "Manage" or "Operate" permission for the relevant school level/subject.

When adding questions in My Question Bank, users can set up knowledge points or chapters as needed, then add questions under the corresponding knowledge point or chapter. When adding questions on computer or tablet, users can add several question types: single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, short-answer, and comprehensive questions (a comprehensive question can contain several sub-questions, supporting single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and short-answer sub-types). When adding questions on phone, only single-choice, multiple-choice, and true/false questions are supported. Once questions are added, users can delete, duplicate, forward, or move them to another subject. The primary account, organization question bank administrators, and teachers with "Manage" permission for the relevant school level/subject can also add questions to My Question Bank.

1. Select the school/institution.

## 6. Adding an Exam Paper

Organization question bank members with "Manage" or "Operate" permission.

Users can add an exam paper in the organization question bank. When creating a paper, you can select questions from both My Question Bank and the organization question bank to add to it, or add new questions directly while creating the paper; on computer, bulk-adding questions is also supported. An already-added paper supports duplicating, forwarding, deleting, moving to a different school level or subject, and creating a quiz; on computer, you can also download the paper locally. The primary account, organization question bank administrators, and teachers with "Manage" permission for the relevant school level/subject can also add questions to My Question Bank.

1. Select a school level/subject and Exam Papers.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-08d_cloud-drive-question-bank.md -->
