# 8. Cloud Drive Space (Part 5: ClassIn File Formats and Types)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassIn File Formats and Types"
source_title_zh: "ClassIn_文件格式与类型"
```

## ClassIn File Formats and Types

## I. ClassIn File Format Overview

| File Format | Purpose | Can Users Create/Develop It? | How to Get Existing Resources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| edb | A whiteboard file made up of images and text | Yes | Space → Resource Center → Featured Zone → EDB Courseware |
| edoc | Collaborative document | Yes | Must be created by the user |
| edoc | Online PPT | Yes | Must be created by the user |
| eda | Classroom extension tool | No | Space → My Cloud Drive → "?" → ClassIn User Guide → Other Classroom Extension Tools |
| edlink | Web link | Yes | Space → Resource Center → Elementary Math → Math Mini-Tools |
| edu | Interactive classroom widget | Can be developed, but not recommended | Not recommended |
| edx | Interactive classroom widget | Yes | Must be created by the user |
| edv | A file opened in the classroom that's visible to the teacher's side but not visible to students | Can be developed, but not recommended | Not recommended |
| edt | Classroom skin | Yes | Must be created by the user |

## II. Files Supported for Opening in the Classroom

All the file formats listed below can be uploaded to your ClassIn cloud drive, and all can be opened in the classroom.

| File Type | Formats |
| --- | --- |
| ClassIn Whiteboard | edb |
| ClassIn Files | edt, edu, eda, edv, edx |
| PowerPoint Presentations | pptx, ppt, pptm |
| Word Documents | docx, doc |
| Excel Spreadsheets | xlsx, xls, csv |
| PDF Documents | pdf |
| Images | jpeg, jpg, png, bmp |
| Audio | mp3, wav, wma, aac, flac, m4a, oga |
| Video | mp4, 3gp, mpg, mpeg, 3g2, avi, flv, wmv, h264, m4v, mj2, mov, ogg, ogv, rm, qt, vob, webm |
| Text Documents | txt, html, htm, css, js, as, cpp, c, cc, cxx, h, java, md, matlab, pascal, pl, php, py, r, rb, ru, sql, swift, rbx, rs, go |
| Go (board game) | sgf |
| Chess/Xiangqi | fen, pgn |

## III. Introduction to ClassIn File Types

### 1. EDB Files

#### (1) EDB Overview

An EDB whiteboard file is a ClassIn-exclusive format made up of images and text, on which you can drag, draw, and otherwise mark up courseware content.

#### (2) Creating an EDB Whiteboard File

**Method 1 (create a new EDB whiteboard file):** Space → My Cloud Drive → New Whiteboard.

**Method 2 (edit an EDB whiteboard file):** Space → My Cloud Drive → open the EDB whiteboard file → Edit.

**Method 3:** enter the Whiteboard (no scheduling needed) or the classroom → create/edit the EDB whiteboard file → Save Whiteboard.

**a. Creating an EDB file inside the Whiteboard or classroom**

Use the classroom's mini-tools: select Move/Pen/Text/Eraser/Screenshot/Load Local Image, and so on.

Use standard shortcuts to quickly copy and paste an image: Copy: Ctrl+C; Paste: Ctrl+V.

**b. Saving an EDB file inside the Whiteboard or classroom**

When a teacher needs to save whiteboard content they just edited, click the toolbox's "Save/Share Whiteboard" to save it, or share it with a friend.

When saving a whiteboard, you can change the background color (transparent is supported).

When saving a whiteboard, you can choose from three file formats — edb/png/pdf. Multiple formats can be selected when saving locally; only one format can be selected when saving to the cloud drive.

### 2. EDOC Files

#### (1) EDOC Overview

EDOC is a document format ClassIn provides for collaborative editing within ClassIn. It can be used for teaching-research lesson prep, or for collecting information. Opening an EDOC document in the classroom does not support marking it up with the pen or text tools.

#### (2) Ways to Create an EDOC

**Method 1 (create a new collaborative document):** Space → My Cloud Drive → New → Collaborative Document. You can find it in My Cloud Drive, and share it with a ClassIn friend or class.

**Method 2 (create a new collaborative document):** Inside the classroom → Toolbox → Collaboration → Document. This also creates an EDOC, and you can authorize students, temporarily granting them collaborative editing permission.

**Method 3 (edit a collaborative document online):** Space → My Cloud Drive → open a Word file → click Online Edit.

#### (3) Adding Comments Within an EDOC

Within an EDOC, click the "+" in the document to add a comment.

### 3. EPPT Files

#### (1) EPPT Overview

EPPT is a PPT format ClassIn provides for editing within ClassIn. It can be used during teaching-research lesson prep.

#### (2) Ways to Create an EPPT

**Method 1 (create a new online PPT):** Space → My Cloud Drive → New → Online PPT. You can find it in My Cloud Drive, and share it with a ClassIn friend or class.

**Method 2 (edit an uploaded PPT):** Space → My Cloud Drive → open the PPT → click Online Edit.

### 4. EDA Files

#### (1) EDA Overview

EDA files are a category of classroom extension tools developed by ClassIn and provided as a shared resource for users. There are currently four: Go, Minesweeper, Tug of War, and Sudoku. Once authorized, students can operate them.

#### (2) Where to Find EDA Files

Space → My Cloud Drive → "?" in the bottom-right corner → ClassIn User Guide → Other Classroom Extension Tools.

### 5. EDLINK Files

#### (1) EDLINK Overview

EDLINK is a web link. Compared to saving a link in a browser, EDLINK can be uploaded to the cloud drive and forwarded; in the classroom, only the teacher role can operate it, while the teaching assistant role and student role can watch it being used.

#### (2) How to Create an EDLINK

Create a new TXT text file locally on Windows (Notepad file format).

Open the TXT file and paste in the URL (just enter the URL itself).

Save the TXT file as a different name, choosing "All Files" as the save type, and enter ".edlink" as the file extension.

After locating the file locally, right-click it and check Properties to confirm the file type shows as EDLINK.

Upload the local EDLINK file to Space → My Cloud Drive in ClassIn — it can then be opened.

### 6. EDU Files

#### (1) EDU Overview

An EDU file is a special file that contains a website address. When a teacher opens an EDU file during class, both the teacher and every student in the classroom will independently open that website address through their own browser. This way, every student can browse and use the website on their own, without interfering with each other. EDU files are typically used in scenarios such as:

**Surveys/questionnaires:** the teacher can distribute a survey or exam to each student and collect each student's responses.

**Self-paced practice:** students can use a self-testing practice website to practice independently. EDU files support audio, allowing students to do speaking and listening practice.

#### (2) How to Create an EDU

**Step 1:**

Get the URL of the website you'll need during class.

Using NoBook as an example of how to get the URL:

a. Visit the "NoBook" official website: https://www.nobook.com/index.html, and register a new account or log into an existing one.

b. From Premium Experiments, select one that requires students to do hands-on operation during class.

Note: if some students don't have a paid NoBook account, choose a free experiment so students aren't blocked by permission restrictions.

c. Click the selected experiment, then use the share button to get that NoBook experiment's share URL.

d. Open the share URL in a browser — it will redirect, giving you the experiment's actual website address.

Note: if the URL doesn't open properly in an EDU file, try removing the trailing "=" character from the address, then try opening it in EDU again.

Using Wenjuanxing (a survey tool) as an example of how to get the URL:

a. Visit the "Wenjuanxing" official website at www.wjx.cn, and register a new account or log into an existing one.

b. After logging in, start creating a survey.

c. Click the option you need to add questions, or click "Bulk Add Exam Questions" on the right.

d. Once you've finished editing the exam paper, click Finish Editing.

e. Once the paper is edited, click Distribute Survey.

f. Click the "Copy" button to copy the link — this gives you the Wenjuanxing website address.

**Step 2:**

Create a new EDU file, and fill in the file's name and website address.

Note: once created, open the file within "ClassIn Classroom → Space → My Cloud Drive" to check whether the website address is correct.

**Step 3:**

During a formal class, the teacher can open this EDU file from the cloud drive; each student's device will then independently open that website address for self-paced practice.

Note: if the website requires login before students can practice, we recommend scheduling a trial session first so students have enough time to log in — once logged in on a device, they won't need to log in again afterward.

**Step 4:**

While students practice independently, they won't affect one another and can complete their own tasks on their own.

Teachers cannot see students' progress within the ClassIn classroom. If the website has its own data-tracking feature (such as survey statistics), you can view the data directly in that website's backend.

Teacher-side view.

Student A's view.

Student B's view.

### 7. EDV Files

#### (1) EDV Overview

EDV is a courseware format opened within the classroom. Unlike other courseware formats, EDV is only visible to the teacher — it's not visible on the student side (neither the window nor its content).

#### (2) EDV Usage Notes

Teachers upload the EDV file to Space → My Cloud Drive, then open it to view it there.

### 8. EDX Files

An EDX file is a special file that contains a website address. When a teacher opens an EDX file during class, it launches the Multi-Directional Browser to open the URL inside the file; the way students and the teacher interact with it is the same as when the teacher opens the Multi-Directional Browser tool directly.

#### (2) How to Create an EDX

Get the URL of the website you'll need during class — for example, www.eeo.cn.

Create a new EDX file, and fill in the file's name and the website address.

Note: once created, you can open it directly for a preview to check whether the webpage displays correctly.

During a formal class, the teacher can open this EDX file from Space → My Cloud Drive; once opened, class can proceed exactly as with the Multi-Directional Browser.

Note: within the classroom, this file type can only be opened by the teacher — no other role has permission to open it. Outside the classroom, there's no such restriction, and it can be previewed normally.

Student-side view is as follows.

### 9. EDT Files

#### (1) EDT Overview

EDT is used for the skin background of the ClassIn classroom; only 1280 x 720 pixel JPG or JPEG images with no transparency channel are supported, saved in EDT format.

#### (2) How to Create an EDT

Open a 1280 x 720 pixel JPG or JPEG image with no transparency channel in an image-editing tool.

Save it as a different name, choosing JPEG as the save type, and enter ".edt" as the file extension.

After locating the file locally, right-click it and check Properties to confirm the file type shows as EDT.

Upload the local EDT file to Space → My Cloud Drive in ClassIn — it can then be opened in the classroom.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-08e_cloud-drive-file-formats.md -->

# 9. Public Class

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Creating a Public Class"
source_title_zh: "创建公开课"
```

## Creating a Public Class

### What Is a "Public Class"?
On the ClassIn platform, a "Public Class" is a quick, simple way to set up a class session. Unlike a regular class, a "Public Class" has no class group chat — creating one immediately generates a standalone class session. Students can join a "Public Class" in one of two ways: scanning the public class QR code, or entering the public class's "In" passcode. Because of this, "Public Class" is especially well suited to scenarios like parent meetings, one-off tutoring sessions, interest-group classes, and various lectures.

### Applies to
The school/institution's primary account.

Backend school/institution administrators with "Client — Create Public Class, Class" permission.

## Usage Notes
Teachers with the relevant permission can create a public class from the top of the ClassIn app's home page; the lead teacher defaults to whoever created it.

### Related Articles
"Adding Students to a Public Class"

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Home.
2. Click Create Public Class.
3. Configure the relevant parameters.

#### Phone

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Adding Students to a Public Class"
source_title_zh: "公开课添加学生"
```

## Adding Students to a Public Class

### Applies to
The public class's lead teacher or co-teacher.

### Usage Notes
In a public class, teachers cannot add their ClassIn friends as public class students directly. Instead, the teacher shares the "Public Class QR Code" and "Public Class In Passcode" with the students who need to join, and students then sign up on their own to enter the public class.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Schedule.
2. Select the date.
3. Click the public class.
4. Choose a way to add students: QR code sharing, In passcode, or email invitation.

#### Phone
1. Click Invite Students.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Editing a Public Class"
source_title_zh: "修改公开课"
```

## Editing a Public Class

### Applies to
The public class's lead teacher.

### Usage Notes
In the ClassIn client, the public class's lead teacher can edit an already-created public class. Editable information and settings include: the public class name, class date, class start time, class duration, co-teacher(s), on-stage headcount, cloud recording, web live stream, web playback, and so on. Please follow the related rules and time limits below.

Settings that can be changed up to 20 minutes before class starts: public class name, class start time and duration, co-teacher(s), OMO livestream broadcast, on-stage headcount, cloud recording (Record ClassIn Classroom, Record On-Site), web live stream, web playback, show on-stage seats, and students auto-join on stage.

Settings that can be changed at any time before the class session ends: adding/replacing co-teacher(s), and web playback.

Settings that can be changed at any time, without time restriction: web playback.

### Notes
Before the public class officially starts (including the pre-entry window), it can be deleted at any time. However, once the public class reaches its scheduled start time, it can no longer be deleted.

A public class that has already ended cannot be deleted.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Schedule.
2. Select the date.
3. Click the public class.
4. Click Edit.

#### Phone
1. Click "···."

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Deleting a Public Class"
source_title_zh: "删除公开课"
```

## Deleting a Public Class

### Applies to
The public class's lead teacher.

### Usage Notes
In the ClassIn client, the public class's lead teacher can delete an already-created public class before it officially starts.

### Notes
Before the public class officially starts (including the pre-entry window), it can be deleted at any time. However, once the public class reaches its scheduled start time, it can no longer be deleted.

A deleted public class cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

A public class that has already ended cannot be deleted.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Schedule.
2. Select the date.
3. Click the public class.
4. Click Delete.

#### Phone
1. Click "···."

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-09_public-class.md -->

# 10. Prep Room and Local Classroom

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Local Classroom (Study Room / Whiteboard Editor)"
source_title_zh: "本地教室（自习室/板书编辑器）"
```

## Local Classroom (Study Room / Whiteboard Editor)

### Applies to
Everyone.

### What Is a Local Classroom?
In ClassIn, the "Local Classroom" refers to the "Whiteboard" feature on the ClassIn main interface. Unlike the "whiteboard" used for teachers and students to write or draw within a class session, the "Whiteboard" on the main interface is actually a local classroom for getting familiar with ClassIn's features and controls — especially useful for teachers and students using ClassIn for the first time. Using this feature can significantly improve classroom efficiency and teaching quality.

For teachers already skilled with ClassIn, they can go into the "Whiteboard" on the main interface anytime to create whiteboard content and write lesson plans. In addition, the "Whiteboard" on the main interface also supports local recording, giving teachers more convenience for teaching prep and practice.

### When to Use This
**Getting a full picture of classroom features:** teachers and students can go into the "Whiteboard" on the ClassIn main interface anytime to learn and get familiar with the various classroom features.

**Better class prep:** teachers can go into the "Whiteboard" on the ClassIn main interface ahead of time to learn how to use the tools and features they'll need in class. Teachers can prepare lesson plans, create whiteboard content, and edit courseware, getting fully ready for class in advance, ensuring the class content flows smoothly and continuously.

**More classroom interaction:** for teachers already skilled with ClassIn, the "Whiteboard" on the main interface becomes an efficient teaching aid. They can create polished whiteboard content, presenting the lesson's key points through a mix of text and images, which grabs students' attention and improves teaching outcomes.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Click Whiteboard to enter the local whiteboard.

#### Phone
1. Click Growth.
2. Go to Whiteboard.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Teacher Lesson Prep"
source_title_zh: "教师备课"
```

## Teacher Lesson Prep

# How Do Teachers Prepare Lessons?

The "Prep Room" is a lesson preparation feature ClassIn provides for teachers, for creating courseware and whiteboard content before class officially starts. Once a class session is created, the lead teacher and co-teacher(s) can enter the prep room to prepare, starting 20 minutes before class starts. Only the lead teacher and co-teacher(s) can access the prep room — no one else can enter.

In the prep room, teachers can prepare and edit courseware and whiteboard content in advance, and can exit and re-enter the prep room anytime to keep working on their teaching content. The prep room is an independent virtual classroom, so teachers won't run into other teachers there. Once there's less than 20 minutes left before class officially starts, the lead teacher using a computer can go directly from the prep room into the formal classroom.

When the lead teacher prepares on computer, the whiteboard content in the prep room is automatically saved once the lead teacher exits, and they can choose to open the prep content once they enter the formal classroom. When the lead teacher prepares on phone or tablet, when exiting the classroom they can choose to save the whiteboard's content to the cloud drive; once in the formal classroom, if they need to open that prep content, they can find and open it from the cloud drive.

Regardless of which device a co-teacher uses to prepare, exiting the prep room does not automatically save the prep content — when exiting, they're prompted whether to save the whiteboard content to the cloud drive.

# Applies To
"Lead teacher" and "co-teacher."

# Notes
Within 20 minutes of the official class start time, a lead teacher preparing on phone or tablet cannot automatically enter the formal classroom — the teacher needs to manually exit the prep room and re-enter the formal classroom.

# Steps

## Step 1: Enter the Prep Room

#### Computer
1. Go to Schedule in the left navigation.
2. Select the class date.
3. Enter the prep classroom.

## Step 2: Create Whiteboard Content

### (1) Opening Teaching Courseware

The teacher opens already-uploaded courseware, or directly drags courseware from their local computer into the classroom. If the courseware contains animation effects or video, we recommend testing it in advance to make sure it plays properly. In the classroom, you can use the "Click Tool" to operate it.

### (2) Pen

Teachers can mark up, write, and draw on the whiteboard or courseware. While drawing, you can choose to draw several shapes, including a perfect circle, ellipse, square, rectangle, irregular triangle, equilateral triangle, straight line, and curve. This variety of shape options makes drawing more flexible and versatile, meeting different drawing needs. Besides choosing a shape, the Pen tool also lets teachers freely adjust the pen's color and thickness, achieving more professional, refined drawing effects. Teachers can choose a suitable color as needed — whether bright or deep tones — to give the drawing more artistic character. In addition, teachers can choose solid or dashed lines for more professional, delicate drawing effects.

### (3) Text Entry

Teachers can use the "Text" tool to type any text, letters, or numbers onto the whiteboard or courseware. You can set font color and size before typing.

### (4) Select/Move (Secondary Editing)

Teachers can use this tool to single-select, multi-select, and move various whiteboard elements — images, shapes, text, and so on. Once you select an element on the whiteboard, a "secondary editing" bar pops up below it. Teachers can use the shortcuts in this bar to modify and adjust the selected element.

### (5) Eraser

Teachers can use the eraser tool to erase content drawn or written with the Pen tool on the whiteboard, and it also includes a "one-click clear" feature — if you encounter whiteboard elements that can't be erased normally, use "one-click clear" to wipe the entire whiteboard clean.

### (6) Saving the Whiteboard

Teachers can use this tool during or after lesson prep to save the whiteboard's content locally on their computer or to the cloud drive.

## Step 3: Going from the Prep Room into the Formal Classroom

When a lead teacher prepares on computer, once there's less than 20 minutes left before official class start, the prep room shows a prompt asking whether to enter the formal classroom right away — clicking "Enter Now" jumps to the formal classroom and automatically loads the prep content; if the lead teacher exits the prep room and then enters the formal classroom, the formal classroom shows a prompt asking whether to load the prep content — click "Yes" to load it.

When a teacher prepares on phone or tablet, once there's less than 20 minutes left before official class start, the prep room shows a notification that they can now enter the formal classroom; the teacher then needs to manually exit the prep room and enter the formal classroom, and when exiting can choose whether to save the prep room's whiteboard content to the cloud drive.

The prompt for a lead teacher preparing on computer to enter the formal classroom looks like this:

Once a lead teacher using a computer goes from the prep room into the formal classroom, the prompt to load the prep room's content looks like this:

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-10_prep-room-local-classroom.md -->

# 11. Contacts

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Friend Management"
source_title_zh: "好友管理"
```

## Friend Management

## I. How to Add a Friend

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
Students can add each other as friends to communicate privately, share learning experiences, form study partnerships, motivate each other, and support each other's success. Students can also start a temporary classroom with a friend to work through learning questions and challenges together.

Students and teachers can also add each other as friends. Teachers can add a student as a friend to send them a notice or content privately; students can also ask a teacher for help with a personal learning problem and get professional guidance and advice, further improving their learning outcomes and efficiency. This kind of communication and interaction helps build a closer connection between students and teachers, fostering a good teacher-student relationship.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Click the "+" icon at the top.
2. Select Add Friend.
3. Enter a phone number or email to search for a friend, or share your own QR code or In passcode with a friend.

#### Phone
1. Go to Home.
2. Click the "+" icon in the top-right corner.
3. Add a friend via search, phone contacts, QR code scan, In passcode, WeChat invite, and so on.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->

# 12. To-Dos

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "To-Dos"
source_title_zh: "待办"
```

## To-Dos

## I. What Is "To-Dos"?

The "To-Dos" feature is designed to help users efficiently manage and track unfinished learning and teaching activities. By bringing together every class activity a user is part of into one place, the To-Dos module makes it easier to check progress and complete tasks. It also reminds users about tasks that are about to come due, making sure important tasks don't get missed. Whether you're a student or a teacher, To-Dos can significantly improve how efficiently you manage tasks.

## II. Getting to a Task from To-Dos

### Applies to
Teachers and students with an activity, announcement, or schedule item.

### Usage Notes
When a teacher publishes a learning activity in a class — such as a class session, assignment, quiz, notice, discussion, answer sheet, check-in, recorded course, or learning materials — students can find these pending tasks in their own To-Dos. Tapping the name of a to-do takes the student to the corresponding page to complete the task. Once a student completes a task, the teacher who created the activity can check the student's progress in To-Dos and grade it.

Users can also view and confirm their personal schedule and class announcements in To-Dos.

Once inside "To-Dos," users can view three sections: "Pending," "Upcoming," and "Processed."

**Pending:** shows every unfinished task, grouped by past due, due within a day, due within a week, due after a week, and no due date. Users can filter by role, class, or to-do type to quickly find a task, then tap its name to go to that item and view/complete it.

**Upcoming:** shows to-dos that aren't flagged red — tasks the teacher or student doesn't need to handle yet, or that haven't started — grouped the same way (past due, due within a day, due within a week, due after a week, no due date), making it easy for users to see what's coming up and plan their time. Users can filter by role, class, or to-do type to quickly find a task, then tap its name to go to that item and view/complete it.

**Processed:** tasks that are completed, or manually marked/cleared from their current category, are automatically moved here.

### Notes
A class session only appears under "Pending" once its scheduled class time arrives — before that, it shows under "Upcoming."

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to To-Dos in the left navigation.
2. Select Pending / Upcoming / Processed.
3. Search (by activity name) or filter your to-dos.
4. Click the button on the right to go to the corresponding to-do task page.

#### Phone
1. Go to To-Dos.
2. Tap to go to the corresponding to-do task page.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Marking or Clearing the Current Category"
source_title_zh: "标记或清空当前分类"
```

## III. Marking or Clearing the Current Category

Users can manually mark or clear to-do tasks under "Pending" and "Upcoming" that they no longer need to complete, to better manage their task list. Tasks manually marked/cleared from the current category are automatically moved to "Processed."

Class sessions do not support marking.

1. Select Pending / Upcoming.
2. Mark, or Clear Current Category.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Unmarking a Processed Item"
source_title_zh: "已处理取消标记"
```

## IV. Unmarking a Processed Item

If you accidentally mark a task as processed by mistake, you can find that task under "Processed" and unmark it. Once unmarked, the task can be found again under "Pending" or "Upcoming," or you can jump directly to the task page from "Processed" to keep working on it.

Class sessions do not support unmarking.

1. Go to Processed.
2. Click the checkmark to the left of the title to unmark it, or click on the right to go to the corresponding to-do task page.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-12_to-dos.md -->

# 13. Schedule

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Personal Calendar Event"
source_title_zh: "日程"
```

## Personal Calendar Event

## I. Creating a New Calendar Event

## Applies to
Everyone.

## When to use this
Students can use this to plan personal study tasks, mark important academic milestones, and record activities outside of class; teachers can use it to schedule personalized teaching work, note lesson-prep and research items, and record one-on-one tutoring tasks. Creating a personal calendar event in Schedule helps both teachers and students efficiently manage their own time without conflicting with the established teaching schedule.

## Usage Notes
Users on computer or tablet can create a new calendar event in Schedule. An event supports entering a subject, setting the time, whether it's all-day, whether it repeats (no repeat, repeats daily, or repeats weekly), whether to add it to To-Dos, and adding a description. Once created, the event shows up on your personal calendar within Schedule.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Schedule in the left navigation.
2. Click "+" in the top-right corner.
3. Create the new event.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Editing a Calendar Event"
source_title_zh: "编辑日程"
```

## II. Editing a Calendar Event

Users on computer or tablet can edit an event whose end time hasn't passed yet.

Every field in the event's details supports editing.

For a repeating event, you can choose the scope of your edit: "This Event" or "This Event and Following Events."

## Notes
Phone only supports viewing an event.

1. Find and click the event.
2. Click Edit.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Deleting a Calendar Event"
source_title_zh: "删除日程"
```

## III. Deleting a Calendar Event

Users on computer or tablet can delete an event; a deleted event cannot be recovered — proceed with caution.

For a repeating event, you can choose the scope of deletion: "This Event," "This Event and Following Events," or "All Events."

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Schedule"
source_title_zh: "课程表"
```

## Schedule

## I. What Is "Schedule"?

Schedule is a detailed calendar table recording the courses a given school, grade, or class needs. It lists the weekly course arrangement, class times, teaching teachers, and class locations, making it easy for students and teachers to understand and plan learning content and progress. Schedule is an important teaching tool, and also part of a school's overall teaching management.

## II. Viewing a Class Session/Activity/Calendar Event

### Applies to
Everyone.

### Usage Notes
In Schedule, users can find and enter class sessions, activities, and calendar events based on their role and the date, or click a date to view class sessions, activities, and personal calendar events they have permission to take part in on that date. Schedule also supports a calendar view — in calendar view, activities are shown below the date, and class sessions and calendar events are shown within the time grid.

A class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students can enter the classroom for class from Schedule; the lead teacher and co-teacher(s) can also enter the class session's prep room from here. After the class session ends, the lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students can view the session's playback video, whiteboard courseware, teaching report, or learning report.

Only published activities with a due date can show up in Schedule. If there's an activity that needs to be completed, the corresponding teacher and students can also view and enter that activity's details page.

If there's a calendar event, it can also be viewed or entered from here.

### Steps

#### Computer/Tablet
1. Go to Schedule in the left navigation.
2. Select the date.
3. View or enter the class session, activity, or calendar event.

#### Phone
1. Go to Schedule in the bottom navigation.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Watching the 'Class Playback Video' in Schedule"
source_title_zh: "课程表中观看「录课回放视频」"
```

## III. Watching the "Class Playback Video" in Schedule

The class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students.

When creating the class session, if you checked cloud recording (Record ClassIn Classroom / Record On-Site), and the lead teacher's recording during the class session went normally, then about half an hour after class it will automatically be turned into a "playback video." The class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students can all watch the "playback video" in "Schedule." Class teachers and the class session's students can also view this class session's "playback video" in the class.

1. View the playback video.
2. Select the date.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Viewing 'Whiteboard Courseware' in Schedule"
source_title_zh: "课程表中查看「板书课件」"
```

## IV. Viewing "Whiteboard Courseware" in Schedule

If whiteboard courseware retention is enabled at www.eeo.cn, and the conditions for generating "whiteboard courseware" are met in the formal classroom, then after class ends, the class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students can view this session's "whiteboard courseware" in Schedule. Class teachers and the class session's students can also view this class session's "whiteboard courseware" in the class.

1. View the whiteboard courseware.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Viewing the 'Teaching Report' in Schedule"
source_title_zh: "课程表中查看「教学报告」"
```

## V. Viewing the "Teaching Report" in Schedule

The class session's lead teacher and co-teacher(s).

## Usage Notes
Provided the formal classroom's lead teacher or co-teacher(s) attended normally, a "teaching report" for that session's teacher is generated half an hour after class ends. The session's lead teacher and co-teacher(s) can view it in Schedule, and can also view it in the class; the head teacher, however, can only view the "teaching report" in the class. Once you're in the teaching report, you can also view students' learning reports.

1. View the teaching report.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Viewing the 'Learning Report' in Schedule"
source_title_zh: "课程表中查看「学习报告」"
```

## VI. Viewing the "Learning Report" in Schedule

Class session students.

Half an hour after the formal classroom ends, a "learning report" is generated for that session's students; the session's students can view it in Schedule, and can also view the "learning report" in the class. If the class session enabled the feature allowing students to view each other's learning reports, students can view classmates' "learning reports" in the class session's info after class.

1. View the learning report.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-13_schedule.md -->

# 14. Personal Information & Account Security

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Personal Information"
source_title_zh: "个人信息"
```

## Personal Information

## I. Personal Information

### Usage Notes
ClassIn is an online education platform that not only gives students and teachers a convenient learning and teaching environment, but also lets users customize their personal information based on their preferences and needs. In ClassIn's personal information settings, users can add or edit their ClassIn avatar, nickname, gender, birthday, region, signature, and other details.

### Notes
A non-genuine phone number cannot be edited.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Personal Settings.
3. Set your avatar, nickname, gender, birthday, age, region, and signature.

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Tap your nickname.
3. Set your personal information.

#### Phone
1. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
2. Tap your nickname.

## II. Privacy Settings

In account privacy settings, you can configure: whether your personal information is public, and whether others can find you by phone number. Adjusting these privacy permissions helps effectively prevent your personal information from being exposed.

1. At the bottom, set how your personal information is shared, and how others can add you.

Click App Settings.
Click Privacy Settings.
Set how your personal information is shared, and how others can add you.

Click Home.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Account and Security"
source_title_zh: "账号与安全"
```

## Account and Security

## I. Viewing Your Account

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
If you can't see the classroom or activity you should be attending in ClassIn, check whether you're logged into the correct account. Being logged into the wrong account will make classrooms or activities you're supposed to attend invisible.

### Usage Notes
If you have multiple accounts, you can go to Account and Security to check which account is currently logged in, making it easier to manage and use them.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Account and Security.
3. View the currently logged-in account.

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Account and Security.

#### Phone
1. Go to Home.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Binding or Changing Your Phone Number"
source_title_zh: "绑定或修改手机号"
```

## II. Binding or Changing Your Phone Number

If a user registers for ClassIn using email, they'll need to bind a phone number after registration, so they can log in with it going forward.

If a user's phone number is no longer in use, they can change their current phone number to a new one in ClassIn — this way, all of their existing class data is preserved and won't be lost when they switch numbers. The new phone number must not already be registered with ClassIn, and you'll need to verify your current ClassIn login password to make the change. After the change, all class data under the old phone number will be transferred to the new number — including class records already completed, class playbacks, and so on — and you can then log in with the new phone number to continue using ClassIn.

### Notes
If a user's ClassIn account was registered with a phone number, or already has a phone number bound, they cannot bind again — to switch to a different number, use "change phone number" instead.

If a user is a primary account in the "Backend Management System," they cannot make this change themselves — please contact ClassIn support for help, at 400-077-1585.

A ClassIn account cannot be changed to a non-genuine phone number.

1. Bind or change your phone number.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Binding or Changing Your Email"
source_title_zh: "绑定或修改邮箱"
```

## III. Binding or Changing Your Email

If a user registered for ClassIn with a phone number, they can bind an email address, making it easier to log in going forward.

If a user's email is no longer in use, they can change their current email address in ClassIn. The new email must not already be registered with ClassIn, and you'll need to verify your current ClassIn login password to make the change. After the change, all class data under the old email will be transferred to the new email — including class records already completed, class playbacks, and so on — and you can then log in with the new email to continue using ClassIn.

1. Bind or change your email.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Changing Your Password"
source_title_zh: "修改密码"
```

## IV. Changing Your Password

If you register and log in with a verification code, we recommend setting a ClassIn login password, so you can still log in later if it's ever inconvenient to receive a verification code.

You can also change your current ClassIn password.

1. Tap Password to set or change it.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Deactivating Your Account"
source_title_zh: "注销账号"
```

## V. Deactivating Your Account

If a user no longer wants to use ClassIn, they can log into ClassIn on a phone or tablet and deactivate their account. Once an account is successfully deactivated, every course and other content under it will be deleted together and cannot be recovered; the deactivated account will become unregistered. Please proceed carefully.

If a user's account is the primary account in the "Backend Management System," it cannot be deactivated.

If your account isn't tied to a genuine phone number, it cannot be deactivated.

If a user's account has unfinished class sessions or temporary classrooms under it, the account cannot be deactivated.

If a user's account is currently suspended, it cannot be deactivated.

1. Click Deactivate Account.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Device Management"
source_title_zh: "设备管理"
```

## VI. Device Management

If a user is logged into the same account on multiple devices, you can force-logout certain devices — from any device you're logged into, you can log another device out remotely. A device that's been force-logged-out will have its account and password information related to that account cleared.

1. Find the device you want to log out, then click its name to log it out.

Find the device you want to log out, then click Log Out.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classin-14_personal-info-account-security.md -->

# 15. App Settings

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Switching Accounts"
source_title_zh: "切换账号"
```

## Switching Accounts

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
Once logged into ClassIn, if you want to switch to a different account, you can do this: go to Settings in the bottom-left corner of the software, select "Switch Account," and this logs you out of the currently logged-in account. On phone or tablet, you can only log out first, then log back in with a different account.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Click Switch Account.
3. Click Confirm.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Exiting the App"
source_title_zh: "退出软件"
```

## Exiting the App

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
Once you're done with an activity or class, you can proactively exit ClassIn to shut down the software's related background processes. On computer, click your avatar in the bottom-left corner, then click Exit App; on phone or tablet, click your avatar on the home page, then click Log Out.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Click Exit App.
3. Click Confirm.

#### Phone
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Tap Log Out.

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "System Permission Management"
source_title_zh: "系统权限管理"
```

## System Permission Management

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
ClassIn's privacy settings include a system permission management feature. Users can use this feature to view and manage, all in one place, the various device permissions the app has been granted (such as camera, microphone, and photo album access). Once you tap into this feature, the page jumps directly to your phone or tablet's system settings screen, where you can quickly turn each permission on or off.

### Notes
Users on phone or tablet can view and access system permission management within ClassIn; on computer, you'll need to go to your computer's system settings to check which permissions ClassIn has been granted.

### Steps

#### Phone
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Tap App Settings.
4. Go to Privacy Settings.
5. Go to System Permission Management.
6. View or go to the permission management page.
7. Turn a permission on or off.

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Upgrading ClassIn"
source_title_zh: "升级ClassIn"
```

## Upgrading ClassIn

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
The new version of ClassIn not only improves the user experience but also adds brand-new features. To make your teaching or learning go more smoothly, we recommend upgrading ClassIn to the latest version.

### Notes
If you run into an error while upgrading ClassIn that prevents the upgrade from completing normally, you can uninstall your currently installed copy of ClassIn, then re-download and install the ClassIn client from the official website, www.eeo.cn.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to About.
3. Upgrade, or Check for Updates.

#### Phone
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Go to About.
4. If a new version is available, tap Upgrade to update the app to the latest version.

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Tablet/Phone Mode"
source_title_zh: "平板/手机模式"
```

## Tablet/Phone Mode

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
A tablet meeting the screen-size requirements will show the IM interface (outside the classroom) in tablet mode by default. If you run into laggy, unresponsive controls or slow page loading while using the software in tablet mode, we recommend switching to phone mode, either in App Settings after logging in or on the login page. Switching from phone mode back to tablet mode is also supported.

## I. Switching to Phone Mode from App Settings

### Steps

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to App Settings.
3. Enable Phone Mode.
4. Click Restart Now.

## II. Switching to Tablet Mode from App Settings

1. Go to Home.
2. Click your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Turn off Phone Mode.

## III. Switching to Phone Mode at Login

1. Click "Use Phone Mode" below the login page.

## IV. Switching to Tablet Mode at Login

1. Click "Use Tablet Mode" below the login page.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Recording Codec"
source_title_zh: "录课编码"
```

## Recording Codec

### Applies to
The teacher recording the class.

### Usage Notes
On Windows computers, the recording codec comes in two types: hardware encoding and legacy mode. By default, recording uses hardware encoding; we don't recommend individually changing this setting without good reason — if you have a specific need, we suggest consulting ClassIn support first.

Also, for the same recording scenario, hardware encoding produces a larger recorded file than legacy mode.

Changing the recording codec only takes effect the next time you enter the classroom and start recording.

### Notes
Phone and tablet do not have a "Recording Codec" setting.

Mac computers do not have a "Recording Codec" feature.

### Steps

#### Computer (Windows)
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change the Recording Codec.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Recording Mode (Software/System Sound)"
source_title_zh: "录课模式（软件/系统声音）"
```

## Recording Mode (Software/System Sound)

### Applies to
The teacher recording the class.

### Usage Notes
Teachers recording on computer can choose which sound range to capture based on their teaching-recording needs — either system sound or software sound, with software sound being the default. If the resulting class playback video's sound is too quiet or you can't hear it at all, try recording with software sound next time.

**Software sound:** only records sound within the classroom; sound from other software on your computer desktop won't be recorded. The teacher also needs to make sure the speaker selected in the classroom is working properly.

**System sound:** records all sound both within the classroom and from other software on your computer desktop — for example, QQ message alert sounds, WeChat message alert sounds, or video sound playing on a webpage. The teacher also needs to make sure the speaker selected in the classroom is working properly.

Also, changing the recording mode requires restarting the ClassIn app to take effect.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change the Recording Mode.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Advanced Recording Mode (iOS)"
source_title_zh: "高级录课模式（IOS系统）"
```

## Advanced Recording Mode (iOS)

### Applies to
The teacher recording the class.

### When to use this
When a teacher recording class is using an Apple iPhone or iPad, and needs to use screen sharing while recording the shared content and its sound, we recommend enabling Advanced Recording Mode before entering the classroom to record. In addition, if the classroom shows a "recording error" that interrupts recording and prevents it from continuing, the teacher can also try enabling Advanced Recording Mode and re-entering the classroom to record.

### Notes
Computer does not have an "Advanced Recording Mode" feature.

Phone and tablet (Android, HarmonyOS, or Google's system) do not have an "Advanced Recording Mode" feature.

### Steps

#### iPhone
1. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
2. Go to App Settings.
3. Go to Advanced Settings.
4. Turn Advanced Recording Mode on/off.

#### iPad
1. Tap your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Recorded Video Resolution (HD/Full HD)"
source_title_zh: "录制视频分辨率（高清/全高清）"
```

## Recorded Video Resolution (HD/Full HD)

### Applies to
The teacher recording the class.

### Usage Notes
Teachers recording on computer can adjust the recorded video's resolution, with two options:

**Full HD mode (1920 x 1080):** suited to scenarios that demand higher playback video quality; we recommend a computer with stronger performance, with a CPU of 6th-generation Intel i5 or higher. Also, if the recording area is set to the minimum-size classroom window, this mode cannot be selected.

**HD mode (1280 x 720):** the default mode, recommended for computers with weaker performance, with a CPU of Intel i5 or higher.

If the teacher's monitor resolution is lower than the selected recording resolution, the recording will use the lower resolution instead.

Changing the recorded video resolution only takes effect the next time you enter the classroom and start recording.

### Notes
For teachers recording on phone or tablet, the recorded video resolution is fixed and cannot be adjusted.

Compared to HD mode, Full HD mode produces a larger recorded video file, taking up more storage space, whether cloud or local.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change the Recorded Video Resolution.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Recording Area (Minimum Size / Current Size / Entire Computer Desktop)"
source_title_zh: "录制画面范围（最小尺寸/当前尺寸/整个电脑桌面）"
```

## Recording Area (Minimum Size / Current Size / Entire Computer Desktop)

### Applies to
The teacher recording the class.

### Usage Notes
Teachers recording on computer can flexibly choose the recording area based on their computer's specs and recording needs. The recording area options are:

**Minimum-Size Classroom Window:** once enabled, the classroom window automatically shrinks to 1280 x 720px, and records what's inside the teacher's current classroom window; classroom window resizing is not supported — suited to lower-performance computers. During screen sharing, the shared area is recorded.

**Current-Size Classroom Window:** once enabled, records what's inside the teacher's current classroom window, and allows freely resizing the classroom window; a larger window demands more from your computer's CPU. During screen sharing, the shared area is recorded.

**Entire Computer Desktop:** once enabled, records everything the teacher does on the computer desktop where their classroom window is located; a larger monitor screen demands more from your computer's CPU.

If your device has weaker performance, we recommend "Minimum-Size Classroom Window" mode; if you need to teach full-screen or resize the window, choose "Current-Size Classroom Window" mode; if you need to record both the classroom view and desktop activity at the same time (for example, demonstrating by switching between multiple apps), you can enable "Entire Desktop Recording" mode.

Also, changing the recording area only takes effect the next time you enter the classroom and start recording.

### Notes
For teachers recording on phone or tablet, the recording area is fixed and cannot be adjusted.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change the Recording Area.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Speaker"
source_title_zh: "扬声器"
```

## Speaker

## I. Speaker Mode

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
If you run into the following issues while using ClassIn, try enabling "Legacy Mode 1" or "Legacy Mode 2" under "Speaker Mode" in ClassIn's settings. For phone/tablet users, try enabling "Speaker Mode" in settings:

If a Windows computer user hasn't muted their speaker in the classroom but still can't hear any sound in the classroom, and the issue persists after using "Fix Hardware Driver," try enabling "Legacy Mode 1" or "Legacy Mode 2" under "Speaker Mode" in the app settings.

If an Android phone or tablet user hasn't disabled their speaker in the classroom, and the speaker volume is normal, but they still can't hear any sound in the classroom, try enabling "Speaker Mode" in settings.

### Notes
After a Windows computer user changes "Speaker Mode," ClassIn must be restarted for the change to take effect.

### Steps

#### Computer (Windows)
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change the Speaker Mode.

#### Phone/Tablet (Android)
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Go to App Settings.
4. Go to Advanced Settings.
5. Turn Speaker Mode on or off.

## II. Fixing the Speaker

If a Windows computer user's speaker test plays sound normally locally via the small speaker icon in the bottom-right corner, but there's no sound from the speaker in the ClassIn classroom, they can use the "Fix Hardware Driver" feature to fix the speaker; we recommend restarting the computer once the fix is complete.

Phone and tablet don't have "hardware driver fix" — if you run into this kind of issue on phone or tablet, try restarting the device instead.

Mac computers don't have a "Fix Hardware Driver" feature — if this happens on a Mac, try restarting the computer instead.

1. Go to System Settings.
2. Scroll the right-side scrollbar all the way down.
3. Under Hardware Driver Fix, click Fix.
4. (If a firewall prompt blocks it, click Allow or Yes.) Click Fix Speaker; once it reports the fix is complete, we recommend restarting your computer.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Camera"
source_title_zh: "摄像头"
```

## Camera

## I. Camera Mode

### Applies to
Everyone.

### When to use this
If your computer's local camera app shows your camera feed fine, but you run into the following issues while using ClassIn:

Clicking "Start Class" to enter the classroom causes ClassIn to freeze and become unresponsive, unable to enter the classroom normally, with the mouse cursor spinning continuously.

After turning on the camera in the classroom, the camera toggle keeps jumping back to "disabled."

After turning on the camera in the classroom, you see the message: "Camera is being used by another app." You've confirmed no other app is using the camera, confirmed you've exited any security/antivirus software on your computer, and used "Fix Hardware Driver" to fix the camera — but your own video still won't display properly.

For any of the issues above, we recommend trying to check "Legacy Mode" under "Camera Mode" in ClassIn's app settings. After changing "Camera Mode," ClassIn must be restarted for the setting to take effect.

### Notes
Phone and tablet do not have a "Camera Mode" setting.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to Classroom Settings.
3. Change the Camera Mode.

## II. Fixing the Camera

If a Windows computer user's local camera app shows the camera feed fine, but they run into the following camera issues in the ClassIn classroom, this feature can also help fix the camera:

The camera video appears green, gray, or black.

The camera video is glitchy/garbled.

The camera reports being occupied by another app.

The camera automatically switches to disabled once turned on.

We recommend restarting your computer once the camera fix is complete.

Phone and tablet don't have "hardware driver fix" — if you run into this kind of issue on phone or tablet, try restarting the device instead.

Mac computers don't have a "Fix Hardware Driver" feature. If this happens on a Mac, first check whether "Camera" access is authorized for ClassIn in your Mac's local settings, and grant authorization if not. If it's already authorized and the issue persists, try restarting your computer.

#### Computer (Windows)
1. Go to System Settings.
2. Scroll the right-side scrollbar all the way down.
3. Under Hardware Driver Fix, click Fix.
4. (If a firewall prompt blocks it, click Allow or Yes.) Click Fix Camera; once it reports the fix is complete, we recommend restarting your computer.

## III. Video Software Decoder

When a user takes class on an Android phone or tablet (Android, HarmonyOS, or Google's system), if their own camera feed looks fine to themselves, but other classroom members can't see them properly — for example, seeing a glitchy/garbled image — the user can try enabling "Video Software Decoder" and disabling "Video Hardware Decoder" in app settings to fix the issue.

Computer does not have a "Video Software Decoder" feature.

iPhone/iPad devices do not have a "Video Software Decoder" feature.

#### Phone/Tablet (Android)
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Go to App Settings.
4. Go to Advanced Settings.
5. Turn Video Software Decoder on or off.

## IV. Video Hardware Decoder

Computer does not have a "Video Hardware Decoder" feature.

iPhone/iPad devices do not have a "Video Hardware Decoder" feature.

1. Turn Video Hardware Decoder on or off.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassIn App Notifications"
source_title_zh: "ClassIn_APP通知"
```

## ClassIn App Notifications

## I. Class Notifications

### Applies to
The class session's lead teacher, co-teacher(s), and students.

### When to use this
If you want to receive class reminder notifications in the ClassIn app, you can enable the "Class Notifications" feature in ClassIn's settings.

### Usage Notes
Once "Class Notifications" is enabled in the ClassIn app, it will push a class reminder to the teacher 80 minutes and 20 minutes before class officially starts; students receive a class reminder 70 minutes and 10 minutes before class officially starts.

In addition, on computer, ClassIn needs to be logged in; on phone or tablet, ClassIn needs to be logged in and running in the background, and the device's own system settings need to allow ClassIn to send "notifications." On computer, the notification appears as a pop-up in the bottom-right corner; on phone or tablet, the pop-up style is determined by the device's own notification settings.

### Steps

#### Computer
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.
2. Go to System Settings.
3. Turn Class Notifications on or off.

#### Phone
1. Go to Home in the bottom navigation.
2. Tap your avatar in the top-left corner.
3. Go to App Settings.
4. Go to New Message Notifications.

#### Tablet
1. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner.

## II. Learning Activity Notifications

Teachers and students with an activity.

If you want to receive notification reminders in the ClassIn app for LMS learning activities (class sessions, recorded courses, assignments, quizzes, check-ins, discussions, answer sheets, learning materials, and so on), you can enable the "Learning Activity Notifications" feature in ClassIn's settings.

Once "Learning Activity Notifications" is enabled in the ClassIn app, students will receive a push notification 1/3/7 days before an activity's due date, once a teacher grades or sends back the activity for revision, or when a teacher reminds students to submit the activity; teachers will receive a push notification once a student submits or revises an activity.

1. Turn Learning Activity Notifications on or off.

## III. New Message Notifications

Everyone.

Users on phone or tablet can turn New Message Notifications on or off within the ClassIn app.

In addition, you'll need to make sure ClassIn is logged in and running in the background, and that the device's own system settings allow ClassIn to send "notifications." The pop-up style shown on phone or tablet is determined by the device's own notification settings.

1. Turn New Message Notifications on or off.

## IV. New Message Alert Sound

Users on computer can turn the new-message alert sound on or off within the ClassIn app. If you're on phone or tablet, ClassIn does not let you configure the message alert sound — you'll need to configure it in the device's own system settings.

1. Turn the New Message Alert Sound on or off.

```yaml
title: "Recording Countdown"
```

## Recording Countdown

## Applies to
The "Backend Management System" primary account.

Sub-accounts with "School Settings" permission.

## When to use this
Academic teachers can change the recording countdown time in the "Backend Management System" based on the teaching teacher's habits. The default recording countdown is 10 minutes — meaning cloud recording automatically starts 10 minutes after the teacher enters the classroom each time. If the teacher wants cloud recording to start the moment they enter the classroom, academic staff can change the countdown to 0 minutes. If the teacher wants more time to prepare and doesn't want recording to start so quickly, academic staff can change the countdown to 20 minutes.

## Usage Notes
The recording countdown time in the "Backend Management System" can be set to: 0 minutes, 1 minute, 3 minutes, 5 minutes, 10 minutes, or 20 minutes.

## Notes
After enabling a new custom classroom configuration, the teacher needs to exit the classroom and re-enter for the new configuration to take effect.

## Related Articles
"Adding Custom Classroom Settings"

"Editing Custom Classroom Settings"

"Adding a Sub-Account in the Backend Management System"

### Steps
1. Log into the Backend Management System.
2. Go to School Settings in the left navigation.
3. Go to Classroom Settings above.
4. Create or edit custom classroom settings.
5. Go to Parameter Settings.
6. Under Recording Countdown Settings, change the recording countdown time, then click Confirm.
7. Enable the newly configured custom classroom setting.

```yaml
title: "ClassInX Download/Login/Logout/Full Shutdown"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 下载/登录/退出/彻底关闭"
```

## ClassInX Download/Login/Logout/Full Shutdown

# I. Downloading ClassInX Software

## Usage Notes
ClassInX software is an all-in-one education tool for online, offline, and blended teaching, covering three core scenarios, suited to K-12, higher education, tutoring institutions, and other user types — designed for teacher use.

ClassInX software can be downloaded from the official website, www.eeo.cn, and supports Windows 7 and higher — it's not compatible with other operating systems.

## Steps
1. Visit www.eeo.cn in your browser.
2. Click to go to the Download Center.
3. Scroll down using the scrollbar on the right side of the page, and click "Download for Windows" under ClassInX (Large Display Edition).
4. Once downloaded, double-click to open the ClassInX installer.
5. When User Account Control asks whether to allow this app to make changes to your device, click Yes.
6. Select the installation language, then click Confirm.
7. Check the agreement, then click Quick Install or Custom Install.
8. Once installation finishes, the system will automatically open the ClassInX software.

# II. Logging Into a ClassInX Account

Entering a classroom, using cloud drive files, and creating a class within ClassInX all require you to be logged into a ClassIn account.

Once ClassInX is running, users can click or swipe up from the very bottom of the screen to open the dock, then click the avatar on the left to log in.

Login methods include: scanning a QR code with your phone or tablet after logging into ClassIn to log into ClassInX; or entering your ClassIn account (phone number/email) and password to log in.

1. Go to the dock at the very bottom of the classroom.
2. Click the avatar on the left.
3. Scan the QR code, or enter your ClassIn account and password, to log in.

# III. Logging Out of a ClassInX Account

Users can click or swipe up from the very bottom of the screen to open the dock, then click the avatar on the left to log out of their ClassIn account.

1. Click Log Out.
2. Click Confirm Logout.

# IV. Switching ClassInX Accounts

Users can click or swipe up from the very bottom of the screen to open the dock, then click the avatar on the left to switch ClassIn accounts.

1. Click Switch Account.

# V. Fully Closing ClassInX Software

Logging out doesn't mean ClassInX software is closed. To fully close ClassInX software, click "Go to Desktop" in the dock below, then press and hold the ClassInX window in the desktop's taskbar to close the software.

1. Click Go to Desktop.
2. Press and hold the ClassInX window in the taskbar at the bottom of the desktop, then click Close Window.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classinx-01_batch1.md -->

# ClassInX (Batch 2)

```yaml
title: "ClassInX Other Common Settings"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 其他常用设置"
```

## ClassInX Other Common Settings

# I. Touch Response Size

## Applies to
Everyone.

## Usage Notes
When a user is using ClassInX on the large display without the Eraser tool selected, single-finger operation or two-finger swiping may sometimes be mistakenly recognized as an eraser gesture.

If this happens, we recommend going to the dock at the very bottom of the classroom screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → Classroom Settings, find "Touch Response Size," and reduce it slightly (relative to the actual size of the large display).

## Steps
1. Tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock.
2. Click ClassIn.
3. Click the avatar in the bottom-left corner.
4. Click Classroom Settings.
5. Go to Touch Response Size and adjust it.

# II. Auto-Run on Startup

If you want ClassInX to open automatically every time you power on the large display, we recommend going to the dock at the very bottom of the classroom screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → System Settings, find "Auto-Run on Startup," and turn it on (or off, if you'd prefer the opposite).

1. Click System Settings.
2. Turn Auto-Run on Startup on or off.

# III. Touchscreen Auto-Trigger On-Screen Keyboard

When a user opens the whiteboard or classroom using ClassInX on the large display, if they'd like to be able to type using the system's built-in on-screen keyboard, we recommend going to the dock at the very bottom of the screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → System Settings, find "Touchscreen Auto-Trigger On-Screen Keyboard," and turn it on.

1. Click System Settings.
2. Turn "Touchscreen Auto-Trigger On-Screen Keyboard" on or off.

# IV. ClassInX Software Log Reporting

If a user runs into an issue using ClassInX software that they can't resolve on their own, they can provide ClassIn support with a description of the issue, the account involved, when it happened, and similar details, then go to the dock at the very bottom of the screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → System Settings, and click "Report" under "Software Log Reporting," so support staff can quickly and efficiently locate the issue.

1. Under Software Log Reporting, click Report.

# V. Reporting Voice Assistant Recordings

When a user on a ClassInX 2.0 large display runs into issues like abnormal speech recognition while using the DaKe voice assistant, they can provide ClassIn support with a description of the issue, the account involved, when it happened, and similar details, then go to the dock at the very bottom of the screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → System Settings, and click "Report" under "Report Voice Assistant Recording," so support staff can quickly and efficiently locate the issue.

1. Under Report Voice Assistant Recording, click Report.

# VI. Clearing ClassInX Cache Files

If a user opens a certain feature page in ClassInX and it takes too long to load, failing to display content properly, they can go to the dock at the very bottom of the screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → File Transfer, click "Clear" under "Cache Files," and once cleared, click "Restart Now."

1. Click File Transfer.
2. Under Cache Files, click Clear.
3. Click Restart Now.

# VII. Clearing ClassInX Data Files

If a user in ClassInX has confirmed their schedule is set up correctly and they're logged into the right account, but still can't see the classroom entry point, they can go to the dock at the very bottom of the screen → ClassIn → click the avatar in the bottom-left corner → File Transfer, click "Clear" under "Data Files," and once cleared, click "Restart Now."

1. Under Data Files, click Clear.
2. Click Restart Software Now.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Extended Display Usage Guide"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 扩展屏使用指南"
```

## ClassInX Extended Display Usage Guide

### I. Extended Secondary Display

When two large displays are connected, open ClassIn X software on the ClassIn X 2.0 large display, tap or swipe up to view more tools, click screen projection settings for the extended display, then select "Extend" to use the secondary display as an extended display.

### II. Extended Whiteboard (Dual-Display Sync)

If you need the extended display to show whiteboard content, you can select "Extended Whiteboard" within ClassInX's extended display settings.

**(1)** Open ClassIn X, tap or swipe up to view more tools, click Extended Display, then select or add "Extended Whiteboard."

**(2)** The extended whiteboard has "Dual-Display Sync" enabled by default. In the bottom-right corner of the extended display settings panel, you can set the whiteboard content shown on the extended display to be the "previous page," "next page," or "same page" relative to the main display. Once set, turning the page on one display will also turn the page on the other. Both displays can be written on, and content written on one syncs to the other.

**(3)** The top-right corner of the extended display settings panel also lets you set the extended display's background.

**(4)** In the classroom, once "Extended Whiteboard" is selected and set up by the teaching teacher, students in the classroom can use the extended-display control button in the bottom-right corner of the classroom to switch between viewing the main display and the extended display.

### III. Extended Whiteboard (Dual-Display Not Synced)

Once you turn off "Dual-Display Sync" in the bottom-left corner of the extended display settings panel, both whiteboards will show the same content but can be turned to different pages independently.

### IV. Extended File

If you need the extended display to show a file from Cloud Drive (Space), you can select "File" within ClassInX's extended display settings.

**(1)** Open ClassIn X, tap or swipe up to view more tools, click Extended Display, then select or add "File" — this jumps to the Cloud Drive Space page. Once you select a file (only PDF, PPT, DOC, and EXCEL formats are supported), the selected file will display on the extended display. You can write and annotate on files shown on the extended display.

**(2)** Video cannot be played on the extended display — if a PPT contains video, that video is automatically moved to the main display to play.

**(3)** The extended display supports showing up to 2 files at once. Users can click "Add" in the extended display settings window to select another file, and switch between files to adjust what's shown on the extended display.

**(4)** In the classroom, once "Extended File" is selected, the teaching teacher can set "Allow Students to Browse Freely" permission for the file in the extended display window panel. Once enabled, students in the classroom can view the extended display file in the bottom-right corner of the classroom, and can also freely turn pages in the file themselves.

### V. Showing the Video Wall on the Extended Display

Besides showing the whiteboard or file content, the extended display can also show the video wall. Users can go into the toolbox from the dock at the bottom-center of the screen, open the Video Wall tool, and the video wall feed will automatically display on the extended display.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Classroom Operation Gestures"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 教室操作手势"
```

## ClassInX Classroom Operation Gestures

# I. Shape-Drawing Shortcut

ClassInX offers a shortcut for sketching shapes, such as straight lines, circles, ellipses, rectangles, squares, diamonds, and more. Teachers just need to select the Pen tool, draw a rough shape on the whiteboard, and hold their finger on the whiteboard for 1 second — this produces a corrected, standardized version of the shape, as shown in the image.

# II. Single-Finger Operations

## Moving Courseware

Users can use any finger on either hand, placed on the edge of the courseware, to move it — for example, PPT, PDF, Word, audio, or video courseware.

## Moving Whiteboard Text, Lines, and Shapes

Users first need to select the "Select and Move" tool from the radial toolbar, then place one finger on the text/image/shape/line they want to move and drag it to the desired location.

## Playing PPT Animations or Video

Users first need to select the "Select and Move" tool from the radial toolbar, then use one finger to tap the PPT page — this triggers any animation effect on the current page, or plays any video on the current page.

## Turning PPT Courseware Pages Forward/Backward

Users first need to select the "Select and Move" tool from the radial toolbar, then use one finger to tap the PPT page and swipe forward or backward to turn the page forward or backward.

# III. Two-Finger Operations

## Swiping the Whiteboard Up/Down

Swiping two fingers on the large display can turn pages on the large whiteboard.

## Turning a Full Page of Whiteboard Content

Swiping two fingers left or right can turn a full page of whiteboard content.

## Zooming In/Out

Placing two fingers on an image, courseware, or video and swiping them together or apart zooms in or out.

## Two-Finger Selection

Placing two fingers together on an element on the whiteboard selects that element, letting you move, delete, duplicate, and otherwise operate on it. Elements that can be selected with two fingers include images, text, shapes, and lines.

# IV. Four-Finger Operations

## Summoning the Tool Dial

In the classroom whiteboard, as long as the teacher touches any location on the large display with four fingers, the tool dial will move to that location, making it convenient for the teacher to select functions from the tool dial anytime.

# V. Back-of-Hand and Palm Operations

## Eraser

The eraser is triggered by placing as much of your hand's surface area as possible against the whiteboard — the palm, back of the hand, and side of the hand are the three areas with the largest surface area, so placing any of these three against the whiteboard triggers the eraser, letting you erase whiteboard content. Note: to make sure the eraser is properly triggered, hold your hand against the whiteboard for about one second, wait for the eraser shape to appear, then move it to erase — your hand must stay in contact with the whiteboard throughout the erasing process.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classinx-02_batch2.md -->
