# ClassInX Classroom Additional Settings

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Classroom Additional Settings"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 教室更多设置"
```

## ClassInX Classroom Additional Settings

# I. Showing/Hiding the On-Stage Seats Area

## Usage Notes
The on-stage seats area is the row at the very top of the whiteboard. It's used only to display teacher and student camera feeds — you cannot write on it.

Besides choosing whether to show the on-stage seats area when creating a class session, once inside the classroom, the teaching teacher or co-teacher can also show or hide the on-stage seats area from the classroom's additional settings.

Also, the teacher's on-stage seat rotation setting only takes effect while the on-stage seats area is shown. When the teacher needs to write full-screen, they can hide the on-stage seats area.

## Steps
1. Tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock.
2. Click Settings on the far right.
3. Click Additional Settings.
4. Click General.
5. Choose to Show or Hide the on-stage seats area.

# II. Focus Mode

## Applies to
Teaching teacher, co-teacher.

To keep students from getting distracted during class, we recommend using Focus Mode. Backend administrators can apply a skin with "Enable Focus Mode" checked to a class, and formal classrooms under that class will have Focus Mode enabled by default. In addition, once the teaching teacher or co-teacher enters the classroom, they can also turn Focus Mode on or off from the classroom's additional settings.

Once Focus Mode is enabled: if a student enters the classroom on a Windows computer, the classroom window will stay maximized and pinned on top, unobstructed by other windows. If a student enters the classroom on a phone or tablet, switching to another app will automatically exit the classroom.

Focus Mode set by the teaching teacher or co-teacher within the classroom only applies to the current classroom.

## Notes
Focus Mode does not take effect for students using a Mac OS device.

Focus Mode does not take effect for auditors.

If a student's device supports split-screen or similar features, Focus Mode may also fail to take effect.

1. Turn Focus Mode on or off.

# III. Raise Hand Sound Alert

## When to use this
When a student raises their hand in the classroom, the teacher's device automatically plays a raise-hand alert sound, so the teacher can still notice a student's raised hand while focused on teaching, writing on the board, or viewing files, and won't miss a chance to interact.

Once inside the classroom, the teaching teacher and co-teacher can each set their own raise-hand alert sound independently, with no effect on each other.

In raise-hand alert settings, teachers can choose no alert sound, or select a "ding," "tick-tock," or "ding-dong" sound as the alert.

The alert sound is only audible to the teacher themself — students in the classroom won't hear it.

1. Select a Raise-Hand Alert Sound.

# IV. Entry/Exit Notifications

Once inside the classroom, if the teacher enables entry/exit notifications in the classroom's additional settings, a pop-up notification will appear at the bottom of the teacher's screen whenever a student joins or leaves the classroom, helping the teacher track attendance status in real time.

The teaching teacher and co-teacher can each set their own entry/exit notifications independently, with no effect on each other.

If the teaching teacher has this feature enabled, they'll also be notified when a co-teacher joins or leaves.

1. Turn entry/exit notifications on or off.

# V. Classroom Background

A classroom background can be set in advance in the Backend Management System; once inside the classroom, teachers can also set it themselves under the classroom's additional settings. Once a teacher changes the classroom background, the new one takes effect immediately.

Teachers can choose from the system's built-in background images, or upload a local image as the classroom background. Uploaded images must be JPG format and no larger than 1MB.

A classroom background changed within the classroom's additional settings only applies to the current classroom.

1. Click Classroom Background.
2. Select or upload a classroom background image.

# VI. Classroom Window Layout

Dragging cameras, courseware, and widgets to preset positions with automatic resizing helps teachers quickly organize the classroom whiteboard interface, efficiently switch teaching scenarios, and stay focused on instruction and interaction.

Once inside the classroom, teachers can go to Classroom Additional Settings → Other → Window Layout to choose an existing layout template. Custom layout templates are also supported — you can add a template using either tiled mode (pane size and position are fixed and cannot be freely adjusted) or free-pane mode (pane size and position can be freely adjusted).

Once you've selected a template, if the teacher is using a large display, they can drag a camera, courseware, or widget with one finger and hold for 0.5 seconds to enter layout mode; if using a computer, they can drag with the mouse while holding Shift on the keyboard to enter layout mode.

1. Click Other.
2. Under Layout Settings, click Window Layout.
3. Select or add a layout template.
4. Drag a camera/courseware/widget with one finger, holding for 0.5 seconds to enter layout mode.
(On computer, hold Shift while dragging.)

# VII. Classroom Help Request

Teaching teacher, co-teacher, class session students (excluding auditors).

When a teacher or student in the classroom runs into an issue they can't resolve on their own, they can request assistance from the backend academic administrator.

Once inside the classroom, teachers can go to Classroom Additional Settings → Other → Help Request to open the help request window. Select the person(s) with the issue, describe the issue, then click Confirm. The backend academic administrator can view the classroom help request information under Academic Management → Classroom Monitoring at www.eeo.cn, including the issue description and a system-captured screenshot from every user's classroom view at that moment. Once the academic teacher replies, a reply window will pop up automatically on the teacher's screen in the classroom.

Once backend administrators apply a skin with "Allow Students to Send Help Requests to the School Backend" enabled to a class, students using a computer or iPad to enter a classroom under that class can then use the help request feature. In the help request window, students describe the issue and click Confirm. The backend academic administrator can view the classroom help request information under Academic Management → Classroom Monitoring at www.eeo.cn, including the issue description and a system-captured screenshot from that student's classroom view. Once the academic teacher replies, a reply window will pop up automatically on that student's screen in the classroom.

Students (except auditors) can only use the help request feature if they enter, via the ClassIn app on computer or iPad, a classroom under a class with "Allow Students to Send Help Requests to the School Backend" enabled.

1. Under Quick Help Request, click Help Request.
2. Teacher: select the person(s) with the issue, describe the issue, then click Confirm.
(Student: describe the issue, then click Confirm.)

# VIII. Upgrading ClassInX Software

Everyone.

To ensure smoother use, we recommend upgrading ClassInX software to the latest version.

Users who aren't logged in can check the current ClassInX software version and upgrade it via the dock at the very bottom of the screen → Settings → Additional Settings → About.

Logged-in users can also check the current ClassInX software version and upgrade it via the dock at the very bottom of the screen → ClassIn → avatar in the bottom-left corner → About.

1. Click About.
2. Check the current ClassInX software version, or click Upgrade.

# IX. Classroom Stylus Settings

When using a stylus to write on the whiteboard in ClassInX, if the stylus is meant to be used only for writing, we recommend enabling "Stylus for Writing Only" via the dock at the very bottom of the screen → Settings → Additional Settings → Hardware.

Once enabled, the stylus is used only for writing, and finger touches will behave according to whichever tool is currently selected on the radial dial (note: tilting the stylus tip may cause it to be misidentified as a finger touch).

1. Click Hardware.
2. Turn "Stylus for Writing Only" on or off.

# X. Classroom Touch Lock Settings

To prevent students in an offline classroom from accidentally touching the large display's screen, teachers can enable "Lock Screen Touch" during breaks via the ClassInX software's dock at the very bottom of the screen → Settings → Additional Settings → Hardware.

When touch lock is on, users can turn it off by tapping the touch lock button at the bottom of the screen, or by pressing and holding the "Previous Page" button on the page-turner remote.

When touch lock is off, users can turn it on the same way — by pressing and holding "Previous Page" on the page-turner remote.

1. Turn "Lock Screen Touch" on or off.

# XI. DaKe Voice Assistant

The DaKe voice assistant helps users complete ClassIn-related operations on a ClassInX 2.0 large display more conveniently through voice commands.

The voice assistant feature is only supported on ClassInX 2.0 large display devices, and requires microphone permission to be enabled in the ClassInX software.

In the ClassInX software's dock at the very bottom of the screen → Settings → Voice Assistant, you can turn the "DaKe Voice Assistant" feature on or off.

Once the DaKe voice assistant is enabled, you can also turn on or off: "Wake-Free Mode" (no need to say "DaKe DaKe" to wake it — you can speak commands directly), "Text Feedback" (voice recognition results display as text on the large display), and "Sound Feedback" (DaKe responds with a "ding" sound). These features can also be turned on or off by tapping the DaKe icon in the bottom-right corner of the classroom or whiteboard.

In addition, in the formal classroom, the teaching teacher, co-teacher, and group leaders can use the DaKe voice assistant feature when eligible; eligible students do not have this feature's permission.

1. Click Voice Assistant.
2. Turn the DaKe Voice Assistant on or off.

# ClassInX Classroom Audio/Video Features

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Classroom Audio/Video Features"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 教室音视频功能"
```

## ClassInX Classroom Audio/Video Features

# I. Quickly Adjusting Camera, Microphone, and Speaker

## Usage Notes
Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock and control their own microphone and camera. Clicking the microphone icon on the right side of the dock quickly turns the microphone on or off; if the on-stage seats area is hidden, clicking the camera icon on the right side of the dock lets you go on or off stage yourself; if the on-stage seats area is shown, clicking the camera icon on the right side of the dock turns your own camera on or off.

To switch to a different audio/video device or adjust audio volume, go to Settings on the far right of the dock. You can also do this under Additional Settings → Audio Settings.

# II. Adjusting the Camera

## 1. Switching Cameras

### Usage Notes
Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Video" to switch camera devices.

## 2. Adding a Network Camera

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Video" to add a network camera. In the Add Network Camera window, just fill in the network camera's name and URL. Editing or deleting already-added network cameras is also supported.

## 3. Adjusting Network Camera Volume

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Video" to adjust the network camera's volume. Users themselves cannot hear that network camera's sound — this setting adjusts the volume other users in the classroom hear.

## 4. Rotating the Camera

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Video" to rotate the camera. Clicking the rotate button once rotates the camera image 90 degrees to the right. Network cameras do not support rotation or mirroring.

## 5. Camera Mirroring

By default, users see their own camera feed reversed relative to reality. If you'd like to adjust this, you can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Video" to turn on camera mirroring.

Also, by default, other users in the classroom also see your camera feed mirrored. If a user has enabled "Camera Mirroring" and wants other classroom users to also see this mirrored feed (that is, so what they see of themselves matches what others see of them), they can contact the academic staff with access to the "Backend Management System" and ask them to add a classroom skin under 【School Settings → Classroom Settings】 in the backend, enabling the 【Camera Mirroring Mode Setting】 feature within that skin, then apply that skin to the class. Once this is set, every user in the classroom needs to exit and re-enter class for it to take effect.

Network cameras do not support rotation or mirroring.

## 6. Camera Virtual Background

Windows 10 and higher supports setting a virtual camera background within ClassInX software. You can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Virtual Background" to set it.

Users can choose from the system's built-in virtual backgrounds, or upload a local image as a virtual background. Uploaded images must be in PNG format, with up to 10 uploaded at once. There's no size limit on individual images, but if a single image exceeds 2MB, the system automatically compresses its resolution down to 60% of the original.

# III. Adjusting the Microphone

## 1. Switching Microphones

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to switch microphone devices.

## 2. Testing the Microphone

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to test whether the microphone is working normally.

Click the "Test" button next to the microphone device — a 10-second countdown will begin. During the countdown, speak (for example, count from 1 to 10); if the microphone indicator shows a green wave moving while you speak, and you can hear your own voice, the microphone is working normally. If the indicator shows a yellow wave, the microphone volume is too low — try speaking closer to the microphone, or raise the microphone volume. If there's no wave movement while speaking at all, try switching to a different microphone device, or fix the microphone and then restart your computer/large display.

## 3. Adjusting Microphone Volume

If the microphone's wave indicator shows yellow while you speak, or shows no movement at all, you can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to raise the microphone volume, or enable "Auto-Adjust Microphone Volume."

If manually raising the microphone volume, we don't recommend setting it too high, since this can introduce noise and other issues.

While "Auto-Adjust Microphone Volume" is enabled, manually adjusting microphone volume is not supported.

Also, once "Auto-Adjust Microphone Volume" is enabled, "Background Noise Reduction" is enabled by default along with it, and "Music Mode" is disabled by default. Conversely, once "Auto-Adjust Microphone Volume" is disabled, "Background Noise Reduction" stays enabled and "Music Mode" stays disabled — adjust these yourself if needed.

## 4. Background Noise Reduction

If the environment around a user is too noisy, they can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to enable "Background Noise Reduction." Once enabled, ambient noise will be automatically reduced, making it easier for other users in the classroom to hear speech clearly. We recommend keeping this enabled in most usage scenarios.

In a music scenario, you need to disable "Background Noise Reduction" before you can enable "Music Mode." Also, once "Auto-Adjust Microphone Volume" is enabled, "Background Noise Reduction" is enabled by default along with it.

### Notes
In a music scenario, once the teacher enables the classroom's "Music Mode," the "AI Noise Reduction" or "Background Noise Reduction" feature for every user in the classroom stops working — this is by design, to ensure instrument sound comes through smoothly.

## 5. Music Mode

When a class involves a professional music scenario (such as playing an instrument), we recommend the teacher tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to enable the classroom's "Music Mode."

"Music Mode" can only be enabled once both "Background Noise Reduction" and "Auto-Adjust Microphone Volume" are disabled. Once "Music Mode" is enabled, the system's noise reduction for voices and ambient noise will be weakened.

## 6. Auto-Enable Microphone on Entering the Classroom

If a user wants their microphone to turn on automatically every time they enter a ClassInX classroom on computer or large display, they can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to enable "Auto-Enable Microphone on Entering Classroom."

# IV. Adjusting the Speaker

## 1. Switching Speakers

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to switch speaker devices.

## 2. Testing the Speaker

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to test whether the speaker is working normally.

Click the "Test" button next to the speaker device — a sound will play. If you can hear a drum sound, the speaker is working normally. If you don't hear anything, try raising the speaker volume, switching to a different speaker device, or fixing the speaker and then restarting your computer/large display.

## 3. Adjusting Speaker Volume

If the sound a user hears is too quiet or too loud, they can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Audio" to adjust the speaker volume.

# V. Hardware Fix (Camera/Microphone/Speaker)

**Fixing the camera:** if the local camera app on Windows shows the camera feed normally, but the image still won't display once you've selected that camera in ClassIn X, you can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Hardware Fix" in the bottom-left corner to fix the camera; we recommend restarting your computer/large display once the fix is complete.

**Fixing the microphone:** if the microphone works normally locally on Windows, but there's no green wave movement when speaking once you've selected that microphone in ClassIn X, you can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Hardware Fix" in the bottom-left corner to fix the microphone; we recommend restarting your computer/large display once the fix is complete.

**Fixing the speaker:** if sound plays normally locally on Windows, but clicking the "Test" button next to the speaker device in ClassIn X still produces no sound, you can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go to "Settings" → "Additional Settings" → "Hardware Fix" in the bottom-left corner to fix the speaker; we recommend restarting your computer/large display once the fix is complete.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: classinx-04_classroom-av-features.md -->

# ClassInX Class Recording Tutorial

title: "ClassInX Class Recording Tutorial"

## ClassInX Class Recording Tutorial

# I. Recording Notes

## 1. Recommended Recording Equipment

Computer or large display requirements are as follows:

| | Minimum Requirements | Recommended Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processor | Intel i5 8th gen or higher / AMD Ryzen 5 1st gen or higher | Intel i7 9th gen or higher / AMD Ryzen 7 2nd gen or higher |
| OS | Windows 7 or higher | Windows 10 or higher |
| Memory | Windows: 4GB RAM | Windows: 8GB RAM |
| Display | 1280x720 or higher | 1920x1080 or higher |
| Network | 4Mbps or higher | 6Mbps or higher |

## 2. Recording Area Settings

### Usage Notes
If you checked "Record ClassIn Classroom" when creating the class session, or need local recording, the teacher enters the classroom using ClassInX on a computer/large display.

If you only want to record what's inside the classroom, you can check "Record" for either:

**"Minimum-Size Classroom Window"** (once recording starts, the classroom window shrinks to 1280x720 and cannot be resized)

or **"Current-Size Classroom Window"** (once recording starts, you can drag to resize the classroom window; it can be maximized but not minimized) under "Recording Area" in ClassInX's classroom settings.

Once you're in ClassInX, it defaults to full-screen display with no way to resize the window — so whether you choose the minimum-size or current-size window, the recording captures the classroom's full-screen view either way.

If you'd like to record the entire computer/large display desktop, including pop-up notifications and similar elements, you can check "Record Entire Computer Desktop" under "Recording Area" in ClassInX's classroom settings — once recording starts, everything both inside and outside the classroom will be recorded. Note that a larger display screen demands more from your computer's performance.

### Notes
When "Minimum-Size Classroom Window" or "Current-Size Classroom Window" is selected, if the teacher clicks "Return to Desktop" in ClassInX or uses the toolbox's "Screen Share" feature, the recording captures the entire computer/large display desktop where the ClassInX classroom window is located.

If the teacher is using Windows 7 and wants to record the classroom window, they'll also need to set the system theme to the Aero theme.

This setting only applies to the current computer/large display.

### Steps

#### Current-Size Classroom Window:

#### Entire Computer Desktop:

#### Setting the Aero Theme on Windows 7:

## 3. Recording Video Quality Settings

If you need to improve the recorded video's quality, you can choose the recording quality under "Recorded Video Resolution" in ClassInX's classroom settings.

HD mode records the class video at a resolution of 1280x720; Full HD mode records it at 1920x1080.

When "Recording Area" is set to "Minimum-Size Classroom Window," Full HD resolution is not available under "Recorded Video Resolution."

## 4. Recording Sound Settings

If you want to record all sound from the entire computer/large display, you can select "System Sound" under "Recording Mode" in ClassInX's classroom settings. Once "System Sound" is checked, recording captures all sound on the computer, both inside and outside the classroom — for example, video or music playing outside the classroom, and notification sounds from messaging software, will all be recorded.

If you only want to record sound within the classroom, you can select "Software Sound" instead. Once "Software Sound" is checked, recording only captures sound within the classroom, and sound from outside the classroom won't be recorded.

## 5. Recording FAQ

While recording is in progress, please don't plug or unplug speaker devices like headphones or external speakers — make sure the classroom's speaker sound can be heard normally.

While recording is in progress, please don't proactively exit the classroom.

Make sure the classroom's microphone is working normally while recording.

Make sure your network connection is stable while recording.

While using Record On-Site, make sure the camera feed selected for the on-site recording window displays properly.

## 6. Recording Status

### 6.1 How the Lead Teacher Checks Record On-Site Status

Once a class session has "Record On-Site" checked, the lead teacher can check the classroom's recording status indicator after entering the classroom to determine whether recording is working normally.

Once the lead teacher's recording starts, on computer/large display they can check the recording status in the dock right below the classroom window. The recording icon is a camera + small cloud; when the small cloud is "green," Record On-Site is recording normally; when the small cloud is "red," Record On-Site has been interrupted.

### 6.2 How the Lead Teacher Checks Record ClassIn Classroom Status

Once a class session has "Record ClassIn Classroom" checked, the lead teacher can check the classroom's recording status indicator after entering the classroom to determine whether recording is working normally.

Once the lead teacher's recording starts, on computer/large display they can check the recording status in the dock right below the classroom window. The recording icon is a camera + small cloud; when the small cloud is "green," Record ClassIn Classroom is recording normally; when the small cloud is "red," Record ClassIn Classroom has been interrupted.

### 6.3 Checking Local Recording Status

After entering the classroom, teachers can check the classroom's recording status indicator to determine whether recording is working normally.

Once local recording starts, on computer/large display you can check the recording status in the dock right below the classroom window. The recording icon is a camera + small circle; when the small circle is "green," local recording is recording normally; when the small circle is "red," local recording has been interrupted.

## 7. Recording-Related Parameters

### 7.1 Bandwidth Requirements by On-Stage Headcount

| On-Stage Headcount | Upload Bandwidth Required | Download Bandwidth Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1v6 | ≥2Mbps | ≥2Mbps |
| 1v12 | ≥4Mbps | ≥4Mbps |
| 1v1 HD | ≥1.5Mbps | ≥1.5Mbps |
| 1v1 Full HD | ≥3Mbps | ≥3Mbps |
| 1v1 Dual Camera Full HD | ≥6Mbps | ≥6Mbps |
| 1v6 HD | ≥8Mbps | ≥8Mbps |
| 1v6 Full HD | ≥15Mbps | ≥15Mbps |

### 7.2 Bandwidth Add-On Rules for Additional Features

**Cloud recording / livestream (affects only the teacher's side):**

HD video: +1Mbps upload bandwidth

Full HD video: +2Mbps upload bandwidth

**Screen sharing:**

Sender: +2Mbps upload bandwidth

Receiver: +2Mbps download bandwidth

**Video Wall:**

Bandwidth requirement = on-stage headcount bandwidth requirement × 2

### 7.3 Recording Technical Specifications

| Parameter | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| File Format | MP4, FLV |
| Aspect Ratio | 16:9 |
| Video Codec | H.264 @ 15fps |
| Resolution | 1080p/720p |
| Audio Bitrate | 64kbps (customizable/extendable) |

```yaml
title: "Differences Between Record ClassIn Classroom, Record On-Site, and OMO Livestream Broadcast"
source_title_zh: "录制教室、录制现场和OMO站播的区别"
```

## II. Differences Between Record ClassIn Classroom, Record On-Site, and OMO Livestream Broadcast

Cloud recording has two modes: Record ClassIn Classroom, and Record On-Site. These two modes can be enabled individually or together.

**Record ClassIn Classroom:** this mode has two recording area options: the first only records what's inside the lead teacher's classroom window; the second records the lead teacher's entire large display, including the classroom window and everything the user does on the large display's desktop. These two recording area options can be configured in the app settings. If the lead teacher only wants to record what's inside the classroom window, they can check "Current-Size Classroom Window" under recording area settings. If the lead teacher wants to record both what's happening inside the ClassInX classroom and everything on the large display's desktop, they can check "Entire Computer Desktop" under recording area settings.

**Record On-Site:** this mode only records the camera feed the lead teacher selects for on-site recording during the class recording process — anything outside that camera's view is not recorded. Online students in the classroom can open the on-site recording window to view a larger, clearer feed of the teacher's instruction. Users watching class via the web livestream link can also switch directly to viewing the on-site recording feed. In addition, when watching class playback, students can likewise switch to on-site recording mode for a better review and understanding of the teacher's explanation.

**OMO Livestream Broadcast:** when students only need to watch the teacher's livestream feed within the classroom and recording isn't needed, we recommend using OMO Livestream Broadcast. This is a high-definition on-site recording mode where only the camera feed the lead teacher selects in the OMO livestream broadcast settings is recorded within the classroom — anything outside that camera's view is not recorded. Online students in the classroom can open the OMO livestream broadcast window for a clearer view of the teacher's instruction. This mode is especially well suited to teaching scenarios that need high-definition video quality.

When Record On-Site and OMO Livestream Broadcast are both enabled at the same time, they cannot each use a different camera — that is, when the lead teacher selects a camera for Record On-Site, OMO Livestream Broadcast automatically switches to that same camera, and vice versa.

Record On-Site and OMO Livestream Broadcast are only supported when the lead teacher uses a computer or large display (Windows) — other devices (such as phone/tablet) are not supported.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Record On-Site"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX录制现场"
```

## III. ClassInX Record On-Site

### What Is "Cloud Recording"?
"Cloud recording" includes two recording modes — "Record ClassIn Classroom" and "Record On-Site." Once recording is checked when creating a class session, ClassIn's built-in recording feature can fully capture the entire teaching process from the lead teacher's perspective while they teach. These recorded videos are automatically uploaded and stored on ClassIn's servers. After class ends, the recording is turned into a "class playback video" in about half an hour, for students and teachers to review and watch afterward.

### Applies to
The lead teacher.

### Prerequisites
When creating the class session, you need to check "Record On-Site" under "Cloud Recording" before the lead teacher can use the "Record On-Site" cloud recording feature during class.

Record On-Site means that while the lead teacher uses ClassInX to record class, only the camera feed selected in the on-site recording window is recorded — anything outside that camera's view is not recorded, so make sure the selected camera feed displays properly.

Every time the lead teacher enters the classroom, they'll be shown a recording prompt; once they click Confirm, they'll see the on-site recording window along with a "Recording Countdown" prompt.

In this window, you can view the current on-site recording feed, and switch which camera device is being recorded via the settings in the window's top-right corner — recording only proceeds normally if the on-site recording feed is displaying correctly.

Once the lead teacher has adjusted the on-site recording camera feed, they can manually click "Start Recording Now" on the countdown prompt to begin recording, or wait for the countdown to finish and recording will start automatically. The default recording countdown is 10 minutes; to change this, please contact a teacher with "Backend Management" permission to go into the "Backend Management System" and change the recording countdown time.

Recording cannot be stopped once class is underway — if you don't want to record, you can disable the camera in the on-site recording window, or turn off "Record ClassIn Classroom" the next time you create a class session. Recording automatically stops once the lead teacher exits the classroom; when the lead teacher re-enters the classroom, they'll be prompted to start recording again.

In addition, online students in the classroom can also view the "Live On-Site" feed (i.e., the on-site recording feed) in the bottom-right corner.

Record On-Site is only supported when the lead teacher uses a computer or large display (Windows).

If the lead teacher's network is unstable, recording may fail. The recording icon will turn red, and ClassInX will automatically retry recording after a failure.

If the lead teacher plugs or unplugs a speaker device on their computer/large display, or the speaker becomes disconnected due to an unstable connection, recording will also stop. In this case, the lead teacher will see a "Recording Interrupted" prompt — to continue recording, reconnect the speaker device securely or switch to a more stable speaker device, then click Retry in the classroom's "Recording Interrupted" prompt window.

### Related Articles
"Editing the Recording Countdown"

### Steps
1. Enter the classroom.
2. Read the recording prompt, then click Confirm.
3. View the on-site recording feed, select a camera in the settings in the top-right corner of the on-site recording window, then click Done.
4. Click "Start Recording Now" to the right of the Recording Countdown, or wait for the countdown to finish for recording to start automatically.
5. Check the recording status.

### The Lead Teacher's On-Site Recording Feed Looks Like This:

### Students Viewing the On-Site Recording Feed on Computer in the Classroom:

### Students Viewing the On-Site Recording Feed on Phone or Android Tablet in the Classroom:

### Students Viewing the On-Site Recording Feed on iPad in the Classroom:

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Record ClassIn Classroom"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX录制教室"
```

## IV. ClassInX Record ClassIn Classroom

When creating the class session, you need to check "Record ClassIn Classroom" under "Cloud Recording" before the lead teacher can use this "Record ClassIn Classroom" cloud recording feature during class.

"Record ClassIn Classroom" records what's happening within the classroom itself.

If the lead teacher's recording area setting in ClassInX is set to Current-Size Classroom Window or Minimized Classroom Window, the recording captures the lead teacher's classroom view; however, if the lead teacher uses the "Screen Share" tool or clicks "Return to Desktop," the recording instead captures the computer/large display desktop where the ClassInX classroom window is located.

If the lead teacher's recording area is set to Entire Computer Desktop, the recording captures the computer/large display desktop where the classroom window is located.

Every time the lead teacher enters the classroom, they'll be shown a recording prompt; once they click Confirm, they'll see a "Recording Countdown" prompt, and can manually click "Start Recording Now" to begin recording, or wait for the countdown to finish and recording will start automatically. The default recording countdown is 10 minutes; to change this, please contact a teacher with "Backend Management" permission to go into the "Backend Management System" and change the recording countdown time.

Recording cannot be stopped once class is underway — if you don't want to record, you can only turn off "Record ClassIn Classroom" the next time you create a class session. Recording automatically stops once the lead teacher exits the classroom; when the lead teacher re-enters the classroom, they'll be prompted to start recording again.

If a teacher realizes after starting class that they forgot to enable "Record ClassIn Classroom," they can use the "Local Recording" feature to record and save the class to their computer/large display locally, or create a new class session and check "Record ClassIn Classroom" when creating it.

If the lead teacher's network is unstable, recording may fail.

Once recording fails, ClassInX will automatically retry — if it fails 3 times in a row without successfully starting, a pop-up will appear in the classroom prompting the teacher to switch from cloud recording to local recording; the lead teacher can then manually switch to local recording (this switch is only supported on computer/large display). Once switched to local recording, the recorded file is stored by default in a newly created folder under ClassInX file, in MP4 format by default; local recording can be manually stopped and restarted. If you don't click to switch to local recording, cloud recording continues, and ClassInX keeps retrying — the switch prompt won't reappear, but you can reopen it by clicking the red "recording failed" icon.

Also, if the lead teacher exits and re-enters the classroom, ClassInX will retry cloud recording again.

### Record ClassIn Classroom Feed Looks Like This:

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Local Recording"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX本地录课"
```

## V. ClassInX Local Recording

### What Is "Local Recording"?
"Local Recording" refers to a teacher recording the class using ClassInX's screen recording (recording the classroom window) and saving it to their computer/large display locally.

As long as either Record ClassIn Classroom or Record On-Site is enabled (or both), the class session's co-teacher can use local recording.

If neither Record ClassIn Classroom nor Record On-Site is enabled, the class session's co-teacher can still use the local recording feature.

An "academic teacher" who enters classroom monitoring via the "Classroom Monitoring" module in the "Backend Management System" can use the local recording feature.

Anyone who enters the "Whiteboard" in ClassInX can use the "Local Recording" feature.

You can use "Local Recording" after creating and entering a temporary classroom from a class or friend chat interface.

Teachers who enter the prep room can use the "Local Recording" feature.

### When to Use This
When a classroom has a co-teacher, if the lead teacher's cloud recording of the classroom becomes unstable (for example, recording gets interrupted and the classroom's recording status icon turns "red"), the co-teacher can use local recording in the classroom to make sure the class is fully recorded without gaps; after class, the academic teacher can upload the co-teacher's local recording to the "Backend Management System" to replace the lead teacher's incomplete recording for that session.

When a classroom has no co-teacher, if the lead teacher's cloud recording becomes unstable (for example, recording gets interrupted and the classroom's recording status icon turns "red"), the academic teacher can log into the "Backend Management System," enter classroom monitoring under "Classroom Monitoring," and perform local recording; after class, the academic teacher can upload their own local recording to the "Backend Management System" to replace the lead teacher's incomplete recording for that session.

If a classroom doesn't have Record ClassIn Classroom or Record On-Site enabled, but the classroom content needs to be recorded during the lesson anyway, the lead teacher or co-teacher can use local recording, and afterward send the local recording's playback video to anyone who needs to watch it.

Once the prerequisites for local recording are met, click the recording icon in the dock below; in the recording video save-path window, choose the save path and the recording's file type (FLV/MP4, defaulting to FLV), and recording will begin. Local recording captures what's inside the classroom.

If the teacher's recording area setting in ClassInX is set to Current-Size Classroom Window or Minimized Classroom Window, the recording captures the lead teacher's classroom view; however, if the teacher uses the "Screen Share" tool or clicks "Return to Desktop," the recording instead captures the computer/large display desktop where the ClassInX classroom window is located.

If the teacher's recording area is set to Entire Computer Desktop, the recording captures the computer desktop/large display where the ClassInX classroom window is located.

Clicking the recording icon again ends local recording. You can start local recording again afterward if needed.

If the teacher's network is unstable, recording may fail — you can manually try restarting recording if it fails.

If the teacher plugs or unplugs a speaker device on their computer/large display, or the speaker becomes disconnected due to an unstable connection, recording will also stop. In this case, the lead teacher will see a "Recording Interrupted" prompt — to continue recording, reconnect the speaker device securely or switch to a more stable speaker device, then click Retry in the classroom's "Recording Interrupted" prompt window.

### Steps
1. Enter the Whiteboard or classroom.
2. Click the recording icon in the dock right below.
3. Read the recording prompt, then click Start Recording.
4. Choose the local recording video's save path and save type, then click Save.
5. Check the recording status. Click the recording icon again to end local recording.

### Local Recording Feed Looks Like This:

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Switching to Local Recording When ClassInX's Record ClassIn Classroom Fails"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX录制教室失败时切换本地录课"
```

## VI. Switching to Local Recording When ClassInX's Record ClassIn Classroom Fails

If the lead teacher's network is unstable and causes Record ClassIn Classroom to fail, ClassInX will automatically retry recording — if it fails 3 times in a row without successfully starting, a pop-up will appear in the classroom prompting the teacher to switch from cloud recording to local recording; the lead teacher can then manually switch to local recording (this switch is only supported on computer/large display). Once switched to local recording, the recorded file is stored by default in a newly created folder under ClassInX file, in MP4 format by default; local recording can be manually stopped and restarted. If you don't click to switch to local recording, cloud recording continues, and ClassInX keeps retrying — the switch prompt won't reappear, but you can reopen it by clicking the red "recording failed" icon.

After class ends, when the teacher views the playback from "Schedule" or "Class," the playback button will show a small red dot; clicking it shows the teacher a message: "A local recording file is pending upload — please contact your administrator to upload the recorded video." Clicking "Local Recording File" opens the folder where the recording is stored. You can send the local recording to your academic teacher, who can then log into the Backend Management System and upload it to the corresponding class session's playback slot. If there's no local recording file (for example, if it was deleted), no such prompt will appear.

### Steps
1. Read the recording error prompt, then click Switch Now.
2. When viewing the class playback afterward, find the video and provide it to your academic teacher.

# ClassInX Classroom Interaction and Common Features

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassInX Classroom Interaction and Common Features"
source_title_zh: "ClassInX 教室互动与常用功能"
```

## ClassInX Classroom Interaction and Common Features

# I. Entering the Classroom

## Usage Notes
When there's a classroom you can enter (teachers can enter the formal classroom up to 20 minutes early, students up to 10 minutes early), a class notification pops up in the bottom-left corner. Users can also tap or swipe up in the bottom-left corner to open the notification center, then click the "Start Class" button to enter the classroom.

## Steps
1. Tap or swipe up in the bottom-left corner of the screen to open the notification center.
2. Click Start Class.

# II. Exiting the Classroom

While in the classroom, users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, click the Settings button on the far right, then click "Exit Classroom" to leave the current classroom.

If it's not yet the formal class start time, users can also exit the current classroom from the notification center in the bottom-left corner. In addition, if the skin applied to the class's classroom settings doesn't allow the teacher to end class early, the lead teacher can still click Exit from the notification center in the bottom-left corner.

As long as it's not past the overtime period, exiting the classroom lets you re-enter to continue class. Once the overtime period is reached, you can no longer re-enter.

1. Tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock.
2. Click Settings on the far right.
3. Click Exit Classroom.

# III. Ending Class for Everyone

## Applies to
The lead teacher.

Provided the skin applied to the class's classroom settings has "Allow Teacher to End Class Early" checked, the lead teacher can, once the formal classroom is in session, tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, go to Settings on the far right, then swipe "End Class for Everyone" to end the session early. Alternatively, they can click "End Class" from the notification center in the bottom-left corner.

Once "End Class for Everyone" is triggered, every user in the classroom is automatically removed, the classroom is closed, and neither teachers nor students can re-enter.

1. Swipe "End Class for Everyone."

# IV. Checking Class Session Elapsed Time

Once a user is in the classroom, they can use the "collapse" action in the notification center in the bottom-left corner to keep the notification dock pinned, showing the elapsed class time — for example, "01:05:06 elapsed." Once pinned, tapping or swiping up on the notification dock in the bottom-left corner again will make the elapsed-time display disappear.

1. Click the collapse button next to the notification center.

# V. Returning to the Desktop

Tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then click "Go to Desktop" to switch to the Windows system desktop.

While on the desktop, users can use the Click Tool from the radial dial to open, move, and perform other operations, or use the Pen tool to write on the desktop; once done, click the button below the radial dial to return to the whiteboard/classroom.

If a teacher clicks "Go to Desktop" while recording ClassIn Classroom or doing a local recording, the recording area switches to the entire Windows system desktop.

Also, in a formal classroom, if a teacher clicks "Go to Desktop," other users in the classroom cannot see what the teacher does on the desktop.

1. Click Go to Desktop.
2. Use the Click Tool to open/move files on the desktop, and so on.
3. Once done, click Return to go back to the whiteboard/classroom.

# VI. Classroom Chat Tool

Once inside the classroom, users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go into the chat tool. The chat tool includes a Messages area and a Questions area.

In the Messages area, users can send text, emoji, and screenshots. Teachers can mute a student's chat access (a muted student cannot send messages or ask questions), and can copy, translate, or delete a student's chat message; if the message is an image, the teacher can also place that image onto the whiteboard for display.

In the Questions area, teachers can view and reply to questions raised by other users in the classroom.

In addition, teachers can also mute everyone or move the chat window off-screen from the settings below.

1. Click the Chat Tool.

# VII. Roster

## 1. Co-Teacher On-Stage/Off-Stage

### Usage Notes
By default, a co-teacher enters the classroom off-stage (camera not shown, cannot speak via microphone). If a co-teacher needs to go on stage (to show their camera and speak via microphone), they can click to go on stage themselves in the roster; if interaction isn't needed, they can click again to go off stage. Besides the co-teacher operating this themselves, the lead teacher can also send the co-teacher on or off stage from the roster.

In the roster, the on-stage button next to the co-teacher's name shows green when they're on stage, and gray when they're off stage.

### Steps
1. Click Roster.
2. Toggle the co-teacher's on-stage/off-stage status next to their name.

## 2. Student On-Stage/Off-Stage

In the classroom, the lead teacher or co-teacher can send students on or off stage from the roster. If a student is already on stage, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also click the student's on-stage camera and click the off-stage button in the tools below the camera to send that student off stage.

If the teacher wants every on-stage student sent off stage at once, they can click their own on-stage camera and click the "Send All Off Stage" button in the tools below their camera. The teacher's camera tools also include "Swap On-Stage Students," a related on/off-stage tool.

A student being on stage means they can show their camera and speak via microphone. A student being off stage means they're still in the classroom, but their camera isn't shown and they can't speak via microphone.

In the roster, the on-stage button next to a student's name shows green when they're on stage, and gray when they're off stage.

1. Toggle a student's on-stage/off-stage status next to their name.

Teacher clicking their own on-stage camera's tools to operate "Send All Students Off Stage" / "Swap On-Stage Students":

## 3. Authorizing/Revoking a Student's Authorization

In the classroom, the lead teacher or co-teacher can authorize or revoke a student's authorization from the roster. If the student is on stage, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also click the student's on-stage camera and click the authorize button in the tools below the camera to authorize or revoke authorization.

If the teacher wants every on-stage student authorized, every on-stage student's authorization revoked, or students automatically authorized once they go on stage, the teacher can click their own on-stage camera and click the corresponding button in the tools below their camera.

An authorized student can use certain classroom tools, such as the pen, text, eraser, and operating the whiteboard.

Once authorized, a student's authorize button shows yellow; if the student is on stage, a yellow crown icon also appears in the top-right corner of their camera, indicating authorized status. Conversely, an unauthorized student's authorize icon shows gray, and no crown icon appears on their camera while on stage.

1. Toggle authorization/revoke authorization for a student next to their name.

Teacher clicking their own on-stage camera's tools to operate "Authorize On-Stage Students" / "Auto-Authorize Students on Stage" / "Revoke All Authorization":

## 4. Rewarding/Un-Rewarding a Student

In the classroom, the lead teacher or co-teacher can award a student a trophy from the roster as a reward, and the trophy count that student has earned this session also shows next to the trophy button. If the student is on stage, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also click the student's on-stage camera and click the trophy button in the tools below the camera to award them a trophy, with the trophy count also shown in the bottom-right corner of the student's camera.

If the teacher needs to undo a student's reward, the student must be on stage, then the teacher can press and hold the trophy icon in the tools below that student's camera to remove one trophy (press and hold on a large display; right-click with the mouse on computer).

Also, if the teacher wants to award every on-stage student a trophy, they can click their own on-stage camera and click the trophy button in the tools below their camera.

If the teacher needs to reward every student, they can use the Answer Clicker tool from the toolbox — once students respond, the teacher can recall the answer clicker to award every participating student a trophy.

1. Click the reward button next to a student's name to award them a trophy.
(While the student is on stage, pressing and holding/clicking the reward button in the tools below their camera removes a trophy.)

Teacher clicking their own on-stage camera's tools to operate "Reward On-Stage Students":

## 5. Muting/Unmuting a Student's Microphone

In the classroom, the lead teacher or co-teacher can mute or unmute a student's microphone from the roster.

If the student is on stage, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also click the student's on-stage camera and click the mute button in the tools below the camera to mute or unmute that student's microphone.

A student's microphone shows green when it's on and they can speak normally; once a teacher mutes them, their microphone turns red and they can no longer speak via microphone.

If the teacher needs to mute every student's microphone, they can click their own on-stage camera and click the mute button in the tools below their camera to mute or unmute every student's microphone at once. A red microphone icon in the bottom-right corner of the teacher's own on-stage camera indicates they've enabled mute-all.

1. Click "···" next to a student's name, then click Mute/Unmute Student's Microphone.

Teacher clicking their own on-stage camera's tools to operate "Mute All" for students' microphones:

## 6. Private Chat with a Student via the Roster

In the classroom, if the lead teacher or co-teacher needs to communicate privately with a student, they can start a private chat from the roster. If the student is on stage, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also click the student's on-stage camera and click the private chat button in the tools below the camera. Besides these two ways to start a private chat, teachers using the Video Wall tool can also start a private chat with a student from below their camera in the video wall.

Clicking the private chat button quickly pulls the teacher and that student into a group discussion classroom, while other students remain unaffected in the main classroom. Once the teacher and student finish communicating, the teacher can click Group Discussion in the dock below, then click "End" in the bottom-right corner of the group discussion window — this returns the teacher and student to the main classroom and closes the group discussion classroom.

Note: if the teacher is recording class, the private chat will also be captured in the recording.

1. Click "···" next to a student's name, then click Private Chat.
2. Once the conversation ends, click Group Discussion in the dock right below.
3. Click End in the bottom-right corner of the group discussion window.

## 7. Muting/Unmuting a Student in Chat via the Roster (Chat Tool)

In the classroom, besides muting or unmuting a specific student's chat access within the classroom chat tool, the lead teacher or co-teacher can also do this from the roster.

A muted student cannot send messages or ask questions in the classroom chat tool.

1. Click "···" next to a student's name, then click Mute Chat.

## 8. Removing a Student from the Classroom

Provided the skin applied to the class's classroom settings doesn't have "Hide Remove Student Setting" checked, the class session's lead teacher or co-teacher can remove a student from the classroom via the roster.

The removal duration can be set — the default is 5 minutes, and you can adjust the duration after clicking the remove button, with a maximum of the entire class session and a minimum of 1 minute. If set to 5 minutes, the student can only click "Start Class" to re-enter the classroom after 5 minutes have passed.

Note: once the classroom enters the overtime period, students cannot enter the classroom.

1. Click "···" next to a student's name, then click Remove from Classroom.
2. Set the removal duration in the system prompt, then click Confirm.

## 9. Raise Hand to Auto-Go-On-Stage

In the classroom, when an off-stage student needs to speak with the teacher, besides the teacher sending the student on/off stage via the roster, the teacher can also enable "Raise Hand to Auto-Go-On-Stage" in the settings in the bottom-left corner of the roster. Once enabled, students can tap or press and hold the raise-hand button in the bottom-right corner of the classroom to raise their hand, and they'll automatically go on stage.

Note: if a classroom has many students, many students raising their hands at once could cause frequent, disruptive on-stage/off-stage switching, affecting teaching quality.

1. Click Settings in the bottom-left corner.
2. Turn "Raise Hand to Auto-Go-On-Stage" on or off.

## 10. On-Stage Seat Rotation

In the classroom, once the on-stage seats area is shown, the lead teacher or co-teacher can enable on-stage seat rotation from the roster, letting students take turns going on stage to show their camera and interact.

Once enabled, you can set the rotation scope (online students / students with camera on), rotation order (sequential/random), and rotation interval (in seconds).

If the teacher needs to interact with a specific student for an extended time and doesn't want them rotated off, they can drag that student's camera onto the whiteboard and adjust its position there.

1. Turn On-Stage Seat Rotation on or off (once on, set the rotation scope/order/interval).

# VIII. ClassInX Opening/Uploading Files (Courseware)

If a user needs to open a file from Cloud Drive/Space, or upload a desktop file into the classroom, they can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, click "Files," then go into Cloud Drive/Space to do this. Once opened, the file displays on the whiteboard.

In the classroom, only courseware opened via "Files" in the dock by the lead teacher or co-teacher can be seen by other users in the classroom.

1. Click Files.

# IX. Toolbox

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go into the "Toolbox" to use more teaching tools, such as Small Blackboard, Countdown Timer, Browser, Answer Clicker, and more.

Also, some teaching tools are only usable in a formal classroom, such as Group Discussion and Livestream Chat.

1. Click Toolbox.

# X. Classroom LMS

Besides viewing and using a class's LMS activities within the class itself, teachers can also open and use them within the classroom. Once inside the classroom, teachers can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then go into "LMS" to view the class's activities — what the teacher sees here stays in sync with what students see.

Teachers can also create and publish quizzes and answer sheet activities from the classroom's LMS. Once published, students in the classroom can answer directly within the classroom, and the teacher can go over the answers. In addition, teachers can create and publish assignment activities; unlike quizzes and answer sheets, students cannot answer or submit assignments within the classroom — they can only view and submit them later within the ClassIn class.

1. Click LMS.
2. Teacher views or creates an activity (quiz/answer sheet/assignment activity).

# XI. Entering the ClassIn Client

Users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then click "ClassIn" to enter the ClassIn interface, where they can view and use features outside the classroom, such as creating a class/classroom.

1. Click ClassIn.

# XII. ClassInX Screen Projection

When a teacher or student wants to display content from their phone/tablet or another computer in the classroom, they can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock and go into "Screen Projection," or click "Screen Projection" in the toolbox. For projection to work, the projecting device and the receiving device must be on the same network.

**(1)** To project from another computer into the classroom, the projecting device needs to log into ClassIn, click Screen Projection in the left navigation, enter the receiving device's projection code and click Project, or select the receiving device's name to complete projection. The four green corners on the projecting device's screen indicate the projection area, which cannot be adjusted — the entire screen is always used.

**(2)** An Apple phone, tablet, or computer can project using the device's built-in screen mirroring feature, selecting the receiving device's name to complete projection; you can also download the ClassIn Screen Projection app from the App Store, entering the receiving device's projection code in the app and clicking Project, or selecting the receiving device's name to complete projection.

**(3)** An Android phone or tablet needs to download the ClassIn Screen Projection app from the app store, entering the receiving device's projection code in the app and clicking Project, or selecting the receiving device's name to complete projection.

**(4)** Other video apps with a built-in projection feature can also project their content into the classroom. Open the video app, play the video, then click the app's own projection button and select the receiving device's name to complete projection.

While using the screen projection tool, the bottom-right corner of the projection tool window offers more settings for this projection session:

**Sharing settings:**

Play the projecting device's sound through this device's speaker; share the projecting device's sound with everyone else in the classroom.

**Privacy settings:**

Allow receiving projections from all devices; once the projection window is open, allow receiving projections from all devices.

In addition, multiple devices can project into the classroom at once — once multiple devices have projected successfully, the receiving device can switch between different devices in the projection tool window's bottom-right corner to view different projected content.

1. Click Screen Projection, or go into the toolbox and click Screen Projection.

#### Projecting from another computer to the ClassIn X whiteboard or classroom:

#### Projecting from an Apple phone, tablet, or computer to the ClassIn X whiteboard or classroom:

#### Projecting from an Android phone or tablet to the ClassIn X whiteboard or classroom:

# XIII. Classroom Network/CPU Status

Once inside the classroom, users can tap or swipe up at the bottom-center of the screen to open the dock, then click the network icon to check current network and CPU status. When this icon turns orange or red, it means the network connection is poor or CPU usage is too high.

1. Click the network icon.

# XIV. ClassInX OMO Livestream Broadcast

## Prerequisites
Backend administrators need to enable the "OMO Livestream Broadcast" feature under School Settings → Value-Added Services in the backend, then check "OMO Livestream Broadcast" when creating the class session.

## When to Use This
When students only need to watch the teacher's livestream feed within the classroom and recording isn't needed, we recommend checking "OMO Livestream Broadcast" when creating the class session.

OMO Livestream Broadcast is a high-definition on-site recording mode — once the lead teacher selects the camera feed to display in the OMO livestream broadcast settings, online students in the classroom can open the OMO livestream broadcast window in the bottom-right corner of the classroom for a clearer view of the teacher's livestream instruction.

The lead teacher can also disable OMO Livestream Broadcast mid-class; once disabled, online students in the classroom will no longer see the livestream feed.

## Notes
When Record On-Site and OMO Livestream Broadcast are both enabled at the same time, they cannot each use a different camera — that is, when the lead teacher selects a camera for Record On-Site, OMO Livestream Broadcast automatically switches to that same camera, and vice versa.

Record On-Site and OMO Livestream Broadcast are only supported when the lead teacher uses a computer or large display (Windows) — other devices (such as phone/tablet) are not supported.

1. Enter the classroom.
2. Click OMO Livestream Broadcast in the dock right below.
3. Select a camera in the settings in the top-right corner of the OMO livestream broadcast window, then click Done; view the livestream feed.
4. Minimize the OMO livestream broadcast window.

### The Lead Teacher's OMO Livestream Broadcast Feed Looks Like This:

### Students Viewing the OMO Livestream Broadcast Feed on Computer in the Classroom:

### Students Viewing the OMO Livestream Broadcast Feed on Phone or Android Tablet in the Classroom:

### Students Viewing the OMO Livestream Broadcast Feed on iPad in the Classroom:

# XV. ClassInX Class Extension

Provided the skin applied to the class's classroom settings has "Allow Teacher to Extend Class Duration" checked, the lead teacher or co-teacher can, within 8 to 3 minutes before class ends, extend class duration by 15 or 30 minutes (multiple extensions are allowed, but total class duration cannot exceed 24 hours; billing follows the extended class duration).

Once the extension pop-up appears, if the teacher hasn't decided yet, they can click "Think About It" — as long as it's still within the allowed extension window, the teacher can later click "Extend" from the notification center in the bottom-left corner of the classroom, then choose to extend by 15 or 30 minutes.

# XVI. AI "Material Search"

When a teacher uses ClassIn X software on a ClassInX 2.0 large display, they can use the AI "Material Search" (i.e., AI image search) agent to enrich their teaching. This agent combines AI semantic understanding, multimodal recognition, and a curated official image library, offering teachers a one-stop, intelligent way to search for and display teaching materials.

**Instant in-class retrieval:** seamlessly find and use image materials while teaching, with direct insertion onto the whiteboard.

**Intelligent search:** quickly locate needed materials via natural language, voice, image, and other multimodal input methods.

**High-quality resource aggregation:** integrates ClassIn's official curated library.

Once a teacher selects a text/image element on the whiteboard, they can click the AI button in the secondary editing tools and choose the "Material Search" agent to use it; if this agent hasn't been added yet, first click the "+" in the AI button, then search for and add it in AgentIn. In the agent's dialog box, click or press and hold to start voice input; you can also click "+" to upload a local image or screenshot — only one image can be sent at a time. Clicking an AI-generated material image inserts it onto the whiteboard, where you can select the image to adjust its position, size, and so on. You can also invoke this agent through the DaKe voice assistant.

Besides using this agent via the secondary editing tools on the whiteboard, you can also add and use it from the AgentIn agent store in the dock in the bottom-right corner of the whiteboard or classroom.

# XVII. AI "Function Graph"

When a teacher uses ClassIn X software on a ClassInX 2.0 large display, they can use the AI "Function Graph" agent, which directly generates function graphs, helping teachers make classroom demonstrations more visual, making abstract function teaching more efficient and easier for students to understand.

Once a teacher selects a function-related text/image element on the whiteboard, they can click the AI button in the secondary editing tools and choose the "Function Graph" agent to use it. The agent's dialog box supports uploading a local image or screenshot — only one image can be sent at a time. Clicking an AI-generated function graph inserts it onto the whiteboard, where you can select the graph to adjust its position, size, and so on. You can also invoke this agent through the DaKe voice assistant.

# XVIII. AI "Chinese Character Stroke Order"

When a teacher uses ClassIn X software on a ClassInX 2.0 large display, they can use the AI "Chinese Character Stroke Order" agent, which accurately recognizes one or more Chinese characters, automatically breaks down the character's stroke structure, and shows the standard writing order, helping teachers teach Chinese character writing more efficiently and visually.

Once a teacher selects a Chinese-character text/image element on the whiteboard, they can click the AI button in the secondary editing tools and choose the "Chinese Character Stroke Order" agent to use it. The agent's dialog box supports uploading a local image or screenshot — only one image can be sent at a time. Clicking an AI-generated stroke-order image inserts it onto the whiteboard, where you can select the image to adjust its position, size, and so on. You can also invoke this agent through the DaKe voice assistant.

# XIX. Agents in the Dock

When a teacher uses ClassInX software on a ClassInX 2.0 large display, the AgentIn agent store in the dock in the bottom-right corner of the whiteboard or classroom supports adding and using agents to assist teaching and enrich teaching scenarios.

When using an agent, the default input method is voice — click or press and hold to start voice input; you can also click "+" to upload a local file or image, making classroom interaction smarter.

If you no longer need a given agent, press and hold its icon in the bottom-right corner to remove it.

# XX. Tool Dial (Radial Menu)

ClassInX's tool dial includes commonly used teaching tools, such as the Pen, Text Tool, Eraser, Select/Move, Click Tool, Screenshot, Save/Share Whiteboard, Scan-to-Upload Image, and Undo/Redo.

If a user doesn't interact with the tool dial for a while, it automatically shrinks to a minimized state; clicking it again restores it to its normal (expanded) state. While expanded, clicking the center of the dial also switches it back to minimized state.

## Time Reminders

### Countdown Timer

The countdown timer offers a countdown feature, letting you set a fixed duration and start the countdown, with a maximum settable duration of one hour (durations over one hour cannot be set). Pausing isn't supported once counting down, and a bell rings when the countdown ends. Once finished, you can reset the countdown, restoring it from 0:00 back to the originally set duration.

| Command | Description | Example Phrasing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Countdown Timer | Opens the countdown timer tool | "Open countdown" |
| Reset Countdown Timer | Resets the countdown timer from its finished 00:00 state back to the initial set duration | "Reset countdown" |
| Start Countdown Timer | Starts the countdown | "Start countdown" |
| Set Countdown to 5 Minutes | Sets the countdown timer to five minutes and starts it | "Give everyone 5 minutes" |
| Close Countdown Timer | Closes the countdown timer tool | "Close countdown" |

### Timer (Stopwatch)

The timer offers a stopwatch feature, counting up from zero. It supports starting, pausing, and — while paused — resuming or resetting. Useful for measuring how long students take to complete a task, or for pacing an activity.

| Command | Description | Example Phrasing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Timer | Opens the timer tool | "Open stopwatch" |
| Start Timer | Starts the stopwatch | "Start timing" |
| Pause Timer | Pauses the stopwatch | "Pause timing" |
| Resume Timer | Resumes the stopwatch | "Resume timing" |
| Reset Timer | Resets the timer to zero | "Reset timing" |
| Close Timer | Closes the timer tool | "Close stopwatch" |

# Distributed Answer Boards

This category of tools is used to organize and run various teaching activities, including interactive exercises, virtual labs, and teaching aids.

### Whiteboard Small Blackboard

Whiteboard Small Blackboard is a window-based small blackboard tool. Once the teacher opens it, they can draw preset content on it — such as practice questions — then distribute it to other online students in the classroom, who can then continue writing their own answers on it. During this time, the teacher can view what students are writing in real time, and recall the small blackboard whenever needed to end the answering period. Once recalled, the teacher can then go over what students wrote. The teacher can also reset the small blackboard to start a new round of activity.

| Command | Description | Example Phrasing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Whiteboard Small Blackboard | Opens the whiteboard small blackboard tool | "Open small blackboard" |
| Distribute Whiteboard Small Blackboard | Distributes the whiteboard small blackboard to students for use | — |
| Recall Whiteboard Small Blackboard | Recalls the whiteboard small blackboard's write permission from students | "Recall small blackboard" |
| Open and Distribute Small Blackboard | Opens the whiteboard small blackboard tool and distributes it to students | — |
| Close Whiteboard Small Blackboard | Closes the whiteboard small blackboard tool | "Close small blackboard" |

### Text Small Blackboard

Text Small Blackboard is a text-editor-style window tool. Once the teacher opens it, they can type text content — such as a question or set of instructions — then click "Distribute" to send it to all or specific students. Once students receive it, they can add and edit their own text answers in the text area. Throughout, the teacher can view every student's answer in real time and offer guidance as students type. Once the activity ends, the teacher can click "Recall" to take back students' access to the text small blackboard, then display and go over student answers in class. The teacher can also reset it to clear the content and start a new round of text interaction.

| Command | Description | Example Phrasing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Text Small Blackboard | Opens the text small blackboard tool | — |
| Distribute Text Small Blackboard | Distributes the text small blackboard to students for use | — |
| Recall Text Small Blackboard | Recalls the text small blackboard's write permission from students | — |
| Close Text Small Blackboard | Closes the text small blackboard tool | — |

### Go Small Blackboard

Go Small Blackboard is a window-based tool designed specifically for teaching Go (the board game). Once the teacher opens it, they'll see a standard 19x19 Go board, and can place black and white stones to demonstrate a specific game position or tactic. The teacher can click "Distribute" to send the current board state to students, who can then continue placing stones to try solving the position or continue playing. The teacher can monitor each student's moves in real time, and use voice guidance or markup features to point out key spots as needed. Once the activity ends, the teacher clicks "Recall" to end student input, then can show the correct move or best tactic, along with commentary and explanation. The teacher can also reset the board to start new content.

| Command | Description | Example Phrasing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Go Small Blackboard | Opens the Go teaching board | — |
| Close Go Small Blackboard | Closes the Go teaching board | — |

### Multi-Directional Browser

Multi-Directional Browser is a window-based tool for web-based teaching. Once the teacher opens it, they can preview and prepare the webpage content needed for the lesson, then click "Distribute" to send the currently viewed webpage to students. Once received, students can browse, search, and interact with that webpage — for example, filling out a web form, reading specified content, or completing an online task. The teacher can monitor students' webpage activity in real time to track their progress. Once the web-based activity ends, the teacher clicks "Recall" to take back students' control of the browser, then can show a reference walkthrough or guide students on proper use of the web resource. The teacher can also switch to a new URL to move on to the next web-based teaching segment.

| Command | Description | Example Phrasing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Multi-Directional Browser | Opens the multi-directional browser tool | — |
| Close Multi-Directional Browser | Closes the multi-directional browser tool | — |

Group Discussion lets you split online students into multiple small groups, each entering their own independent virtual classroom for group activities — groups can't see each other, and only the teacher can enter any group's virtual classroom at any time. Well suited to organizing group discussions, collaborative learning, and competitive activities, boosting classroom participation and interaction efficiency.
