# Getting Started (Batch 1)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Quick Start"
source_title_zh: "极速体验"
```

## Quick Start

## Step 1: Download and Install ClassIn

Go to the ClassIn official website (www.eeo.cn), then go to the Download Center.

Download the installer and follow the on-screen prompts to install ClassIn.

## Step 2: Log Into ClassIn

Enter your registered account to log into ClassIn.

## Step 3: Set Up Your Personal Information

Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner of the software.

Set your avatar and nickname.

## Step 4: Device Check

Before entering the classroom, "check" your network connection and audio/video devices to make sure you can take class normally. Click your avatar in the bottom-left corner of the software, go to Device Check, and follow the on-screen prompts to run the check.

## Step 5: Uploading Courseware

Before class, teachers can go to Space from the left navigation and upload local courseware to Space, making it ready to use during class. (If you don't have any courseware to show, you can skip this step.)

## Step 6: Entering the Classroom

Find the corresponding class session at the top of the software, then click "Start Class" to enter the classroom.

## Step 7: Checking Your Appearance

After clicking "Start Class," you'll enter the screen for adjusting your microphone and camera.

Check your appearance here, then click "Enter Classroom" once you're ready.

## Step 8: Common Classroom Tools

Once the teacher enters the classroom, they can control their camera and microphone in the top-right corner of the classroom, with common teaching tools on the right side. To show or hide student cameras, use the last tool in the right toolbar — "Roster."

Once a student enters the classroom, they can control their camera and microphone in the top-right corner of the classroom; by default, only three tools appear on the right — "Class Notes," "Chat Window," and "Roster."

## Step 9: Watching the Class Playback Video After Class

If cloud recording was enabled for the class session, about half an hour after class ends you can go to Schedule and find that session's playback video by date.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "ClassIn Introduction"
source_title_zh: "ClassIn简介"
```

## ClassIn Introduction

# I. ClassIn Introduction

### 1. Product Concept and Supported Subjects
ClassIn pursues "professionalism" in teaching, dedicated to delivering an outstanding teaching experience for users.

It supports a wide range of subjects, including children's English, language training, professional training, STEAM, and can even be used to teach specialized subjects like horsemanship, dance, and seal engraving.

### 2. Teaching Scenarios
ClassIn can perfectly support many teaching scenarios — one-on-one teaching, small classes, large classes, livestreaming, dual-teacher (domestic and foreign teacher) instruction, and more — meeting the needs of different educational institutions and users.

### 3. Mobile Teaching and Interactivity
ClassIn offers strong mobility — teachers can livestream a lecture from real-world settings like Yellowstone National Park, a planetarium, or an art exhibition, and students can also share and present what they've seen and experienced during an online class.

It supports synchronized face-to-face teaching for up to 16 people, with both teachers and students able to use video windows and audio to interact. Video windows can be freely dragged and resized, suited to small-group learning, discussion, and presentation scenarios.

### 4. Personalized Teaching Tools
ClassIn features an interactive electronic whiteboard, with pre-editing, multi-page scrolling, and unlimited use, supporting simultaneous operation by multiple authorized users.

It comes equipped with dozens of teaching tools — an interactive small blackboard, answer clicker, timer, teacher screen share, video wall, random student picker, and more — making it easy for teachers to run different types of classroom instruction.

### 5. Teaching Courseware Support
ClassIn supports a wide variety of interactive teaching courseware, including animated PPTs, video, audio, Word, and PDF, and also supports combining multiple courseware types in a single lesson, meeting a wider range of teaching needs and enriching lesson content.

### 6. Classroom Atmosphere and Management Features
ClassIn offers classroom management features like raise hand, buzzer, awarding rewards, and sending students on/off stage, helping create a lively, competitive classroom atmosphere that boosts student participation and enthusiasm.

Its real-time learning report system makes it easy for teachers and students to communicate outside of class hours and track teaching quality, helping build a well-rounded learning ecosystem.

### 7. Not Limited by Geography
Against the backdrop of globalization, ClassIn shows remarkable adaptability and convenience. No matter where in the world you are, as long as you have a network connection, you can easily use ClassIn to learn or teach.

For students, this means that whether you're in a bustling international city or a remote, quiet village, on the vast African savanna or in a cold Arctic settlement, as long as you can connect to the network, you can open ClassIn and interact with teachers and classmates from around the world — the door to knowledge opens globally. You can take part in a wide variety of excellent courses, broaden your horizons, and grow together with people from different cultural backgrounds.

For teachers, ClassIn's global nature means teaching is no longer bound by geography. You can enroll students from different countries and regions and share your expertise and experience. Across the bridge of the network, the flame of knowledge spreads, crossing borders and cultural differences to achieve truly borderless education.

# II. What Can ClassIn Do for Teachers?

In modern education, online courses have become an indispensable part of the landscape. Whether an experienced retired teacher or a young educator, many people choose to teach on a well-regarded online education platform. So how can students find the right teacher for themselves more quickly? Online education courses not only bring teachers and students closer together, but also help teachers accomplish a range of important goals.

First, online education platforms give teachers more opportunities and resources. These platforms have a large user base, letting teachers reach far more students. Whether retired or newly starting out, teachers can use these platforms to interact with and teach students from all over the country. This gives teachers a much bigger stage to fully apply their teaching abilities and experience.

Second, online education systems come with a wide range of features that effectively improve teaching outcomes. A mature education platform makes the teaching process smoother and easier. Teachers can present courseware and documents directly through the system, without spending a lot of time writing on a physical board. In addition, teachers can assign homework and exam papers on the platform, and checking that work becomes much more convenient. This lets teachers focus on the content of their teaching, improving overall teaching quality.

In addition, online education systems can support dual-teacher tutoring, further strengthening collaboration among teachers. By setting up a lead teacher and an assisting teacher, the lead teacher's workload can be lightened, giving them more time and energy for lesson prep and improving teaching quality. The dual-teacher model can also foster a positive educational atmosphere among teachers, encouraging mutual growth. For educational institutions, this also helps attract more outstanding teachers and raise the overall standard of education.

In summary, online education platforms bring teachers many benefits. Through these platforms, teachers can reach more students and achieve their teaching goals; the platform's many features improve teaching outcomes and make the teaching process smoother and easier; and the dual-teacher model strengthens collaboration among teachers and raises overall education standards. Online education is therefore not only an important part of modern education, but also a powerful tool for teachers to achieve their personal goals.

# III. What Can ClassIn Do for Students?

**Flexible learning:** online education breaks through the limits of time and space, letting students learn according to their own schedule, no longer bound by fixed class times. This greatly benefits students' daily learning life.

**Improved learning efficiency:** online education platforms offer rich learning resources and diverse learning methods. Students can choose materials and methods suited to their own level and needs. In addition, online teaching offers real-time interaction and personalized tutoring, which helps improve learning efficiency.

**Suited to busy schedules:** for people with busy jobs and irregular study time, traditional offline education often can't meet their needs. The flexibility of online education lets these people learn according to their own schedule, better balancing work and study.

**Access to shared, quality educational resources:** online education can bring together outstanding teaching resources from around the world, giving students access to broader, more diverse learning content. Through online learning platforms, students can also communicate and discuss with other students, sharing learning insights and experiences, enriching the learning process.

In summary, online education offers significant benefits to learners by providing flexible learning options, improving learning efficiency, accommodating busy schedules, and sharing quality educational resources. That said, students still need good self-management skills and study habits to fully take advantage of what online education offers and achieve the results they're hoping for.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Keyboard Shortcuts"
source_title_zh: "快捷键"
```

## Keyboard Shortcuts

# I. Outside the Classroom

Take a screenshot: Ctrl+Alt+C

Open the software: Ctrl+Alt+X

Send a message: Enter

# II. Inside the Classroom

### (1) Shortcut Differences Between Mac and Windows

The "Ctrl" key on Windows corresponds to the "Command" key on Mac.

The "Alt" key on Windows corresponds to the "Option" key on Mac.

The "Page Up/Down" keys on Windows correspond to "Fn+Up/Down" on Mac.

The "Home/End" keys on Windows correspond to "Fn+Left/Right" on Mac.

### (2) General Classroom Shortcuts

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Select All | Ctrl + A |
| Copy | Ctrl + C |
| Paste | Ctrl + V |
| Delete | Ctrl + D / Delete |

### (3) Shortcuts for the Right-Side Toolbar or Radial Tool Dial

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| PPT Animation Click (once selected, you can trigger PPT animation effects) | Ctrl + G |
| Select & Move | Ctrl + M |
| Pen | Ctrl + P |
| Eraser | Ctrl + E |
| Text Tool | Ctrl + T |
| Screenshot | Ctrl + Alt + X |
| Laser Pointer | Ctrl + L |

### (4) Pen and Text Tool Shortcuts

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Bring up a matching shape/color | Alt + corresponding number/letter |
| While drawing a curve | Hold Shift to draw a straight line instead; hold Alt to draw a perfect circle |
| While drawing a straight line | Hold Shift to draw a 45-degree angled line |
| While drawing a circle | Hold Shift to draw a perfect circle |
| While drawing a square | Hold Shift to draw a perfect square |

### (5) Shortcuts Supported Only on the Main Whiteboard (Not Supported in Courseware or Small Blackboard)

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Undo the last action (step back) | Ctrl + Z |
| Redo the last undone action (step forward) | Ctrl + Y |
| One-click clear (clears whiteboard/courseware content, including images) | Ctrl + N |
| Open File feature (load an image or whiteboard) | Ctrl + O |
| Bring up Save/Share Whiteboard | Ctrl + S |
| Jump to the middle page of the whiteboard | Ctrl + Shift + O |
| Previous page | Page Up |
| Next page | Page Down |
| Return to first page | Home |
| Turn to last page | End |
| Move selected content | Left/Right/Up/Down |

### (6) Shortcuts Supported Only on the Local Whiteboard and in the Prep Room (Not Supported in the Classroom)

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Move up one layer | Ctrl + Shift + Page Up |
| Move down one layer | Ctrl + Shift + Page Down |
| Move to top layer | Ctrl + Shift + Home |
| Move to bottom layer | Ctrl + Shift + End |

Note: holding Ctrl and left-clicking content on the whiteboard also lets you adjust layer settings from the top-right corner of the selected content.

### (7) Shortcuts for Operating Classroom Cameras

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Move a camera from the on-stage seats area onto the whiteboard (keeping the same size) | Ctrl + drag the camera with the left mouse button |
| Drag a camera into a window layout | Shift + drag the camera with the left mouse button |

### (8) Shortcuts Available While a PPT/Audio Courseware/Video Courseware Is Open

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Play/advance one step | Spacebar |

### (9) Shortcuts Available While a PDF/Word Courseware Is Open

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Turn to next page | Spacebar |

### (10) Other Classroom-Affecting Shortcuts

| Function | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Close the classroom | Alt + F4 |
| Adjust volume | Your system's volume keys |

# Glossary of Terms

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Glossary of Terms"
source_title_zh: "名词注释"
```

## Glossary of Terms

| ClassIn Term | Explanation |
| --- | --- |
| IM | Short for Instant Messaging area. The main interface you land on after logging into ClassIn is the IM interface, which includes modules like your personal avatar, message list, to-dos, contacts, space, schedule, whiteboard, and settings. |
| Personal Avatar | Located in the top-left corner of the ClassIn main interface; click it to set your personal information, including avatar, name, contact card sharing, QR code sharing, phone number binding, email binding, password change, gender, date of birth, region, and personal signature. |
| Message List | A module in the ClassIn main interface for receiving messages from classes and friends. Computer users access it via the left navigation bar; phone and tablet users access it via the bottom navigation bar. In this list, you can receive messages from classes and friends, and pin, mute, or delete conversations. |
| Contacts | Users can go to the "Contacts" module via the left navigation bar (on computer) or bottom navigation bar (on phone/tablet) to add friends, view class and friend lists, handle friend requests, and view/manage friend details. |
| Authorized Resources | Public teaching resources — such as courseware and exam papers — that a school grants specific teachers access to use. Through authorization, teachers can use standardized teaching resources, ensuring consistency and quality in teaching content. |
| On Stage | In the classroom, the position where a teacher invites a student to show their camera using the "Roster" tool is called being "on stage." An on-stage student can communicate via voice with the teacher and other on-stage students, and every classroom member can see their camera feed. |
| Go On Stage | The action of a teacher inviting a student to show their camera "on stage" via the "Roster" tool. |
| Go Off Stage / Return Off Stage | When a teacher stops a student from showing their camera, this is called having them "return off stage." |
| Off Stage | Classroom members not showing their camera "on stage" are considered to be listening from "off stage." |
| Authorization | The permission a teacher grants a student, via the "Roster" tool, to use classroom tools such as the pen, select/move tool, click tool, eraser, text input tool, screenshot tool, and cloud drive. |
| Blank | When a user opens a certain ClassIn screen and nothing displays in it, this is called "blank." Common cases include a blank screen after opening assignments, quizzes, the cloud drive, or courseware. |
| White Screen | When a user opens a certain ClassIn screen and nothing displays in it, this is called a "white screen." Common cases are similar to "blank." |
| Black Screen | When a user opens a certain ClassIn screen and nothing displays except a solid black page, this is called a "black screen." Common cases include a black screen after opening the cloud drive or courseware. |
| Scheduling a Class Session | The user clicks "Create Class" on the ClassIn main interface, goes into the "Course" tab within the newly created class, clicks "New," and selects "Class Session" to schedule it. |
| Starting a Class Session | The user clicks "Create Class" on the ClassIn main interface, goes into the "Course" tab within the newly created class, clicks "New," and selects "Class Session" to start it. |
| Creating a Class Session | The user clicks "Create Class" on the ClassIn main interface, goes into the "Course" tab within the newly created class, clicks "New," and selects "Class Session" to create it. |
| Video Wall | A teaching tool that lets the teacher monitor every student's camera feed in the class in real time, making it easy to observe how students are doing during class. If a student hasn't turned on their camera, the teacher will only see their video placeholder. |
| Online Classroom, Local Classroom, Temporary Classroom | **Local Classroom:** the "Whiteboard" feature on the ClassIn main interface, for users to get familiar with classroom features and create whiteboard content, with no time limit.<br>**Online Classroom:** the "class session" in ClassIn, where teachers and students take class.<br>**Temporary Classroom:** can be created anytime by teachers and students, free to use. |
| Learning Activity | Any activity within a class that's for teaching purposes and content, including class sessions, recorded courses, assignments, quizzes, check-ins, answer sheets, discussions, and learning materials. |
| Multi-Class Quiz | When creating a quiz, the teacher checks multiple classes under the "Class" field in the quiz settings, letting students from every selected class take part in that quiz. |
| Echo | When a classroom speaker's sound gets picked up by the microphone and played back into the classroom, causing an echo. This is usually caused by the microphone being too close to the speaker. |
| Focus Mode | A feature that helps improve students' focus during class. Once enabled, a computer user's classroom interface stays full-screen and can't be switched away from; a phone or tablet user will automatically exit the classroom if ClassIn is sent to the background. |
| Fix Hardware Driver | A hardware-fix feature in ClassIn used to resolve issues with devices like the microphone, speaker, and camera. |
| EDB | ClassIn's proprietary electronic whiteboard file format, used to save whiteboard content a teacher creates in the classroom, making it easy to reuse and share later. |
| Whiteboard | **Whiteboard feature on the main interface:** refers to the local classroom, for teachers and students to get familiar with classroom features.<br>**Whiteboard within the classroom:** the interactive tool teachers and students use during class.<br>**Small Blackboard tool in the classroom toolbox:** used for answering and interacting during the teaching process. |
| Large Display All-in-One | A device that integrates a display screen and a computer host together, typically used for presentations, demonstrations, and information display. |
| Large Display All-in-One vs. Large Display Mode | **Large Display All-in-One:** the device that integrates a display screen and a computer host.<br>**Large Display Mode:** the control interface mode used in the ClassIn classroom. |
| Course | **The "Course" module within a class in the software:** where you can add unit topics and learning activities.<br>**The "Course" in the Backend Management System:** has the same meaning as "class" in the software. |
| Backend Management System | ClassIn's management platform, where academic teachers can create courses and class sessions, manage teachers and students, monitor classroom data, and configure personalized settings, among other things. |
| Time Units | Half an hour = 30 minutes; one hour = 60 minutes. |
| Data Units | 1GB = 1024MB, 1MB = 1024KB, 1KB = 1024 bytes. |
| Phone | A portable electronic communication device supporting calls, texts, internet access, and more, typically running iOS, Android, or HarmonyOS. |
| Tablet | A portable electronic device using a touchscreen and virtual keyboard, typically running iOS, Android, or HarmonyOS. |
| Class-Taking Client | Refers to the ClassIn client (app). |
| Web Playback | The web version of a class playback video, viewable via a shared link starting half an hour after class ends; requires cloud recording to be enabled. |
| Teaching Assistant | Refers to the co-teacher. |
| Classroom | "Classroom" refers to any location where a teaching activity takes place, including: the formal class session, a class's temporary classroom, a friend's temporary classroom, and the local classroom. |
| Space | Space, also known as the cloud drive, refers to a feature that provides online storage. Using Space, users can upload files from a local device to the cloud, enabling remote storage and access to files. Users just need to connect any device to the internet, log into ClassIn, and go to the Space tab to view, share, download, or edit their files online.<br><br>Space's advantage lies in its high reliability and excellent cross-device compatibility. User file data is stored on cloud servers, which not only ensures data integrity and security, but also lets users conveniently access and manage files remotely from any location on any device. In addition, Space offers a variety of online editing tools, letting users edit and process files directly online without downloading local editing software. In short, Space is an efficient, convenient, and secure way to store and manage files online, offering users great convenience and peace of mind.<br><br>In ClassIn, you can reach "Space" from two different locations: one is via the navigation bar on the ClassIn main interface, and the other is via the "Space" tool within the classroom's teaching tools — data in "Space" is shared and synced between both entry points. Space's main function is to give users a place to store courseware online. Within Space, users can use authorized courseware from the "Resource Center" and "Authorized Resources," and can also build custom exam papers using the "ClassIn Question Bank" and "ClassIn Exam Paper Library." Users can also directly access TeacherIn from Space. |
| Client | Refers to the ClassIn client (app). |
| 1v1 | "1v1" refers to the number of people whose camera feed is shown simultaneously in the classroom — that is, 1 teacher and 1 student. The ClassIn platform supports various on-stage headcount configurations, including 1v1, 1v2, 1v3, 1v4, 1v5, 1v6, 1v7, 1v8, 1v9, 1v10, 1v11, 1v12, 1v13, 1v14, and 1v15. |

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: getting-started-03_glossary.md -->

## [Other] Hardware Usage Issues

# 1. Re-Pairing the Page-Turner Remote and Receiver

**Symptom:** the page-turner remote isn't working and needs to be re-paired with its receiver.

**Solution:** to pair, press and hold Button 1, then quickly press Button 2 five times in a row; the indicator light will start blinking, entering pairing mode. Release Button 1 to finish pairing.

# 2. The Page-Turner Remote's Range Is Too Short

**Symptom:** the page-turner remote's range is too short, making it inconvenient to use.

**Solution:** plug the receiver into a USB port on the side of the large display, as close as possible, to ensure there's nothing blocking the receiver.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "[Handwriting Tablet] Hardware Usage Issues"
source_title_zh: "【手写板】硬件使用问题"
```

## [Handwriting Tablet] Hardware Usage Issues

# 1. Writing Behaves Abnormally

**Symptom:** the handwriting tablet doesn't write correctly.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

**Confirm the driver is installed:** make sure the ClassInTablet driver is correctly installed. Driver download: https://www.eeo.cn/cn/download (once installed, please make sure the driver keeps running minimized in the background — don't close it.)

**Check for driver conflicts:** confirm no other handwriting tablet drivers are installed on your computer, such as Gaomon or Wacom. If any are installed, please uninstall them to avoid conflicts.

**Check the cable:** please use the original cable or a compatible Huawei phone cable to connect (a charging-only cable won't work).

# 2. Replacing the Stylus Nib

**Symptom:** the stylus's nib is significantly worn down, affecting normal use, and needs to be replaced.

**Solution:** try the method shown in the image below to resolve this.

# 3. Driver Shows "Not Connected"

**Symptom:** the handwriting tablet's driver shows "not connected."

Try connecting through a different USB port.

Try using a different USB cable to connect.

If you're on a Mac, try connecting through a different USB hub/dock.

# 4. Laggy Writing

**Symptom:** the handwriting tablet lags while writing.

**Solution:** please download and install 360 Driver Master, and use it to update your graphics driver, to improve the handwriting tablet's writing experience.

# 5. Writing Registers Without Touching the Tablet

**Symptom:** the stylus registers writing even without touching the tablet.

**Solution:** this is usually caused by a faulty stylus — we recommend contacting ClassIn after-sales support to replace it with a new one.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "[Wireless Microphone] Hardware Usage Issues"
source_title_zh: "【无线麦克风】硬件使用问题"
```

## [Wireless Microphone] Hardware Usage Issues

# 1. The Charging Case Won't Charge (Mammoth LARK150)

**Symptom:** the Mammoth LARK150 wireless microphone's ("little bee") charging case won't charge.

**Solution:** follow these steps to reset the device.

Connect the charging case to a charger.

Using a pin, press and hold the reset pinhole on the charging case, microphone, and receiver for 5 seconds each.

Remove the microphone and receiver from the charging case, and charge the case alone for 30 minutes.

After 30 minutes, put the microphone and receiver back into the charging case — you should now see the battery level displayed, and the charging case should charge normally again.

# 2. How Do I Wire It Up? (Mammoth LARK150, M1, Rode)

**Symptom:** microphone cable connection issue.

**Solution:** follow these steps.

**Connecting a wireless microphone to a large display all-in-one device (using a TRS-to-TRS cable):**

One end connects to the wireless microphone ("little bee").

The other end connects to the red microphone audio jack on the large display's OPS host.

**Connecting a wireless microphone to a laptop (using a TRS-to-TRRS cable):**

The TRS end connects to the wireless microphone ("little bee").

The TRRS end connects to the laptop's 3.5mm audio jack.

**Connecting a wireless microphone to a phone or tablet (using a TRS-to-USB-C cable):**

The other end connects to the phone or tablet's USB-C port.

**Connecting a wireless microphone to a USB sound card (using a TRS-to-TRS cable):**

The other end connects to the red microphone audio jack on the USB sound card.

# 3. Indicator Light Status (Mammoth M1)

| Device State | Indicator Light Status |
| --- | --- |
| Normal standby | Solid blue |
| Video stream on | Solid green |
| Tracking on | Solid green (low brightness) |
| Whiteboard mode | Solid yellow |
| Gesture recognized successfully | Blue, fast blink |
| Gesture unavailable | Orange, fast blink |
| Upgrade mode | Solid white |
| Firmware updating | Blue, slow blink |
| Fault | Solid red |
| Privacy standby | Off |

For more information, visit: https://www.insta360.com/support/supportdetail?name=link

# 4. Sound Is Hard to Hear Clearly (Mammoth LARK150, Mammoth M1, Rode)

**Symptom:** when using the Mammoth LARK150, Mammoth M1, or Rode wireless microphone ("little bee"), the sound is too quiet and hard to hear clearly.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

**Adjust the device's own volume:** first, check and raise the volume setting on the wireless microphone device itself. Make sure the device volume is at an appropriate level.

**Adjust the ClassIn classroom microphone volume:** once in the ClassIn classroom, find the microphone volume setting and raise it appropriately, to make sure the sound is clearly audible.

**Turn off ClassIn classroom background noise reduction:** in the ClassIn classroom, disable background noise reduction. This can help boost the microphone's volume and audio quality, making the sound clearer.

# 5. Battery Life

**Symptom:** wanting to know the battery life of the Mammoth M1's transmitter, receiver, and charging case.

**Answer:**

**Mammoth M1 wireless microphone:**

Both the transmitter and receiver can run continuously for 8 hours on a full charge.

The included charging case can fully recharge the transmitter and receiver twice each, supporting extended use.

**Mammoth LARK150 wireless microphone:**

The transmitter runs continuously for 4 hours on a full charge.

The receiver runs continuously for 7 hours on a full charge.

The charging case, once fully charged, can recharge two transmitters and one receiver 2.5 times.

Note: as with a phone, battery life may shorten in cold environments. In addition, different usage distances can also affect the transmitter's and receiver's battery life.

# 6. Three Working Modes (Mammoth LARK150)

Press and hold the button on the left side of the Mammoth LARK150 receiver to cycle through three working modes: mono mode, stereo mode, and safety-track mode.

# 7. What Do the Three Working Modes Do? (Mammoth LARK150)

The Mammoth LARK150 has three working modes, each with the following effect:

**Stereo mode:** when audio is captured using two microphones (MIC1 and MIC2), the receiver outputs MIC1's audio to the left channel and MIC2's audio to the right channel. This way, users can clearly distinguish the sound captured by each of the two microphones.

**Mono mode:** in this mode, the audio captured by both microphones (MIC1 and MIC2) is merged, and the receiver outputs the merged audio to both the left and right channels. This way, the left and right channel content is identical, forming mono audio.

**Safety-track mode:** in this mode, the receiver merges the audio from MIC1 and MIC2, but the left and right channel volumes differ. The left channel plays at normal volume, while the right channel plays 6dB quieter than the left. This provides a backup audio track during recording, protecting against audio distortion caused by excessive volume, ensuring both audio quality and user privacy are protected.

# 8. What's the Point of Safety-Track Mode?

During live recording, you may run into a sudden spike in volume, and audio that's too loud can distort or ruin the recording file. To handle this, you can use the Mammoth LARK150's safety-track mode. This mode generates two-channel audio while recording — the left channel records audio at normal volume, while the right channel records audio at a lower volume. This way, even if the left channel's audio clips or distorts, the right channel's audio can still serve as a backup, ensuring your recording material isn't rendered completely unusable.

# 9. Pairing the Transmitter and Receiver

**Enter transmitter pairing mode:** press and hold the yellow button on the transmitter for about 3 seconds, until the blue indicator light blinks rapidly.

**Enter receiver pairing mode:** press and hold the "+" button on the receiver for about 3 seconds, until the blue indicator light blinks rapidly.

**Wait for pairing to finish:** once the transmitter's and receiver's blue indicator lights turn solid, pairing has succeeded.

**Mammoth LARK150 wireless microphone:**

To pair the Mammoth LARK150, simply place the transmitter and receiver into the charging case and power it on — they'll pair automatically, with no extra steps needed.

# 10. How to Lock/Unlock the Frequency on a WP1 Wireless Microphone

**Symptom:** needing to change the frequency lock status on a WP1 microphone.

**Answer:** please follow these steps.

**Locking the handheld mic:**

Once the handheld mic and receiver are paired, on the handheld unit, press and release "Page Up" + "Page Down" together — the screen will show the channel blinking; then press and release "Volume Up" to complete the operation. Once locked successfully, a small lock icon appears at the top of the screen.

**Unlocking the handheld mic:**

Press and release "Page Up" + "Page Down" together — the screen will show the channel blinking; then press and release "Volume Down" to complete the operation.

**Locking the receiver:**

Once the receiver automatically pairs with the handheld mic, flip all three "channel" DIP switches on the receiver to the ON position to complete the lock.

**Unlocking the receiver:**

Adjust the receiver's "channel" DIP switches so that not all three are in the ON position.

Note: frequency lock settings require both the handheld mic and receiver to be set to frequency lock mode — otherwise they cannot link and pair.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "[PTZ Camera] Hardware Usage Issues"
source_title_zh: "【云台相机】硬件使用问题"
```

## [PTZ Camera] Hardware Usage Issues

# 1. Blurry Camera Image

**Symptom:** once the computer is connected to the camera, the displayed camera image is blurry.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

Check whether the lens has dust or another obstruction, and clean it if so.

Adjust the focus using the remote control or the camera software.

Use the remote control or the camera's companion software to adjust the camera's focus. We recommend not checking image sharpness through the ClassIn whiteboard interface, since the image may be compressed there. Please use ClassIn's Auxiliary Camera feature, or Windows' built-in Camera app, to check the camera's true sharpness.

Install the iSmart CMS software on your computer, and adjust image sharpness using the focus feature (Focus +/-).

# 2. Camera Image Has Ripple/Flicker Artifacts

**Symptom:** once a computer or large display all-in-one device is connected to the camera, the displayed camera image shows a rippling/flickering pattern.

**Using the remote control:**

Go into the menu via the remote.

Select "Image" > "Exposure" > "Anti-Flicker" in sequence.

Change the anti-flicker parameter to 50Hz or 60Hz.

**Regarding the display type:**

If the large display isn't a ClassInX-brand display, and is a dot-matrix screen or uses PWM (pulse-width modulation) dimming, the ripple/flicker effect may not be fully eliminated.

Try increasing screen brightness or adjusting the camera's exposure settings to improve the ripple/flicker effect.

# 3. Disabling Person Tracking (CAM35/CAM36)

**Symptom:** once the computer or large display all-in-one device is connected to the camera, you need to disable person tracking.

Install the iSmart CMS software on your computer, and make sure the camera and computer are connected to the same local network.

Open iSmart CMS, click "Online Devices," then click "Start Search" to scan for camera devices on the local network, as shown below.

In the search results, select the camera device whose settings you want to change, then click "Add to Management" to make it appear in the "Managed Devices" list, as shown below.

Go into "Main Preview," select the corresponding camera device, and configure tracking settings, as shown below.

Click "Parameter Settings," go into the "Basic 2" settings screen. There, change "Default State on Power-On" to "No Tracking," then click "Save" to finish, as shown below.

# 4. Setting Preset Positions

**Symptom:** once the camera is installed, you need to set preset positions to save the camera's position, focus, and image parameters in advance.

**Solution:** try the method below to resolve this.

**CAM34 camera:**

Setting a preset position: press a number key, then press the "Set Preset" key.

Recalling a preset position: press the corresponding number key + "CALL" key.

Clearing a preset position: press the corresponding number key + "CLEAR" key.

**CAM37 camera:**

Setting a preset position: press a number key, then press the "SET" key.

**P1 camera:**

Setting a preset position: press and hold a number key until the camera's indicator light blinks once, and the setting is complete.

# 5. Power Indicator Light Doesn't Turn On After Powering Up

**Symptom:** after the camera is powered on, the power indicator light doesn't turn on.

**Solution:** if the camera shows no response after powering up, and the power indicator light doesn't turn on, there may be a hardware fault — please contact ClassIn hardware after-sales support for repair or replacement.

# 6. Resetting the Preset Position

**Symptom:** needing to adjust the camera's preset position.

**Solution:** try either of the following methods to resolve this.

Press the corresponding number key directly to move the camera back to its preset position.

First press the corresponding number key, then press the CALL key, to move the camera back to its preset position.

# 7. No Image Displayed (CAM34)

**Symptom:** the CAM34 camera's blue POWER light and green STANDBY light are both on at the same time, but no image is displayed.

**Solution:** when the CAM34 camera's blue POWER light and green STANDBY light are both on, it means the camera is still starting up. Please wait patiently for about 20 seconds until only the blue POWER light stays on, indicating the camera has finished starting up. Only then will the image display normally.

# 8. Glitchy/Garbled Image (CAM37)

**Symptom:** the CAM37 camera's image appears glitchy or garbled.

First, check what type of cable connects the camera to the computer — usually an HDMI or SDI cable.

If you're using an HDMI or SDI cable, try replacing it with a new one.

If the issue persists after replacing the cable, we recommend connecting using the camera's included Mini USB cable instead.

# 9. No Image Displayed (CAM37)

**Symptom:** no image displays after connecting the CAM37 camera.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

**Check the cable:** make sure the cable between the CAM37 camera and the computer is correctly and securely connected. Confirm the cable isn't damaged or loose.

**Confirm the power connection:** make sure the CAM37 camera's power is correctly connected, and its power indicator light is on normally.

**Try restarting:** use the power button on the remote control to try restarting the camera.

# 10. No Image Displayed (CAMP1)

**Symptom:** the CAMP1 camera's green light and red light are both on at the same time, but no image is displayed.

**Solution:** when the CAMP1 camera's green light and red light are both on, it means the camera is still starting up. Please wait patiently for about 20 seconds until the red light turns off, indicating the camera has finished starting up. Only then will the image display normally.

# 11. Disabling Auto-Zoom

**Symptom:** needing to disable the camera's auto-zoom feature.

Find the camera's remote control.

Press the "Manual" button on the remote.

# 12. Adjusting Camera Brightness (CAM34)

**Symptom:** needing to adjust the camera's image brightness.

**Solution:** follow these steps to adjust the CAM34 camera's brightness.

Press the "Menu" button on the CAM34 camera's remote control.

The camera's settings screen will pop up on your computer screen.

In the settings screen, select and go into the "Exposure" section.

Within "Exposure," find and adjust the "Brightness Compensation" option, until you reach a satisfying brightness level.

# 13. Adjusting Camera Focus

**Symptom:** needing to adjust the camera's focus value.

Use the "-" or "+" key on the remote control to adjust the focus.

# 13. USB Camera Not Recognized

**Symptom:** after installing the camera, the large display can't recognize this hardware.

Unplug and re-plug the USB connector on the computer side.

Restart the camera — ideally by cutting power and restarting it.

Open your computer's Device Manager, uninstall "Unknown USB Device," then reload/reinstall it.

If none of the above resolves it, consider whether the USB cable itself is faulty.

**Symptom:** needing to change tablet mode.

**Solution:** follow these steps.

## [Large Display All-in-One] Power/Signal Issues

# 1. No Signal After Power-On, Cannot Reach the Windows Desktop

**Symptom:** after powering on the large display all-in-one device, the screen keeps showing "Connecting Signal," "No Signal," or "NO SIGNAL," and it never reaches the Windows desktop.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

**Confirm the OPS host is receiving power normally:**

Check the "POWER" indicator light on the OPS host on the back of the all-in-one device: if the "POWER" light is on, the computer is powered on and running normally; if the "POWER" light is off, click the POWER button below to power it on (as shown in the image).

**Try switching the OPS input:**

Click the power button on the right side of the all-in-one device, select the signal source, and switch it to the built-in computer.

**Restart the OPS host:**

Find the POWER button on the OPS host on the back of the all-in-one device.

Press and hold the POWER button until the OPS host fully shuts down.

Press the POWER button again to restart the OPS host.

# 2. System Shows a Blue Screen

**Symptom:** unable to enter Windows — the screen shows a blue-screen error (as shown in the image).

**Solution:** please try the following steps.

Restart the system to see if that resolves it.

Click the power button on the right side to enter the Android menu.

Tap Settings, then tap About This Device.

Select Windows System Restore.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->

```yaml
title: "[Large Display All-in-One] Audio/Video Issues"
source_title_zh: "【大屏一体机】音视频问题"
```

## [Large Display All-in-One] Audio/Video Issues

# 1. No Sound from the Large Display All-in-One

**Symptom:** while using the large display all-in-one device, no sound can be heard at all.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

Check whether the sound setting in the all-in-one device's Android menu has been disabled.

**Check whether Windows system volume is muted:**

Click the "arrow" icon in the bottom-right corner of the Windows desktop.

Click the "speaker" icon.

Drag left or right to adjust the system volume (as shown in the image).

**Check whether the "86 (XX) Monitor" device is disabled in Windows sound settings:**

Right-click the "speaker" icon and select "Sounds."

Go to the "Playback" tab.

If the "86 Monitor" device is disabled, right-click it and select "Enable."

Click "OK" below (as shown in the image).

If none of the above resolves it, we recommend restarting the large display all-in-one device and reinstalling the audio driver using 360 Driver Master or Driver Genius.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "[Large Display All-in-One] Display Issues"
source_title_zh: "【大屏一体机】显示问题"
```

## [Large Display All-in-One] Display Issues

# 1. Adjusting Screen Brightness

**Symptom:** while using the large display all-in-one device, the screen brightness isn't right.

**Solution:** please follow these steps to adjust the screen brightness.

Click the all-in-one device's power button.

In the Android pop-up, manually adjust the backlight brightness.

# 2. The Screen Shows Jumpy/Rippling Touch Points

**Symptom:** while using the large display all-in-one device, the touchscreen shows jumpy or rippling touch points (as shown in the image).

**Solution:** this is caused by the display's screen bulging outward, which disrupts the touch module's signal. You can refer to the fix method below.

Try gently pressing the middle of the screen glass with your fist several times, to try to flatten the screen back out.

If possible, try slightly propping up the bottom of the all-in-one device so the screen tilts up at an angle — this may help restore normal touch function.

If the above doesn't resolve the issue, we recommend contacting ClassIn after-sales support for repair.

# 3. The Screen Shows Lines or Flickering

**Symptom:** the large display all-in-one device's screen shows lines or a flickering image (as shown in the image).

**Solution:** this issue is usually caused by a fault in the screen's OC (driver circuit) or TCON (timing control circuit) board. We recommend contacting ClassIn after-sales support for factory repair.

# 4. The All-in-One Screen Flickers

**Symptom:** after powering on, the screen flickers and cannot be used normally.

**Solution:** download 360 Driver Master, Driver Genius, or a similar tool to update your graphics driver.

# 5. The All-in-One Screen Freezes/Goes Black

**Symptom:** after powering on, the all-in-one device stays frozen on the ClassIn logo screen, or stays on a black screen and never reaches the system.

**Solution:** this issue is most likely a power board or motherboard fault — we recommend contacting ClassIn after-sales support for repair.

```yaml
title: "[Large Display All-in-One] Cable Connection and Screen Projection Issues"
source_title_zh: "【大屏一体机】线路连接及投屏问题"
```

## [Large Display All-in-One] Cable Connection and Screen Projection Issues

# 1. Wireless Screen Projection on the Large Display All-in-One

**Symptom:** while using the large display all-in-one device, you need wireless screen projection.

**Solution:** try the following approach.

**Using Android screen projection:**

Click the power button on the large display.

An Android menu will pop up — select "Screen Projection."

Follow the on-screen prompts to connect to the Wi-Fi network and enter the password to start projecting; the password is: 88887777.

**Using the ClassIn X software to project:**

On the large display, open ClassIn X software, log into your account, then select "ClassIn Screen Projection."

On your computer, log into the ClassIn software, select "Screen Projection" on the left, choose the corresponding Wi-Fi network, and enter the projection code to start projecting.

# 2. Wired Screen Projection on the Large Display All-in-One

Please see below for the different connection methods:

Connect your laptop to the large display all-in-one device using an HDMI cable (the all-in-one device has three HDMI input ports, located on the front panel and as HDMI1/HDMI2 on the rear-left panel — any of them can be used).

Connect your laptop to the large display all-in-one device using a USB A-B touch cable (the all-in-one device has two touch ports, on the front panel and the rear-left panel as TOUCH-USB — either can be used).

If no image displays, try switching to a different HDMI port on the all-in-one device.

When connecting the large display and laptop using the wired methods above, please make sure to connect the microphone and camera to the laptop, not the large display all-in-one device.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "[Large Display All-in-One] Touch Input and Handwriting Issues"
source_title_zh: "【大屏一体机】输入触控手写问题"
```

## [Large Display All-in-One] Touch Input and Handwriting Issues

# 1. On-Screen Keyboard Doesn't Appear

**Symptom:** while using the all-in-one device, tapping the "keyboard" icon in the bottom-right corner of the system desktop doesn't bring up the on-screen keyboard, making it impossible to type using it.

**Solution:** follow these steps.

Click the "Windows" icon in the bottom-left corner of the desktop to open "Settings."

In "Settings," select "Devices."

Select "Typing," then find and enable "Show the touch keyboard when not in tablet mode and there's no keyboard attached" (if it's already enabled by default, try turning it off, back on, and restarting the computer).

# 2. Laggy Writing

**Symptom:** while recording class with ClassIn on the large display all-in-one device, using the classroom's pen tool to write on the whiteboard feels laggy.

**Solution:** try any of the following methods to resolve this.

**Adjust resolution and display scale:**

Set the all-in-one device's Windows desktop resolution to 1920x1080.

Set the display scale to 150%.

**Clear the ClassIn cache:**

Open the ClassIn main interface, click Settings in the bottom-left corner.

Go into "System Settings."

Click "Clear Cache."

```yaml
title: "TI Store Tutorial"

```

## TI Store Tutorial

# I. Activating the TI Store Service

Product management and the TI Store are currently value-added services, available only to enterprise customers — please contact your dedicated account manager to enable them.

# II. Adding / Listing / Delisting Products in the Backend

Academic teachers in the backend can add products through the class's Product Management feature.

During class, all teachers, teaching assistants, and backend academic staff can only have 1 product listed at a time — if someone lists a new product, the previously listed one is automatically taken down from the live stream.

The backend's "livestream listing" and "playback listing" settings can be turned on or off at any time, but the livestream listing setting only takes effect during the livestream, and the playback listing only takes effect during the post-class playback period.

You can select existing products from the product catalog — each class session supports selecting up to 6 products at once.

# III. Listing / Delisting a Product in the Classroom

During a livestream, teachers or teaching assistants can go to "Teaching Tools → TI Store" in the ClassIn livestream classroom, or academic teachers can go to "Class Product Management Settings" in the backend, to set a product's status to "Live for Sale," letting students purchase it directly while watching the livestream.

# IV. Students Purchasing a Product

While watching a livestream or playback, students can purchase any product that's currently set to "Live for Sale" or "Playback for Sale."

## System Maintenance Notice

Dear customer, in order to provide better products and services, the system will be regularly maintained.

During the maintenance, some service would be unavailable. Please make sure the time of the lessons (include 20 minutes before and 20 minutes after the lesson), do not overlap with the following system regular maintenance time.

If your institution opens the API service, all the API requests will receive status code 901 during the maintenance period.

In some special conditions, the system maintenance would happen in other time. If the system is unavailable outside of the above regular time, please contact customer service for more details.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.

Note: below are the maintenance dates for 2022 and 2023.

2022 maintenance schedule:
- August 9, 00:31–05:29

2023 maintenance schedule:

## Temporarily Exiting Antivirus/Security Software

## Introduction

Why exit security software? Most antivirus and security software on the market today uses a certain amount of memory while running, and some security software may also throttle your computer's network connection, causing it to slow down. For users with lower-performance computers or unstable network connections, temporarily exiting security software can improve your computer's speed and network stability.

## Sunlogin Usage Guide

## I. Windows Computer

1.1 In your browser, go to https://sunlogin.oray.com/download, click Personal Edition, select Windows, and download the "Full 64-bit Version."

1.2 Once it's running, click the location shown to display the "local verification code," then provide the "local identification code" and "local verification code" to support staff.

## II. Mac Computer

2.1 In your browser, go to https://sunlogin.oray.com/download, click Personal Edition, select macOS, click "Download Now" below. You can check the download progress in the top-right corner of your browser; once done, double-click the installer.

2.2 In the window that pops up, double-click the installer, then click "Continue" in the window that appears and follow the steps to install.

2.3 Once installation is complete, open Sunlogin and click the exclamation mark next to "Allow Control of This Device" at the top.

2.4 In the access permission settings on the right, enable "Screen Recording" and "Accessibility." A Security & Privacy settings window will automatically pop up on the left — check the box for Sunlogin under both Accessibility and Screen Recording.

2.5 Provide the "local identification code" and "local verification code" to support staff.

```yaml
title: "NFC Setup Tutorial"
source_title_zh: "NFC操作教程"
```

## NFC Setup Tutorial

# Configuring Institution Information

Log into the X edition, click "Avatar → Settings," then click "Advanced Settings → Edit Registration Info."

2. Search for the corresponding institution name, select the matching institution, and confirm.

For school/institution information, you can only select an institution where the current account is set as either the primary account or a sub-account. In other words, if a customer success rep needs to act on a customer's behalf, they must first be added as a sub-account under that customer's account before they can see and select it.

Note: the image shown is a sample institution — select it and save.

3. Tap the NFC card or device against the side of the large display or the card reader, and the system will automatically show a pre-binding verification prompt.

4. Once you verify via QR code scan or password, a binding page appears. Keep the card against the reader without moving it and wait for the "binding successful" message; once bound, you can tap the card to log in or out.

# Frequently Asked Questions

1. Nothing happens after tapping the card

Check whether the institution information from step one has been set — institution information must be configured before binding a third-party NFC card.

Confirm you're using the latest version of the software.

If both of the above are fine, contact your hardware support colleague to confirm the card reader is working properly.

2. Which devices are supported?

In theory, any card or electronic device with an NFC chip should work.

3. After binding via phone NFC, it still prompts for QR-code binding verification

Phone NFC needs to be bound to a virtual card (transit card, bank card, electronic access card) to serve as the bound card. On Android, you can generally create a blank virtual card yourself.

If no card is bound, the phone's NFC module automatically generates a new temporary virtual card number each time, which is why it keeps prompting you to bind every time.

```yaml
title: "Cookie Policy"
source_title_zh: "Cookie政策"
```

## Cookie Policy

Introduction

Together with our User Agreement and Privacy Policy, this policy provides you with information about the cookies and other similar technologies used across all our websites. We review this policy from time to time to ensure it stays up to date.

If we make changes, we'll publish the latest version of the policy here. For significant changes, we'll notify you either the next time you visit our services or through other communication channels.

I. What are cookies, and why do we use them?

To ensure ClassIn runs properly, we store small text files called cookies on your computer or mobile device. A cookie typically contains an identifier, the site name, and some numbers and characters.

The information cookies collect lets us:

Tailor our websites to your individual needs.

Remember notifications already shown to you, so we don't show them again.

Improve and update our websites based on how you use them.

Note: we generally do not use cookies to identify who you are.

II. What kinds of cookies do we use?

We use the following categories of cookies:

Category 1: login cookies

Login cookies help us remember data such as your username, so you don't have to re-enter it on your next visit. All information these cookies collect is anonymous, and they cannot track your browsing activity on other websites.

Category 2: notification cookies

Notification cookies help us remember your setting choices, so you don't need to set them again on your next visit, and we won't repeat notifications you've already seen.

Category 3: functional cookies

Functional cookies collect information about how you use our websites, so we can improve them for you going forward. We also use the HMACCOUNT cookie to track visit counts and traffic sources, to measure and improve our website's performance. All information collected by these cookies is aggregated anonymously.

III. Cookies we use

IV. How to manage your cookie settings

To make sure you get the best experience when visiting our websites, we recommend accepting cookies. However, you can decline cookie use by clicking the "Cookie Settings" button.

Cookie setting options can be found on our website. If you choose to decline cookies, you can still use our website, though some features and sections may be limited. You can also configure or change your web browser's settings to accept or decline cookies.

V. How often do we update this Cookie Policy?

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time, or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons, to reflect changes in the cookies we use. So please check back periodically to stay informed about our use of cookies and related technologies. The date at the top of this Cookie Policy indicates when it was last updated.

VI. Where can I get more information?

If you have any questions about our use of cookies or other technologies, please contact us:

Email: product@eeoa.com

Once we receive your question, comment, or suggestion, and verify your identity, we will respond within fifteen business days.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: more-guides-02_batch2.md -->

## Optimizing Device Performance and Network (Computer/Phone/Tablet)

# I. Optimizing Device Performance

### 1. Desktop Computer

Restart your computer before class — a computer left running for a long time without restarting can become sluggish.

Exit any antivirus or security software on your computer, since this kind of software uses up memory and can make your computer sluggish. Common examples on the market include 360 Total Security, Rising Antivirus, Tencent PC Manager, 2345 Safeguard, Kaspersky, McAfee, and other mainstream antivirus/security software.

Close every app besides ClassIn — having too many apps open can use up your computer's memory and cause sluggishness.

### 2. Laptop

Add a cooling pad underneath your laptop — especially in summer, when high ambient temperatures combined with prolonged high-temperature operation can cause the CPU to throttle and the laptop to become sluggish.

### 3. Phone and Tablet

Restart your phone or tablet before class.

Close every other app running in the background besides ClassIn (how to do this: swipe up from the bottom edge of the phone screen to open the "recent apps list," then press and hold the app you want to close and swipe it up to close it).

# II. Optimizing Your Network

If a teacher or student experiences audio/video out of sync, an intermittent camera feed, laggy network, slow loading when opening cloud drive courseware, or a sudden classroom disconnection during class, this may be caused by a poor network signal. Try the following solutions to improve it:

Close programs or websites on your computer that use up network bandwidth. For example: QQ Music, games, video streaming sites, or files currently downloading — we recommend temporarily closing or exiting these.

Disable your computer's security software. Some antivirus programs or security suites throttle your network — we recommend disabling them before class. Common antivirus/security programs include 360 Total Security, Rising Antivirus, Tencent PC Manager, 2345 Safeguard, Kaspersky, McAfee, and others.

Avoid running high-bandwidth activities at the same time. On the same network, if multiple users are simultaneously doing bandwidth-heavy activities like streaming video or gaming, it can slow down everyone else's network speed.

Disable your computer's firewall, or add ClassIn to the firewall's allowlist, to prevent it from restricting your network connection.

Periodically restart your router, unplugging it for a few minutes before powering it back on — this helps maintain a stable network connection.

If you're taking class or studying on a school campus, we recommend contacting your school's network administrator to have any network speed limits on your computer removed.

Use your phone's mobile data. If your Wi-Fi is unstable, you can turn on your phone's mobile data, connect the phone to your computer via USB cable, then go to "Settings" on your phone, into "Personal Hotspot," and enable "USB Internet Sharing."

Move your laptop closer to your router before class — too much distance can weaken the signal between your device and the router, affecting connection quality.

If your laptop has an Ethernet port, you can connect via a network cable instead of Wi-Fi for a more stable, faster connection.

### 3. Phone or Tablet

Move your phone or tablet closer to your router before class — too much distance can weaken the signal between your device and the router, affecting connection quality.

If your phone is connected to Wi-Fi, try disconnecting from Wi-Fi and using mobile data instead.

If you're using a tablet, try connecting to a mobile hotspot shared from a phone.

Check whether your phone has good network coverage where you are — if the signal is weak, move to an area with better signal.

# Mac Audio Plugin (ClassIn Audio Device)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Mac Audio Plugin (ClassIn Audio Device)"
source_title_zh: "Mac电脑音频插件（ClassIn Audio Device）"
```

## Mac Audio Plugin (ClassIn Audio Device)

### Usage Notes
ClassIn Audio Device is an audio plugin used in two scenarios when a teacher uses ClassIn on a Mac.

**Scenario 1:** while using the "Screen Share" tool, to share sound from the local computer, the teacher needs to install the ClassIn Audio Device plugin — only then can local computer sound be shared with everyone else in the classroom.

**Scenario 2:** while recording class, if the teacher wants the sound from their computer desktop captured in the class playback video, they need to manually select "System Sound" under "Recording Mode" in the app settings. Once this mode is enabled, the teacher needs to install the ClassIn Audio Device plugin — only then can local computer sound be captured during recording.

### Notes
macOS version required to install the audio plugin: macOS 10.13 or higher.

The ClassIn Audio Device plugin only needs to be installed once.

Windows computers do not need to install the ClassIn Audio Device plugin.

Once ClassIn Audio Device is installed, your computer's speaker defaults to ClassIn Audio Device. If the teacher wants to use a different speaker, please close ClassIn first, then switch the system's speaker device.

### Installing ClassIn Audio Device During Screen Sharing

**Step 1:** when a teacher uses the screen share tool, a window will appear asking for their username and password. In this window, the teacher just needs to enter their computer's username and password to automatically complete installation of the ClassIn Audio Device plugin. (Please don't cancel the installation, or sound won't be shareable during screen sharing.)

**Step 2:** to check whether ClassIn Audio Device was installed successfully, the teacher can click the audio icon in the top-right corner of their computer and check whether there's a "ClassIn Audio Device" option. If it's there, the installation succeeded. At this point, the user can select the ClassIn Audio Device as the sound output in their computer's sound settings.

### Installing ClassIn Audio Device Before Recording Local Sound

**Step 1:** the teacher goes to "Recording Mode" in the app settings and checks "System Sound."

**Step 2:** once they enter the classroom and start recording, the teacher will be prompted to install the audio plugin — click Confirm on the prompt.

**Step 3:** ClassIn will show the teacher a dialog asking for their username and password; the teacher enters their computer's username and password to automatically complete installation of the ClassIn Audio Device plugin. (Please don't cancel the installation, or local computer sound won't be captured into the playback video while recording.)

**Step 4:** to check whether ClassIn Audio Device was installed successfully, the teacher can click the audio icon in the top-right corner of their computer and check whether there's a "ClassIn Audio Device" option. If it's there, the installation succeeded.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: more-guides-04_mac-audio-plugin.md -->

```yaml
title: "OBS Usage Guide"
source_title_zh: "OBS 使用说明"
```

## OBS Usage Guide

# I. Streaming a Livestream Using OBS

Streaming with OBS means the user first gets ClassIn's class session stream-push URL and adds it to OBS. Once the corresponding ClassIn class session starts, the user can use OBS to capture their computer desktop or a specific app's window and start streaming. This way, students watching the livestream via the ClassIn web link will see the content captured in OBS. When streaming with OBS, the user doesn't need to enter the ClassIn classroom.

## (1) Downloading OBS

In your browser, go to obsproject.com, then download the installer for your operating system.

## (2) Adding Video in OBS

### 2.1 Creating a Scene

Create a new scene in the Scenes panel in the bottom-left corner.

### 2.2 Adding Video to the Scene

Add a media source under Sources at the bottom.

Set a name for the source, then click OK.

Add a local video.

### 2.3 Resizing the Video

Select the video, then drag its edges to resize it.

## (3) Adding the Stream URL

Open OBS Settings.

Go to the Stream tab and change the service type to Custom.

Add the server address and stream key.

Full stream URL format: rtmp://livepush.eeo.cn/classlive/3786113a1b9e9ed9d1aa_406b449dd48bccac?txSecret=e7dd199f9e005588e3402cd33a97d2c4&txTime=7d8d37cd&record=mp4&record_interval=7200

Tip: in the format above, the first part goes into the "Server" field, and the second part goes into the "Stream Key" field.

## (4) Starting the Stream

Once you click Start Streaming, users can see the feed using the viewing link.

## (5) Playing a Video

Select the video you want to play, then click Play.

## (6) Stopping

When you need to stop the livestream, click Stop Streaming.

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Virtual Classroom Livestream"
source_title_zh: "教室虚拟直播"
```

## Virtual Classroom Livestream

### 2.2 Adding a Local Video to the Scene

### 2.4 Enabling Local Sound for the Media Source

Switch the media source's monitoring mode to "Monitor and Output."

## (3) Enabling the Virtual Camera Feature

Turn on the virtual camera feature in OBS.

## (4) Installing Virtual Microphone Software

Install the virtual microphone software → click to download and install.

Tip: after installing, you must restart your computer to complete the installation.

## (5) Hiding the Classroom's On-Stage Seats

Go to Classroom Settings, and under the General tab, check "Hide" for the on-stage seats area.

## (6) Setting the Camera and Microphone in the Classroom

In the classroom, turn on your camera and microphone, then set the microphone to the device starting with "VoiceMeeter," and set the camera to the device starting with "OBS." Then double-click the now-open camera to maximize it.

## (7) Playing the Video

Switch back to OBS, select the video, and start playback.

Tip: don't play any other sound on your computer desktop, since the virtual microphone picks up all sound currently playing on the computer desktop.

# CamIn Usage Guide

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "CamIn Usage Guide"
source_title_zh: "CamIn 使用说明"
```

## CamIn Usage Guide

#### What Is CamIn?

CamIn is a virtual camera and video production tool, designed to help every user easily create polished videos. By adding PPT/PDF/images alongside your on-camera presence, you can easily record demo videos, teaching videos, or micro-lectures.

You can also apply effects like beauty filters, virtual backgrounds, and stickers, and pair CamIn with video conferencing or livestream teaching software to make your teaching explanations or video conferences more professional and engaging.

#### Minimum System Requirements for CamIn

CamIn currently supports desktop use only — mobile isn't supported yet. Below are the minimum requirements for each OS.

| | Windows | Mac |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 10 64-bit or higher | macOS 10.15 or higher |
| Processor | Intel Core 6th generation or newer / AMD Ryzen 3000 series or newer | 2017 MacBook Pro or newer |
| Memory | 8GB RAM | 8GB RAM |
| Disk Space | 8GB free disk space (for program install, cache, and media storage) | 8GB free disk space (for program install, cache, and media storage) |
| Graphics | NVIDIA GTX 900 series or higher / AMD RX560 or higher / Intel HD 5500 or higher, with a GPU driver dated 2018 or newer, and 2GB GPU VRAM (integrated graphics that share system RAM counts toward total RAM) | 2GB GPU memory |
| Display Resolution | 1920x1080 or higher | Built-in display: 2560x1600 or higher; external display: 1920x1080 or higher |

#### Downloading, Installing, and Logging Into CamIn

(1) Downloading CamIn

Open a browser on your computer, go to www.camin.cn in the address bar, then click "Download Now" on the page.

(2) Installing CamIn

Run the downloaded CamIn installer; if Windows shows a security prompt, click "Yes." On the language selection screen, click "Confirm," check "I have read and agree," then click "Quick Install." Wait for installation to finish.

(3) Logging Into CamIn

If you already have a ClassIn account, you can log into CamIn directly with it. You can also log in by scanning a WeChat QR code or via SMS. Alternatively, you can open the ClassIn app on your phone and log in by scanning a QR code.

#### Creating and Configuring Scenes

(1) Creating a New Scene

CamIn comes with one scene by default. Users can create up to 5 scenes, and each scene can contain multiple video or image sources.

(2) Setting a Background

For each scene, users can set a background image of their choice — either from CamIn's built-in options or a local image from their computer.

#### Managing the Content Area

**(1)** Adding a Camera Source

Users can add multiple video sources within each scene — for example, if your computer has two cameras connected, you can add both camera sources at once to show different camera feeds. The camera window supports full-screen enlargement or custom resizing, and can switch between a square or circular border. In the settings below the camera window, users can configure various camera settings, including virtual background, green-screen chroma key, beauty filters, custom headwear, virtual avatar, saturation, contrast, opacity, zoom, and brightness.

CamIn also supports adding a physical camera as a content source. When using a camera as a content source, please choose the official app provided by your camera's brand. Then select and add the camera following the steps below.

For Sony cameras, see: https://www.sony.com/zh-cn/electronics/support/articles/00247038

For Fujifilm cameras, see: https://fujifilm-dsc.com/zhs/manual/x-h2_connection/overview_usage/webcam/

For Nikon cameras, see: https://www.nikon.com.cn/sc_CN/service-and-support/downloads/app.tag/app/webcam.dcr

For Canon cameras, see: https://www.canon.com.cn/special/webcam/index.html

For other camera brands, check the corresponding official website's recommendation.

**(2)** Opening a Local File

Users can insert various local files into each scene — PPT courseware, PDF courseware, images, videos, and more.

2.1 Courseware

Once you open a courseware file, first select "Cursor Mode" below, which lets you resize the courseware and turn pages. You can also use the pen and other teaching tools below to mark up or draw on the courseware.

2.2 Video

Once you open a video file, first select "Cursor Mode" below, which lets you resize the courseware, turn pages, toggle loop playback, adjust playback speed, and adjust the volume. You can also use the pen and other teaching tools below to mark up or draw on the video.

**(3)** Sharing Your Screen

Users can share their screen within each scene — supporting sharing the entire desktop or a specific app's window, including websites. Screen sharing also supports sharing computer sound, and the shared window can be freely resized. Users can also use the common tools below to mark up or draw on the shared window.

**(4)** Phone Screen Mirroring

Users can mirror a phone or tablet screen within each scene. Mirroring modes include "Apple Mirroring" and "ClassIn Mirroring." If you're using an iPhone or iPad and don't want to download any mirroring tool, choose "Apple Mirroring" mode; if you're using an Android phone or tablet, choose "ClassIn Mirroring" mode.

**(5)** Opening a Cloud Drive File

Users can load a file from their ClassIn cloud drive into CamIn to open it.

**(6)** Adding an Online Media Source

Users can add polished images or motion graphics provided officially.

**(7)** Adjusting Content Layers

When some content is obscured by other content, users can adjust the layering between pieces of content.

**(8)** Deleting Content

Delete content you've added (the background cannot be deleted).

#### Teleprompter

The teleprompter is only visible to yourself — no one else can see it.

#### Recording, Editing, and Saving Video

Once a user finishes recording a video with CamIn, they can edit it directly.

#### Adjusting Video Quality (Resolution)

Adjust the resolution used when streaming live.

#### Activating CamIn Membership

Activating CamIn membership unlocks access to more personalized features.

#### Streaming a Livestream

Once you add a stream-push URL from ClassIn or another platform to CamIn, you can use CamIn to go live.

Full stream URL format: rtmp://livepush.eeo.cn/eeolive/3786113a1b9e9ed9d1aa_406b449dd48bccac?txSecret=e7dd199f9e005588e3402cd33a97d2c4&txTime=7d8d37cd&record=mp4&record_interval=7200

Tip: in the format above, the first part is the "stream push address," and the second part is the "stream key."

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: more-guides-06_camin-usage-guide.md -->

# Classroom Order Management

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Classroom Order Management"
source_title_zh: "课堂秩序管理"
```

## Classroom Order Management

## I. School Management Plan

### 1. School Management (Administrator)

#### 1.1 Enabling Anti-Unauthorized-Recording

1.1.1 Editing a Custom Classroom

Log into the ClassIn backend, go to "System Settings" in the left navigation, select "Classroom Settings," then under "Custom Classroom Settings" below, edit an already-enabled custom classroom or create a new one.

1.1.2 Enabling the Scrolling Marquee

After opening custom classroom settings, go to "Toggle Settings," find item 7, "Student and Auditor Classroom Marquee Setting," and check "Once a student enters the classroom, that student's nickname and phone number will move randomly around the classroom."

Tip: this is intended as an anti-recording/anti-leak deterrent — the moving nickname and phone number make it harder to screen-record or screenshot the class content without it being traceable back to the student.

#### 1.2 Hiding the Classroom Chat Window

1.2.1 Editing a Custom Classroom: log into the ClassIn backend, go to "System Settings" in the left navigation, select "Classroom Settings," then under "Custom Classroom Settings" below, edit an already-enabled custom classroom or create a new one.

1.2.2 Hiding the Chat Window: after opening custom classroom settings, go to "Toggle Settings," find item 2, "Chat Window Settings," and check "Hide Chat Button." Tip: disabling the chat window school-wide effectively prevents disorderly text chatting among students during class. Suited to school-wide meetings or events.

### 2. Class Management (Head Teacher)

#### 2.1 Disabling the Join-Class Entry Point

Go into the class, then from the class group chat's top-right corner go into class settings, then go to "Class Management," and disable both "Allow Open Joining" and "Show Join-Class Entry Point on Share Page."

#### 2.2 Managing Speech in the Class Group Chat

2.2.1 Muting a Specific Student

Go into the class, then from the class group chat's top-right corner go into class settings, then in "Class Members," right-click the student you want to mute and select "Mute."

2.2.2 Muting All Students

Go into the class, then from the class group chat's top-right corner go into class settings, and check "Mute All Students."

#### 2.3 Hiding a Message in the Class Group Chat

Go into the class, right-click the message you want to hide, then select "Hide."

#### 2.4 Requiring Students to Use Their Real Name in Class

Go into the class, then from the class group chat's top-right corner go into class settings, then in "Class Members," right-click a student and select "Edit Class Nickname."

#### 2.5 Removing a Student from the Class

Go into the class, then from the class group chat's top-right corner go into class settings, then in "Class Members," right-click a student and select "Remove Member."

## II. Teacher Management Plan

### 1. Muting a Student's Microphone

If a student is disrupting order during class, the teacher can mute a specific student's microphone, or mute every student's microphone, to help maintain classroom order.

### 5. Muting Students in the Chat Window
