# Cross-Class Linked Lessons Usage Guide (Dual-Teacher Class)

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Cross-Class Linked Lessons Usage Guide (Dual-Teacher Class)"
source_title_zh: "跨班联课使用说明（双师课）"
```

## Cross-Class Linked Lessons Usage Guide (Dual-Teacher Class)

# I. What Is a Dual-Teacher Class?

A dual-teacher class is an innovative teaching model that uses the ClassIn platform to bring students from different classes together to learn as one. This approach breaks past the boundaries of a traditional single class, significantly improving both teaching and learning efficiency and outcomes. By removing spatial limits, dual-teacher classes let an outstanding teacher's lesson be replicated without limit, letting more students benefit from top-quality educational resources.

# II. Applicable Scenarios

**Teaching Management:** an outstanding teacher can livestream a lesson to multiple small classes at once, dramatically extending that teacher's reach while preserving high-quality teaching content in one place.

**Learning Outcomes:** each small class's teaching assistant can interact with students within their own class, and can also grade assignments and distribute materials before and after class, enabling personalized management.

**Service Operations:** meets parents' need to closely monitor classroom attendance and student learning behavior — the teaching system continuously records performance data and progress for every student.

**Enrollment and Renewals:** delivers the pricing and scale of a large class with the experience and outcomes of a small class, helping institutions establish a differentiated advantage, build their reputation, and multiply their revenue.

# III. Usage Notes

**Dual-teacher classroom:** made up of one main classroom and multiple sub-classrooms. Each main classroom can link up to 100 sub-classrooms.

**Video and audio:** during teaching, the video and audio of the "lead teacher" and any "student brought into a live call" in the main classroom are transmitted to every classroom. Beyond that, students and teaching assistants in a sub-classroom cannot see or hear the video/audio of anyone else in the main classroom (including its teaching assistants), and cannot see or hear the video/audio of students and teaching assistants in other sub-classrooms. Likewise, the lead teacher, teaching assistant, and students in the main classroom cannot see or hear the video/audio of students and teaching assistants in other sub-classrooms.

**Text chat:** in the main classroom, every teacher and student can use the chat tool to see text messages sent by teaching assistants or students in every sub-classroom. In a sub-classroom, however, teaching assistants and students can only see text messages sent by members of their own classroom, plus text messages from the main classroom's "lead teacher" — they cannot see messages from other sub-classrooms, nor messages sent by anyone else in the main classroom besides the "lead teacher" (including its teaching assistants).

**One-Click Reset:** before class starts, students in a sub-classroom may have been granted permission to write and draw on the whiteboard. To keep content consistent between the main classroom and sub-classrooms, once the "lead teacher" enters the main classroom, they can use the "One-Click Reset" feature before starting the lesson. To do this: click the four-dot icon in the top-right corner and select "Reset." This performs the following: clears the whiteboard content in every classroom, closes all courseware and tools, sends every teaching assistant and student in every classroom off stage, clears every student's authorization status, and resets trophy counts and each student's on-stage count. This ensures every classroom starts from the same state, supporting a smooth start to the lesson.

**Teaching tools available in the main classroom:** Cursor Mode, Select/Move tool, Pen, Eraser, Text Entry, Screenshot, Laser Pointer, Cloud Drive, Class Notes, Chat tool, Roster, Open Local File, Save/Share Whiteboard, Projection tools, Screen Share, Dice, Timer, Countdown Timer, Browser, Physics/Chemistry Lab, Trophy Leaderboard (only shows the main classroom's leaderboard), Teaching Materials Library, Auxiliary Camera, Drag-and-Point Laser Pointer, Ruler & Compass Tools, Geometric Shapes, Dual-Teacher Answer Clicker, Live Call, and Two-Device Single Account (PC/iPad only — using PC as the primary device is recommended).

**Tools and features disabled in the main classroom:** LMS, Small Blackboard, Group Discussion, VNC, Livestream Chat, Random Student Picker, Buzzer, Video Wall (including viewing only the main classroom's students or viewing every sub-classroom's students), Student Screen Share, Text Collaboration, and Multi-Directional Browser.

Before officially starting the class, we recommend running a complete rehearsal covering every step — scheduling, lesson prep, teaching, maintaining classroom order, recording, and post-class student review. Only start the class officially once every step has been confirmed to work correctly.

# IV. Must-Read for Academic Staff

## 1. Activating the Dual-Teacher Class Service

To activate the dual-teacher class service, please contact your dedicated account manager.

## 2. Creating a Class Session in the Backend

Note: a dual-teacher class doesn't need a separate class group — you can use an existing class for teaching. If you do need to create a new class, just follow the standard class-creation process.

### 2.1 Creating the Main Class Session

In the main class, select a specific class session (note: not the entire class group) to serve as the basis for the main classroom, then create its sub-sessions. If no class session has been added to the class group yet, refer to the image below to create one. (Path: log into the backend → Class Management → go into the class → Add Class Session.)

### 2.2 Adding Sub-Sessions

Go into the class group, check an already-created class session to designate it as the main session, then click "Bulk-Create Sub-Sessions." While adding sub-sessions, you'll need to specify which class group each sub-session belongs to. Refer to the image below to create them. (When choosing the class group, you can search by class name or by tag in the search bar above for faster results.)

Notes:

**(1)** Each main class session can have up to 100 sub-sessions created for it (up to 50 at a time — if you need more than 50, you'll need to run the process twice).

**(2)** You cannot create sub-sessions if the main class session's start time is less than 5 minutes away, or has already passed.

**(3)** You can add a co-teacher to all sub-sessions in bulk, or add a co-teacher individually to each sub-session. (Adding a co-teacher is optional, not required. If you add one by mistake, you can use the "Remove All" feature to remove them.)

**(4)** If a co-teacher needs to monitor chat activity across multiple classes at once during the lesson, you can assign that co-teacher to both the main session and multiple sub-sessions, letting them view the overall chat area from within the main classroom.

**(5)** Once created, any non-shared details of a sub-session can be edited within the corresponding class.

**(6)** For recording, you can choose either "Use the Main Session's Class Recording" or "Cloud Recording (each sub-session recorded separately)." Note: if you choose to have sub-sessions record separately in the cloud, each recording sub-classroom needs a teaching assistant present the whole time to handle the recording.

### 2.3 Editing and Deleting

Both the ClassIn app (client) and the backend interface let you edit and delete the main class session, and the related content in sub-sessions will automatically update to match. (Edit the session in the software) (Edit the main session in the Backend Management System.)

The ClassIn app (client) doesn't let you directly edit or delete a sub-session — you can only do this in the backend. You can go into the class corresponding to the sub-session to edit or delete it through the standard process, or click the "Actions" button on the far right of the main session, select "Online Dual-Teacher," and then delete it from there.

## 3. Downloading Post-Class Support Materials

**(1)** Screenshots the teacher takes with the main classroom's answer clicker tool can serve as a starting point for a teaching assistant's follow-up conversations. These screenshots are stored in the backend under Class Management → Class Data (Main Session) → Teaching Analysis → Answer Clicker Data.

**(2)** Click to view images to see every answer-clicker screenshot from that session; clicking "Download Images" in the top-right corner lets you download all images in a bundle, making it easier for post-class support teachers to communicate with students/parents.

**(3)** For institutions where teaching assistants don't have backend access, an academic teacher will need to download these on their behalf.

**(4)** Post-class support teachers can use these answer-clicker screenshots and student response data to provide personalized tutoring.

# V. Must-Read for Teachers

## 1. Lead Teacher Devices

Lead teachers can only teach using a computer or iPad (we recommend prioritizing a computer, since it offers more complete functionality) — phone and Android tablet are not supported for teaching.

## 2. Key Classroom Tools

**Live Call**

Live Call is an important channel for the lead teacher to communicate with students.

**(1)** In a dual-teacher class's main classroom, the lead teacher can bring a specific student into a live call by either "opening the teaching tool for live call" or "right-clicking a chat message" (only one person can be in a live call at a time); once a student is brought into a call, their audio/video syncs to the main class and every sub-class.

**(2)** Once the live call ends, you can hover over the video window and select "End Live Call," or "Open Live Call List" to choose another student for a call.

**(3)** The live call video window supports free resizing and repositioning; its resolution matches the resolution of the student on-stage seats, and its display logic is independent of the on-stage seats — meaning a single student can appear both in the live call window and in the on-stage seats at the same time.

**(4)** Both the lead teacher's computer and iPad support the live call feature.

**Chat**

The chat area is an important channel for the lead teacher to communicate with students in sub-classrooms (features like authorizing sub-classroom students or awarding trophies are not supported here).

**(1)** When a sub-classroom student speaks, their class name appears before their name.

**(2)** The main classroom's chat tool lets you choose to view "chat from every classroom" or "chat from one specific sub-classroom" at the top.

**(3)** The chat area in both the main classroom and sub-classrooms doesn't support the "Questions" feature. If a student has a question, they can ask it in the "Chat" window instead.

**(6)** Note: the chat area blocks part of the courseware in the playback recording; sub-classroom students watching the class playback will also see chat content from other, unrelated classes. Teachers can manually click the "Move Chat Window Outside the Classroom" button before recording so the chat area isn't recorded.

**Dual-Teacher Answer Clicker**

The answer clicker is the lead teacher's main way of gathering data on student understanding.

**(1)** Sending an answer clicker in a dual-teacher classroom works the same way as a regular answer clicker.

**(2)** While students are answering, the teacher can see the overall correct-answer rate and how many students chose each option, across every class.

**(3)** You can filter by class above the answer clicker to view a specific class's answers.

**(4)** Once answering ends, you can award trophies to students who answered correctly, or to everyone who participated. This is the only way for the lead teacher to award trophies to sub-classroom students.

**(5)** At any point during answering, the teacher can use the answer clicker's built-in screenshot tool (typically used after explaining a question, to capture the problem-solving approach) — this screenshot is saved in the backend as material for the teaching assistant's later follow-up.

**(6)** Once answering ends, sub-classroom students can only see their own class's answer details. (If academic staff have set "sub-classrooms use the main classroom's class recording," sub-classroom students will be able to see every class's answer data in the playback.)

**One-Click Reset**

Before class starts, sub-classroom students may in some cases have been authorized to write and draw on the whiteboard, and so on. To keep the main classroom and sub-classrooms consistent, once the lead teacher enters the classroom, they can use the classroom reset feature before starting the lesson (top-right four-dot icon → Reset):

Clears the whiteboard content in every classroom

Closes all courseware and tools

Sends every teaching assistant and student in every classroom off stage

Clears every student's authorization status, trophy count, and on-stage count

**Ending Class**

**(1)** A sub-classroom's co-teacher does not have the "End Class for Everyone" feature.

**(2)** Once the main classroom uses "End Class for Everyone," every sub-classroom ends class together with the main classroom.

## 3. Tools Available in the Main Classroom's Toolbox

Open File

Save/Share Whiteboard

Screen Projection Tool

Teacher Screen Share

Dice, Timer, Countdown Timer

Browser

Physics/Chemistry Lab

Trophy Leaderboard (only shows the main classroom's leaderboard)

Teaching Materials Library

Auxiliary Camera

Drag-and-Point Laser Pointer

Ruler & Compass Tools

Geometric Shapes

Two-Device Single-Account Classroom Entry

### 4. Features Disabled in the Main Classroom

All LMS activities

Small Blackboard

Group Discussion

VNC

Livestream Chat

Random Student Picker

Buzzer

Video Wall (including viewing only the main classroom's students or viewing every sub-classroom's students)

Student Screen Share

Text Collaboration

# VI. Must-Read for Teaching Assistants

## 1. Basic Teaching Assistant Responsibilities

During class:

1. On the backend's Classroom Monitoring page, check for absent students and reach out to them.

2. Maintain classroom order — if inappropriate content appears in a classroom's chat area, address it or delete it promptly within that sub-classroom.

3. Use the sub-classroom Video Wall to check students' learning status in real time and give reminders as needed.

4. Help resolve any software issues students run into.

5. Provide supplementary guidance for their own class, in addition to what the lead teacher covers.

Prohibited actions:

1. A co-teacher in the main classroom should not casually operate the courseware or whiteboard, since those changes won't sync to sub-classrooms (this will be improved in a future version).

2. A co-teacher in a sub-classroom should not operate the same feature (whiteboard, courseware, teaching tools) at the same time as the lead teacher, since this could cause the main classroom and sub-classrooms to become out of sync.

After class:

1. Grade assignments, quizzes, and other pre/post-class activities.

2. Communicate with families, using materials such as the teacher's answer-clicker screenshots from class to provide thorough, personalized analysis of student progress and tutoring.

## 2. Using the Chat Area

When scheduling, the academic teacher schedules the teaching assistant (co-teacher) into both the main class session and every sub-session they're responsible for.

By default, a co-teacher watches student messages in the main classroom's chat area; if they notice something unusual (for example, an inappropriate comment or question from a student), the co-teacher can use the student's class information to go into that sub-classroom, open the chat area, and handle it — deleting the message, muting the student, or replying directly.

Currently, a teaching assistant cannot handle issues directly from within the main classroom — this will be supported in the future.

Students in a sub-classroom can only see chat content from their own class, plus chat messages the lead teacher posts in the main classroom.

## 3. Post-Class Communication Materials

Besides regular communication content like assignments and quizzes, screenshots the lead teacher takes with the main classroom's answer clicker can also serve as a starting point for a teaching assistant's follow-up. These screenshots are stored in the backend under Course Management → Class Data → Answer Clicker Data.

Click to view images to download all of that session's answer-clicker screenshots as a bundle.

Teaching assistants without backend access can ask an academic teacher to download these on their behalf.

<!-- BATCH_FILE_END: more-guides-08_dual-teacher-class.md -->

# K-12 Backend Management System

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "K-12 Backend Management System"
source_title_zh: "中小学后台管理系统"
```

## K-12 Backend Management System

## I. Campus/Class/Course Management

#### Campus Management

**Creating a Campus**

If no school exists yet: log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → click "Create Grade/Homeroom Class" → create a new school and campus.

If a school already exists: log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → click the "···" to the right of the campus → select "Create Campus" to create a sub-campus under an existing school.

Note: the steps above require a "primary account" or "administrator" account.

**Editing a Campus**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → click the "···" to the right of the campus name to edit the campus name.

**Deleting a Campus**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the campus → click the "···" to the right of the campus name → select "Delete Campus."

#### School Level/Grade Management

**Creating a School Level/Grade**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the school and campus → click the "···" to the right of the campus → click "Create School Level."

**Editing a Grade**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → click the "···" to the right of the grade name → select "Edit."

**Deleting a Grade**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the grade → click the "···" to the right of the grade name → select "Delete Grade."

**Deleting a School Level**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the school level → click the "···" to the right of the school level name → select "Delete School Level."

#### Class Management

**Creating a Class**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the campus and grade → click the "···" to the right of the grade → click "Create Homeroom Class."

**Editing a Class**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the class → click the "···" to the right of the class name → select "Edit."

**Deleting a Class**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the class → click the "···" to the right of the class name → select "Delete Homeroom Class."

#### Course Management

**Creating a Course**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → find the class → click "Create Course" within the class.

**Editing a Course**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course and click "Edit" under "Settings" to change the course's information and permissions.

**Ending a Course**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course and select "End Course" under "Settings."

#### Member Management

**Adding a Head Teacher**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go to the "Members" tab → click "Set Head Teacher."

Note: the steps above require a "primary account" or "administrator" account (see how to add an administrator).

**Replacing the Head Teacher**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course, and in "Members," click the "···" next to the head teacher and select "Replace Head Teacher."

**Adding a Teacher**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go to the "Members" tab → click "Set Teacher."

**Removing a Teacher**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course, and under "Members," remove an already-added teacher.

Notes:

**(1)** The steps above require a "primary account" or "administrator" account.

**(2)** A teacher who is currently teaching, or who has an upcoming class session that hasn't started yet, cannot be removed.

**Adding a Student**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go to the "Members" tab → click "Set Course Students."

**Removing a Student**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course, and under "Members," remove a student.

**Bulk-Removing Students**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course, and under "Members," click "Bulk Actions" then select "Bulk Delete."

#### Class Session Management (Classroom)

**Adding a Class Session**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go to the "Class Sessions" tab within the course → click "Add Class Session."

**Bulk-Adding Class Sessions**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go to the "Class Sessions" tab within the course, and click "Bulk-Add Class Sessions."

**Editing a Class Session**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → then go into the course, select calendar view under "Class Sessions," open the session you want to edit, then click "Edit."

**Bulk-Editing Class Sessions**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → then go into the course, select list view under "Class Sessions" → find the information/permission you want to change → hover your mouse over that information/permission, then click the pencil icon to edit it.

**(2)** Bulk editing only supports editing class session information on the current page.

**Deleting a Class Session**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → then go into the course, select list view under "Class Sessions," find the session you want to delete, then open Actions on the right and select "Delete."

**(2)** A class session can be deleted anytime before it officially starts.

**Bulk-Deleting Class Sessions**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → then go into the course, select list view under "Class Sessions," find the sessions you want to delete, open Actions on the right and select "Delete," then check "Bulk Edit."

**(2)** Bulk deletion only supports deleting class sessions on the current page (a session can be deleted anytime before it officially starts).

**Restrictions When Editing a Class Session**

Different pieces of a class session's information and settings have different editable time windows — see the timing table below for details.

#### Weekly Schedule

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → go into the class and find the course (if no campus has been created, look for the course directly under "Uncategorized Courses") → go to the Class Sessions tab → Copy Weekly Schedule.

Once you set a teaching cycle, the current week's schedule will be filled into the date range of that teaching cycle.

If class sessions already exist within the selected teaching cycle, existing sessions will not be overwritten.

## II. Class Playback Video Management

**Downloading a Playback Video**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Class Session Management" → find the session, click "Actions" on the right → then go to "Recorded Video Data."

Download method for Windows users:

Method 1: once in the video player window, click the three dots below, then select Download.

Method 2: once in the video player window, right-click and "Save Video As."

Method 3: right-click directly in the video list and "Save Video As."

Download method for Mac users:

Go into the video list, right-click the video's download button, and choose "Save File As." If there's no such option, hold Option while clicking the download button.

**Uploading a Playback Video**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Class Session Management" → find the class session you want to upload video for → click "Actions" on the right → go to "Recorded Video Data" → click "Upload Video" → select a local video and upload it.

**(1)** Video cannot be uploaded for a class session that didn't have recording enabled.

**(2)** The system only supports MP4 files encoded with H.264. Before uploading, please confirm the encoding using a media player or video processing tool — if the encoding is incorrect, you may end up with audio but no video. If the file isn't in MP4 format, it may fail to play.

**(3)** The maximum supported resolution is 1080P — anything higher may fail to play.

**Deleting a Playback Video**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Class Session Management" → find the class session whose video you want to delete → click "Actions" on the right → go to "Recorded Video Data" → find the video you want to delete → click "Delete" on the right.

## III. Livestream/Playback Management

#### Getting the "Livestream/Playback" Link

**Getting the Course Link**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → then go into the campus on the left to find the class (if your course isn't under any class, look for it under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course and select "Class Sessions" → select list view on the right → then get the course's livestream/playback link below.

**Note:** if none of the class sessions under a course have recording enabled, no course livestream/playback link will appear here.

**Getting the Class Session Link**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Class Session Management" → get the course's and class session's playback link from within the teaching class or activity class.

#### Livestream/Playback Settings

**Changing Client-Side Playback Viewing Permission**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → enable or disable client-side playback viewing under "Class Session Playback Settings" (once disabled, every student under this platform will be unable to watch historical playbacks or playbacks generated by new class sessions).

**Note:** the playback permission here only affects the ClassIn client — it doesn't affect users watching playback via the web.

**Changing Historical Playback Viewing Permission for Newly Added Students**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → under "Class Session Playback Settings," allow or disallow students newly added to a course from watching playback videos of historical class sessions.

**(1)** You need to turn the toggle on first, then add students, for it to take effect.

**(2)** This setting doesn't apply to the scenario of a course's auditor becoming a formal student.

**(3)** A course's auditors will never be able to watch playback videos of historical class sessions.

**(4)** Once this changes a student's status in a historical class session, it cannot be reversed — please proceed carefully.

**Changing Historical Playback Viewing Permission for Removed Students**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → under "Class Session Playback Settings," allow or disallow a student removed from a course from continuing to watch playback videos of historical class sessions.

**(2)** Once this changes a student's status in a historical class session, it cannot be reversed — please proceed carefully.

**(3)** A student removed and blocked from watching playback becomes a "transfer student" in historical class sessions, marked with a red icon in the school's backend.

**(4)** If a student removed and blocked from watching playback is later re-added to that class session's class as a "transfer student," they still won't be able to watch that session's playback or learning report.

**Changing Livestream/Playback Viewing Permission**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Course Management" → then go into the campus on the left to find the class (if your course isn't under any class, look for it under "Uncategorized Courses") → go into the course and select "Class Sessions" → go to calendar view on the right → then click the session you want to edit → click Edit → change the web livestream/playback viewing permission below in the edit screen.

**(1)** Once "Web Livestream" is checked, if the teacher shares the livestream link and the lead teacher records normally, anyone holding the livestream link can watch the class's web livestream (unchecking it means the link can no longer be used to watch that session's livestream).

**(2)** Once "Web Playback" is checked, if the teacher shares the link and the lead teacher's recording succeeded, anyone holding the playback link can watch the class's web playback (unchecking it means the link can no longer be used to watch that session's playback).

**(1)** Web livestream/playback only works for class sessions that have recording enabled.

**(2)** Web livestream can only be edited up to 20 minutes before class starts.

**(3)** Web playback can be edited at any time.

**Livestream Reservation Feature**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → enable or disable the web livestream reservation feature under "Web Livestream/Playback Settings."

**Note:** reservations can be made anytime more than 30 minutes before class; within 30 minutes of class start, reservations are no longer possible. One minute before a livestream session starts, the system sends an SMS notification to remind the user — for domestic and international SMS billing, see the financial overview.

**Changing the Livestream/Playback Cover Image**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → set the default web livestream/playback cover image under "Web Livestream/Playback Settings."

**Note:** if a class session has its own web livestream/playback cover set individually, that session's cover takes priority for display.

**Livestream Data Display**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → set what livestream data to display under "Web Livestream/Playback Settings."

**Changing the Prompt Text**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → change the web livestream/playback prompt text under "Web Livestream/Playback Settings."

**Anti-Recording Protection for Client-Side Playback Video**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "System Settings" → "Class Session Playback Settings" → under Anti-Recording Settings below → enable or disable anti-recording protection for client-side playback viewing (this displays the student's client nickname).

## IV. Resources and Storage

**Uploading Public Resources**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "School Materials" to upload public courseware resources.

**(1)** A single courseware file can be up to 500MB.

**(2)** The backend courseware resources support creating up to 2,000 folders.

**(3)** We recommend putting courseware into folders, since when granting a teacher courseware access, you can only select a folder — not an individual courseware file directly.

**Enabling Client Download for Authorized Courseware**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "School Materials," where you can enable or disable permission for courseware to be transferred and downloaded within the app.

**Note:** this feature isn't supported for folders.

**Storage Management**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to the "Storage Management" tab → here you can view the total storage used across the current school's backend, and delete or lock/protect recorded videos and classroom monitoring images for individual class sessions (bulk deletion supported).

**Authorized Resources**

**(1)** Schools can grant students access to content within School Materials from here.

**(2)** Students can view and open these anywhere — IM, classroom, prep room, whiteboard editor, and so on.

**(3)** You can choose public authorization, or authorize an individual student separately.

Note: once the organization question bank goes live, students will no longer be able to see authorized exam papers, though other file formats remain accessible and viewable as normal.

## V. Setting Up Administrators

#### Role Management

**Creating a New Role**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Settings" → add a new role under Role Management; each role can have different permissions configured.

**Editing a Role's Permissions and Name**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Settings" → go to the Permission Settings tab → find the role whose name or permissions you want to change under Role Management, then click Edit on the right.

**Deleting a Role**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Settings" → find the role you want to delete under Role Management → click Delete on the right.

#### Setting Up Administrators

**Adding an Administrator**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Settings" → add a new administrator under Personnel Management.

**Adding Permissions for an Administrator**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Settings" → edit an already-added administrator under Personnel Management.

**Removing an Administrator**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Settings" → remove an already-added administrator under Personnel Management.

## VI. Classroom Monitoring Management

**Adding a Classroom Monitor**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Permission Management" → create a role under "Role Management" (this role needs "Classroom Monitoring" permission checked) → then add a monitoring account under "Personnel Management" and link it to the newly created role.

**Starting Classroom Monitoring**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to "Classroom Monitoring" → find the class session by its name or the teacher's account → click "Enter Classroom."

**(1)** Once a monitor enters the classroom, no one else can see them.

**(2)** Monitors can use local recording.

## VII. Bell Schedule (Class Timing Template)

**Creating a Bell Schedule**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to School Settings → Bell Schedule Configuration → click "Create Bell Schedule" → you can create class periods for any day Monday through Sunday, up to one week's worth of classes at a time, up to 20 periods per day, with each period's duration customizable, and you can copy one day's class period arrangement to other days. (An already-created bell schedule can be applied directly when creating class sessions.)

**Editing a Bell Schedule**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to School Settings → Bell Schedule Configuration → hover your mouse over the schedule's name → an options button appears on the right → click it and select Edit.

**Deleting a Bell Schedule**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to School Settings → Bell Schedule Configuration → hover your mouse over the schedule's name → an options button appears on the right → click it and select Delete, then click Confirm in the prompt that appears.

## VIII. Classroom Data

**Teaching Analysis**

Log into the Backend Management System → go to Class Session Management → search for the class session, then view its classroom data on the right.

**Learning Analysis**

# Offline Teaching

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Offline Teaching"
source_title_zh: "线下教学"
```

## Offline Teaching

Traditional offline teaching emphasizes knowledge and skills instruction, training students' problem-solving efficiency and ability. Building on this, by using learning task sheets and scaffolding to shape how lectures support student learning, and by arranging better instruction based on process-level data analysis from assignments, quizzes, or in-class teaching, lectures can evolve based on data-driven experience. Running idea generation alongside knowledge and skills instruction, and applying learning task sheets for precision teaching, opens up new possibilities for traditional offline teaching. ClassIn X/ClassIn is an education platform built for offline teaching scenarios, connecting lesson prep with pre-class, in-class, and post-class implementation, and connecting all content and data together — letting it fully coordinate and support every element and process involved in precision teaching.

## I. Lesson Prep

Teachers can choose teaching resources from the Resource Center, or upload their own local teaching resources to the cloud drive, then open them in the classroom for teaching. Courseware supports online editing and online printing.

## II. Teaching

When teachers use ClassIn X on a large display for offline teaching, the following features are available (click a feature name to see how to use it):

### 2.1 Teaching Content Interaction

Play PPT, multimedia, and other courseware

Write on the whiteboard with the pen, mark up and annotate — writing is supported on both courseware and the whiteboard

Drag teaching elements like images, useful for generative classroom activities

Screenshot, scan-to-upload image, and auxiliary camera — useful for going over practice problems and showing classroom work

Save and share the whiteboard, making it easy for students to review after class and for teachers to keep teaching resources on file

### 2.2 Real Teaching Case Studies

**Beijing No.1 Normal University Affiliated Primary School — "Classification and Organization"**

Teacher Gao used ClassIn's whiteboard layer feature to turn shapes of different colors and forms into movable images, guiding students to freely drag the images to learn about classification and grouping concepts. Since the teacher didn't specify a classification standard, students' dragging actions ended up visualizing their own thinking.

The teacher used ClassIn's split-screen feature to show the whiteboard and PPT together — first guiding students to count different fruits on the whiteboard, then using the PPT to have students trigger the matching fruit count and write the answer in Arabic numerals. Using the same teaching materials across different classes, the teacher got a variety of randomly generated student responses.

**Beijing Xinxian Hutong Primary School — "Bringing in the New Year"**

During the pre-reading segment, Teacher Yang designed an EDB drag-and-drop game where students dragged Spring Festival–related elements down under the digital blackboard (elements for other holidays were locked in advance by the teacher and couldn't be dragged), activating students' existing vocabulary and preparing them for the while-reading segment. Students eagerly took part, and the classroom atmosphere was very lively.

Teacher Yang used the scan-to-upload image feature to upload practice questions students had completed on paper task sheets onto the digital blackboard, then dragged out pre-made whiteboard content from the side of the digital blackboard, using an interactive classroom intro to help students connect new material with what they already knew.

**Beijing Xinxian Hutong Primary School — "Double Ninth Festival — the Character 'Nine' (九)"**

After small-group inquiry, Teacher Hu had students arrange the two strokes of the character "九" (nine) on a gold-colored grid, focusing on issues like incorrect stroke placement and where long/short strokes should land. The teacher then took screenshots of students' arrangements to generate examples of the character's stroke features for comparison and understanding, tackling the lesson's key difficulty — the character's slanting posture and tightened center. The greatest value of this segment was that the teaching difficulty emerged from the students themselves rather than being preset by the teacher, truly making students the center of the activity.

Based on the characters "重阳" (Double Ninth) shown in the pre-made whiteboard content, students found the matching "九" in that font to complete a character-collecting exercise. By observing the stroke features of different calligraphic styles, students gained a deeper understanding of the Zhao-style regular script taught in this lesson. At the end of class, the teacher photographed and uploaded outstanding student work, turning it into home decor pieces — extending classroom learning beyond the classroom and reinforcing the moral value of respecting one's elders.

### 2.3 Subject-Specific Tool Interaction

Auto-recognition of standard shapes like straight lines, triangles, and circles, useful for STEM teaching

Ruler & compass tools, geometry board, and browser, adding convenience to teaching

Virtual labs (physics, chemistry), making experiments more accessible

### 2.4 Teacher-Student Interaction

Timer and countdown timer, for in-class interaction and timed task completion

Random Student Picker and dice-rolling, boosting student participation

Awarding trophies, for classroom rewards

### 2.5 Real Teaching Case Studies

**Beijing No.1 Normal University Affiliated Primary School — "Volume and Units of Volume"**

Teacher Yang used ClassIn's built-in physics virtual lab feature during a math lesson — using a beaker-and-buoyancy experiment, students dropped small stones into the beaker, letting the rising water level give them an intuitive sense of the concept of volume, visualizing an abstract idea.

Teacher Yang used ClassIn's screen projection feature, having students operate ClassIn plus an iPad to directly measure the volume of the offline classroom and learn about volume that way.

**Beijing Xinxian Hutong Primary School — "Tick Tock"**

Teacher Lang designed a line-matching exercise, guiding students to complete the matching activity using the "straight line" pen tool. Students eagerly took part, and the classroom atmosphere was very lively — enriching the format of classroom practice and boosting students' interest and engagement.

Teacher Lang used the whiteboard's layer design feature, guiding students to drag cartoon images to find the picture matching each word, helping them more intuitively learn the English word "T-shirt" and practice answering special questions starting with "How many."

**Beijing No.109 Middle School — "Conservation of Mechanical Energy"**

Features used: iPad-controlled PPT, iPad same-screen annotation, photo upload, countdown timer, physics virtual lab

**Qingdao Taiping Road Primary School, Shandong — "24-Hour Time Notation"**

During the in-class practice segment, Teacher Liu combined EDB whiteboard content with teaching tools to have students classify different ways of expressing time. Teacher Liu rolled the dice for students, moving a rocket forward based on the number shown — enriching the format of classroom practice and boosting students' interest and engagement.

Once the rocket reached its destination, students had to judge whether the time shown on the star used 24-hour or 12-hour notation. After students made their judgment, the teacher dragged the star into the corresponding category box.

## III. Before and After Class: Supporting Reinforcement and Learning Analysis

Generate a class teaching report after class ends

Assign homework/quiz tasks, gradable whether submitted online or offline, with scores kept on file

Present class students' scores, filterable and exportable, for learning analysis

title: "Dual-Teacher Scenarios and Cross-Disciplinary On-Site Teaching"
source_title_zh: "双师场景与跨学科实景教学"

## Dual-Teacher Scenarios and Cross-Disciplinary On-Site Teaching

## I. Scenario Overview

### Dual-Teacher Classroom

China's 2022 curriculum plan and curriculum standards brought cross-disciplinary courses and teaching to the forefront, setting clear requirements for schools and teachers. The preface to the curriculum plan and each subject's curriculum standards clearly lays out the main changes to the standards, especially the optimization of curriculum content structure; the curriculum plan's core principles emphasize strengthening the integrated nature of coursework; guidance on curriculum design and implementation stresses that comprehensive practical activities should focus on cross-disciplinary, inquiry-based learning and social practice; and curriculum standard development and textbook writing set clear class-hour ratio requirements for cross-disciplinary practice — in principle, every subject should devote no less than 10% of its class hours to cross-disciplinary themed teaching. In addition, many scenarios that need to break through spatial boundaries — cross-school teaching research, educational support programs, expert-teacher classrooms, emergency online classrooms during a pandemic, and more — can all be realized through the dual-teacher classroom.

ClassIn, an integrated teaching-and-learning digital platform, supports both teaching and teaching-research scenarios well. Beyond regular offline/online/OMO classrooms, when paired with the right hardware, it can effectively support synchronized dual-teacher classrooms, expert-teacher classrooms, emergency online classrooms during a pandemic, and support programs for remote regions. On the research side, it can meet teachers' needs for remote lesson observation and evaluation, joint teaching research, and group training.

### Application Scenarios

### Hardware Checklist

Notes:

For non-interactive spaces (such as lecture halls or museums), equipment should be assessed based on actual conditions.

## III. How to Put It into Practice

### Lesson Prep

Teachers can choose teaching resources from the Resource Center, or upload their own local teaching resources to the cloud drive, then open them in the classroom for teaching. Courseware supports online editing and online printing.

Teachers doing dual-teacher instruction can create a class session during lesson prep to communicate and co-create the lesson.

Beyond preparing the subject knowledge, they should also plan the interaction and communication between the two sides.

### Pre-Class Hardware and Software Setup

When setting up the dual-teacher class session, please set the teachers' roles as "teacher" and "co-teacher."

Please test your equipment ahead of time — once in the classroom, set up the front and rear cameras, microphones, and classroom layout (camera and microphone settings are remembered).

If using a mobile microphone, please make sure it's fully charged in advance.

Both teachers should enter the classroom ahead of time to test network conditions and confirm audio/video transmission is smooth (with good hardware and network conditions, ClassIn's audio/video technology achieves under 300ms of latency, ensuring smooth dual-teacher instruction).

Check that the materials needed for the lesson have already been uploaded to the cloud drive and finished transcoding, making sure you can smoothly pull up materials and operate tools, keeping the pace of the class smooth.

If using dual or triple displays, open Video Wall ahead of time and test what will be shown on each screen (in a dual-display setup, the reflection display shows the students from the paired class; in a triple-display setup, the reflection display shows the paired class's students, while the second front display shows the paired teacher).

If students are using smart devices, make sure the devices are charged, connected to the network, and logged into the correct accounts ahead of time; for any segment requiring students to operate their smart device, the teacher needs to authorize them.

Note: for your first time teaching in a dual-teacher scenario, we recommend seeking help from a consultant.

## V. Dual-Display/Triple-Display Scenarios

### Dual-Display Scenario

Building on a standard dual-teacher setup, adding a second screen as a "reflection display" — placed at the back or side of the classroom — creates a dual-display scenario.

Dual-display dual-teacher setups let the lead teacher face their own class while simultaneously seeing the remote class's students. When teachers are new to dual-teacher instruction, they're often not yet used to camera-facing presentation and keep wanting to turn around to check the remote class's camera feed on the large display. In a ClassIn-supported dual-teacher classroom, this is easily solved by enabling Video Wall to show the remote class's camera feed and placing that video wall on the reflection display — truly letting the two classes' students learn together as if in the same room, breaking through spatial limits.

### Triple-Display Scenario

Building on the dual-display scenario, adding a third screen at the front of the classroom — dedicated to showing the remote teacher's video window — helps teachers and students across locations make eye contact and share gestures, while also creating a sense of "being face-to-face," strengthening the emotional connection between teacher and students, truly achieving the feeling that "though far apart, we're as close as neighbors" in dual-teacher instruction.

As shown, the red box is the main display, used for teaching; the yellow box is the second front display, letting students from both classes see the remote teacher in real time; the green box is the reflection display, placed at the back of the classroom, letting both teachers see the remote class's students in real time.

## VI. Dual-Teacher Best-Practice Case Studies

(Haidian Jinxiao Education Group)

**1. AI-Assisted Practice for "Dual-Teacher Classroom" and "Integrated Joint Research"**

Using lesson examples as a vehicle, Haidian Jinxiao Education Group carried out on-site teaching practice for the "dual-teacher classroom" and "integrated joint research" activities. **[Dual-Teacher Classroom]** Two teachers jointly prepared the lesson, co-taught, and interacted with each other, forming a "lead teacher + assisting teacher" practice partnership. Together they presented an 8th-grade biology lesson on-site, centered on "The Path to High-Quality, High-Yield Domestic Tomatoes — Applying Principles of Genetic Variation in Breeding," as part of a "dual-teacher classroom" on-site teaching practice.

The image shows a dual-display dual-teacher scenario, with the rear reflection display showing students from the remote class.

**[Integrated Joint Research]** This joint research activity's theme was "Bringing the Winter Olympics into the Classroom: Moving Toward the Future Together, China Steps Up," with civics teachers from all 8 K-12 schools in the Haidian Jinxiao Education Group taking part throughout.

Teacher representatives joining the joint research online — from Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated middle school, Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Yuyuantan Middle School, Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Geology Middle School, Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated primary school, Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Third Primary School, and Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Fourth Primary School — plus teachers from the Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Experimental School's North/South campus and Xiangshan branch campus joining offline, offered suggestions on designing challenging learning activities in lesson plans, each tailored to the characteristics of students at the elementary, middle, and high school levels.

The images show, in order, a teacher presenting a lesson plan, group-school teachers conducting research, and group-school teachers discussing and exchanging ideas.

**2. AI-Assisted Practice for "Dual-Teacher Classroom" and "Integrated Joint Research" — Elementary Chinese Language**

**[Dual-Teacher Classroom]** This activity combined "on-site dual-teacher classroom teaching practice + online/offline discussion + nationwide livestream," bringing together education peers from 18 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities across the country to watch the class online and take part in discussion — the livestream drew over 40,000 views. Anning City in Yunnan Province organized all its elementary Chinese-language teachers to join online.

Teacher Du Chunhuan from Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Experimental Primary School and Teacher Liu Caizhao from Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Third Experimental Primary School served as the lead teachers, delivering a lesson on "Zhaozhou Bridge," centered on the theme "Learning Tasks That Promote Deep Interaction." Teachers and students from both schools broke through spatial boundaries, interacting, presenting, and sharing as if in the same room. Students engaged actively in learning, listened attentively to one another, proactively expressed their views, discussed enthusiastically, and completed the lesson's learning tasks to a high standard. Teacher Du took the lead in assigning classroom tasks, organizing activities, and providing guidance and demonstrations, while Teacher Liu provided timely organization, guidance, prompts, and personalized support for the students. The two teachers taught in close coordination, and their interaction with each other also helped drive interaction among the students. In addition, the online teaching platform's features — photographing and uploading work to display, zooming in to track and get close-ups of students, and smoothly switching between multiple video feeds — also strongly supported communication and sharing between the two schools' teachers and students.

**3. Haidian "Grand Teaching Research" Dual-Teacher Classroom and Integrated Joint Research — 8th-Grade Chinese Language**

**[Dual-Teacher Classroom]** Centered on the theme "Multi-Way Interaction to Foster Character Education Through Chinese Language," Haidian Jinxiao Education Group carried out a dual-teacher classroom and integrated joint research activity using the 8th-grade Chinese lesson "The Boat of the Core" as a vehicle. The activity combined "on-site dual-teacher classroom teaching practice + online/offline discussion + nationwide livestream," bringing together education peers from 31 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities across the country to watch the class online and take part in discussion — the livestream drew over 6,000 views.

Teacher Gu Xiaohong from Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Middle School and Teacher Zhang Bo from Haidian Jinxiao-affiliated Experimental School's Xiangshan branch campus formed a "dual-lead" dual-teacher partnership. Students from both classes engaged actively in learning, thinking about questions from multiple angles, helping one another, and gaining a positive learning experience of success and enjoyment. Both teachers took a leading role, coordinating closely on assigning learning tasks, organizing activities, guiding their own students, and facilitating interaction between the two classes. In addition, pre-class assessment and analysis of learning status, tablet-based group learning, and the online teaching platform's features — same-screen writing, zooming in to track and get close-ups of students, and photographing and uploading work to display — also strongly supported communication and sharing between the two schools' teachers and students.

# Blended Scenarios and Core Competency Teaching

<!-- DOC_BOUNDARY -->
```yaml
title: "Blended Scenarios and Core Competency Teaching"
source_title_zh: "混合式场景与核心素养教学"
```

## Blended Scenarios and Core Competency Teaching

## I. Concept Overview

### 1.1 What Is Blended Teaching?

Implementing core-competency curriculum teaching is a challenging learning theme (unit course) that requires active student participation and proactive learning, sparking intrinsic motivation and developing higher-order thinking, and calls for deep engagement with a wide range of learning tasks and subject-based practice activities.

A process like this inevitably won't happen within a single classroom space alone. In terms of the space where teaching and learning happen, this necessarily becomes a ubiquitous learning space that combines in-school classroom teaching with independent, out-of-school learning and practice; it necessarily becomes a blended learning space, supported by informatization and digital tools, that merges the physical world with the virtual world; and it necessarily becomes a learning space supported by modern technology, suited to a comprehensive, well-rounded process of learning and development.

## II. How to Put It into Practice

Adapted from Professor Yang Xiaozhe's "Transformations in Learning Environments and Methods Under New Technology"

### 2.1 Seven Common Problems with Integrating Technology Into Teaching Today

**Stance:** it's usually the teacher using the technology, not the student

**Unit:** technology use tends to be overly fragmented, often applied to a single segment within an activity rather than to learning as a whole

**Orientation:** knowledge or functionality gets broken down (into points) rather than integrated (with technology blending into the full experience of learning, life, and society)

**Goal:** stuck at basic knowledge and skills, with separated three-dimensional objectives, rather than being oriented toward competency goals

**Focus:** more attention goes to teachers using technology to present information better, rather than to helping students process information (learning how to learn)

**Attention:** more focus on overall achievement, overlooking individual differences

**Tension:** excessively chasing or overstating smart technology, while ignoring the basic consensus, basic conditions, and basic applications of the current situation

### 2.2 Seven Effective Strategies for Blended Online-Offline Teaching

Use a learning management system to weave technology into the complete learning process

Design at least some portion of learning to happen online

Make every offline class also joinable online

Provide a variety of learning resources to support unit-based learning

Choose tools suited to promoting student cognition and collaboration

Use a variety of different teaching organization methods as needed

Design personalized learning informed by data feedback

### 2.3 Inquiry

Why should we emphasize students using technology to learn?

Does the teacher always hold the practical authority over technology use?

Is technology's role in teaching being oversimplified and reduced to just using a PPT?

**Think about it**

If you assigned students a task to share their own experience using technology for subject-area learning, how would you frame that task?

How would you guide students to use technology for subject-area learning?

### 2.4 How to Use Technology in the Classroom?

**Three dimensions of technology in instructional design:**

Multi-dimensional context building: deep learning grounded in authentic scenarios

Interactive inquiry tools: competency-based unit design

Personalized progress tracking: staged assessment of problem-solving

Build or use a variety of resource formats — text, images, video, models, datasets, virtual scenarios, and so on — to highlight the unit's authentic context, giving students vivid, intuitive, thought-provoking learning materials. Let students immerse themselves in context from multiple angles, strengthening their ability to identify, analyze, and solve problems.

Play PPT, multimedia, and other courseware

Write on the whiteboard with the pen, mark up and annotate — writing is supported on both courseware and the whiteboard

Drag teaching elements like images, useful for generative classroom activities

Screenshot, scan-to-upload image, and auxiliary camera — useful for going over practice problems and showing classroom work

Save and share the whiteboard, making it easy for students to review after class and for teachers to keep teaching resources on file

### 2.9 Classroom Practice

**Beijing No.1 Normal University Affiliated Primary School — "Classification and Organization"**

Teacher Gao used ClassIn's whiteboard layer feature to turn shapes of different colors and forms into movable images, guiding students to freely drag the images to learn about classification and grouping concepts. Since the teacher didn't specify a classification standard, students' dragging actions ended up visualizing their own thinking.

The teacher used ClassIn's split-screen feature to show the whiteboard and PPT together — first guiding students to count different fruits on the whiteboard, then using the PPT to have students trigger the matching fruit count and write the answer in Arabic numerals. Using the same teaching materials across different classes, the teacher got a variety of randomly generated student responses.

**Beijing Xinxian Hutong Primary School — "Bringing in the New Year"**

During the pre-reading segment, Teacher Yang designed an EDB drag-and-drop game where students dragged Spring Festival–related elements down under the digital blackboard (elements for other holidays were locked in advance by the teacher and couldn't be dragged), activating students' existing vocabulary and preparing them for the while-reading segment. Students eagerly took part, and the classroom atmosphere was very lively.

Teacher Yang used the scan-to-upload image feature to upload practice questions students had completed on paper task sheets onto the digital blackboard, then dragged out pre-made whiteboard content from the side of the digital blackboard, using an interactive classroom intro to help students connect new material with what they already knew.

Teacher Yang used ClassIn's built-in physics virtual lab feature during a math lesson — using a beaker-and-buoyancy experiment, students dropped small stones into the beaker, letting the rising water level give them an intuitive sense of the concept of volume, visualizing an abstract idea.

Assign homework/quiz tasks, gradable whether submitted online or offline, with scores kept on file

## III. Lesson Example and Method

Using "Area of a Circle" as an example

**Thoughts during lesson prep:**

Learning how to calculate a circle's area and its applications. Building on foundational knowledge of the concept of area and calculating polygon area, students explore the formula for calculating a circle's area.

How can a comprehensive application problem be framed in an authentic context to give students room to explore? How should instruction be designed to develop students' mathematical thinking methods, such as transformation and limits?

How can students develop the ability to formulate and solve problems, and appreciate the beauty of mathematical exploration and practice during self-directed learning...

**Learning Activity — Discussion**, pre-class discussion on "What circles exist in everyday life?"

Teachers can publish a discussion activity to spark student thinking and let students communicate independently.

Teachers can see every student's discussion contributions, making it easier to provide personalized guidance and more flexibly adjust learning content and teaching methods. Students and teachers can comment and like each other's posts, creating good interaction and giving everyone a chance to voice their views.

**Learning Activity — Quiz**, a pre-class quiz to help students review the concept of area and how to calculate polygon area; a post-class quiz to check learning outcomes

Teachers can give students a pre-class quiz to help them review what they've learned and identify gaps, while also letting the teacher gauge students' current level to plan the upcoming lesson appropriately and improve classroom efficiency.

Quizzes can also be assigned individually, used to check students' understanding after class.

**Learning Activity — Class Session**, teaching the lesson's content, flexibly using in-classroom mini-tools to enrich classroom activities.

Class sessions support real-time audio/video interaction, and can happen online, offline, or in a blended, mixed format.

Teachers can use in-classroom mini-tools — such as the answer clicker and small blackboard — to enrich classroom activities and improve learning outcomes.

**Learning Activity — Learning Materials**, syncing the class task file, with students completing the class learning task according to the file's instructions (openable within the classroom)

Teachers can use Learning Materials to publish a learning guide, letting students understand the learning plan for each upcoming module before class. Teachers can also publish pre-class materials, guiding different student groups toward purposeful, personalized learning, improving the effectiveness of preview and deep learning.

Learning Materials support audio recordings, cloud drive files, local files, web links, and other formats, for students to study independently, rewatch repeatedly, and download anytime.

**Learning Activity — Assignment**, an optional assignment exploring the area of a circle, for students with capacity to go further to attempt

Teachers can assign homework to help students think more deeply and understand course content, developing their thinking and expression skills.

**Learning Activity — Recorded Course**, a pre-class micro-lecture for the second class period, "The Math in Pizza"

Teachers can publish supplementary knowledge and extension content in the form of a recorded course, boosting students' initiative and independence in learning. The system automatically tracks each student's viewing progress, so teachers always have a clear picture of how students are doing.

**Pre-Setting a "Competency Skills" Evaluation Plan**

Before creating a new learning activity, teachers can first set up competency skill groups, adding the relevant skill indicators and indicator descriptions.

When creating a teaching activity, they can then quickly link it to competency skills and grade based on student completion — the system automatically generates a competency evaluation result.

**Process-Based Evaluation and Competency Evaluation**

During course implementation, both teachers and students can see process-level learning data, helping teachers better understand students' actual performance and offer timely support. At the same time, students can better understand their own learning status, identify and fill gaps, and improve their learning outcomes.

## IV. Course Examples

**Precision Teaching — Shanghai Fushan Foreign Language Primary School, Zhengda Campus**

Guided by the new curriculum standards toward "new" teaching and evaluation, every subject group has shown their strengths around "data empowerment" and "precision teaching"!

The English group's teachers started from issues in students' online teaching interactions and dove into the LMS learning management system.

The math group's teachers boldly rolled out data-driven precision classroom teaching.

The general-studies group's teachers carried out precision evaluation grounded in education data and focused on core competencies.

**Teacher Training — Shenzhen Futian District Liyuan Primary School (Liyuan Education Group), Head Teacher Course**

Teacher Xue is a seasoned key teacher with extensive class management experience.

She shared her class management experience and insights through the LMS, and organized a team of teachers to share as well, in the form of livestream and recorded courses.

She shared documents and materials via Learning Materials.

She gathered teachers' questions and views through Discussion/Quiz activities.

She had teachers submit their reflections and suggestions after observing recorded lesson demonstrations via Assignments.

The school has now launched sharing sessions across multiple subjects and topics, and plans to roll this format out across the Liyuan Education Group.

**Reading and Learning — Teacher Growth Exchange**

*"New Plan, New Standards, New Journey"* is a book interpreting the new curriculum standards, written by professors from East China Normal University.

To help teachers better understand the new curriculum standards and apply them in teaching, our company organized a shared-reading group activity — outstanding teachers were nominated by basic-education schools within a set quota to take part.

The activity ran a kickoff session, a closing session, and expert sharing sessions through class sessions, with teachers holding small-group discussions.

Teachers' questions and desired sharing topics were gathered through Discussion.

Debate competitions and "roast" sessions were explained and demonstrated via recorded courses.

Assignments and quizzes were used to check teachers' understanding.

Accumulated scores were used to recognize outstanding individual teachers.

Through the LMS, dialogue was made possible between basic-education teachers and new-curriculum-standard experts — teachers broke through spatial boundaries to form study groups and exchange experience. After the activity, teachers used the LMS again to pass on what they'd learned in the shared-reading group to teachers at their own schools.
